The Tinkers' Union gave Ziz Fizziks a new position, but not the easy life he expected. On the western edge of Windshear Crag, he found that Sputtervalve drove him as hard as any Venture Company foreman. Still, Ziz would rather labor under a demanding goblin superior than share an engineering workshop with a gnome.

quest:1484.text: The Corrupter. Maurin Bonesplitter has found the demon lord far more dangerous than expected. He is certain Takata Steelblade doubts his abilities, and leaving the swordsman uninformed of what happened would insult Takata's honor. Maurin sends you to speak with Takata, who is nearby. Maurin Bonesplitter finds the creature much more dangerous than he had anticipated. No doubt Takata Steelblade questions whether Maurin can handle it, and not being told of what just happened would insult Takata's honor. Maurin asks you to speak to the swordsman and offer to slay the demon, should Takata allow it. Maurin cautions you not to press Takata too hard, since it is better if Takata believes the idea is his own. Takata Steelblade is close at hand, just across the path from Maurin, on a cliff overlooking the Kodo Graveyard.

quest:1487.text: Deviate Eradication. Deviate Eradication is a task assigned by the night elf druid Ebru above the entrance to the Wailing Caverns. While other disciples focus on waking their slumbering leader, Ebru asks adventurers to purge the caverns of mutated deviate beasts spawned by his twisted vision. Ridding the subterranean oasis of these horrors is an essential step in stemming the corruption threatening the Barrens. The night elf druid Naralex brought his followers to the subterranean springs of the Barrens with an ambitious vision: tap into the Emerald Dream to regrow the parched plains into a lush, thriving woodland. Instead, Naralex became ensnared within the Dream, his slumber twisting into an agonizing nightmare. Rather than healing the land, the power surging through the caverns warped the native wildlife and plant life into monstrous, aggressive mutants known as deviate beasts. Perched in the cliff-face cavern overlooking the cave entrance, Ebru and a handful of surviving Disciples of Naralex watch in despair as their numbers dwindle. While some among them dedicate their energy toward awakening their fallen master, Ebru recognizes an immediate crisis. Left unchecked, the rapidly multiplying deviate vipers, shamblers, ravagers, and dreadfangs will spill outward into the Barrens. Ebru therefore recruits passing adventurers to descend into the deep tunnels and cull the aberrant monstrosities at their source.

quest:149.text: Ghost Hair Thread. Madame Eva seeks ghost hair in the hills south of Darkshire. She needs the strands to spin Ghost Hair Thread for Abercrombie, and sends travelers to find Blind Mary at an abandoned farmhouse. An ethereal comb lets them gather hair from the tormented spirit. Madame Eva needs ghost hair to spin thread for Abercrombie. Linen and wool cannot serve the rituals of Duskwood, so she gives you a Spectral Comb to gather strands from a spirit. It can pass through the veil of death and catch loose spectral hair without violence. South of Darkshire, Blind Mary haunts an abandoned farmhouse. The tormented spirit despairs over her appearance and screams at intruders to look away. In anguish over what she had become, she tore out her own eyes. The Spectral Comb offers a brief comfort: she can groom her ghostly hair, though her torment continues.

quest:150.text: Murloc Poachers. Along Lake Everstill, Murloc Poachers are stripping Lakeshire's waters of fish. Dockmaster Baren needs you to thin their swelling ranks before the town loses its main food supply. Dockmaster Baren needs you to protect the fish that feed Lakeshire. Lake Everstill supplies the mountain town and its market with fresh catches. Large tribes of murlocs now crowd the shallows and scour the waters for food. Left unchecked, they could wipe out the local fish and leave Lakeshire without its main food supply. Murlocs usually scavenge along the coast, so their numbers high in the Redridge Mountains are hard to explain. Dockmaster Baren wonders why they have come so far from the open ocean. They may be fleeing predators at sea, losing territorial fights, or drawn by Lake Everstill's plentiful waters. Whatever brought them inland, their presence points to trouble elsewhere in the region.

quest:1505.text: Veteran Uzzek. Veteran Uzzek is a Horde quest that sends promising young warriors to seek out a seasoned combat instructor. Stationed just south of Far Watch Post between Durotar and the Barrens, Uzzek teaches new recruits that true martial greatness requires disciplined study as well as strength. In the culture of the Horde, martial strength is unquestioned and revered above all else. Yet brute force alone does not make a champion. Seasoned commanders know that the greatest warriors are also humble students of the craft, willing to hone their instincts through discipline and study. Aspiring fighters ready to advance beyond basic training are directed to seek out those who have survived the crucible of war. To receive advanced combat guidance, young fighters travel to the arid borderlands between Durotar and the Barrens. Just south of Far Watch Post, the fortified orc garrison watching the eastern frontier, resides Uzzek. A veteran of countless bloody conflicts, Uzzek now dedicates his years to mentoring promising new recruits in the vital arts of combat and tactical survival.

quest:1507.text: Devourer of Souls. Gan'rul Bloodeye sends an aspiring Horde warlock to begin the path to summoning and commanding a succubus. In Orgrimmar's Cleft of Shadow, the warlock seeks Cazul's counsel on luring and binding the demon. Horde warlocks who master lesser demons such as imps and voidwalkers may seek a succubus next. Gan'rul Bloodeye oversees the dark arts beneath Orgrimmar and judges when a warlock is ready to call one from the Twisting Nether. A succubus can turn the frail against themselves, so binding one takes subtlety as well as strength. A succubus preys on mortal desire, so raw incantations cannot call one alone. The summoner must lure it with an object filled with pure love and devotion. Gan'rul is unwilling or unable to provide such a relic himself, so he sends the warlock across the Cleft of Shadow to Cazul. The ancient warlock knows the arcane and demonic rites needed for the next part of the ritual.

quest:1508.text: Blind Cazul. In the Cleft of Shadow, an initiate seeks Blind Cazul’s help with a succubus ritual. The sightless warlock points toward an object charged with mortal emotion. A succubus answers to mortal longing, sorrow, and desire. To draw one across the veil, an aspiring summoner needs more than willpower; the demon is known to devour souls. Blind Cazul understands what the initiate seeks and knows where to find a fitting lure. Though blind, Blind Cazul senses the lives and sorrows within Orgrimmar’s red ramparts. He sends the initiate to Zankaja, an orc woman who lives atop the bluffs near the wind rider roost. She anxiously awaits her mate Dogran’s return, and her despair can draw a demon’s attention.

quest:1509.text: News of Dogran. A missing grunt named Dogran leaves Zankaja waiting in Orgrimmar. His mate has heard nothing for days, so she sends you to question his superior, Gazrog, at the Crossroads. For a warlock, the search also serves a ritual to bind a succubus. Zankaja waits on the bluffs of Orgrimmar, fearing for her mate Dogran. He was sent to the Crossroads on an honorable promotion, but his return is overdue and she has heard nothing for days. She asks you to seek news from his commander, Gazrog. She does not know that dark arts are at work behind the search.

quest:1510.text: News of Dogran. In Stonetalon's foothills, Dogran's life hangs on a healing draught from Malaka'jin. The first runner sent to fetch it never returned, and you travel deep into the foothills to find Ken'zigla, a Darkspear troll. Dogran, a Horde grunt at Camp Taurajo in the southern Barrens, was badly wounded fighting entrenched quilboar. His fellow grunts brought him back, but his wounds had festered. They feared moving him without first treating him. Taurajo sent word north to the Crossroads for a traditional healing draught made by the jungle trolls of Malaka'jin.

quest:1511.text: Ken'zigla's Draught. In the Horde warlock chain to summon a succubus, Ken'zigla's Draught is bound for Camp Taurajo. The troll apothecary prepared it in the Stonetalon Mountains to save Dogran, a missing operative. Ken'zigla prepared a second dose after trouble with the first courier. The troll apothecary in the Stonetalon Mountains feared the emissary sent to find medicine for the missing scout Dogran had never returned. His draught is volatile and powerful. Half a dose gives a mortally wounded soldier strength to move without making the wounds bleed anew. The rest must wait until the next day, when it completes the recovery.

quest:1512.text: Love's Gift. In Orgrimmar, Gan'rul Bloodeye awaits a pendant for the succubus rite. Dogran gives up a treasured keepsake after being found and revived in the Barrens. A warlock needs a talisman charged with strong, unblemished emotion to summon and control a succubus. These demons feed on mortal desire and twist genuine affection into anguish. Dogran's pendant bears his devotion and their parting. Bring it to Gan'rul Bloodeye in Orgrimmar's shadowy clefts, where it is cleaned and polished. Its bright emotional force can draw the soul-devourer across the Twisting Nether.

quest:1513.text: The Binding. At Neeru Fireblade's circle in Orgrimmar, a warlock faces the trial of binding a succubus. Dogran's Pendant draws the demon from the Twisting Nether, where spellcraft and force of arms must break its will. Beneath the clefts of Orgrimmar, Neeru Fireblade keeps a tent with a circle prepared for dangerous rites. Under Gan'rul Bloodeye's guidance, you activate its runes and face the summoned succubus in battle. Calling a demon is only the beginning; you must overpower it alone and bend its spirit to your will.

quest:1515.text: Dogran's Captivity. At Camp Taurajo, a warlock faces a vital trial in Horde training: rescue a captured orc warrior. With Ken'zigla's Draught, you must find battered Grunt Dogran in a quilboar camp and give him strength to escape. Grunt Logmar at Camp Taurajo will not risk Horde soldiers in a costly attack on the entrenched quilboar. Dogran's fate rests with you, an aspiring warlock armed only with Ken'zigla's Draught. Travel north through the brambles and hostile camps to find where the quilboar hold him captive.

quest:1519.text: Call of Earth. The earth calls a shaman to begin a patient trial of communion. By accepting an earthen sapta, the seeker steps onto a path of spiritual rebirth and learns to hear the foundation of life. A shaman learns to commune with the primal force of earth through a formative rite. Earth is the most stubborn and wise of the elements, the steady bedrock beneath existence. It moves through slow cycles of erosion and rebirth. Mountains wear into deserts, and rivers carve canyons over ages. To hear the earth's voice, an initiate needs that same patience. Answering the call changes a seeker beyond return to former ignorance. When the initiate proves readiness and respect for the laws of the Earth Mother, they receive an earthen sapta. The elixir opens a new way of seeing, and the shaman begins to grasp earth's secrets of strength, stamina, and elemental protection.

quest:1522.text: Call of Fire. A shaman sees your strength in earth and sends you north to Kranal Fiss. There, you can learn the ways of fire. Kranal Fiss lives north of the Crossroads. The shaman says he is easy to find, but warns you not to go too far, lest you reach the elves' lands.

quest:1529.text: Call of Water. Your path to the Call of Water begins in Thunder Bluff, where a shaman is ready to seek the element of water. To meet Islen Waterseer, you travel east across the Barrens to its eastern shore. The meeting begins a spiritual journey toward the Water Totem. You have mastered earth and fire, and now your trainers judge you ready to study water. In Thunder Bluff, Xanis Flameweaver recognizes when you have shown the discipline to approach this cleansing element. Your path leads away from Mulgore's mesas and east across the dry plains of the Barrens. You find Islen Waterseer in a fishing shack on the eastern coast, south of Ratchet and the mouth of the Southfury River. She lives apart from the settlements, beside the open ocean. Islen reads your readiness in the elements around you. Earth, wind, and fire already touch your spirit, and she prepares you for trials that will teach you the purity of water.

quest:1530.text: Call of Water. Islen Waterseer sends Horde shamans south through the Barrens to seek Brine. There, they learn what water can cleanse and heal. Islen Waterseer teaches that water brings rebirth. Its flow can carve rock, wash away impurities, and mend flesh, but its healing depends on purity. Polluted water brings blight instead of life. Every shaman must understand this balance before seeking communion with water. You travel far south through the arid Barrens to find Brine. Quilboar raids trouble the wastes, yet Brine lives alone without guards or fear. She holds the knowledge and trials that help you bind yourself to water.

quest:1531.text: Call of Air. At Grommash Hold, Searn Firewarder sends seasoned shamans south to seek the Air Totem. Prate Cloudseer guides them toward the final elemental pillar of their craft. A shaman who has earned the favor of earth, fire, and water now stands ready to harness air, the last of the four elements. In Orgrimmar, troll trainer Searn Firewarder recognizes when a disciple has reached the height of early training and is prepared for this final foundational step. He sends the shaman south across the Barrens, then down into the canyon labyrinth of Thousand Needles. Prate Cloudseer waits in a high cave among the sandstone mesas of Thousand Needles. The hermit lives quietly with her partner, far from Horde encampments. She demands deference before revealing the secrets of the wind. Meet her with proper respect, and she shares the knowledge and focus to manifest the Air Totem, completing the shaman's elemental circle.

quest:1532.text: Call of Air. Xanis Flameweaver sends seasoned Horde shamans from Thunder Bluff south to seek Prate Cloudseer in Thousand Needles. There they seek communion with the wind and the Air Totem, needed to channel its swift forces. A shaman who has attuned to earth, fire, and water now faces air, the final element. From Thunder Bluff, Xanis Flameweaver guides initiates through a trial of humility, focus, and respect for the sky. The winds are fickle and harder to control than the elements they have already learned. The path leads south, past the Barrens and into the canyons of Thousand Needles. Far to the east, Prate Cloudseer dwells in a secluded cave on the cliffs, where canyon drafts howl day and night. She tests each initiate's preparedness before giving them the Air Totem, which channels gusts, lightning, and swift wind spirits.

quest:1534.text: Call of Water. A shaman travels from the Barrens to the Ruins of Stardust for the final gathering trial in the journey to earn Call of Water. Brine sends the initiate north into Ashenvale to draw pure water from its ancient fountain. After gathering water from the pool below Brine’s hut in the Barrens and the pure well of Tarren Mill, the shaman needs one final essence. Brine sends the initiate north across the dry plains and into Ashenvale, an ancient woodland sacred to the night elves. The dry Barrens give way to Ashenvale’s deep canopy, where water takes another form. A shaman must understand this variety to live in harmony with the element. Beyond the shimmering waters of Mystral Lake, near the mountain pass between Ashenvale and the Stonetalon Mountains, lie the Ruins of Stardust. An ancient fountain rests among quiet waters and old stones in this secluded elven sanctum. Untamed elemental and nature spirits guard the ruins and resent intruders. The shaman must tread carefully to draw water from the fountain.

quest:1535.text: Call of Water. Brine sends shamans into the Barrens to gather water for a sapta. The trial begins with a sample from the guarded pool below her hill, where water means survival. Brine asks shaman initiates to study water in all its forms before she grants the water sapta that lets them commune with the spirits. In the arid Barrens, water means the difference between survival and starvation. She asks them to notice what water makes possible: forests flourish where it flows, deserts starve where it is absent, and living beings will kill to protect even the humblest spring. Native quilboar fiercely guard the watering hole beneath Brine's hill. They treat every pool as a priceless hoard and feast whenever rain comes. Brine regrets the violence their hoarding brings, but their insular greed and divided clans keep their threat contained. For the other races surviving on the plains, that leaves a precarious balance.

quest:1536.text: Call of Water. You set out from the Barrens for a pure spring in Forsaken-held Tarren Mill. The water will help Brine prepare the Water Sapta, and its survival offers a lesson in hope. Brine sends you across the sea to Tarren Mill in Hillsbrad Foothills for water to prepare the Water Sapta. Human resistance and the newly allied Forsaken surround the town, yet its small central well gives pure spring water. To Brine, the spring is a sacred remnant of cleanliness in an unhallowed land. Brine sees the pure well in Tarren Mill as more than an ingredient. She compares its endurance to Warchief Thrall, who bore hardship, captivity, and sorrow before rising to lead the orcish people. Thrall gives the Horde hope, and the well shows that life and purity can endure through tragedy and corruption.

quest:154.text: Return the Comb. Madame Eva waits in Darkshire for the comb Blind Mary has returned. Its ghostly strands can be spun into Ghost Hair Thread. Blind Mary waits in a shack south of Darkshire, mourning her death and the change it brought. Madame Eva’s comb reminds her of mortal grooming, and deepens her sorrow. She sees only an apparition, a monster stripped of mortal grace, certain no one can love her again. In horror, she thrusts the comb and the ghostly hair tangled in its teeth back into your hands. Madame Eva awaits the comb in Darkshire, knowing the task was grim. The ghostly hair gives the fortune teller what she needs to spin a spool of Ghost Hair Thread. She pays you for any strands left over after the delicate work.

quest:156.text: Gather Rot Blossoms. In Duskwood, Tavernkeep Smitts needs rot blossoms for his zombie juice. The plants grow inside the skulls of skeletal horrors and fiends in the graveyards. Tavernkeep Smitts sometimes brews a strange drink at the Scarlet Raven Tavern. His recipe for zombie juice calls for rot blossoms, which root inside the empty skulls of animated skeletons. Smitts avoids the undead, so passing mercenaries gather the blossoms for him. Rot blossoms grow on skeletal horrors and fiends in the overgrown plots of Tranquil Gardens Cemetery and across Raven Hill Cemetery. The Night Watch militia is stretched thin fighting the woods’ creeping terrors. Smitts commends adventurers who hunt the dead to Commander Althea Ebonlocke, helping cull the restless ranks that threaten Darkshire.

quest:157.text: Deliver the Thread. Madame Eva sends ghost hair thread from Darkshire across Duskwood to Abercrombie near Raven Hill Cemetery. The hermit says he needs it to guard his hut from restless spirits. Madame Eva gives you a spool of Ghost Hair Thread, spun from hair gathered from the ghost Blind Mary. You carry it west through Duskwood, where spiders and undead roam. Abercrombie waits in his ramshackle shack just north of Raven Hill Cemetery.

quest:158.text: Zombie Juice. Abercrombie sends travelers from his lonely shack in Duskwood to fetch Zombie Juice in Darkshire. He says the chill of the night leaves him cold. Abercrombie lives alone among the horrors of Duskwood's shadowed woods and often sends sympathetic travelers on strange errands. He says the creeping dusk drains his warmth and vitality, then asks you to travel east to Darkshire. At the Scarlet Raven Tavern, Tavernkeep Smitts sells the potent drink Abercrombie seeks. Its ominous name is Zombie Juice, and Abercrombie says it will put fire back in his veins. Tavernkeep Smitts serves weary guards and frightened townsfolk at Darkshire's tavern, but few ask for Zombie Juice. The drink is known for its dangerous strength, and Smitts recognizes the vintage. Abercrombie's taste for such a morbid brew raises quiet eyebrows in a region besieged by the restless dead.

quest:159.text: Juice Delivery. In Darkshire, a potent brew draws raised eyebrows as you carry it west. Tavernkeep Smitts entrusts you with Zombie Juice for Abercrombie, a reclusive hermit on Duskwood’s western edge. The drink is meant to warm the shivering old man, but its uncanny potency raises questions. Tavernkeep Smitts of Darkshire brews a legendary draught called Zombie Juice. When it is ready, he hands you the bottle and warns you to handle it gently, saying the concoction is stout enough to raise the dead. You carry the potent drink across a haunted forest to an eccentric loner, on what seems like a simple act of charity.

quest:160.text: Note to the Mayor. Abercrombie sends a message from western Duskwood to Darkshire, where its mayor awaits an unexpected delivery. He calls himself an old friend of Mayor Lord Ello Ebonlocke, but the note raises questions. After you recover Abercrombie’s stolen chest from the ogres at Vul'Gol Ogre Mound, the hermit sends you down the misty roads toward town. He laughs with delight and says he and Mayor Lord Ello Ebonlocke are old friends. Abercrombie insists the mayor will be as thrilled as he is when he learns what you have done.

quest:163.text: Raven Hill. In western Duskwood, shadows move through Raven Hill, and a light flickers in a ruined window. Elaine Carevin sends travelers from Darkshire to learn what has taken shelter there. The Night Watch has long left Duskwood’s far west to the dead and wilderness. Yet signs of life there demand attention. Calor, a watcher on the gloomy roads, saw movement among Raven Hill’s silent houses two nights in a row. A lantern flickered in a window. With ghouls, skeletons, and beasts across the land, the Night Watch cannot ignore what stirs among the ruins.

quest:164.text: Deliveries to Sven. In Darkshire, Elaine Carevin sends aid to Sven Yorgen's camp in northwestern Duskwood. Sven and his few followers struggle against the dangers of the blighted woods. Sven Yorgen and a few companions keep a camp on Duskwood's northwestern frontier. Darkshire faces wolves, spiders, and restless dead, yet Sven's band holds its ground beyond the town's walls. Constant danger leaves them unable to spare anyone for the perilous journey back to town for provisions. Elaine Carevin arranges for travelers to carry supplies so the fighters can keep going. The Carevin family respects Sven and sees his stand as devotion to the Light. Elaine organizes and sends supplies to support his camp. When Sven receives the crate, he recognizes the Carevins' support, though his attention remains on the battle at hand.

quest:1642.text:
The Tome of Divinity. In Stormwind, The Tome of Divinity guides the first steps of paladin training. Its teachings call champions of the Holy Light to humility, compassion, and patience, not godhood or strength alone. The Tome of Divinity’s sacred texts teach paladin initiates what it means to serve the Light. Divinity means neither seeking godhood nor claiming rule over others. Instead, champions reflect the Light’s grace through pure intent and goodness in every deed. Paladins take up arms against evil, but strength without moral purpose means little. Their true distinction lies in how they treat ordinary people across Azeroth, keeping power bound to righteousness and humility. Scripture is only the beginning of a paladin’s service. After an initiate studies the Tome of Divinity, Duthorian Rall in Stormwind tests whether its lessons have taken root in the candidate’s heart and mind. The Light asks for more than the slaying of beasts. It calls for patience, bravery, and understanding.

In the city and the surrounding lands, people suffer and humble tasks go without glory. By aiding the less fortunate and comforting those in despair, an initiate proves they have the sound mind and selfless spirit to bear the Light’s blessings responsibly.

quest:1643.text: The Tome of Divinity. In Stormwind, initiates of the Light are sent to help someone in need. They seek a citizen of pure heart and noble motive, and find Stephanie Turner in the Trade District. Initiates of the Light begin this sacred trial by walking Stormwind’s streets. They seek someone of noble intent and pure motive who depends on the kindness of strangers. Before deeper instruction in holy duties, they learn that service to the vulnerable matters more than glorious combat. In Stormwind’s Trade District, Stephanie Turner makes clothing for children in the city’s orphanage with her husband. More tradesmen have come to the city, and competition for cloth and leather has made donations harder to find. Her husband has gone to Ironforge to seek support. Stephanie remains in Stormwind, carrying on their work.

quest:1644.text: The Tome of Divinity. Stephanie Turner in Stormwind needs help clothing children orphaned by the Scourge. Her husband John is gathering supplies as an aspiring paladin brings linen cloth to her home. Stephanie Turner cares for children whose families were lost to the Scourge in the northern lands over the last decade. Her husband John is away gathering supplies. So Stephanie must keep the children fed, warm, and sheltered while finding time to make them clothes. An aspiring paladin proves compassion by bringing linen cloth to Stephanie. With the cloth, she can sew shirts and pants for the children while tending to their food and shelter. Such humble aid shows how the Light's protectors guard the weak. Stephanie says this year has grown harsher. John must make long, difficult journeys as far as Ironforge to gather supplies. Even within Stormwind's high stone walls, the pain of recent tragedies in the north is still felt.

quest:1646.text: The Tome of Divinity. In Ironforge, Tiza Battleforge teaches young paladins what the Light asks of them. The Tome of Divinity says devotion calls for patience, compassion, and humble service to the needy, alongside martial strength. For a paladin, strength in battle must serve a higher purpose. Tiza Battleforge in Ironforge gives initiates the Tome of Divinity to teach them why they wield their arms. It turns their thoughts from dominion and godhood toward moral goodness. A paladin's calling is to serve as a steady instrument of the Light. The tome teaches that smiting evil is not enough to make a paladin. Compassion, patience, and humility set these warriors apart from common combatants. After studying its words, initiates undertake trials in Ironforge and nearby lands. Through charity and service, they show sound judgment and unwavering devotion.

quest:1647.text: The Tome of Divinity. At Ironforge's temple, an initiate seeks a lesson in the Light through service. Sent by a mentor into the outer ring, you search for someone with pure intent and a genuine need. There, John Turner shows how compassion and selfless work belong on the path of the Light. Initiates of the Light stationed in Ironforge face a trial of compassion. Their mentor sends them into the dwarven city to find someone truly in need of aid. The search calls for discernment: you must recognize a pure heart, noble intent, and a real need for kindness. Humble service lies at the heart of this calling. In Ironforge's outer ring, a humble worker named John Turner plies his trade. Startled by your approach, he calls out about the Orphanage of Stormwind, then tells you why he works so hard. Separated from his beloved wife by long hours of toil, Turner labors so orphaned children can have clothes and food. Help him, then return to the temple to continue your journey in the Light.

quest:1648.text: The Tome of Divinity. In Ironforge, The Tome of Divinity calls servants of the Light to show compassion. John Turner seeks aid for the Stormwind orphanage he runs with his wife, caring for children left parentless by the Scourge. The trial asks an initiate to choose charity over martial glory. For an initiate walking the path of the Light, the trial in Ironforge calls for charity rather than arms. John Turner has come to the dwarven halls seeking help. He and his wife oversee an orphanage in Stormwind, where they care for children left without parents by the Scourge's rampages over the past decade. His journey to Ironforge speaks to the hardships shared by the Alliance's common folk. Provisions are hard to gather across borders. More tradesmen have come to work across Azeroth, and local supplies have grown scarce. John Turner has spent weeks in Ironforge appealing to civic groups and citizens, with little to show for it. His wife needs linen cloth to make clothes for the children. Giving it freely shows the selfless devotion at the heart of a servant of the Light.

quest:1649.text: The Tome of Valor. In Stormwind, The Tome of Valor calls paladins to prove their faith and courage. Duthorian Rall awaits those ready to petition the Church. The Tome teaches that valor is forged through hardship. Its sacred text likens virtues to precious ores, valuable when found but refined to endure. Through hard trials and true commitment, a paladin binds faith, compassion, and courage into strength against the evils threatening Azeroth. After reading the Tome, you are directed to Duthorian Rall, a respected paladin leader in Stormwind's Cathedral of Light. He hears petitions from those seeking the trials of valor. The tests are no mere ritual. Defending the innocent and upholding the Church may cost your life, and only the steadfast earn recognition in the order.

quest:165.text: The Hermit. Elaine Carevin in Darkshire sends you to check on Abercrombie, an elderly recluse who has not come to town for provisions. He lives in a rickety shack at the edge of Raven Hill Cemetery. Elaine Carevin remembers an old man who came to Darkshire for provisions, then stopped appearing. With danger on Duskwood’s roads, she asks you to visit his shack by Raven Hill Cemetery and see whether he is safe. At the shack, you find Abercrombie alive. He chuckles at the Carevins’ concern and says age and the monsters in the woods have kept him from town. Glad to have an able traveler at his door, he quickly asks for help with a few errands.

quest:1650.text: The Tome of Valor. Duthorian Rall sends you to guard Daphne Stilwell on Westfall’s distant shore. Her husband is away, and Defias bandits threaten their homestead. At Stormwind’s Cathedral of Light, Duthorian Rall tests those who seek to become paladins. He asks them to defend the people of the realm. Now you have taken up the mantle of valor, and must put those ideals to work where law and authority have failed. Daphne Stilwell and her husband Jordan keep an outpost at Westfall’s isolated Longshore. Jordan is away in Ironforge, consulting dwarven blacksmiths, while Defias Brotherhood activity runs rampant. So Duthorian sends you west to protect Daphne before thieves overwhelm her homestead.

quest:1651.text: The Tome of Valor. At her Westfall farm, Daphne Stilwell calls for aid as the Defias Brotherhood closes in. A paladin must answer her plea. The Defias Brotherhood still contests the land around Daphne's homestead. Earlier clashes have not ended the danger, and another assault is expected. You are sent to hold the ground beside her house. There is no retreat. Your pursuit of the virtues in the Tome of Valor now faces a test of courage. Daphne has only her own firearm, while you can call on the blessings of the Holy Light. Wave after wave of Defias raiders attacks, and the fight tests whether you can protect someone vulnerable under crushing pressure. True valor means standing between innocent civilians and ruthless violence, even when danger bears down on you.

quest:1652.text: The Tome of Valor. At Stormwind's Cathedral of Light, you tell Duthorian Rall that Daphne Stilwell is safe after the defense of her Westfall homestead. Your courage fulfills the Church's trials of valor and its charge to shield the innocent without thought for yourself. Your defense shows you can stand between danger and the defenseless, as the Church expects of an aspiring paladin. The homestead holds firm, and Daphne is safe from the bandits who threatened her. Jordan Stilwell, Daphne's husband, remains in Ironforge, lending his renowned craftsmanship to the Alliance. Duthorian Rall prepares to send word north, so Jordan can focus on his work knowing his family is protected.

quest:1653.text: The Test of Righteousness. In Cathedral Square, Duthorian Rall sends you to Ironforge with news for Jordan Stilwell. His wife Daphne survived the Defias attack in Westfall. You guarded Daphne Stilwell at her Westfall homestead when Defias outlaws attacked, and she survived. Her husband had left for Ironforge, fearing his family was in danger. Now Rall sends you to tell Jordan in person, so he can learn what happened to Daphne. Jordan Stilwell once hoped to join the paladins, but chose his father's craft and became a master weaponsmith. He works at an anvil outside Ironforge's gates, holding fast to his faith as he shapes weapons. When you tell him Daphne survived, gratitude moves him to help you forge a blessed weapon of righteousness.

quest:1654.text: The Test of Righteousness. Jordan Stilwell has a sacred weapon in mind for a paladin worthy of the Light. The Ironforge smith needs rare materials from distant lands, including his lost family hammer. Outside Ironforge's gates, Jordan Stilwell cannot forge the paladin's weapon on his own. You gather the materials his craft demands. Jordan Stilwell needs four things for the weapon: Whitestone Oak lumber, refined ore from master prospectors, a purified Kor Gem, and his smithing hammer. He left the hammer behind while escaping Shadowfang Keep. Finding all four means facing dangers across the Eastern Kingdoms and beyond.

quest:1655.text: Bailor's Ore Shipment. In Loch Modan, Bailor's Ore Shipment is bound for Jordan Stilwell's sanctified weapon. Mo'grosh ogres plundered the alloy on the road from the Wetlands. Jordan Stilwell awaits ore refined by his old friend Bailor Stonehand, but the shipment never reaches Ironforge. As the caravan travels south from the Wetlands into Loch Modan, Mo'grosh ogres ambush it and slaughter its guards. One wounded guard reaches a camp, then dies soon after. The shipment is left in ogre territory. Bailor Stonehand camps in Loch Modan and sends paladins across the Loch toward the northeastern hills. The stolen crate of alloy lies abandoned among the Mo'grosh camps. Recovering it means entering hostile territory, and will let Bailor keep his agreement with Jordan Stilwell.

quest:1656.text: A Task Unfinished. A Task Unfinished is a simple delivery quest highlighting the strain young tauren endure during their coming-of-age rites on Red Cloud Mesa. Overburdened by the demands of their trials and a filial chore, an exhausted youth asks a passing traveler to carry a bundle of furs down to Innkeeper Kauth in Bloodhoof Village. High upon Red Cloud Mesa, young tauren face rigorous trials of passage to prove their readiness for the wider world. Balancing traditional rites against ordinary tribal chores can push a youth to the brink of physical exhaustion. Faced with an unfinished Rite of Strength and an urgent chore from their father, one young tauren seeks the aid of a passing traveler to carry a bundle of furs down the mesa. The destination for the furs is Bloodhoof Village, a welcoming haven resting in the open plains below. Innkeeper Kauth eagerly receives the delivery, intending to turn the pelt bundle into warm blankets for weary wanderers. The errand highlights both the hospitality of the plains tauren and the importance of rest, showing that community support underpins every solitary trial of strength.

quest:166.text: The Defias Brotherhood. In Westfall, The Defias Brotherhood still holds the farmlands in fear. Gryan Stoutmantle has found their stronghold beneath Moonbrook and calls for a final blow against their leader. Gryan Stoutmantle and the People's Militia have fought the Defias Brotherhood across Westfall for months. Now the thieves' stronghold lies exposed beneath Moonbrook. Stoutmantle orders Edwin VanCleef assassinated, believing his death will break the rebellion once and for all.

quest:167.text: Oh Brother. . .. Wilder Thistlenettle waits in Stormwind after a cave-in beneath Moonbrook. He asks you to search the mines for his brother, Foreman Thistlenettle, or recover the dwarf's Explorers' League Badge. Wilder Thistlenettle and his brother worked for a mining company in the tunnels beneath Moonbrook. Thieves swarmed the mines, then a cave-in sealed the lower passages. Wilder escaped to Stormwind, but his brother and the rest of the crew remained trapped behind the rubble.

quest:1678.text: Vejrek. In the foothills south of Frostmane Hold, you face Vejrek to prove your mettle. Muren Stormpike wants proof you can handle real foes. Your success begins a lesson in strong defense. Muren Stormpike says you need toughness before he can teach you new moves. Vejrek is the toughest troll in these parts, and his hut lies in the foothills south of Frostmane Hold. Muren asks you to bring back Vejrek’s head as proof you can handle real foes.

quest:1680.text: Tormus Deepforge. In Ironforge, Tormus Deepforge waits for fighters sent by Muren Stormpike. Before he forges a weapon for them, he asks them to face a perilous trial. Tormus Deepforge is a master dwarven weaponsmith in Ironforge. Warriors who show their growing skill to Muren Stormpike are sent across the city to consult him. Tormus is known for sturdy, potent arms, but he does not give fine blades or bludgeons to every passerby. A warrior must earn his work through action. Before Tormus agrees to forge a weapon, he asks the adventurer to promise him a favor. He speaks plainly about the danger ahead and warns that it could cost a life. To him, peril is no reason to turn back. It is the proper test of a warrior's mettle.

quest:169.text: Wanted: Gath'Ilzogg. In Redridge, Magistrate Solomon offers a generous bounty on the warlord behind Blackrock's invasion of Stonewatch. The reward goes to anyone who storms the conquered keep and brings back the commander's severed head. Gath'Ilzogg commands Blackrock raids across the Redridge Mountains. His orcs stormed Stonewatch Keep and made the former human bastion a fortified staging ground for attacks on nearby settlements. From its highest ramparts, he plans further incursions into Lakeshire, threatening to cut Redridge off from the rest of the kingdom. Stormwind's royal army has failed to send reinforcements to the border regions, so Magistrate Solomon takes matters into his own hands. Lakeshire lacks the soldiers to retake Stonewatch Keep by force. Solomon posts a public bounty on Gath'Ilzogg, hoping to break Blackrock's leadership and begin reclaiming the keep for the crown.

quest:1698.text: Yorus Barleybrew. At the Lakeshire Inn, Yorus Barleybrew awaits bold Alliance warriors with an eccentric challenge. Trainers across Alliance capitals send seasoned fighters from Stormwind toward the Redridge borderlands to meet the dwarf and face his test of arms. Across Alliance capitals, warrior trainers watch fighters outgrow their first drills. When an apprentice proves their mettle around their twentieth season, Kelv Sternhammer, Wu Shen, and Darnath Bladesinger pass along word of Yorus Barleybrew. The dwarf offers no standard military order. Instead, he has issued an open wager and a test of arms to any Alliance warrior bold enough to answer. Yorus Barleybrew waits at the tavern in Lakeshire, on the front lines of Redridge's struggle against encroaching gnolls and Blackrock orcs. Those who find him meet a boastful dwarf with a hearty drink in hand, ready to judge any challenger who claims true fighting spirit. For warriors seeking to prove themselves beyond the capital's safe cobbled streets, his trial opens onto the harsher battles of the frontier.

quest:1699.text: The Rethban Gauntlet. In Lakeshire, Yorus Barleybrew sends challengers on a perilous run north and back. They drink his family's fiery Barleybrew Scalder, reach Rethban Caverns, and return within an hour. In Lakeshire, grim talk of gnoll raids and missing town guards fills the inn. The dwarf Yorus Barleybrew offers a different kind of diversion: a test of speed, courage, and endurance. Before setting out on foot for the northern foothills, challengers drink a draught of his family's Barleybrew Scalder. Redridge gnolls roam the hills between Lakeshire and Rethban Caverns. Runners must fight or slip past their packs, reach the first fork inside the dark tunnels, then hurry back to Yorus within an hour. The fiery drink makes the run harder, leaving challengers staggering as they make their way through the hills.

quest:1700.text: Grimand Elmore. In Stormwind City, Grimand Elmore receives Furen Longbeard's technical notes. Their brief exchange carries intricate findings between two headstrong weaponsmiths who share the city. Furen Longbeard forged the specialized Fire Hardened Mail and uncovered intricate heat-treating techniques and elemental principles. He records his findings on parchment, then asks you to deliver them straight to Grimand Elmore, a seasoned crafter at a nearby weapon shop. Grimand Elmore bristles at the manuscript. He insists he taught Furen everything the younger dwarf knows, and the thought that his former pupil could teach him wounds his pride. Yet Grimand cannot resist reading the notes. Soon he finds an intriguing idea and is eager to test it himself.

quest:1701.text: Fire Hardened Mail. In Stormwind, Furen Longbeard offers an Alliance warrior a new design for Fire Hardened Mail. He will forge it if you bring rare materials from both continents. Furen Longbeard has forged an exceptional buckler for you. Now the dwarf armorer proposes a greater work: mail made to withstand fierce blows. His craft calls for more than iron or steel. He needs rare materials touched by elemental heat and natural resilience. Furen cannot leave his Stormwind forge, so you must gather these dangerous ingredients. Furen sends you to distant wilds and dangerous depths for the materials. The recipe calls for fangs from venomous spiders in the Wetlands' damp crevices. It also needs scorched and galvanized horns from fierce chimaeras in the Stonetalon Mountains. To bind and temper these beast parts into mail, Furen needs volatile phlogiston from Roogug, a geomancer deep within Razorfen Kraul's thorny maze in the Barrens.

quest:1702.text: The Shieldsmith. In Stormwind, Yorus Barleybrew sends warriors to claim the shield he promised. A hard trial in the Redridge Mountains is behind them, and a cask of Barleybrew Scalder is bound for Furen Longbeard, the smith who will shape their shield. You have faced the gnolls and dangers of the Rethban Gauntlet, and Yorus Barleybrew keeps his bargain. Lakeshire cannot provide the promised shield, so he sends proven fighters back to Stormwind City. There, a dwarven armorer is ready to repay a personal debt. Yorus gives you a heavy cask of Barleybrew Scalder in place of a letter of credit. Carry it to Furen Longbeard in Stormwind's Dwarven District. The seasoned smith knows whose name stands behind the cask and lends his skill to a warrior who seeks a stout shield.

quest:1703.text: Mathiel. Furen Longbeard sends his crafting notes across the sea to Mathiel in Darnassus. The night elf smith works on the Warrior's Terrace, where dwarven mail forging may reach a new pair of hands. Furen Longbeard has mastered the forging of fire-hardened armor and chooses to share what he has learned with other Alliance craftsmen. He copies his technical diagrams and sends you across the continents to Mathiel, a smith on Teldrassil. On Darnassus's Warrior's Terrace, Mathiel tends a forge for the Sentinels and other fighters who defend the night elf capital. Furen's notes carry dwarven methods from the underground forges of Khaz Modan to kaldorei armorers, whose craft is shaped by their bond with nature.

quest:1704.text: Klockmort Spannerspan. In Tinkertown, Furen Longbeard's fire-hardened mail findings reach Klockmort Spannerspan. The dwarf smith trusts his gnomish colleague to discover what the new techniques can do. You carry Furen's notes from Stormwind to Ironforge, then on to Tinkertown. There, Klockmort Spannerspan works as a blacksmith and can test the discoveries in his own craft. Gnomish blacksmiths are rare among their dwarven hosts. Klockmort is eager to move beyond traditional metalwork, and the notes excite him with the promise of a breakthrough. He is ready to try the fiery techniques in his own unusual projects.

quest:1705.text:
Burning Blood. In Stormwind, Grimand Elmore puts Furen Longbeard’s smithing methods to the test. To try them at his own forge, he needs burning blood and a burning rock from Duskwood. Grimand Elmore is one of the Alliance’s finest armorers. He seldom believes another smith can surpass his methods. Yet Furen Longbeard’s unusual discoveries have stirred his professional curiosity, and Grimand agrees to make a piece of armor using them.

For the work, he needs strange, volatile materials from the dark reaches of the south. They will quench and temper the metal to his exact requirements. Ordinary water and common coals will not do. Grimand sends you to Roland’s Doom, an abandoned mine in Duskwood. Savage Nightbane worgen have overrun its tunnels, and burning ichor pulses in their cursed veins.

He needs vials of their burning blood and a rare flaming core called a burning rock. Gutspill, leader of the pack, carries it. Bring both scorching materials back so Grimand can test Furen’s methods at the forge.

quest:1706.text: Grimand's Armor. Grimand Elmore now offers you a coif made from rare materials. It tests Furen Longbeard's smithing methods and is built to endure crushing blows, a hard-won step in your training as an Alliance warrior. The coif shows that Furen Longbeard's daring methods can strengthen armor against crushing impacts. Grimand Elmore forged it from rare elemental and beast components you gathered in hostile territory, putting the dwarven master armorer's theories to the test. Grimand Elmore treats the metal to bear pressure and blows that would warp ordinary steel. Then he gives you the finished coif. Its strength honors Furen Longbeard's craft and your resolve, and may help you hold the frontline against Azeroth's greatest threats.

quest:1708.text: Iron Coral. In Tinker Town, Klockmort Spannerspan seeks searing coral for a new suit of armor. The gnome blacksmith hopes to test new smithing methods with this rare sea material on the Wetlands coast. Klockmort Spannerspan has shared discoveries with Furen Longbeard, a master dwarven smith. Now he hopes to unite Furen's skill in metallurgy with his own tinkering. Mountain ore alone will not give him the resilient armor he seeks. So he needs searing coral, a material hardened by the sea. Searing coral grows underwater off the Wetlands coast, south of Menethil Harbor. You need to bring back twenty clusters while aquatic predators prowl below. Then carry the harvest to Ironforge. Klockmort plans to smelt and hammer the coral into experimental armor plating.

quest:1709.text: Klockmort's Creation. In Tinker Town, Klockmort Spannerspan puts Furen Longbeard's forging method to work on rare materials. The result is armor made to endure. Using Furen Longbeard's methods, Klockmort finishes a pair of armored gauntlets in Tinker Town. Dwarven metalworking and gnomish mechanical skill come together in gauntlets built to endure punishment that would crush ordinary steel. Klockmort says a siege engine could run over the armor without leaving lasting distortion. Peculiarly treated rare components give it resilience. Dwarven forging and gnomish ingenuity join in armor built to withstand the fiercest frontline battles.

quest:1710.text: Sunscorched Shells. In Darnassus, Mathiel seeks wyvern eggshells to strengthen a new mailcrafting technique. The armorer works with the dwarven smith Furen Longbeard and sends warriors to gather shells from Highperch in Thousand Needles. Mathiel works from the Warrior's Terrace in Darnassus and looks beyond night elven methods. He corresponds with Furen Longbeard, a skilled dwarven armorer in Stormwind, and draws on Furen's discoveries in metalwork and armor-smithing. Mathiel hopes to make mail reinforced with natural materials that can withstand great strain. To test the idea, he needs materials found nowhere near Teldrassil. Mathiel's experiment calls for shells from Highperch, far south across the sea in the canyon gorges of Thousand Needles. Wyverns nest high above the salt flats and red stone mesas, beneath Kalimdor's blazing sun. Constant exposure to heat and altitude hardens their eggshells. Mathiel plans to grind the sun-baked fragments into a resilient lacquer and coat chainmail links, making armor that bends while enduring exceptional strain.

quest:1711.text: Mathiel's Armor. At the forge in Darnassus, Mathiel's Armor brings night elf and dwarven craft together. Mathiel works in the Warrior's Terrace, using methods devised by Furen Longbeard to shape exotic materials into armor for Alliance warriors. Night elf armorers have favored methods honed over millennia, with work shaped by nature, supple leathers, and carefully worked metals. Trade with the Eastern Kingdoms has led smiths such as Mathiel to try new ways. He brings the dwarven techniques devised by Furen Longbeard together with elven craft. Mathiel needs sunscorched eggshells from the Highperch wyvern nests in Thousand Needles. He renders the sun-hardened shells into lacquer and uses Furen's heat-treatment formulas to forge resilient leggings for the front lines.

quest:1712.text: Cyclonian. Cyclonian is a mighty wind lord whose defeat has been sought for ages. To challenge him, a champion must gather the components required to summon the elemental and strike him down to claim his whirlwind heart. Defeating the wind lord allows the heart's power to be infused into a formidable weapon. Cyclonian is a raging elemental wind lord whose presence commands reverence and caution. For ages, an attentive watcher has kept vigil over the summoning site, waiting for a combatant possesses enough raw martial prowess to challenge and destroy this tempestuous entity. Calling forth Cyclonian requires a ritual of summoning using rare materials detailed upon a special parchment. Once summoned, the wind lord must be faced in direct combat, testing whether the challenger is truly a champion or merely another victim of his howling gale.

quest:1713.text: The Summoning. At Bath'rah Windwatcher's camp, a warrior faces a trial against Cyclonian, the wind lord. Slay the elemental and claim the Whirlwind Heart, whose storm force can be bound into a weapon. Bath'rah Windwatcher has prepared an ancient ritual to summon Cyclonian into the mortal realm. The fearsome elemental is known as the wind lord. There will be no bargain with the tempest. An able champion must strike it down as soon as it takes form. Cyclonian's Whirlwind Heart sustains his physical form. When the wind lord falls, Bath'rah wrenches the heart free and harnesses the gale within. Its volatile power can imbue a weapon with the force of the storm.

quest:1714.text: Essence of the Exile. At the cauldron, Essence of the Exile draws travelers with its beckoning vapors. Charms set off a violent reaction that reveals molten rock. A bubbling cauldron sends out vapors that draw travelers to its churning depths. Specific enchanted charms stir an intense reaction within the vessel. The charms sink slowly through the liquid. Then a large bubble rises and bursts, revealing a churning lump of molten rock forged from the combined materials.

quest:1716.text: Devourer of Souls. An Alliance warlock crosses the sea to seek Takar the Seer’s counsel on summoning a succubus. Gakin the Darkbinder sends Stormwind initiates into the Barrens for the wisdom they need. Beneath the Slaughtered Lamb in Stormwind’s Mage Quarter, Gakin the Darkbinder guides promising warlocks toward summoning a succubus. The demon devours souls, destroys hearts, and dominates minds, so it cannot be called blindly into Azeroth. A warlock needs a potent lure: an object tied to pure love. That token draws the succubus from the Twisting Nether, where the warlock can defeat and bind it. Stormwind’s covens cannot teach them where to find such an object. Gakin sends his pupils across the Great Sea to Kalimdor in search of the needed catalyst. Takar the Seer waits in the arid Barrens, near the Horde settlement of Camp Taurajo. To reach him, an Alliance warlock must cross wilderness patrolled by hostile centaur, quilboar, and Horde warriors. The journey tests whether a summoner can survive before the ritual even begins.

quest:1717.text: Gakin's Summons. From Ironforge, Gakin's Summons sends promising Alliance warlocks south to Stormwind. Beneath the Mage Quarter, Gakin the Darkbinder awaits to oversee their progress in commanding greater fiends. Demonology stays hidden across Alliance lands. In Ironforge, Lago Blackwrench quietly watches wandering practitioners for the brotherhood in Stormwind. When a warlock masters their first minions, word travels quickly. Lago sends word to leave the snowy mountains of Khaz Modan and report south without delay. Beneath The Slaughtered Lamb in Stormwind's Mage Quarter, Gakin the Darkbinder coordinates the city's warlocks. He sees every capable student as a valuable but hazardous investment. His summons marks the threshold of true demonic binding. Now begin the trials to subjugate a succubus from the Twisting Nether.

quest:1718.text: The Islander. Warrior trainers across Azeroth send proven fighters to Fray Island for a test among their peers. The island lies off the Merchant Coast, where chief warrior Klannoc Macleod awaits those who seek the next step in their training. Warrior trainers in Alliance and Horde capitals send students who have outgrown basic drills to test themselves against their peers. A fighter's progress comes through combat, not rank or loyalty. The journey leads away from civilized sparring yards to a rugged isle in the Great Sea. Fray Island lies east of the Merchant Coast, just south of Ratchet in the Barrens. You can reach it by swimming across waters that pass over submerged sandbar shallows. Political ties matter little on the island, where fighters gather before Klannoc Macleod, its chief warrior, and await the trial he chooses.

quest:1719.text: The Affray. On Fray Island, warriors face a trial before Klannoc Macleod will train them. The Affray pits them against island challengers and their champion. Fray Island lies apart from the mainland, drawing brawlers, outcasts, and combat instructors. Klannoc Macleod does not teach every wanderer who arrives by boat. Aspiring warriors must first enter the Affray, where stamina and awareness in battle prove who can fight beyond mere boasting. A warrior begins the Affray by stepping onto the central iron grate among the spectators. Ringmaster Twiggy Flathead then sends challengers into the ring one after another. Those who survive face the island's heavyweight champion, Big Will. Defeating him is the only way to earn Klannoc's respect.

quest:173.text: Worgen in the Woods. In Darkshire, Calor sends hunters after Nightbane Shadow Weavers in Duskwood. The disillusioned former guardsman is stationed in town, and the hunt leads through Brightwood Grove and the Rotting Orchard. Those who face the worgen can prove their mettle to Master Jonathan Carevin's monster hunters. The Night Watch is hard pressed by undead, spiders, and outlaws along Darkshire's borders. Calor grew tired of a guard too slow and complacent to cleanse the land. He left the Watch and joined Master Jonathan Carevin, setting his blade against heresy and corruption. Carevin does not take just anyone into his circle. Those who want to aid him must first show they can survive the woods' fiercest horrors. Feral worgen hold dominion over Brightwood Grove and the blighted Rotting Orchard. The Nightbane Shadow Weavers among them use dark magic to blind and ensnare their victims before tearing them apart. Calor sends aspiring hunters to slay these spell-weaving beasts, testing their resolve while thinning a threat whose origins deeply unsettle Darkshire's defenders.

quest:1738.text: Heartswood. In the years since the Third War, Heartswood draws warlocks toward an old night elf tragedy. Takar the Seer sends them into Ashenvale for Gakin the Darkbinder, who needs the wood to lure and subjugate a succubus in Stormwind. Takar the Seer says Heartswood grew where the night elf lovers Anathera and Latherion fell during the War of the Ancients ten thousand years ago. Their last breaths and devotion nourished the tree. To mortal eyes, it marks a tragic love; to practitioners of the dark arts, its concentrated emotion is potent magical fuel. Succubi feed on mortal passion, desire, and torment. Takar knows ordinary temptations cannot match an artifact filled with thousands of years of devotion. A piece of Heartswood gives Gakin the Darkbinder the catalyst he needs to draw a cunning demon through the Nether and into a summoning circle in Stormwind's Mage Quarter.

quest:1739.text: The Binding. In Stormwind, warlocks seek to bind a succubus to their will. Beneath The Slaughtered Lamb, an initiate uses an enchanted Heartswood core to summon the demon and defeat it in combat. Beneath The Slaughtered Lamb in Stormwind's Mage Quarter, a crypt shelters the city's warlocks. They practice forbidden arts there, away from the city watch and the Cathedral of Light. Stone summoning circles channel the Nether's power and let initiates reach across the veil between worlds. A warlock needs a prepared Heartswood Core to summon a succubus. The ritual opens a breach at the summoning circle, but the demon can corrupt and overwhelm even a fortified mind. To master it, the warlock must defeat it in single combat. Its physical form returns to the Twisting Nether, while its true tether is secured.

quest:174.text: Look To The Stars. In Duskwood, Viktori Prism'Antras looks beyond the canopy for answers to the forest's curse. He trusts observation over arcane superstition and asks you to gather parts for a telescope drawn up by his gnomish associate. Viktori Prism'Antras sees Duskwood's troubles differently from many in fearful Darkshire. He doubts that black magic, curses, and restless dead alone explain the land's corruption. He believes answers may lie above the canopy. With blueprints from his gnomish partner, Cog, he plans to build an instrument for looking into the heavens. Viktori needs a sturdy frame to begin building the stargazing instrument. Cog's plans call for a machined bronze tube, and Viktori asks you to find one. He trusts practical engineering and careful observation to shed light where mysticism has failed.

quest:1740.text: The Orb of Soran'ruk. In the southern Barrens, Doan Karhan sets warlocks to gather the scattered pieces of Soran'ruk. They seek to rebuild an orb that holds a disgraced demon's essence. Failure within the Burning Legion brings an eternal sentence. When lesser demons lose favor with their masters, their spirits are bound inside crystal orbs. The Legion gives these prisons to mortal conjurers and warlocks as vessels for power under demonic control. Shattering an orb does not free its captive; even the shards hold potent magic. Soran'ruk's orb lies in pieces across two continents. Twilight's Hammer cultists hold smaller fragments in the damp caverns of Blackfathom Deeps in Ashenvale. A sorcerer in the haunted ruins of Shadowfang Keep in Silverpine Forest claimed the larger, mostly intact half. Doan Karhan has spent his life studying Legion orbs and assembled the Orb of Zargain before. With the recovered pieces, he can restore Soran'ruk as a working implement.

quest:175.text: Look To The Stars. In Darkshire, Viktori Prism'Antras seeks a mirror for the telescope he is building from Cog's blueprints. He sends you into southern Duskwood to find Mary, remembered for carrying a looking glass. Viktori Prism'Antras has the bronze tube for his telescope. Now he needs a mirror to guide and reflect light through it, as Cog's blueprints require. Fine silvered glass is hard to make while Darkshire faces shortages, so Viktori recalls Mary, a local woman known across the region for carrying a looking glass. Mary's old home lies deep in southern Duskwood, just north of Tranquil Gardens Cemetery. To reach it, you pass beyond the Night Watch's safe patrols and enter blighted groves where ravenous wolves, feral spiders, and wandering undead roam.

quest:1758.text: Tome of the Cabal. Above Ratchet, Strahad Farsan sends an aspiring Alliance warlock to the Library of Ironforge. A felhunter’s hunger can overwhelm an unprepared summoner, and the Tome of the Cabal holds the knowledge needed to summon and bind the demon. An imp, a voidwalker, or a succubus can be subdued through ritual, but a felhunter brings a different hazard. Felhunters serve the Burning Legion and hunt down arcane energy to devour it. A standard summoning circle will crumble before one, draining the summoner’s magic before a binding can take hold. From his redoubt in the Barrens, Strahad Farsan watches over Ratchet and knows an amateur must not attempt the binding unprepared. An acolyte needs the arcane formulas in the Tome of the Cabal to draw forth and bind a felhunter safely. The earliest mortal cabal of warlocks who successfully broke a felhunter without outside aid authored the manuscript. Its pages detail the geomancy, materials, and binding runes needed to withstand the creature’s hunger. The copy was lost long ago, leaving Strahad and his circle without the masterwork. Strahad sends Alliance warlocks across the Great Sea to the Hall of Explorers in Ironforge, since he cannot provide the text himself. Krom Stoutarm, an itinerant dwarven warlock, resides there and spends his twilight years combing through ancient manuscripts and library records. If any trace of the lost grimoire remains recorded in the Eastern Kingdoms, it rests buried in Krom’s meticulous catalogs.

quest:177.text: Look To The Stars. Viktori Prism'Antras needs Blind Mary's looking glass for his telescope in Darkshire. An Insane Ghoul took it to Tranquil Gardens Cemetery in southern Duskwood. Blind Mary once treasured an ornate looking glass. After an incident took her sight and sanity and left her a weeping spirit, she threw it into the dirt behind her family barn. Now the astronomer Viktori Prism'Antras needs the mirror for his telescope in Darkshire. The looking glass was taken long before he began studying the heavens. An Insane Ghoul scavenged the looking glass from behind the ruined farmsteads. Restless hunger drove the undead creature south, carrying the mirror to Tranquil Gardens Cemetery. It haunts an abandoned chapel among the overgrown tombstones. You face the flesh-eating horrors of the southern woods to reclaim Mary's lost treasure from its rotting claws.

quest:1778.text: The Tome of Divinity. In Ironforge, Tiza Battleforge teaches initiates what service to the Holy Light demands. They aid someone in need, then return to tell her how they served. Paladins begin their trials by learning humility, duty, and charity. Tiza Battleforge does not ask for feats of arms. A servant of the Holy Light must understand the troubles ordinary people face and offer help without seeking praise or gain. After helping someone in Ironforge, an aspiring paladin returns to Tiza Battleforge. The initiate tells her how they spent their time away and whose burdens they helped bear. When she is satisfied that they acted with charity and duty, Tiza commends them. Such selfless service is what it means to follow the Light.

quest:1779.text: The Tome of Divinity. In Ironforge, The Tome of Divinity tests paladin initiates in holy power and martial devotion. Entrusted with the Symbol of Life, an initiate is sent to aid Muiredon Battleforge, wounded after a deadly encounter with Dark Iron dwarves. In Ironforge, paladin initiates face a trial of martial skill and holy power. They have already shown humility, patience, and charity. Now they are entrusted with the Symbol of Life and sent into the city to help those suffering from conflicts beyond its gates. Muiredon Battleforge lies badly wounded after a clash with Dark Iron dwarves. A priest tends his immediate injuries as he prepares to tell what became of his expedition and his companion Narm. The initiate must answer that need with the Light’s gift of renewal.

quest:178.text: Theocritus' Retrieval. In Redridge, an adventurer finds a gnoll pendant and hears a voice through it. The voice belongs to Theocritus, High Mage of Tower of Azora, who has intercepted the gnolls' mystical network and urgently asks for the pendant to study. Across the Redridge Mountains, travelers fighting the savage Shadowhide gnolls sometimes find a Shadowhide Pendant. Touching the enchanted trinket brings a calm, distant voice instead of barking or curses. The speaker is Theocritus, a human mage at Tower of Azora, across the border in Elwynn Forest. His message comes from long research into breaking the dark sorceries that direct the gnoll packs.

quest:1780.text: The Tome of Divinity. In Stormwind's Cathedral of Light, Duthorian Rall guides paladins through a trial of devotion to the Holy Light. They prove their worth through charity, selflessness, and a duty to protect those in need. Paladins in the service of the Holy Light face a defining trial in Stormwind City. At the Cathedral of Light, Duthorian Rall sends initiates to prove their devotion through moral conduct and selfless deeds for the kingdom's citizens. Martial glory alone will not suffice. After aiding the vulnerable, initiates return to Duthorian Rall. They have brought needed relief to children and earned their heartfelt gratitude. Their mentor sees the value in putting others first. He teaches that charity, compassion, and duty to the people of Azeroth mark the path of the Light.

quest:1781.text: The Tome of Divinity. At Stormwind's Cathedral of Light, a trial awaits paladin initiates: they must focus the holy Symbol of Life. Those who prove their virtue are sent to aid Gazin Tenorm, who barely escaped a Defias ambush near Heroes' Vigil in Elwynn Forest. In Stormwind's Cathedral of Light, patient and charitable paladin initiates receive the Symbol of Life. Duthorian Rall entrusts them with this holy vessel to test their devotion to the Light. Only a worthy champion can focus one of the Light's greatest gifts, the power to restore life to the fallen. Gazin Tenorm shows why the Symbol is needed. He crawled back to Stormwind after Defias bandits attacked him near Heroes' Vigil in Elwynn Forest. Priests tend his severe wounds at the cathedral altar. His companion Henze remains in danger where the outlaws struck.

quest:1782.text: Furen's Armor. In Stormwind, Furen Longbeard puts new armor to the test. An aspiring warrior gathers spider fangs, chimaera horns, and phlogiston for his trials. Furen then gives the fire-hardened mail to the warrior and promises to share what he learned with Alliance smiths. Furen Longbeard, a dwarven armorer in Stormwind, seeks stronger armor for the Alliance. He tests how well it withstands heat and crushing blows. For these trials, he asks an aspiring warrior to gather rare materials. The resulting mail succeeds, strengthening Furen's standing among Alliance armorers. Furen gives the finished fire-hardened mail to the warrior who gathered the materials. He is grateful for the help, and the experiments have deepened his knowledge of protective smithing. Now he plans to send his notes and findings to other Alliance smiths, so they can use the new methods.

quest:1783.text: The Tome of Divinity. A paladin initiate carries the Symbol of Life to the frigid shores south of Helm's Bed Lake in Dun Morogh. There, the initiate must find Narm Faulk, a brave scout who fell holding off Dark Iron dwarves, and call him back with the Light. South of Helm's Bed Lake, dwarven scouts Muiredon and Narm Faulk watched Dark Iron dwarves entrench themselves. When they saw an enemy commander issuing orders, they struck at several foes and tried to secure a script. The Dark Irons overwhelmed them with unexpected ferocity. Muiredon fled for reinforcements while Narm held the line.

quest:1784.text: The Tome of Divinity. In Dun Morogh, injured scouts need help exposing Dark Iron spies near Helm's Bed Lake. Their orders may persuade Ironforge's skeptical council to heed the danger. Young dwarven paladins answer the call to defend Dun Morogh when an expedition near Helm's Bed Lake goes wrong. Narm Faulk and Muiredon Battleforge set out to ambush Dark Iron scouts. Narm fell wounded, while Muiredon returned to Ironforge to recover. Rumors of Dark Iron infiltrators have reached Ironforge, yet some council members refuse to believe they have entered Dun Morogh. Near Helm's Bed, the paladin can track down the spies and recover a Dark Iron Script from their captain. The orders offer proof of enemy movements and plots near the capital's gates.

quest:1785.text: The Tome of Divinity. In Ironforge, holy champions face a final trial before Tiza Battleforge. The Tome of Divinity shows whether they are ready to wield the Symbol of Life and call fallen allies back to life. You have crossed the kingdom's trials, and now you come to Tiza Battleforge in Ironforge. She is a revered teacher of the holy arts. Her husband watches with pride as you approach, eager to see the dwarven people acknowledge your readiness before the Holy Light. Tiza Battleforge's final blessing tests whether your heart is ready to wield the Symbol of Life. The relic answers only to one prepared to channel the Light's greatest gifts. Prove your worth, and Tiza grants you a sacred scroll that lets you call fallen comrades back from death. Ironforge needs this power against the Scourge and the Dark Iron clan.

quest:1786.text:
The Tome of Divinity. In Elwynn, faith and sacrifice are tested when a Defias ambush leaves Henze Faulk dead at Heroes' Vigil. With the Symbol of Life, you are sent to restore him and hinder the brotherhood's schemes. Henze Faulk and Gazin traveled to Heroes' Vigil after hearing that Defias Brotherhood agents had crossed into northeastern Elwynn Forest. The island lies in the middle of Stone Cairn Lake. The scouts sought proof to present to the king's royal advisors, so they tried to ambush two conspirators reviewing plans.

Defias spellcasters soon joined the fight, and the scouts were overwhelmed. Henze stood his ground against the mages, sacrificing himself to give Gazin time to escape with his life.

quest:1787.text: The Tome of Divinity. You are proving your devotion to the Light through a trial for Alliance paladins. After helping an injured scout in Elwynn Forest, you face Defias Rogue Wizards and seek papers that threaten the realm. As a paladin in training, you are being tested in Elwynn Forest. Henze was injured while watching illicit activity on an island. Help him learn how far the Defias have spread there.

quest:1788.text: The Tome of Divinity. In Stormwind, paladins face a trial of faith in The Tome of Divinity. An initiate proves mastery of the Symbol of Life by restoring a fallen ally, then earns Duthorian Rall's blessing to wield resurrection. After restoring the fallen Henze with the Symbol of Life in the field, an aspiring paladin returns to the Cathedral of Light in Stormwind. The Defias papers recovered from the island are to go to the King's advisors through Gazin Tenorm. First, Duthorian Rall awaits word of the initiate's success. Calling on the Light to restore the dead is no small gift. Duthorian Rall sees mastery of the Symbol of Life as proof that an initiate has the faith and spiritual strength for one of the paladin order's highest callings: resurrection. With this rite mastered, the paladin can safeguard allies on battlefields across the kingdom.

quest:1791.text: The Windwatcher. Warriors who have mastered the berserker stance are sent north to find The Windwatcher. After the Affray on Fray Island, Klannoc Macleod points them toward a weapon worthy of their fury. You have survived the Affray on Fray Island and learned the berserker stance from Klannoc Macleod. Now Klannoc sends you far from the Barrens coast, across continents, to find a solitary craftsman who can forge an exceptional weapon. Bath'rah the Windwatcher lives beside the river that runs north past Tarren Mill. His camp rests among stone ruins in the contested land between the Alterac Mountains and the blighted Western Plaguelands. The troll hermit crafts weapons and commands potent elemental shamanism. He waits for warriors determined to forge a weapon of great power.

quest:1792.text: Whirlwind Weapon. A warrior's chosen weapon awaits the storm Cyclonian left behind. The whirlwind heart can bind the elemental's fury into a forged vessel. After Cyclonian falls and the warrior claims its heart, a craftsperson prepares a weapon to hold the storm's power. The heart is fused into the chosen arm, turning forged metal into a channel for elemental fury. Cyclonian's heart holds the violence of howling winds and tempestuous gales. Bound into a forged weapon, it lends the wielder the living might of the storm alongside their own martial skill. Each strike carries the force of the defeated elemental, whose storm now rages in the hands of its vanquisher.

quest:1793.text: The Tome of Valor. In Stormwind and Ironforge, young Alliance paladins face a trial of courage and duty. Their mentors ask them to prove they can fight with skill and protect the innocent. Young paladins in Stormwind and Ironforge must face terrible danger without faltering. Their instructors test their resolve in the Cathedral of Light and the Hall of Mysteries. Dragons and demons may threaten those who cannot defend themselves. The paladins must stay beside them. A holy warrior needs bravery as much as a weapon and shield. The trial teaches paladins that strength means little without a firm vow to shelter the helpless. When danger threatens the Alliance, its defenders must hold their ground and protect those in their care.

quest:1795.text: The Binding. Above Ratchet, warlocks face the rite that binds a felhunter to their will. Strahad Farsan oversees the summoning with the restored Tome of the Cabal, drawing an aggressive demon from the Nether to be subdued in combat. On Kalimdor's bluffs above Ratchet, the goblin port, Strahad Farsan conducts dangerous trials in demon summoning. After a warlock gathers the fragments and reagents needed to restore the ancient Tome of the Cabal, Strahad prepares the binding grounds. He lays an inner glyph of containment while his acolytes channel power through enchanted rods to complete the outer circle. The circles keep whatever emerges isolated from the settlement below. The Tome of the Cabal holds the incantations that open a bridge into the Twisting Nether. Felhunters are ravenous demonic hounds that hunger for arcane power and feast on magical energy. No gentle enthrallment or persuasion will bind one. The warlock must violently subdue and break the summoned beast in combat before it recognizes its rightful master. Surviving the clash proves the summoner can wield the hound against enemy spellcasters.

quest:1796.text: Components for the Enchanted Gold Bloodrobe. In Ratchet, Menara Voidrender asks warlocks to find Robes of Arcana for a garment meant to bear powerful enchantments. Menara Voidrender asks warlocks seeking greater power to bring her a set of Robes of Arcana. She wants a garment strong enough to hold dark magic. The strength of a magical relic depends on the skill, rarity, and effort put into its materials. Ordinary rags would fail under deep enchantments, so the robe must be finely made and ready to receive them. Menara admires warlocks who can weave the robe themselves, but ambition matters more to her than pride. You can sew the silk, commission a skilled artisan, or buy the robe at market. However you obtain it, the finished garment is ready to become a specialized tool of fel mastery.

quest:1798.text: Seeking Strahad. Warlocks leave Stormwind City for Ratchet, where Strahad Farsan can teach them to summon felhunters. Beneath the goblin port, his knowledge offers a path into more dangerous demon summoning. Gakin the Darkbinder sends you from Stormwind to seek help with summoning a felhunter. He guides warlocks in the Slaughtered Lamb, below the Mage Quarter, but the rites call for knowledge beyond what he can offer there. Your journey carries you across the Great Sea to Kalimdor, where another warlock may know the way. Strahad Farsan lives in the arid hills above Ratchet, the goblin harbor. He is a human warlock and a peer of Gakin's in their secret cabal. From neutral territory, Strahad can work beyond the notice of Alliance magistrates, church inquisitors, and Horde sentries. Warlocks come to him hoping to master demons that drain mana.

quest:180.text: Wanted: Lieutenant Fangore. A bounty in Lakeshire calls for Lieutenant Fangore's death. Magistrate Solomon seeks hunters to stop the Shadowhide gnolls pressing into the Redridge Mountains. Fangore serves the renegade sorcerer Morganth, and his death would strike at Morganth's forces. Lakeshire faces growing danger. Stormwind's army is stretched thin, and King Varian Wrynn is mysteriously absent. Highlord Bolvar Fordragon has left frontier settlements like Redridge to defend themselves. The Shadowhide clan raids trade routes, burns farmsteads, and presses against the town's perimeter. Magistrate Solomon posts bounties to draw mercenary blades where royal soldiers will not march. Lieutenant Fangore leads the Shadowhide gnolls as Morganth's enforcer. Morganth is a rogue dark wizard hiding in the Redridge hills. Under Fangore, the gnolls coordinate their attacks instead of fighting as scattered scavengers. Their strikes threaten to sever Lakeshire from Elwynn Forest. Fangore's severed paw would give Magistrate Solomon proof that Morganth's brute vanguard has been broken.

quest:1801.text: Tome of the Cabal. In the Barrens, Strahad Farsan sends Horde warlocks east in search of a lost grimoire. The Tome of the Cabal holds rites for summoning and binding a felhunter, and the search begins with cartographer Jorah Annison in the Undercity. Strahad Farsan says a felhunter takes more than ordinary fel magic to summon. These predators feed on magical energies and resist standard summoning circles. An initiate needs specialized circles and an ancient grimoire called the Tome of the Cabal. The first order of warlocks to bind a felhunter without outside aid wrote the book.
