Its rites and seals show how to enslave such a dangerous demon. Copies of the Tome of the Cabal have long been lost to warlocks in Kalimdor, so Strahad sends his student across the sea to Jorah Annison in the Undercity. Annison works as a royal cartographer, mapping Lordaeron, but knows a great deal about ancient and obscure texts. He admits that he despises mapmaking and hungers for rare histories, occult narratives, and treatises on dark magic.

quest:1802.text: Tome of the Cabal. From Ironforge, your search for the Tome of the Cabal leads to a lost manuscript and a sunken ship. Its scattered pages hold rites for binding a felhunter. Only one copy of the Tome of the Cabal was ever written. Violence tore it apart and defaced its pages, sending the remnants to distant corners of the world. A tattered manuscript crossed the sea to Kalimdor, where centaur clans took it. The other half sailed from Lordaeron toward Khaz Modan, but the vessel sank before reaching port. Two dangers guard the missing pages. Those lost at sea washed ashore on the Hillsbrad coast, west of Southshore. Shoreline murlocs near Azurelode Mine took the waterlogged relics and wreckage. The dry half rests in an ancient chest deep in the centaur caverns of Splithoof Hold in Thousand Needles. Once the pieces are together, Krom Stoutarm can inspect the lost text before it returns to Strahad Farsan.

quest:1803.text: Tome of the Cabal. Horde warlocks seek the Tome of the Cabal's severed halves for Jorah Annison in the Undercity. Once kept in Lordaeron, the grimoire was torn apart and scattered across the world. Its damp, tattered remnants lie along hostile Eastern Kingdoms waters and deep in Kalimdor's centaur territory. The Tome of the Cabal once rested in the library of Lordaeron. Someone deliberately defaced the sinister grimoire, stripping away nearly half its pages and splitting it in two. The surviving formal text was bound for the dwarven halls of Ironforge, but the transport wrecked along the rocky coast west of Southshore. Its pages now rot in the shallows beneath the watch of scavenging murlocs.

quest:1804.text: Tome of the Cabal. In the Barrens, Strahad Farsan waits for a warlock to bring him the Tome of the Cabal and channeling rods. Together, they prepare the way to bind a felhunter. In Ironforge's Hall of Explorers, Krom Stoutarm binds the Tome of the Cabal's tattered, mouldering remnants back together. The dwarf scholar reluctantly parts with this rare work of dark scholarship, but first secures a promise of a copy. He also passes along a fresh missive from Strahad Farsan. The tome holds the rites for breaching the Nether, though parchment alone cannot conduct the ritual. Strahad's acolytes need focus implements to steady the energies summoned to bind a felhunter. Krom sends the warlock to the Wetlands, where Dragonmaw spellcasters carry rods of channeling. Taking the rods from the hostile orcs gives Strahad's circle the conduit it needs to control the rift and stabilize the summoned energies.

quest:1805.text: Tome of the Cabal. A warlock's work with the Tome of the Cabal now leads into hostile territory. After helping Jorah Annison restore the tome, you must claim three Rods of Channeling and bring them to Strahad Farsan in Ratchet. In the Undercity, Jorah Annison studies the recovered fragments of the Tome of the Cabal. The Forsaken scholar pieces together its eldritch passages and welcomes the rare knowledge they offer. Then Jorah delivers an urgent directive from Strahad Farsan. Knowledge alone cannot bind a felhunter. A warlock needs precise instruments to focus demonic power into a binding circle. Strahad needs three Rods of Channeling, carried by renegade orcs of the Dragonmaw clan. They dwell among the ruins of Angerfang Encampment in the Wetlands, far from Horde lands. You must enter contested territory and face clan remnants who hate the modern Horde as much as they butcher Alliance explorers.

quest:1806.text: The Test of Righteousness. At Jordan Stilwell’s forge outside Ironforge, you bring the materials for a paladin’s warhammer. Gathered across the Eastern Kingdoms and Kalimdor, they help turn an apprentice into a recognized champion of the Light. Jordan Stilwell works at his forge outside Ironforge’s gates. He envies paladins who wander the land, yet takes pride in serving their cause. You bring him rare materials gathered from shadowy crypts, sunken ruins, and dangerous mines. With them, the master smith keeps his promise and forges a weapon worthy of a true defender. Jordan Stilwell names the finished warhammer Verigan's Fist, for Bosch Verigan, an honored dwarven paladin and his dear friend. On behalf of himself and his wife, he places the sacred weapon in a young champion's hands. Through it, his fallen friend's memory and valor endure against the darkness threatening Azeroth.

quest:181.text: Look To The Stars. Viktori Prism'Antras needs one final piece for his telescope in Darkshire. Its frame is built, but no local glass is large enough for the lens his plans require. Viktori Prism'Antras is building a telescope in Darkshire from plans by the gnome engineer Cog Glitzspinner. He has gathered brass tubes and sturdy mountings from local supplies, but the design calls for an unusually large focusing lens. Magnifying glasses and optical parts from Stormwind traders are too small, so Viktori looks beyond ordinary materials for the piece he needs.

quest:1824.text: Trial at the Field of Giants. At Camp Taurajo, Ruga Ragetotem sends warrior aspirants south to face an unfamiliar foe. They must slay silithid in the Field of Giants and return with several twitching antennae within half an hour. At Camp Taurajo, Ruga Ragetotem challenges growing warriors to prove themselves against an unfamiliar adversary. The Horde's warrior trainers test more than combat skill: aspirants must slay the creatures and bring back fresh antennae within half an hour. The run across the southern Barrens tests their speed and resolve, while the antennae must still twitch when they reach Taurajo. Silithid hives rise in the Field of Giants, beneath massive fossilized ribcages. The bizarre, crawling insects are recent arrivals in the Barrens, disturbing tauren hunters and shamans who watch the savannas. Ruga says their presence bodes ill for Kalimdor. The trial tests a young warrior's instincts in combat and gathers intelligence on a growing threat to the land.

quest:1825.text: Speak with Thun'grim. After the Trial at the Field of Giants, Thun'grim Firegaze calls warriors to his camp in the Barrens. The orc smith offers custom armor to those who have proved their valor, and sends them to gather materials for Brutal Armor. Word of the warriors’ trial reaches Thun'grim Firegaze after they prove their endurance and fighting skill to Ruga Ragetotem. His camp stands on a ridge east of the Crossroads. Thun'grim wants to forge them an exceptional suit of battle mail. Thun'grim Firegaze reserves his forge for warriors who meet his high standard. He expects steel to match the spirit of the one who bears it. Reaching his camp means a warrior has moved beyond basic militia drills and can take on the hard work of gathering rare materials across Kalimdor.

quest:1838.text: Brutal Armor. A warrior in the northern Barrens faces Thun'grim Firegaze's test. The near-blind smith sends seasoned Horde warriors across distant lands for rare ingredients and smelting agents. Fulfilling his scroll begins the forging of a full set of brutal battle gear. In the northern Barrens, Thun'grim Firegaze listens for news of war. The veteran orc smith's eyesight is failing, but his skill at the forge remains unmatched. Rumors reach him of a warrior whose strength and valor exceed those of ordinary soldiers. Thun'grim sets out to craft mail that can withstand the fiercest battles across Kalimdor and the Eastern Kingdoms. Thun'grim's armor calls for more than common ore. By firelight, his failing eyes guide him as he writes a precise scroll for the core chestpiece. Its ingredients include refined iron, smoky iron ingots carried by burrowing kobolds, powdered azurite worked by miners across the sea, and a volatile vial of phlogiston. Only a warrior ready to face trials across distant lands can bring the required materials together.

quest:1839.text: Ula'elek and the Brutal Gauntlets. Thun'grim Firegaze sends you from the Barrens to Sen'jin Village for the Brutal Gauntlets. There, Darkspear craftsman Ula'elek will forge them. Thun'grim Firegaze sends you east after you prove your valor in the Barrens and begin assembling the Brutal Armor set. The veteran orc smith relies on skilled artisans across Horde lands instead of forging every piece at his mountain perch. For the heavy mail gauntlets, he directs you to Durotar's rocky southern shores. In Sen'jin Village, troll armorsmith Ula'elek works among his Darkspear kin. Thun'grim has already told him of your deeds, and Ula'elek says the spirits have watched your triumphs in battle. For a warrior earning a place among the Horde's elite, fine craft and spiritual acknowledgement go hand in hand.

quest:1840.text: Orm Stonehoof and the Brutal Helm. In Thunder Bluff, Orm Stonehoof has the skill to forge the Brutal Helm. Thun'grim Firegaze sends warriors to him for that work. Warriors who prove their mettle and assemble pieces of the Brutal Armor in the Barrens are sent up to Thunder Bluff. Thun'grim Firegaze is an accomplished armorsmith, but he knows the work has reached beyond his own skill. He refers the warriors to Orm Stonehoof, whose craft is renowned across Kalimdor. Orm can shape resilient battlefield helms from rare, savage trophies. Orm Stonehoof lives and works on the high bluffs of Mulgore, near the tranquil pool beneath Thunder Bluff's towering central totem. When a warrior arrives with Thun'grim Firegaze's word, Orm leaves his routine work to discuss the demanding components needed for a helm worthy of the Horde's front lines.

quest:1841.text: Velora Nitely and the Brutal Legguards. Thun'grim Firegaze sends Horde warriors across the Great Sea for Velora Nitely's Brutal Legguards. In the Undercity, the Forsaken smith draws on the craft she kept from her mortal life to forge the armor. Her work helps assemble a durable suit for the Horde's warriors. Thun'grim Firegaze sends you east across the Great Sea to find a smith for the Brutal Legguards. You've proved your mettle to the veteran smith at his vigil in the Barrens, and now he points you toward the fabled Brutal Armor. Thun'grim cannot make the whole suit alone, so he relies on skilled allies across the Horde. The greaves call for an artisan whose work was revered before northern humanity fell, in the Forsaken's underground kingdom. Velora Nitely works in the Undercity's Trade Quarter, where her old craft still serves the Horde. Before the Scourging of the north ended her mortal life, she was one of the Kingdom of Lordaeron's foremost armorsmiths. Her homeland was corrupted, and she became one of the Forsaken, but death did not take her mastery of metal. She now turns her human skill toward the Horde's warriors, with a dry, macabre wit about being undead.

quest:1842.text: Satyr Hooves. In Sen'jin Village, Ula'elek sends warriors north for Satyr Hooves. He needs their strange power to forge brutal gauntlets. Ula'elek sends you into Ashenvale's ancient woods to gather what his craft requires. Demonic corruption still clings to the satyr covens there, and he seeks more than iron and leather for armor meant to rival Kalimdor's fiercest forces. In northeastern Ashenvale, satyrs feed on the forest's lingering purity and twist it into foul power. Those that take in the most develop swollen hooves without the usual cloven split. Ula'elek plans to draw out that concentrated magic and weave it into the gauntlets he makes.

quest:1843.text: Brutal Gauntlets. Ula'elek has finished a pair of Brutal Gauntlets for a seasoned Horde warrior. Rare materials gathered across distant lands have gone into the work, meant to honor both maker and bearer. Ula'elek brings his lineage and skill to the forging of armor for a seasoned frontline warrior. In Durotar, the Horde craftsman shapes brutal gauntlets from hardened trophies taken from dangerous foes. The finished armor is made to withstand fierce blows and strengthen the wearer's attacks. For orcs and trolls, fine arms and armor carry the forge's prestige and the maker's spirit into battle. When Ula'elek presents the finished gauntlets, he entrusts a warrior with his ancestors' legacy. A champion who wears them is expected to meet that craft with courage, martial discipline, and strength.

quest:1844.text: Chimaeric Horn. Orm Stonehoof sends a Horde warrior into the Charred Vale to face a suffering chimaera matriarch. Her horn is needed for the Brutal Helm, and the hunt tests the warrior’s strength and mercy. Orm Stonehoof will forge the Brutal Helm for Horde warriors, but tradition calls for proof before he begins. He asks for more than metal or coin: the warrior must show martial skill and face the scars left by devastating conflict. In the southwestern Stonetalon Mountains, the Charred Vale lies in ash. Once lush and green, the valley was burned into a smoking wasteland. Beasts still wander its soot-covered craters, twisted by pain and fury. Mighty chimaeras nest among dead trees and searing steam vents. For the tauren smith, the chimaera matriarch’s horn is both a needed piece for the helm and proof of strength. The hunt also ends the matriarch’s torment. By felling her, the warrior brings mercy to a wild spirit driven mad by the destruction of its home.

quest:1845.text: Brutal Helm. In Thunder Bluff, Orm Stonehoof brings the warrior’s trial to its end with Brutal Helm. After gathering rare beast trophies across Kalimdor, an aspiring warrior earns recognition with a horned helm that honors their strength. Orm Stonehoof is a stern smith in Thunder Bluff who guides Horde warriors through hard rites of passage. The trials test their skill in battle. Initiates hunt dangerous creatures in treacherous lands and claim rare trophies. Only those who meet Orm’s high standards may come before him to complete their armor. The warrior proves their resolve in the wild by bringing Orm Stonehoof a rare chimaeric horn. In return, Orm presents Brutal Helm, heavy mail crafted to honor the beast and strengthen its wearer in the front line. As he gives the helm, Orm calls on the Earthmother’s blessing. He looks to the greater deeds the warrior is bound to undertake across Azeroth.

quest:1846.text: Dragonmaw Shinbones. In the Undercity, Velora Nitely sends Horde warriors to gather Dragonmaw Shinbones for Brutal Legguards. The hunt leads to the southern Wetlands, where the hostile orcs carry bones thick enough to brace the armor. Velora Nitely, a Forsaken armorer in the Undercity, needs a strong brace for Brutal Legguards. She sends Horde warriors to the Wetlands for thick, resilient bone from the Dragonmaw orcs. Their dense frames can bear the heavy blows a seasoned warrior faces. Velora needs more than any bone taken from the Dragonmaw. Each one must withstand a hand test; a bone that snaps is too brittle for the forge. Warriors scour the renegade camps along the Wetlands' crags, breaking weak specimens until eight sturdy shinbones remain.

quest:1848.text: Brutal Hauberk. Across the Barrens, Horde warriors face a trial before Thun'grim Firegaze will forge their mail. They gather rare materials and prove themselves against dangerous foes across the lands, then bring their bounty to the reclusive smith. He hammers it into armor built for battle. In the northern Barrens, Thun'grim Firegaze forges armor only for warriors who meet his demands. The reclusive orc sends them far and wide to gather tough beast parts, rare metal, and alchemical reagents before he lights his bellows. The finished hauberk offers protection and marks the endurance and grit its wearer has shown, earning recognition from veteran fighters throughout the Horde. Thun'grim makes his demands punishing by design. Horde arms and armor are expected to carry the sweat and blood of their wearer from the moment they are made. When you hand over the finished Brutal Hauberk, the smith offers no praise. He expects you to prove the armor in brutal combat and return with stories of blood and honor.

quest:185.text: Tiger Mastery. At the northern safari camp in Stranglethorn Vale, the hunter Ajeck Rouack offers to train adventurers in the discipline of big cat stalking. She starts newcomers against the younger tigers prowling near the camp to test basic hunting and tracking prowess. Having learned the art of hunting tigers from her father when she was a girl, Ajeck Rouack shares his craft with travelers who reach Nesingwary's Expedition following Welcome to the Jungle. She insists that tracking and slaying the youngest felines is the essential foundation before any hunter can advance to greater quarry. Young Stranglethorn tigers are often found in the jungle close to the expedition camp. Rouack demands that ten of these beasts be hunted down to prove sufficient skill before she agrees to provide any further training.

quest:186.text: Tiger Mastery. At Nesingwary's Expedition in northern Stranglethorn Vale, Ajeck Rouack escalates her hunting trials. Having seen your early promise with young stalkers, he now sends you into the jungle to fell mature Stranglethorn Tigers. Following your initial success against younger predators, Ajeck Rouack seeks to test your growing skills against more seasoned beasts. She directs you back out into the wilds of Stranglethorn Vale to hunt down ten mature Stranglethorn Tigers before you can pursue even greater challenges.

quest:187.text: Tiger Mastery. Deep in the jungle at Nesingwary's Expedition, Ajeck Rouack raises the stakes of his hunting trials. He demands the death of ten elder Stranglethorn tigers to prove your prowess before the final test. Following the earlier hunts, Ajeck Rouack asks you to pursue ten elder Stranglethorn tigers across the wilds. He considers these beasts both the most elusive to track and the fiercest to overcome. Felling ten of them serves as the prelude to a concluding trial, after which he promises to proclaim you a master tiger hunter before Master Nesingwary.

quest:188.text: Tiger Mastery. Ajeck Rouack offers the ultimate challenge in his series of hunts within northern Stranglethorn Vale. After weeks of tracking an elusive beast, he challenges you to seek out the tiger Sin'Dall and bring back her paw. Having completed the earlier trials against Stranglethorn's tigers, you are offered one last challenge by Ajeck Rouack at Nesingwary's Expedition. The hunting camp has tracked an extraordinarily elusive tiger known as Sin'Dall across the jungle for weeks. Ajeck challenges you to track her down, fell the beast, and claim her paw as indisputable proof.

quest:1884.text: Ju-Ju Heaps. On the Echo Isles, Un'thuwa asks you to destroy Zalazane's ju-ju heaps. Their corruption threatens Durotar's flow of magic. From Sen'jin Village, Un'thuwa asks you to destroy the heaps Zalazane placed among his huts on the main Echo Isle. The tainted fetishes corrupt wildlife and strengthen warlocks and infernal creatures. Left alone, they may change Durotar's flow of magic forever.

quest:189.text: Bloodscalp Ears. Kebok in Booty Bay is losing guards and agents to jungle clashes with the Bloodscalp tribe. Worried about climbing expenses and answering to Baron Revilgaz, he offers coin to any adventurer willing to hunt down the trolls and return with proof of the kill. In the bustling port of Booty Bay, Kebok faces a serious operational dilemma. The local trolls in Stranglethorn Vale have been killing his agents in the jungle, and he has lost many of his best guards in skirmishes with them. With the casualties mounting, so too are the costs, leaving him frantic over how to explain them to Baron Revilgaz. Rather than allowing the losses to accumulate further, Kebok turns to outside help. He offers monetary compensation to travelers who head into the jungle, cull the Bloodscalp trolls, and bring back fifteen of their severed ears as undeniable confirmation of their demise.

quest:19.text: Tharil'zun. Near Stonewatch Keep, Marshal Marris puts a bounty on Tharil'zun, whose outrunners harass the roads. His death is a critical step in breaking the Blackrock clan's hold over northern Redridge, and his severed head brought to Lakeshire marks a hard-fought victory for its watch. The pass between Lakeshire and Stonewatch Keep has become a gauntlet of sudden ambushes. Blackrock outrunners and renegades prowl the rocky ridges, cutting off scouts and threatening reinforcements trying to reach the fortress. Marshal Marris names Tharil'zun as the commander behind these coordinated strikes. He says Tharil'zun must be eliminated, or Lakeshire may be hemmed in entirely. Tharil'zun is a dangerous battlefield leader: vicious, crafty, and able to unite scattered orc raiders into an effective raiding force. To take his head in Stonewatch's shadow, you must cut through entrenched Blackrock outposts. His death breaks the outrunner patrols' cohesion and clears a path for the Alliance to face the garrison inside the keep.

quest:190.text: Panther Mastery. Sir S. J. Erlgadin of Nesingwary's Expedition offers a trial to those seeking to prove their prowess as big-game stalkers in Stranglethorn Vale. To join Hemet's hunting company, adventurers must first demonstrate their basic tracking ability by taking down ten young panthers. Within the wild expanse of northern Stranglethorn Vale, Hemet Nesingwary has assembled a seasoned band of big-game huntsmen. Sir S. J. Erlgadin tells anyone who wants a part of the hunt that they must first prove themselves an able panther hunter. Before Erlgadin entrusts anyone with greater game, he issues an entry test: finding and slaying ten young panthers. Simply finding the beasts is only half the challenge.

quest:191.text: Panther Mastery. Sir S. J. Erlgadin demands that you prove yourself worthy of the big game hunters at Nesingwary's Expedition. Following your initial cull of younger beasts, he challenges you to track down and slay ten fully grown panthers in the wilds of Stranglethorn Vale. After dispatching the young panthers around the jungle, Sir S. J. Erlgadin asks you to raise your sights. To show that you deserve to keep company with seasoned big game hunters, you are sent out to hunt ten mature panthers, which are far tougher and more dangerous than their younger kin.

quest:192.text: Panther Mastery. Sir S. J. Erlgadin of Nesingwary's Expedition challenges big game hunters to track and bring down the deadliest panthers in Stranglethorn Vale. Following your earlier trials, you must now seek out and slay ten Shadowmaw Panthers. Sir S. J. Erlgadin considers Shadowmaw Panthers to be the most dangerous cats prowling the jungles of Stranglethorn. Proving your mettle as a true stalker requires crawling through the dense underbrush to track down ten of these elusive beasts, whose ferocity makes them far harder to kill than to find.

quest:1938.text: Ur's Treatise on Shadow Magic. High Sorcerer Andromath seeks Ur's Treatise on Shadow Magic in Stormwind. Morganth stole the forbidden tome and carried it to the Tower of Ilgalar in the Redridge Mountains. Three promising mages studied together in Stormwind's Wizard's Sanctum. Morganth turned to dark arts and shadow magic despite their desperate warnings. The city's magical order banished him. Before he left, he stole a dangerous work by Ur, an infamous archmage whose studies reached beyond orthodox arcana. Morganth seized the Tower of Ilgalar in the heights of the Redridge Mountains, beyond Stormwind's scrutiny. High Sorcerer Andromath fears the tome's knowledge in the hands of an outcast practicing forbidden sorcery. So he sends Alliance adventurers into the tower to recover it before its wards fall.

quest:1939.text: High Sorcerer Andromath. At Stormwind’s Wizard’s Sanctum, promising Alliance mages are summoned to the tower’s summit. Andromath works among the kingdom’s foremost archmages beyond ruined Dalaran. Jennea Cannon, the apprentice coordinator in Stormwind’s Mage Quarter, sends promising casters to the summit of the Wizard’s Sanctum. High Sorcerer Andromath, one of the southern kingdoms’ most senior active practitioners of the arcane, has asked to meet magi ready for greater responsibilities. Dalaran’s magocracy was ruined in the Third War, and its surviving wizards are busy rebuilding. Without easy access to the Violet Citadel’s libraries, the Alliance relies on senior archmages in Stormwind to study ancient threats and guide research into shadowy, forbidden arts.

quest:194.text: Raptor Mastery. At his expedition camp in northern Stranglethorn Vale, Hemet Nesingwary challenges travelers to prove their prowess in the wilderness. The famed hunter demands ten Stranglethorn Raptors slain to test whether you possess genuine hunting talent. Following your arrival in the jungle after Welcome to the Jungle, Hemet Nesingwary offers to test your tracking and hunting capabilities. Rather than handing out maps or directions, he insists that finding the Stranglethorn Raptors yourself is half the test, challenging you to venture out into the brush and bring down ten of the fierce beasts.

quest:1940.text: Pristine Spider Silk. In Stormwind, High Sorcerer Andromath sends rising Alliance mages to Duskwood for pristine spider silk. They carry eight samples to Wynne Larson in the Mage Quarter, where she weaves an adept’s robe. High Sorcerer Andromath marks a mage’s passage beyond apprenticeship with vestments fit for an adept. In the Wizard’s Sanctum, a mage’s skill is seen in the robes they wear. So each mage must gather pristine silk from dangerous spiders and show both field skill and discernment. Carrion recluse spiders haunt Duskwood’s gloomy woods, and ordinary stalls do not sell their silk. You gather eight fine samples and carry them across Stormwind to Larson Clothiers in the Mage Quarter. There, Wynne Larson weaves the delicate threads into a robe with arcane significance.

quest:1942.text: Astral Knot Garment. In Stormwind City, Wynne Larson weaves pristine spider silk into a garment for dangerous journeys and high-society gatherings. An adventurer brings her rare silk from the wilds, and she shapes it into a magical weave. In Stormwind's Mage Quarter, tailors serve arcane elites and visiting nobles. Wynne Larson weaves pristine spider silk into garments both durable and enchanted. Her playful humor shows when she jokes about saving a few precious scraps for her own wardrobe before handing over her finished work. Spellcasters who wear cloth prize the Astral Knot Garment for its resilience and refinement. Its silk comes from dangerous spiders, and its weave is made to endure combat. It keeps the polished look expected at formal banquets in Stormwind Keep.

quest:1943.text: Speak with Deino. In Orgrimmar, Deino calls promising Horde mages to aid their craft. The troll mage works from the Valley of Spirits and seeks an adept for important work. Her summons opens a path to deeper study and duties across Kalimdor. Horde mages hone their arcane abilities under the guidance of instructors. When a student is ready for harder work, mentors such as Anastasia Hartwell in the Undercity point the way to Orgrimmar. In its troll quarter, specialized knowledge and dangerous work await. Deino lives in Darkbriar Lodge in Orgrimmar's Valley of Spirits. Among the Darkspear, few study arcane magic compared with the many witch doctors and priests, which makes Deino an authority in the capital. Her work serves Horde mages beyond local concerns, and she seeks ambitious spellcasters willing to face dangers far from home.

quest:1944.text: Waters of Xavian. Deino seeks a sample from the waters of Xavian, deep in Ashenvale. The troll mage hopes to study the ancient city's lingering arcane power, and sends her apprentice to draw water from its highest waterfall. Deino, a troll mage in Orgrimmar's Valley of Spirits, searches Kalimdor for traces of primal arcane energy. Her attention turns to Xavian, an ancient night elf city hidden beneath Ashenvale's eastern canopy. Scholars say the city held great magical knowledge before the Sundering. Its waters are believed to retain arcane power that modern mages hope to understand. Xavian lies in ruins, overrun by feral, corrupt satyrs who defend their ground from outsiders. To reach the water, you travel past Satyrnaar and through dangerous waterways, avoiding prowling beasts and demonic sentinels. Deino needs a sample from the pool at the base of the city's highest waterfall.

quest:1945.text: Laughing Sisters. In Ashenvale, dryad hair is sought for an empowered robe. The experienced troll tailor Kil'hala at the Crossroads needs the enchanted locks to weave a mage robe, as Horde mages press against the woodland's native defenders. After securing water from Xavian, rising mages are sent by Deino in Orgrimmar to help craft their own enchanted vestments. These arcane garments need materials touched by raw magic. Dryad locks carry the forest's ancient vitality, giving them what is needed to weave intricate robes that shield and strengthen a caster. Mages seek the laughing sisters near Raynewood Retreat in Ashenvale. These nimble dryads ally with the night elves and fiercely guard their groves from woodsmen and outsiders. They will not willingly give their hair to Horde spellcasters, so the locks are taken by force beneath the ancient trees. The locks travel south across the border to the dusty settlement of the Crossroads in the Barrens. There, troll tailor Kil'hala receives them without remorse. Kil'hala acknowledges the woodland creatures' loss with a touch of irony, then puts the enchanted strands to use, knowing Horde power demands resolve.

quest:1946.text: Nether-lace Garment. At the Crossroads, Kil'hala weaves dryad hair into enchanted cloth for spellcasters. The finished garment marks the end of his specialized work in the Barrens. At the Crossroads in the Barrens, Kil'hala weaves nether-lace from the locks of laughing sisters. The dryads live in Ashenvale, and their hair is harvested for this work. Kil'hala binds the woodland enchantment in those rare, magically resonant locks into cloth that is comfortable and durable. Kil'hala wants more than fine work from his trade. He hopes to win favor with Deino, a respected troll mage who lives in Orgrimmar's Valley of Spirits. By making exceptional garb for aspiring practitioners, he hopes to earn and keep Deino's good graces.

quest:1947.text: Journey to the Marsh. Your class sends you to Dustwallow Marsh, where Tabetha’s knowledge can help you earn your wand. West of Theramore and just north of the Stonemaul Ruins, Tabetha lives in a cottage. Your class asks you to speak with the hermit and learn from her vast knowledge.

quest:195.text: Raptor Mastery. Deep in the jungle of Stranglethorn Vale, Hemet Nesingwary challenges hunters to step up their game against more dangerous quarry. Following an earlier raptor hunt, he directs adventurers to pursue and bring down ten Lashtail Raptors. After proving an initial measure of hunting prowess, Hemet Nesingwary expects more than idly passing time by the camp's fire. To prove true focus and skill, hunters are dispatched into the dense jungle brush just north of Grom'gol Base Camp to track down and slay ten fierce Lashtail Raptors.

quest:1950.text: Get the Scoop. Magus Tirth has locked a crucial spellbook inside his magically sealed strongbox, but he cannot recall the activation phrase to open it. To retrieve the tome, you must locate his missing apprentice somewhere around the Shimmering Flats racetrack and pry the forgotten words from him. Magus Tirth is an eccentric spellcaster dwelling on the cracked salt bed of the Shimmering Flats in Thousand Needles. While he possesses the esoteric knowledge and tomes that advancing mages desperately seek, dealing with him requires patience. Tirth relies heavily on an assistant to manage mundane details, including the spoken passwords guarding his arcane repositories. When tasked with retrieving a book of power, visiting practitioners quickly learn that Tirth has locked the volume away behind magic words that have slipped his mind entirely.

quest:198.text: Supplies to Private Thorsen. Krazek in Booty Bay hires a courier to haul miscellaneous goblin supplies north to Lieutenant Doren's camp. Local troll aggression has halted routine shipments, requiring an outside hand to ensure the goods reach Private Thorsen near the northern border. Lieutenant Doren and his outfit stationed near the border between Stranglethorn Vale and Duskwood rely on regular shipments arranged through Krazek. Persistent attacks from local trolls have made standard delivery hazardous, prompting the goblin merchant to contract an independent courier. The package must travel all the way up the jungle road, with Private Thorsen designated to receive it either in their camp northwest of the road or along his patrol route to the south.

quest:1999.text: Tools of the Trade. Horde rogues are sent from the Undercity to steal a report from Ambermill. Lord Varimathras orders them to obtain lockpicking tools and recover Kirin Tor intelligence on Dalaran’s condition. A prisoner’s interrogation points the Deathstalkers toward intelligence hidden in Ambermill. Silverpine Forest remains a precarious front line, and human mages guard the village’s communications fiercely. Lord Varimathras orders Deathstalker handler Mennet Carkad to direct promising operatives around the Kirin Tor sentries and recover the Dalaran Status Report. Infiltration and lockpicking test skills beyond assassination. Before entering Kirin Tor territory, operatives receive specialized thieves’ tools from Estelle Gendry. Opening the secured chest in Ambermill proves an operative can move beyond street brutality and become an espionage asset for the Forsaken.

quest:2.text: Sharptalon's Claw. Ashenvale's trails grow safer when Sharptalon's Claw is taken from the forest. Bring the trophy to Senani Thunderheart at Splintertree Post to prove Sharptalon has fallen and protect Horde supply lines. Sharptalon hunts the paths to Splintertree Post as the Horde seeks resources in Ashenvale. The aggressive hippogryph strikes peons and couriers traveling between forward logging camps and the outpost. Its attacks hinder Horde work in the region, where night elven sentinels and dangerous wildlife both threaten the newcomers. Senani Thunderheart, a tauren huntress, directs Horde hunters against Ashenvale's deadliest predators. Sharptalon's talon proves the hippogryph has fallen. Bring the trophy to Splintertree Post, where the outpost's defenders honor the hunt and frightened laborers can walk the woods with less fear.

quest:20.text: Blackrock Menace. Redridge's Blackrock orcs press in from the north and southeast, leaving Lakeshire under siege. Marshal Marris calls on adventurers to thin their ranks and bring back their battleworn axes. Lakeshire faces threats from several sides, but the Blackrock orcs are the gravest danger. These seasoned raiders have crossed south from the fiery Burning Steppes into Redridge. They have taken strongholds and roam the craggy passes. Their presence keeps townspeople penned inside Lakeshire, cutting off trade, foraging, and travel along the northern roads. Marshal Marris commands Lakeshire's beleaguered guard, but he cannot spare soldiers to assault the orcs' positions. He calls on you to strike their forward scouts and foot soldiers instead. Their crude, battleworn axes will prove they are dead. Marris hopes to thin the invaders around Stonewatch to the north and in the rugged pockets of southeastern Redridge.

quest:200.text: Bookie Herod. Lieutenant Doren fears a spy among his own men after Kurzen discovered Thorsen's secret. To uncover how the secret slipped out, an investigator must infiltrate Kurzen's Compound and recover the records kept by Kurzen's logistics officer. Following the discovery of Thorsen's secret, Lieutenant Doren suspects that a traitor operates within their midst. The intelligence leak threatens their operations, and finding the traitor has become an urgent concern. Thorsen maintained a line of communication directly into Kurzen's Compound through Bookie Herod, the colonel's logistics officer. Because Herod knows how Kurzen's Compound is run from day to day, Doren believes the officer's written records hold the truth about how the operation was exposed. Reaching Bookie Herod's paperwork requires venturing into Kurzen's Compound. During Doren's time serving under Kurzen, Herod kept his office on the top floor of the compound's lone two-story house. There, among supply requisitions and missives from Colonel Kurzen himself, lie the documents that could trace how the secret was betrayed.

quest:201.text: Investigate the Camp. Investigate the Camp is an expedition task originating in Booty Bay to scout a newly established hunters' campsite in Stranglethorn Vale. Commissioned by Krazek, it tasks travelers with confirming rumors that the legendary dwarven marksman Hemet Nesingwary has arrived near Lake Nazferiti. Reports circulating through the docks of Booty Bay speak of an expedition of big-game hunters encamped in the northern jungles of Stranglethorn Vale. Word has reached Krazek that the camp lies along the river just past the Venture Company's busy mining claim near Lake Nazferiti. In a lawless jungle teeming with dangers and competing interests, unexplained armed encampments always demand a watchful eye. What makes this particular expedition notable is the rumored presence of Hemet Nesingwary himself. The renowned dwarven marksman is known throughout the lands as an elite explorer with influential ties. Krazek prefers to take no chances with powerful figures operating in the hinterlands, sending scouts upriver to confirm whether the legendary hunter has truly arrived.

quest:203.text: The Second Rebellion. At the Rebel Camp in northern Stranglethorn Vale, Sergeant Yohwa seeks help against the overwhelming forces of Colonel Kurzen. Outnumbered ten to one by a cunning tactician, the rebels must rely on swift, covert strikes to survive. Cutting down Kurzen's jungle fighters is the first step toward relieving the relentless pressure on their refuge. The soldiers at the Rebel Camp face dire odds against Colonel Kurzen. Yohwa explains that the Colonel is a brilliant military tactician whose force outnumbers the rebellion by at least ten to one. Unable to wage an open war of attrition, the rebels have no choice but to adopt the Colonel's own covert tactics, launching quick incursions into his encampment to thin his ranks and escaping before heavy reinforcements can retaliate. To stem the tide, Yohwa asks you to push east into Kurzen's stronghold and eliminate a sizable contingent of his jungle fighters. Thinning out these foot soldiers eases the pressure bearing down on the Rebel Camp.

quest:204.text: Bad Medicine. At the Rebel Camp in northern Stranglethorn Vale, Sergeant Yohwa seeks to blunt Colonel Kurzen's military advantage by targeting his medical support. The renegades rely on powerful remedies and toxins concocted by their practitioners, leaving the resistance fighters desperate to turn those same concoctions to their own advantage. Colonel Kurzen has bolstered his jungle force with numerous medicine men who heal his forces and poison Yohwa's fighters with venom fern extracts. To turn the tide of the conflict, Sergeant Yohwa directs adventurers into the Kurzen Compound to scavenge those vital supplies. Securing their jungle remedies will help treat wounded fighters at the Rebel Camp, while capturing a sample of their venom fern extract will enable the resistance to study the toxin and manufacture their own cures.

quest:2040.text: Underground Assault. Shoni the Shilent sends Alliance adventurers into the Deadmines for a power core. The displaced gnomes need it to power drills that can break through the rock around Gnomeregan and help reclaim their home. After Gnomeregan fell catastrophically to primitive troggs, surviving gnomish tinkerers fled across Khaz Modan and Stormwind. Shoni the Shilent is among the engineers already planning how to breach the rock around their lost home. Her gyrodrillmatic excavationators need great power to bore through the underground stone. Without local power grids in human lands, the gnomes have turned to goblin heavy machinery in the criminal underworld. Deep in the twisting shafts of the Deadmines in Westfall, Edwin VanCleef's Defias Brotherhood employs goblin engineers to build war machines. One is a working goblin shredder, a lumbering automaton. Shoni sends Alliance operatives to destroy or dismantle it and recover its specialized heart, the Gnoam Sprecklesprocket. The exiled gnomes need the goblin power supply to drive their drills through the underground rock and begin their counteroffensive to reclaim Gnomeregan.

quest:2078.text: Gyromast's Revenge. Along Darkshore, Gelkak Gyromast seeks payback from the murlocs who plundered his wrecked ship. He sends you to reactivate his mechanical first mate, the Threshwackonator 4100. Gelkak Gyromast is stranded on Darkshore, but he will not accept defeat by the shore-dwelling murlocs. He has salvaged the pieces needed for his scheme and now seeks revenge on the tribe and its chief. Rather than take up his cutlass and wade into the surf, the eccentric captain turns to engineering. He entrusts you with a winding key and asks you to handle his mechanical subordinate.

quest:2098.text: Gyromast's Retrieval. On Darkshore's coast, Gelkak Gyromast needs help restoring his mechanical first mate. His winding key shattered on the rocks, and wildlife and murlocs scavenged the three pieces. Recovering them is the first step toward setting his crew right. Gelkak Gyromast is a gnome pirate stranded on Darkshore, far from the South Seas. He says aggressive threshadons attacked and sank his vessel just off the coast. The wreck cast him ashore among the flotsam, marooned and separated from his crew. Gelkak's first concern is his first mate, not provisions or gold. The companion needs a specialized key to operate, but the key shattered into three pieces when Gelkak crashed on the rocky shoals. Before he could gather them, reef crawlers on the beach, foreststriders near the woods, and scavengers from the Greymist murloc tribe carried the shiny pieces away.

quest:213.text: Hostile Takeover. In Booty Bay, Gelriz's latest move draws Baron Revilgaz's wrath in Hostile Takeover. Gelriz has pushed aside moguls appointed by the trade princes and now moves against the most notorious pirate of all. Kebok sends you to steal strange blue crystals Venture Company geologists have found near Lake Nazferiti. Baron Revilgaz gives Kebok leave to answer the insult as he sees fit. Kebok chooses theft, targeting the strange blue stones Venture Company mining crews have been unearthing. Venture Company geologists working around Lake Nazferiti have taken a keen interest in the unusual crystals. Kebok wants you to bring eight samples back to Booty Bay. How you get them matters little to him, so long as they end up in his hands.

quest:215.text: Jungle Secrets. After being rescued from an ambush in northern Stranglethorn Vale, Private Thorsen explains why he re-enlisted with Kurzen's men. He directs you back to the Rebel Camp so his commander can verify his covert intentions. Following his rescue, Private Thorsen admits the scene looks bad and asks to explain. He claims Lieutenant Doren ordered him to re-enlist with Colonel Kurzen's men to gather desperately needed intelligence for the rebellion. What seemed to be an opportunity to infiltrate Kurzen's Compound quickly turned disastrous, forcing Thorsen to refer you directly to Doren at the Rebel Camp for official confirmation while begging for complete discretion.

quest:2158.text: Rest and Relaxation. Rest and Relaxation is an introductory Alliance quest directing newly trained adventurers from Northshire south along the road to the Lion's Pride Inn. Run by Innkeeper Farley, the bustling Goldshire tavern offers food, drink, and a warm hearth for those seeking a reprieve from the road. After cutting their teeth in Northshire, weary travelers are pointed south toward the Lion's Pride Inn in Goldshire. The road south leads directly to the beloved tavern, run by Innkeeper Farley. For new adventurers stepping out into the wider forest, it represents the first major outpost offering hearth, shelter, and hot meals away from the Abbey. Innkeeper Farley takes pride in his establishment's hospitality, operating under the motto of providing rest and relaxation for the tired and cold. Adventurers who mention their referral can take advantage of Farley's good graces, settling by the open fire to enjoy a warm meal, sturdy ale, and a much-needed respite before journeying further into Elwynn.

quest:219.text: Missing In Action. In the Redridge Mountains, Corporal Keeshan is missing after his regiment was overrun. Blackrock orcs knocked him unconscious and dragged him into a cave fortress. Now he needs an escort back to Lakeshire, where the garrison can learn what became of the missing men. Blackrock orcs descend from the northern peaks, making the Redridge Mountains more perilous. Town guard patrols often meet ambushes, and Corporal Keeshan's unit suffered the worst of them. The regiment was outnumbered and overwhelmed, and most of its soldiers fell in the attack. Keeshan survived when a crushing blow knocked him unconscious before the orcs could execute him. They dragged him to their cave as a prisoner. Battered and concussed, Keeshan is held deep in enemy territory and cannot make the trek down the mountain alone. You escort him toward Lakeshire, past the orc warbands occupying the ridgelines. Marshal Marris has been trying to learn what happened to the missing regiment while preparing Lakeshire for further attacks. Keeshan's safe return brings him sorely needed relief.

quest:220.text: Call of Water. Brine's water reaches Islen Waterseer on the eastern Barrens coast, where the next part of the shamanic trial begins. The vial holds water Brine prepared and blessed, the base for a sapta that lets an initiate see water spirits in Silverpine Forest. After the trials in the southern Barrens, Brine gives the shaman initiate a Vial of Purest Water. The water comes from pure springs and has been consecrated by Brine's rites. The initiate carries it back to the eastern coast, where Islen Waterseer keeps watch. The water links Brine's teachings with the rites of the totem. Islen explains that mortal eyes cannot easily see water spirits. To meet them, an initiate drinks a brew called a sapta. The water from Brine will form the base of that draught and open the shaman's senses to what ordinary sight cannot find. Seeing the spirits is only part of the journey; they will test the initiate.

quest:221.text: Worgen in the Woods. In Duskwood, Nightbane Dark Runners press closer to Darkshire. Calor sends you into the Rotting Orchard to thin their ranks before the pack can surround the town. Calor's scouting has revealed a greater danger than the lone worgen first seen weaving shadowy magic at the forest's edge. Larger and swifter Nightbane Dark Runners have gathered in the Rotting Orchard, just southwest of Darkshire. They make up most of the pack and have turned the orchard into a staging ground within striking distance of the village gates.

quest:222.text: Worgen in the Woods. Calor sends you against the Nightbane pack in southern Duskwood. Their dens and mines bring the worgen threat close to Darkshire. South of Darkshire, the Nightbane worgen are making fortified camps in caves and abandoned mine shafts. Calor watches their bonfires and fears what their growing hold means for the town. The Vile Fangs and Tainted Ones are among the pack’s fiercest breeds. Their savagery and stubbornness threaten Darkshire’s perimeter.

quest:223.text: Worgen in the Woods. Calor sends you to Darkshire with a letter for Jonathan Carevin after your hunts against the worgen in Duskwood. Carevin faces dangers beyond the beasts, and Calor believes your skill can aid him. You have driven the Nightbane pack from Roland's Doom and the shadowed glades, earning Calor's respect. He is stationed on the dark frontier of the woods and rarely offers praise or formal introductions. Calor gives you a faded scrap of parchment and asks you to deliver his recommendation to Jonathan Carevin in Darkshire. He says that with more fighters like you, his small company might outshine the town's beleaguered Night Watch. Jonathan Carevin works in Darkshire under heavy strain, wary of outsiders and short on time. The town faces worgen, restless undead, demonic forces, and cultists aiding the corruption from within. Calor's recommendation wins Carevin's trust, and he sees you as a dependable fighter ready to preserve the Light against Duskwood's terrors.

quest:226.text: Wolves at Our Heels. Lars at Sven's Camp faces hungry, rabid dire wolves in western Duskwood. Hunting them gives Lars room to gather food while he and Sven Yorgen pursue their vendetta against the necromancer Morbent Fel. Sven Yorgen and Lars keep an isolated camp in the western hills of Duskwood, near the Westfall border. They live far from Darkshire and rely on their own hunting and foraging to survive. Lars carries fresh game through the dark woods, where ravenous predators prowl the riverbanks and underbrush. Starving, rabid dire wolves prowl north and east of the camp, toward the river. Killing the frenzied beasts eases the danger to Lars as he hunts. With less need to fight for their daily food, Sven and Lars can focus on Morbent Fel, the necromancer farther east.

quest:2282.text: Alther's Mill. At Alther's Mill, Lucius tests Alliance rogues with a locked chest and thieves' tools. The mill lies northeast along the road from Lakeshire, where Blackrock orcs now draw near. Lucius sends you northeast along the road from Lakeshire to Alther's Mill, with your first set of thieves' tools. There, you face a locked chest and a test of skill. Open Lucius's personal lockbox and bring back the token inside to earn your Certificate of Thievery. Alther's Mill once served as a lumber outpost, but Blackrock orcs now encroach on Redridge and have drawn near. Lucius treats their presence as an added trial. SI:7 expects its agents to pick locks undetected while moving through enemy-held territory.

quest:23.text: Ursangous's Paw. In Ashenvale, Ursangous's Paw proves you brought down one of the forest's fiercest predators. Bring it to Senani Thunderheart at Splintertree Post to earn honor among the Horde's trackers. The Ashenvale Hunt sends trackers from Splintertree Post after the ancient beasts that rule the forest canopy. Ursangous is among the fiercest, known for killing travelers and warriors who cross his path. Bringing back his paw proves the mighty beast has fallen to your hunt.

quest:230.text: Sven's Camp. In Duskwood, Sven Yorgen's grief still drives him to seek answers about his family's slaughter. A buried journal at the ruined farm may reveal who witnessed it. Sven Yorgen returned to find his family dead and his farm in ruins after dark riders struck while he was away. Grief and vengeance drove him to send allies to search the wreckage of the homestead. Beneath a mound of freshly turned earth lay a small, dirt-stained book, hastily hidden by a shadowy figure.

quest:235.text: The Ashenvale Hunt. Warcaller Gorlach sends the Horde north into Ashenvale to join the hunt. Report to Senani Thunderheart at Splintertree Post, where the Horde is pushing its frontier into the ancient forest. Orgrimmar needs timber, meat, and safe trade routes to keep growing. Warcaller Gorlach carries orders from the Horde's high command, sending seasoned wanderers and new adventurers toward active campaigns. For those coming of age in Durotar and the Barrens, Ashenvale is the next test of skill and survival. North of the Barrens, Ashenvale holds two Horde strongholds. Splintertree Post lies in the eastern woods, while Zoram'gar Outpost stands along the western coast. Senani Thunderheart coordinates operations from Splintertree Post, organizing trackers and hunters to face the beasts beneath the canopy and night elven sentinels who contest the Horde's claims.

quest:2359.text: Klaven's Tower. From a camp in Westfall, Agent Kearnen watches Klaven's Tower. Strange shipments and altered guards point to danger within the Defias Brotherhood. At Westfall's southeastern edge, the river runs below Klaven's Tower, north of the Dagger Hills. The Defias Brotherhood holds the stone spire, though its human thieves and brigands are common across the plains. Agent Kearnen has watched the tower alone for weeks. Lately, she has seen strange things: a bizarre shipment came straight from Duskwood's shadowed woods, escorted by monstrous, deformed sentries unlike ordinary highwaymen.

quest:2360.text: Mathias and the Defias. In Westfall, SI:7 has found the Defias unusually active. You are sent to Agent Kearnen near an abandoned Alliance watch tower for a debriefing. The Defias have seized an abandoned Alliance watch tower southeast of Sentinel Hill. SI:7 reports they use it as a base to smuggle goods from the Redridge supply route. You are sent to Westfall to find Agent Kearnen, hidden near the tower, and hear her debriefing.

quest:2383.text: Simple Parchment. A message waits for you in the Valley of Trials, sent while you were away. Frang, your class trainer, is outside the Den. The parchment asks you to read its words and speak with Frang. Your class trainer waits outside the Den in the Valley of Trials.

quest:24.text: Shadumbra's Head. At Splintertree Post, Shadumbra's Head is proof that a feared predator has fallen. Bringing it to Senani Thunderheart completes a trial of the Ashenvale Hunt and helps secure the western roads toward the Zoram Strand. Shadumbra hunted the woods west of Splintertree Post, where Horde scouts and couriers traveled toward the Zoram Strand. Her speed and stealth made those paths perilous, and each westward patrol kept the post's defenders wary. Senani Thunderheart, a tauren huntress, challenges Horde champions to track and fell Ashenvale's great beasts as part of the Ashenvale Hunt. Shadumbra's head proves the hunter has brought down one of Kalimdor's deadliest native stalkers, and that travelers can use the roads with less danger.

quest:240.text: Return to Jitters. At Raven Hill, you bring Jitters a meal from Chef Grual. The cakes finally satisfy the hermit's desperate hunger. Chef Grual cooks at the Scarlet Raven Tavern, where Duskwood's lack of livestock and sea life leaves him to use what the blighted forest provides. His specialty, Dusky Crab Cakes, contain no crab meat. Instead, Grual uses gooey legs from venom web spiders that creep through the wood. He calls it resourceful cooking; delicate stomachs may disagree. At Raven Hill, Jitters huddles in fear, unable to face whatever horrors drove him from the woods. Terror keeps him from hunting or foraging, and hunger deepens his distress. The warm cakes bring a rare moment of relief to the trembling vagrant. Desperate for food, he eats without asking what kind of crab Grual used.

quest:245.text: Eight-Legged Menaces. In Duskwood, venom web spiders crowd the western border. Watcher Dodds calls on travelers to thin their numbers before more Night Watch guards are caught in their webs. Pygmy venom web spiders swarm the brush along the western road from Westfall into Duskwood. Their webs choke the thickets beneath the dense canopy, putting travelers and the Night Watch's fragile defenses at risk. Watcher Dodds keeps a small camp far from Darkshire, with too few troops to hold the border. Commander Althea Ebonlocke cannot send reinforcements while undead and worgen press against the township. Dodds has already lost comrades to the spiders, finding them hanging upside down in the canopy as venom paralyzed them and liquefied their flesh.

quest:2458.text: Deep Cover. Shenthul sends a promising Horde rogue to Sludge Fen to contact an agent hidden among the Venture Company. The Shattered Hand has spent a year placing Taskmaster Fizzule inside the company’s drilling grounds, where he watches their plans. The Shattered Hand protects Orgrimmar’s interests through secret intelligence and assassination. For a year, its members worked to place an agent in the Venture Company’s ranks. Taskmaster Fizzule earned a place at their drilling outpost north of Sludge Fen, among the company’s mercenaries. Fizzule must keep his hard-edged reputation to satisfy the Venture Company’s overseers. An unexpected visitor could bring an attack. Rogues who reach his tower must fire two flares from the signaling gun within sight, approach quietly, and give the Shattered Hand’s secret salute. Then Fizzule can share what he has learned about the company’s growing schemes.

quest:2460.text: The Shattered Salute. In Orgrimmar's Cleft of Shadow, Shenthul teaches a silent sign to new rogues. The Shattered Hand uses it to recognize its agents safely in the field. In Orgrimmar's Cleft of Shadow, the Shattered Hand works in secrecy as Thrall's Horde intelligence and assassination arm. Its agents cannot use banners or military signs on dangerous, secret assignments. Shenthul teaches newly inducted rogues the Shattered Salute, a silent gesture that lets allies recognize one another. For Shenthul's rogues, learning the salute is vital tradecraft, not ceremony. Agents sent into danger or to infiltrate rival factions need to verify contacts without alerting bystanders or targets. Before entrusting an agent with covert fieldwork, Shenthul expects them to recognize and mirror the gesture without hesitation.

quest:247.text: The Hunt Completed. In Ashenvale, the hunt tests a Horde champion against three legendary predators. Felling Ursangous, Shadumbra, and Sharptalon proves strength, tenacity, and primal prowess in a contested forest. Senani Thunderheart tests travelers among the Horde forces in Ashenvale. Her hunt tests more than loyalty to the warchief; it asks whether a hunter understands survival in the wild. Three legendary predators are its quarry: the bear Ursangous, the cat Shadumbra, and the fierce hippogryph Sharptalon. Felling all three and securing their trophies proves a hunter's blood runs true. For the tauren, hunting is a sacred act of balance and respect, even in an active warfront. Overcoming Ashenvale's greatest terrors honors the spirits of the land and earns a hunter the ancestral blessings of Thunderheart. A formal commendation and token of favor mark the hunt's end, while the champion's reputation spreads throughout the forest.

quest:2478.text: Mission: Possible But Not Probable. In the northern Barrens, Horde rogues face a Venture Company outpost that tests stealth, theft, and combat. They infiltrate an oil tower, kill Grand Foreman Puzik Gallywix, and take a potent chemical brew for the Shattered Hand. North of the Sludge Fen oil rigs, the Venture Company keeps an isolated drilling tower. Taskmaster Fizzule, a Shattered Hand operative posing as a Venture Company supervisor, orders rogues to rely on underworld craft instead of an open assault. He asks them to pick the key from Foreman Silixiz and keep it for him. Then they climb past workers and sentries changed by the tower’s experiments.

quest:2479.text: Hinott's Assistance. In Orgrimmar, poisoned rogues seek Hinott's Assistance before Zanzil's mixture claims their lives. The toxin came from an infiltration in the Barrens, and Serge Hinott in Tarren Mill can offer a cure and teach the brewing of poisons. A daring infiltration of the Venture Company's tower north of the Sludge Fen leaves rogues poisoned by Zanzil's altered mixture. It dulls their reflexes and threatens their lives. Shenthul, the rogue trainer in Orgrimmar, knows local remedies cannot help. He sends the poisoned rogue across the sea to the Eastern Kingdoms for care. The search for a cure leads south through Lordaeron to Tarren Mill, a village in Hillsbrad Foothills. Serge Hinott lives there as an apothecary, known for his fascination with virulent brews. Ordinary healers recoil from Zanzil's venom, but Hinott treats the deadly compound with professional glee. He can dissect the foul concoction and teach worthy rogues to brew their own venoms.

quest:248.text: Looking Further. Theocritus watches eastern Redridge from Elwynn through an enchanted conduit. He seeks the cause of the conflict between Morganth and the Blackrock orcs at Stonewatch Keep, and sends you to place the Glyph of Azora in the nearby watch tower. From his sanctum in Elwynn Forest, Theocritus watches eastern Redridge with scrying magic. As he studies the Tower of Ilgalar, he detects a clash between Morganth, a renegade human warlock, and the Blackrock orcs entrenched in Stonewatch Keep. Both hostile factions should be united against the Kingdom of Stormwind, yet they fight over an unknown prize. Theocritus intervenes before their conflict shifts the balance.

quest:2480.text: Hinott's Assistance. At Tarren Mill, a Horde rogue seeks Serge Hinott's help against Zanzil's poison. The Forsaken chemist studies the toxin and prepares a cure. After a Barrens assignment leaves you suffering from a toxin that clouds the mind, you are sent north to Tarren Mill. Serge Hinott, a Forsaken chemist, studies the poison made by Zanzil, a jungle troll exile. Hinott cares little about the troll's identity or kin. He admires the brew's vicious effect and wants to understand how it works before making an antidote.

quest:249.text: Morganth. Across Redridge, Theocritus watches Morganth hunt an ancient relic. From the Tower of Azora in eastern Elwynn Forest, Theocritus watches the crags of Redridge through his scrying spells. He sees Morganth, a warlock in the Tower of Ilgalar, searching for the Scythe of Elune. Fearing Morganth is close to claiming it, Theocritus asks Alliance champions to stop him before Stormwind is threatened. The Tower of Ilgalar rises above the Redridge basin, where gnolls and twisted arcane energies fill its halls. Morganth waits at the summit, wielding shadow magic and guarding his research. To reach him, you climb through hostile ground and face the warlock directly. His Pendant of Shadow can be brought back as proof that the tower has fallen and the threat is broken.

quest:25.text: Stonetalon Standstill. At Mystral Lake, befouled water spirits have halted Horde supply transports on the way to Stonetalon. Mastok Wrilehiss at Splintertree Post sends you to clear the hostile elementals and scout a night elf gazebo overlooking Silverwind Refuge. The Horde needs lumber, supplies, and messengers to travel between Ashenvale and the Stonetalon Mountains. The Talondeep Path carries them past Mystral Lake’s western shore. Hostile water elementals have stopped travel and battered the supply caravans. Mastok Wrilehiss calls for action to reopen the route before the Horde’s supply lines collapse. Water elementals in Mystral Lake have become befouled, aggressive, and unpredictable. They attack those who take the nearby trails. You are sent to cull them and defeat the greater spirit Tideress so the area may become safer. What has tainted the lake’s spirits remains unknown amid the turmoil in Ashenvale’s sacred groves. A night elf gazebo stands on Mystral Lake’s central island, with a clear view across the water to Silverwind Refuge. Horde scouts are sent to assess whether it could serve as a forward observation post. From there, Splintertree’s commanders could watch nearby Alliance movements without being detected.

quest:251.text: Translate Abercrombie's Note. In Darkshire, Translate Abercrombie's Note brings a strange letter before the town's leaders. Mayor Ello Ebonlocke turns to Sirra Von'Indi, the scholar who knows obscure scripts. Abercrombie sends Mayor Ello Ebonlocke a sealed letter from his home. Ebonlocke expects an eccentric plea or bitter ramblings from the cemetery hermit, but the parchment bears strange writing that ordinary Common cannot explain. Without the learning to read ancient or obscure languages, the mayor will not dismiss it. Even a mad hermit may pose a danger in Duskwood. Ebonlocke sends you across the square to Sirra Von'Indi, Darkshire's scholar of esoteric lore. Sirra knows ancient arts and forgotten tongues. He scoffs at Abercrombie's sanity, saying anyone who lives beside a haunted graveyard must have a rotted brain. Still, he takes the parchment seriously and begins the slow work of transcription.

quest:253.text: Bride of the Embalmer. In Darkshire, Lord Ello Ebonlocke sends you to find Eliza's grave. The town has learned that the Embalmer is real, and you are to take his living heart from her cursed remains to strip him of his power. Duskwood's children grew up hearing a tale of the Embalmer. He was said to be a kindly alchemist, driven mad when his beloved wife, Eliza, died. Desperate to cheat death, he turned to sorcery, cut out his own beating heart, and placed it in her chest. Lord Ello Ebonlocke once dismissed the story as village folklore. Recent discoveries have shown that the Embalmer walks among the living, and his work festers beneath the graveyard dirt.

quest:254.text: Digging Through the Dirt. You search for the Embalmer’s missing heart in Duskwood at Raven Hill Cemetery. A mound marked Eliza hides a buried horror that will not stay dead. At Raven Hill Cemetery, a patch of loose, freshly turned soil bears the name Eliza. Other graves in Duskwood lie open to scavengers or feral ghouls, but someone placed this earth with care. Digging below the topsoil uncovers the splintered boards of a coffin. It seals away the remnant the Embalmer meant to hide from the light of day.

quest:256.text: WANTED: Chok'sul. In northeastern Loch Modan, Chok'sul's ogres threaten the settlements and the works that sustain the valley. Magistrate Bluntnose wants the warlord dead before more lives are lost. Ogres now threaten northeastern Loch Modan, where troggs and wild beasts have long tested the valley's borders. They have made camps in the rugged hills and moved beyond simple scavenging. Local scouts and town authorities report raids that are focused, persistent, and dangerous. Magistrate Bluntnose believes Chok'sul directs attacks on Thelsamar, a nearby dwarven excavation site, and the Stonewrought Dam. Fearing for civilian lives and the valley's great engineering work, he offers a bounty for the ogre chieftain's death by any means. Chok'sul's severed head is required as proof.

quest:261.text: Down the Scarlet Path. Brother Anton of the Scarlet Crusade, at Nijel's Point, says his order is at war with the Scourge, an evil that corrupts the people and infects the land. He asks you to prove your allegiance by destroying thirty undead ravagers in the Valley of Bones. Brother Anton speaks bluntly. He says the Scourge must be halted before it swallows the land and pulls the world into darkness, and the Scarlet Crusade has pledged itself to that fight. If you are with them, he wants your courage and allegiance shown by destroying thirty undead ravagers. They are found south of Anton, in the Valley of Bones. Succeed, and the Crusade will welcome you.

quest:262.text: The Shadowy Figure. Near his ruined farm, Sven Yorgen seeks the stranger who watched his family die. He gives you a strange book found among the wreckage and asks you to learn who left it behind. Sven Yorgen hides in Duskwood’s western hills, still haunted by the slaughter of his family. He once blamed the black riders who terrorize the woods, but another memory troubles him: a shadowy figure nearby on the night of the massacre. Sven gives you the strange book found at his ransacked farm, the only physical clue left in the wreckage. No clear trail leads through the perilous wilderness, so you head east to Darkshire. Sven hopes one of the superstitious townsfolk will recognize the curious book. Among them is Madame Eva, whose occult senses let her see beyond ordinary sight. Her divinations may reveal impressions left on mysterious relics.

quest:265.text: The Shadowy Search Continues. In Duskwood, the search for the journal’s origins leads from Madame Eva to Clerk Daltry in Darkshire. The journal came from the ruins of Sven Yorgen’s ransacked farmstead. Madame Eva discerned that the journal’s author was an outsider, but its binding came from within Darkshire. Clerk Daltry often sells blank ledgers and tomes to traveling scholars, spellcasters, and record-keepers. The search follows those local sales for a clue to the sinister trespasser in Duskwood’s groves.

quest:266.text: Inquire at the Inn. In Darkshire, Clerk Daltry sends you to the Scarlet Raven Tavern with a journal from Sven Yorgen's ruined farm. He hopes someone there can tell you who owned it. Clerk Daltry has finished examining the tattered book from Sven Yorgen's farm. He believes any stranger who visited Darkshire would have passed through its tavern. The Scarlet Raven Tavern is across town, the only gathering hall and lodging house in Darkshire. There, you may learn who came through and where they went.

quest:268.text: Return to Sven. You carry Jitters' finished journal back to Sven Yorgen's camp near Westfall. Its pages may answer the questions that have haunted him since his family's murder. When Sven Yorgen's farm was attacked, Jitters fled into the woods, leaving an incomplete diary behind. Afraid of Sven's anger and haunted by what he had seen, Jitters hid deep in Duskwood. When you find him, he willingly gives you his completed journal. He hopes its full account of the attack will spare him from facing Sven in person.

quest:269.text: Seeking Wisdom. In Stormwind, Sven Yorgen asks Bishop Farthing for holy counsel on Duskwood. He sends Jitters' Completed Journal, hoping the bishop can reveal how to break Morbent Fel's shield. Duskwood suffers beneath old curses and ravenous undead. Stormwind's royal court has grown indifferent, and Sven Yorgen knows ordinary strength cannot pierce Morbent Fel's wards. Broken-hearted, he shelters at a camp near the borders and asks you to carry Jitters' assembled journal to the church. The road north leads to the Cathedral of Light.

quest:270.text: The Doomed Fleet. Bishop Farthing sends you north from Stormwind to seek a way past Morbent Fel's wards. The trail leads across Khaz Modan to the wreckage of Kul Tiras's Third Fleet off the Wetlands. Morbent Fel's wards turn aside ordinary steel at his retreat on the Forlorn Rowe. Bishop Farthing sends you to seek a weapon bound to the Holy Light. Its key is Lightforge Iron, a rare consecrated metal whose strikes carry holy truth and pierce sorcerous protections. Duskwood has no supply of Lightforge Iron ready to hand. Bishop Farthing recalls that Kul Tiras's Third Fleet sank years ago along the dangerous Wetlands coast, north of Ironforge. One of its galleons carried a shipment of the precious ore. You travel to Menethil Harbor to meet Glorin Steelbrow, a dwarven contact who knows the marshes and their wrecks.

quest:272.text: Trial of the Sea Lion. Druids in Moonglade seek the sea lion’s spirit through a sacred rite. They recover two scattered pendant halves for agility and endurance, then unite them at the Shrine of Remulos to prepare for Aquatic Form. Druid initiates in Moonglade undergo trials of attunement as they prepare to navigate Azeroth’s deep waters. The Trial of the Sea Lion follows earlier preparations in their spiritual training. Dendrite Starblaze oversees it in Nighthaven, where initiates learn to balance the sea lion’s graceful speed with its resilient stamina. Both are needed to take its form and withstand the ocean depths. The trial centers on reuniting the two halves of the Pendant of the Sea Lion. One represents the sea lion’s agility as it glides through turbulent currents. The other represents its endurance, the fortitude to dive long into freezing water without faltering. Initiates seek guidance from Moonglade’s inhabitants as they search across the world for the scattered relics. Once both halves are found, the initiate brings them near the Shrine of Remulos, where they can be joined into one talisman. The shrine’s energies bind agility and endurance in harmony. The initiate then presents the restored pendant to Dendrite Starblaze in Nighthaven. With the pendant, the druid shows readiness to embrace the sea lion aspect and awaken Aquatic Form.

quest:2745.text: Infiltrating the Castle. At Stormwind Keep, Elling Trias sends you to meet his fellow operative Tyrion. Tyrion has watched Lord Gregor Lescovar from the royal gardens for weeks. At his cheese shop in the Trade District, Elling Trias sees the Defias threat reaching into the kingdom's rule. Ordinary law cannot expose or punish a nobleman as protected and entrenched as Lord Gregor Lescovar. So Trias offers a dangerous path: deliver justice within Stormwind Keep, outside the law, and sever the conspiracy for good. Elling Trias has an operative in the high halls: Tyrion, a clever gnome skilled at concealment. For weeks, Tyrion has watched the keep's courtyards and royal gardens. He has tracked Lescovar's movements, who enters his chambers, and when the traitor meets covert Defias contacts. You need to reach Tyrion without drawing the Royal Guard's suspicion.

quest:2746.text: Items of Some Consequence. Tyrion needs silk and apples to prepare Spybot for a covert approach to Lord Lescovar in Stormwind Keep. The mechanical spy must pass the royal guards and listen to the noble. Elling Trias, the cheese merchant, has moved the operation against Lord Gregor Lescovar forward. He suspects Lescovar's schemes in Stormwind Keep threaten the realm. Tyrion agrees to the tighter schedule in the keep's gardens, but Spybot's disguise needs careful preparation. Tyrion plans to send Spybot, a small mechanical contraption, past the castle guards to reach Lescovar inside the keep. Its strange disguise as a woman should turn suspicion aside. You gather suitably sized apples from Clara's orchard just outside the city walls, along with bolts of silk for the puppet's clothes.

quest:275.text: Blisters on The Land. In the eastern Wetlands, Rethiel senses sickness spreading through the marsh. The bog beast warden asks travelers to destroy Fen Creepers, hoping to ease the land's rising fever. Rethiel the Greenwarden watches the Wetlands from a grove among the marshes. The mire has always been harsh, but now an unnatural sickness spreads through it. Rethiel senses a fever in the earth, warping wild nature into mindless, shambling horrors. Fen Creepers are decaying masses of swamp vegetation that wander the waterways. Rethiel calls them diseased blisters swelling on the land. Their tormented presence agitates the marsh, so Rethiel asks passing allies to destroy them and let their tangled remains settle into the mud.

quest:276.text: Tramping Paws. At Greenwarden's Grove in the Wetlands, Rethiel watches the Mosshide numbers rise near the Gate of Algaz. Their fires and trampling threaten the bog, and Rethiel asks travelers to thin their ranks. Mosshide gnolls lived in the Wetlands for many years without overwhelming the natural order. Now their numbers have surged south toward the pass of Dun Algaz. Their heavy boots and paws crush rare fen plants, while their logging strips groves for campsite fires. If the packs keep growing, the fragile marsh will suffer. Rethiel the Greenwarden watches the marsh for signs of imbalance. The gnolls' existence is not the trouble; their numbers have grown beyond what the Wetlands can support. Thinning the Mosshide gnolls and mongrels helps preserve the fen, and may earn the approval of its ancient guardian.

quest:277.text: Fire Taboo. Along the marsh roads of the Wetlands, Fire Taboo puts Rethiel's concern for the forest into action. The bog beast asks travelers to take the crude flints Mosshide gnolls use to burn living trees, hoping to spare the ancient boughs. Rethiel the Greenwarden feels the Wetlands' trees as kin. Rot and renewal belong to the swamp, but the Mosshide gnolls cut living timber and cast it into their hearthfires. The groans of those boughs weigh on Rethiel, who can no longer watch the trees suffer in silence. The Mosshide pack cuts green trees for warmth and territory instead of gathering deadwood. Rethiel seeks to curb their spread without a long war, so the bog beast asks you to take the crude flints carried by stronger gnolls. Without those tools, the pack cannot burn the timber it fells. Rethiel smashes each stone and casts its dust into the sea, where it can never spark the forest again.

quest:284.text: The Search Continues. The search for the Menethil Statuette continues among nearby Murloc hovels. These shelters hold no sign of it, so you turn to two more. You search this cluster of Murloc hovels, but find no trace of the Menethil Statuette. Two nearby shelters to the north and northeast may hold clues.

quest:285.text: Search More Hovels. Among the Murloc hovels, you have found no sign of the Menethil Statuette. So you press farther north, seeking the next clue. You believe the Menethil Statuette lies in one of the hovels to the north. So you continue your search among the Murloc dwellings.

quest:286.text: Return the Statuette. Karl Boran in Menethil Harbor needs the Menethil Statuette brought back. It was found inside a barrel pulled from the muck, and its return will ease the Blind Princess's captain. The statuette lay packed in fine straw inside the barrel. It shows a young, long-haired Paladin raising a hammer. Karl Boran in Menethil Harbor is waiting for it. The Blind Princess's captain will be relieved to know the cargo is safe.

quest:288.text: The Third Fleet. Outside the Deepwater Tavern, First Mate Fitzsimmons drinks to drown his memories. He alone survived Kul Tiras's Third Fleet, burned off the Wetlands by red dragons enslaved by orcs during the Second War. First Mate Fitzsimmons spends his days outside the Deepwater Tavern in Menethil Harbor, nursing a hangover and memories he cannot shake. He once served as an officer aboard the Wave Mistress, a ship-of-the-line that sailed under Kul Tiras's maritime banner. Now he trades those grim memories for dwarven mead. Anyone who buys him another drink can hear his account of one of the Second War's worst naval slaughters. During the Second War, the Third Fleet sailed along the shores of Khaz Modan when fire came from the sky. The Dragonmaw clan had subdued the red dragonflight at Grim Batol and unleashed dragonfire on the unsuspecting warships. Fitzsimmons remembers helpless wooden hulls burning beneath towering flames, their crews dragged into the deep. He alone survived and washed ashore. His fallen brothers lie in the watery graveyard now known as the Doomed Fleet.

quest:289.text: The Cursed Crew. Off the Wetlands coast, The Cursed Crew still haunts its sunken ships. First Mate Fitzsimmons, the Third Fleet of Kul Tiras's sole living survivor, asks for mercy for his lost brethren. A dark relic aboard one of the wrecks binds the drowned sailors and marines to the ships as restless undead. The Third Fleet of Kul Tiras wrecked along the jagged shores north of Menethil Harbor.
