At the Cathedral of Light, faith becomes a defense against hostile spellcasters. At the Cathedral of Light, High Priestess Laurena warns the acolytes that arcane magic remains dangerous. The Holy Light brings healing, warmth, and divine order. Raw magic can turn volatile and lead to corruption or catastrophe. Warlocks, renegade sorcerers, and magical beasts threaten the faithful, so priests learn to make their faith an active ward against spells. Arcane Feedback turns a hostile spellcaster's power back against them. The ward does more than deflect spells; it burns through the caster's mana and brings agony. Laurena teaches the rite to human priests preparing to travel beyond Stormwind. Thus the Cathedral's emissaries can face sorcery with a defense of their own.

quest:5677.text: Arcane Feedback. In Ironforge, human acolytes seeking deeper teaching are sent back to Stormwind. There, the Cathedral of Light holds the traditions of their people. High Priest Rohan welcomes a human priest who seeks deeper spiritual teaching in Ironforge’s Mystic Ward. Dwarven and human priests both serve the Holy Light, yet each people keeps its own rites, disciplines, and prayers of defense. Rohan reserves Ironforge’s teachings for his own clergy. So he sends human priests back to Elwynn to learn the traditions of humankind. After reaching Stormwind City, the acolyte finds High Priestess Laurena in the Cathedral of Light. Laurena is relieved that Rohan’s guidance has brought the traveler to her, and welcomes them as their powers begin to grow. In the Cathedral, human priests can keep learning Stormwind’s spiritual practices. There they prepare to wield the Holy Light against the threats around the kingdom.

quest:5678.text: Arcane Feedback. In Darnassus, Arcane Feedback sends human priests back to Stormwind. Priestess Alathea at the Temple of the Moon reluctantly honors the Alliance summons. There, High Priestess Laurena prepares the acolyte for deeper instruction. Priestess Alathea oversees visiting priests in the Temple of the Moon in Darnassus. She recognizes the formal alliance between the kaldorei and Stormwind, yet distrusts human magical and spiritual practices. Night elves see arcane power as volatile and dangerous, a view shaped by ten millennia of grief since the War of the Ancients. Even human divine rites trouble the night elf clergy when they blur radiant faith with arcane workings. Alathea honors the bond between the Alliance races and sends you to answer a recall from the Cathedral of Light. High Priestess Laurena has sent couriers across the seas to gather human priests for advanced training. In Stormwind, you leave Elune's moonlit groves behind for the grand stone sanctuaries and golden radiance of the Holy Light.

quest:5679.text: Devouring Plague. Forsaken priests in the Undercity learn Devouring Plague from Priestess Aelthalyste. The rite is for those who have proven their dedication to shadow magic, and teaches a feared curse of the undead priesthood. In the Undercity’s War Quarter, Priestess Aelthalyste teaches Forsaken priests the grim arts of the Shadow. Priests of other races draw power from the Holy Light or ancestral spirits, but the Forsaken have shaped their own spiritual doctrines. Devouring Plague gives form to that path: it torments foes and drains their stolen vitality to sustain the caster’s decaying body. Priestess Aelthalyste shares the plague’s power only with care. The spell is a weapon of potent malice, meant to turn the tide against the Scourge and the Scarlet Crusade. As she teaches it, she warns her disciples to practice until their command is sure. Greater trials await those who seek mastery of the dark arts.

quest:568.text: The Defense of Grom'gol. Commander Aggro'gosh seeks to safeguard the Horde's foothold in Stranglethorn Vale and protect their supply chain to Stonard. To keep that supply chain safe, he directs Horde champions to thin out the Lashtail Raptors outside Grom'gol Base Camp. At Grom'gol Base Camp, Commander Aggro'gosh carries the duty of protecting every member of the Horde within the jungle. The camp exists to keep supplies flowing safely to Stonard, but some of the local inhabitants are standing in the way. The raptors outside Grom'gol are the ones in the way. Aggro'gosh calls upon loyal fighters to thin out the Lashtail Raptors there, then report back to him for reassignment.

quest:569.text: The Defense of Grom'gol. Commander Aggro'gosh seeks to safeguard Grom'gol's supply lines through Stranglethorn Vale. After the earlier hunt thinning the raptors outside the camp, a band of ogres encamped at the nearby Mizjah Ruins continues to harass supply caravans heading toward Stonard. The Horde's presence in northern Stranglethorn Vale is centered on supplying Stonard, an outpost of vital strategic interest. While Commander Aggro'gosh did not arrive with the intention of fighting every native group, a band of local Mosh'Ogg ogres has claimed the Mizjah Ruins southeast of the camp. Warnings have failed to stop their continuous raids against Horde supply shipments, prompting the commander to order a strike against the ogre brutes and witch doctors holding the ruins.

quest:57.text: The Night Watch. Darkshire's volunteer militia faces restless dead rising across Duskwood. Commander Althea Ebonlocke sends travelers into the haunted barrows to hold the skeletal horrors back. The struggle helps keep Darkshire from falling to the darkness. Duskwood's graveyards have grown unnaturally restless as the forest sinks into twilight. Commander Althea Ebonlocke leads Darkshire's volunteer militia, The Night Watch, against an endless siege. With no aid from Stormwind, her forces are stretched thin. Animated skeletons and other horrors rise from the earth and threaten the eastern settlements, so the militia calls on able travelers to enter the deadlands. Two places draw the militia's attention: Tranquil Gardens Cemetery, just south of town, and Raven Hill Graveyard, far to the west. Skeletons pull themselves from forgotten tombs and shallow graves beside the roads, stirred by dark magic lingering in the forest's shadows. Cutting them down gives Darkshire's beleaguered citizens room to breathe, but the battle against this entrenched evil never ends.

quest:570.text: Mok'thardin's Enchantment. Far Seer Mok'thardin seeks to harness the natural magic of Stranglethorn Vale for the benefit of the Horde. Building upon his previous rituals at Grom'gol Base Camp, he asks for sharp claws and a pristine feline fang to weave a powerful enchantment. Within Grom'gol Base Camp, Far Seer Mok'thardin works to understand and bend the feral power of the wild to strengthen the Horde. Having seen success in his initial rites, he promises to craft a specialized enchanted relic for those willing to brave the dense underbrush and stalk the deadly predators prowling the surrounding territory. The ritual demands eight claws taken from shadowmaw panthers and a pristine fang from a tigress. Mok'thardin notes that while these fierce felines wander across Stranglethorn Vale, a gathering of them prowls south-eastward, just past the river running by the Mizjah Ruins.

quest:574.text: Special Forces. Following the reduction of the rogue colonel's rank-and-file soldiers, Sergeant Yohwa asks you to target the elite core of the compound. You are sent into the Stockpile cave to eliminate the commandos and headshrinkers before reporting to Lieutenant Doren. With the regular soldiers of the Kurzen Compound diminished through the work of the Second Rebellion, Sergeant Yohwa sets her sights on the colonel's elite specialists. She knows many of Kurzen's troops personally and calls them skilled, loyal and cruel. When they are not out in the wilderness slaughtering rebel soldiers, they are found in a cave at the back of the compound called the Stockpile. To break their strength, you are sent into the cavern to dispatch ten Kurzen Commandos and six Kurzen Headshrinkers. After the fight, Sergeant Yohwa tells you to report to her commanding officer, Lieutenant Doren, at the Rebel Camp, who will want your account firsthand.

quest:5741.text: Sceptre of Light. Azore Aldamort has heard that the Burning Blade of Thunder Axe Fortress, to the east, now hold the Sceptre of Light, which word says they obtained from the naga. Legend says it could sink whole cities beneath the great seas, and Azore will not let the Burning Blade keep such power. You are asked to bring it back to Ethel Rethor. Word has it that the naga's Sceptre of Light has come into the hands of the Burning Blade at Thunder Axe Fortress. Legend says it can sink whole cities beneath the great seas. Azore Aldamort holds that the Burning Blade cannot be allowed such power. A Burning Blade seer keeps the sceptre and studies it from the top of one of the fortress watchtowers. Azore wants you to take it from there yourself and carry it back to the tower at Ethel Rethor.

quest:5762.text: Hemet Nesingwary. This errand sends travelers across the sea from the salt pans of Kalimdor to the steaming jungles of Stranglethorn Vale. Kravel Koalbeard, an opportunistic merchant at the Mirage Raceway, tasks adventurers with delivering a long-overdue package of specialty supplies to the renowned big-game hunter Hemet Nesingwary. Out in the blinding expanse of the Shimmering Flats, commerce moves fast, but shipments sometimes lag behind. Kravel Koalbeard eventually receives a delayed crate earmarked for one of his wealthy patrons, Hemet Nesingwary. Having departed the Thousand Needles long before the parcel arrived, Hemet paid in advance to have it forwarded along to his wilderness hunting camp in Stranglethorn Vale. Rather than make the arduous trek himself, Kravel enlists roving adventurers willing to bridge the ocean divide. Tracking down Nesingwary's expedition north of Grom'gol Base Camp reveals the contents of the heavy crate: specialized heavy-gauge ammunition vital for bringing down the dangerous predators prowling the jungle. Hemet immediately recognizes the distinctive white crust of the salt flats clinging to the courier's gear, pleased that his old ties with the wily Kravel yielded the firepower his safari desperately needed.

quest:5763.text: Hunting in Stranglethorn. Roon Wildmane, a tauren in Desolace, once hunted beside a dwarf named Hemet. Now Roon sends you off with a kodo horn, bound for Hemet Nesingwary in Stranglethorn, north of Grom'gol Base Camp. Long ago a dwarf named Hemet came to Desolace, eager to hunt great beasts. Hemet handled a rifle with uncanny skill, and the two hunters passed many days together, the old enmity between their peoples set aside. When Hemet went off to Stranglethorn, Roon vowed to welcome Hemet back one day for another hunt, and Roon decides that time has arrived. You are to carry Roon's kodo horn to Hemet, who will know whose it is. Look in Stranglethorn, north of Grom'gol Base Camp.

quest:578.text: The Stone of the Tides. Following rumours of a haunted isle off the jungle coast, Baron Revilgaz suspects an ancient troll relic has resurfaced. He directs explorers to scout the mysterious landmass and delivers a pass to research the artifact within the archives of Stormwind. Having learned of strange apparitions and water elementals haunting an offshore island in Stranglethorn Vale, Baron Revilgaz sees an opportunity. Suspecting that the goblin mage Gazban may have uncovered the fabled Stone of the Tides, the ruler of Booty Bay sends you to locate the island and confirm whether the rumors are true. To satisfy any curiosity about the relic, he provides a library scrip redeemable among the scholars in Stormwind.

quest:58.text: The Night Watch. In eastern Raven Hill, The Night Watch calls on outsiders to enter the crypts. Commander Althea Ebonlocke sends them to destroy the plague spreaders while her guards defend Darkshire. This is the final mission in the town guard’s direct campaign against the undead overrun. Darkshire stands nearly alone, abandoned by Stormwind’s military and reliant on its civilian militia, The Night Watch. Commander Althea Ebonlocke has spent her limited manpower guarding the crossroads, town perimeter, and supply lines. As the restless dead multiply across Duskwood, she turns to wandering champions to carry the fight into Raven Hill’s shadowed depths. The eastern mausoleum in Raven Hill Cemetery holds one of the region’s most dangerous concentrations of undead, unlike the open barrows. Its stone crypt teems with plague spreaders, ghouls whose afflictions can sicken the living. Destroying twenty gives The Night Watch room to breathe and helps keep Darkshire from facing a coordinated undead surge from the west.

quest:581.text: Hunt for Yenniku. Nimboya has returned from Orgrimmar to the jungles of Stranglethorn Vale to search for Yenniku, the youngest son of his chieftain. Suspecting the Bloodscalp tribe holds the youth captive, the scout asks you to hunt their warriors and take their tusks to demonstrate your strength. At Grom'gol Base Camp, Nimboya speaks of a grim fate looming over Yenniku, the youngest son of the Darkspear chieftain. In accordance with an old tribal custom, the boy had been placed among the Gurubashi trolls of Zul'Gurub. When the Darkspear tribe departed their homeland alongside the orc warchief Thrall, Yenniku was left behind and lost. Sent back from distant Orgrimmar, Nimboya has undertaken the responsibility of finding the chieftain's son and bringing him to safety. Nimboya believes the Bloodscalp tribe now holds Yenniku. He demands proof that an adventurer is strong enough to hunt them. You are directed north to hunt Bloodscalp trolls and gather nine of their tusks. Bringing these trophies back to Grom'gol Base Camp proves your martial prowess and begins a longer pursuit to locate the chieftain's boy, leading directly into the hunt known as Headhunting.

quest:582.text: Headhunting. Nimboya at Grom'gol Base Camp needs to determine whether Yenniku, the son of the Darkspear chieftain, is dead. Adventurers are asked to hunt Bloodscalp headhunters and recover their shrunken heads so Nimboya can examine them. Following the search begun in Hunt for Yenniku, Nimboya worries that the chieftain's son may have already perished at the hands of the Bloodscalp tribe. To find out, he asks you to hunt the Bloodscalp Headhunters roaming the ruins of Zuuldaia and Zul'Kunda up the northern coast. By gathering twenty shrunken heads from them, Nimboya hopes to inspect the grisly trophies and confirm whether Yenniku met a violent end, cursing the Bloodscalp chief Gan'zulah if the youth was indeed slain.

quest:5821.text: Bodyguard for Hire. Cork Gizelton and Rigger would normally lead their kodo past the Kolkar centaur village, yet they stop whenever the centaur war drums are heard. Cork asks you to protect the caravan past the Kolkar village, and payment is waiting with Smeed Scrabblescrew, a bit down the road. Cork Gizelton and Rigger would normally take their kodo straight past the Kolkar centaur. Now and then the centaur war drums are heard, and the caravan stops, because dead traders make no profit. Cork asks you to guard the caravan past the Kolkar village, a short distance, and keep it in one piece. The caravan waits north of the Kolkar Village and southeast of Thunder Axe Fortress. Payment waits with Smeed Scrabblescrew at Scrabblescrew's Camp, a bit down the road. Smeed does a little business with the Gizelton caravan.

quest:583.text: Welcome to the Jungle. Barnil Stonepot welcomes newcomers arriving at the hunting camp in northern Stranglethorn Vale. Recognizing a fellow battle-tested wanderer, he arranges an introduction to the expedition's leader, the renowned huntsman Hemet Nesingwary. Barnil Stonepot greets newcomers at the camp in the jungle of Stranglethorn Vale, and he can tell a seasoned combatant when he sees one. He points out Hemet Nesingwary, a famous Alliance war hero and peerless tracker. Nesingwary reserves his fellowship for proven veterans, and Barnil believes the old marksman might be convinced to share his hunting wisdom with someone who has endured the trials of battle.

quest:5881.text: Calling in the Reserves. At Sun Rock Retreat, Calling in the Reserves sends you south to relieve a weary sentry at the Great Lift. Maggran Earthbinder gives you a letter for Grish Longrunner, who has stood watch far from home. Maggran Earthbinder keeps troop welfare and supplies in hand at Sun Rock Retreat in the Stonetalon Mountains. Across central Kalimdor, the Horde strains to keep its garrisons staffed, even in the years after the Third War. Maggran knows that endless watch duty wears seasoned soldiers down. He sends a reassignment letter south to the Great Lift, where Grish Longrunner has stood guard far from home. The Great Lift links the high southern Barrens to the canyons of Thousand Needles. When Grish receives Maggran's letter, he can leave his lonely watch over the lift mechanisms and return to his family. Fresh reserves can take his place.

quest:5925.text: Heeding the Call. Mathrengyl Bearwalker calls a young night elf druid to Darnassus to continue their training. As Archdruid Fandral Staghelm's direct assistant, he prepares the initiate for the trials of the bear. As your basic instruction among Teldrassil's boughs comes to an end, word arrives that Mathrengyl Bearwalker wishes to speak with you. He is the direct assistant to Archdruid Fandral Staghelm and one of the Cenarion Enclave's wisest elders. His summons calls you beyond basic wardenship and toward the deeper arts of nature. You travel to the Cenarion Enclave in Darnassus and climb to the second floor of Archdruid Staghelm's great tree. Bearwalker welcomes you and reminds you that those who answer Cenarius' call must honor plants and beasts as companions and charges. To preserve nature's balance, you need more than quiet reflection. You must learn the ways of the wild bear and master strength of body and heart.

quest:5929.text: Great Bear Spirit. In Moonglade, druids are sent north to seek the Great Bear Spirit. Communion with this ancient guide teaches the bear’s nature and strength, a vital part of a druid’s spiritual and martial training. In northwestern Moonglade, the Great Bear Spirit dwells apart from Nighthaven’s quiet paths. This ancient and noble mentor teaches every initiate who seeks to understand the bear’s nature. Druids have long sought its blessing and wisdom as part of the path of the wild. Dendrite Starblaze guides young druids from Nighthaven into the hills to meet the spirit. Communion brings primal wisdom and an awareness of natural strength. When the druids return, Dendrite tests their focus. The encounter gives them raw strength and knowing intent, but they must learn to direct that power in their daily work.

quest:5943.text: Gizelton Caravan. Rigger Gizelton and Cork launched their caravan to get rich, and found the trade more dangerous than they expected. Mannoroc Coven lies ahead, and Rigger wants a capable adventurer to guard the caravan past it. Rigger Gizelton and Cork set up the caravan to make a fortune, and had no idea how risky turning a profit could be. Mannoroc Coven lies ahead. The demons usually leave the caravan alone, but this time the kodos are spooked. Rigger offers payment if you protect the caravan past the coven. Once it is safely through, your pay waits with Smeed, a business associate of theirs, at Scrabblescrew's Camp.

quest:596.text: Bloody Bone Necklaces. Kin'weelay at Grom'gol Base Camp has his own agenda in Stranglethorn Vale beyond assisting Nimboya. He seeks to weaken the rival Bloodscalp tribe by gathering trophies from their warriors. Though Kin'weelay arrived in the jungle outpost of Grom'gol Base Camp to help Nimboya, he maintains private purposes of his own. The Bloodscalp trolls dwelling to the north are enemies of the Darkspears. Kin'weelay believes that claiming personal trophies from fallen foes bestows spiritual power over them, asking travelers to hunt Bloodscalp warriors and take the bloody bone necklaces they wear around their necks.

quest:601.text: Water Elementals. Following discoveries regarding the Stone of the Tides, Baron Revilgaz seeks a way to counteract the artifact's curse. He sends adventurers back to the island to harvest bracers from conjured water elementals so their magical residue can be inspected by experts. Believing the water elementals were summoned by the goblin wizard Gazban, Baron Revilgaz suspects their magical residue holds clues to dealing with the Stone of the Tides. The stone is said to curse anyone who wields it, causing the bearer to drift in and out of reality. To find a countermeasure, Revilgaz directs you back to the island off the coast to gather elemental bracers that might be scrutinized by the scholarly mages of Dalaran. Upon receiving the bracers, Revilgaz admits he lacks the specialized expertise to tell whether any of them will be of use. Rather than travel to Dalaran himself—he will not leave Booty Bay just to chat with tiresome old mages—he sends you north to have a mage look at them.

quest:602.text: Magical Analysis. Baron Revilgaz directs you northward from Booty Bay to consult the Kirin Tor in Dalaran. Taking a bag of water elemental bracers, you seek out Archmage Ansirem Runeweaver to decipher the arcane curse tied to the Stone of the Tides. Following your hunt for the water elemental bracers, Baron Revilgaz hands over a bundle of their bracers. The goblin leader knows that unraveling the curse behind the Stone of the Tides requires deeper magical expertise than Booty Bay can provide. He directs you north toward the ruins of Dalaran, where the wizards remain deeply engaged in rebuilding their broken kingdom. Convinced that arcane scholars cannot ignore an intriguing puzzle, Revilgaz recommends seeking Archmage Ansirem Runeweaver directly, having had dealings with the knowledgeable wizard in the past.

quest:6027.text: Book of the Ancients. Azore Aldamort of the Ethel Rethor tower trusts you with a gem. Set in the hand of a serpent statue on Ranazjar Isle, northwest of the tower, it calls up the protector of the Book of the Ancients, which holds secrets the naga have kept for centuries. After Sceptre of Light, Azore Aldamort hands you the Gem of the Serpent. A Serpent Statue stands on Ranazjar Isle, a little island to the northwest of the Ethel Rethor tower, and the gem belongs on its hand. That will bring forth the guardian of the Book of the Ancients, a book that holds naga secrets kept for centuries. Azore hopes it will teach much about their scaled foes.

quest:603.text: Ansirem's Key. Following his magical examination, Archmage Ansirem Runeweaver points toward an ancient troll dagger capable of disrupting the focal altar empowering the Stone of the Tides. He passed it long ago to his daughter Catelyn, a headstrong girl who left home for the pirates of Booty Bay. Ansirem Runeweaver determines that an altar or focal point amplifies the power of the Stone of the Tides. Overpowering that magic calls for another troll relic: an ancient dagger he found while researching in Stranglethorn. He passed it long ago to his daughter Catelyn, a headstrong girl who left home for the pirates of Booty Bay.

quest:605.text: Singing Blue Shards. Crank Fizzlebub seeks an enterprising adventurer to gather Singing Crystal Shards from the basilisks of Stranglethorn Vale. Competition with the Venture Company prevents him from harvesting the mineral deposits directly, leaving basilisk hides as the next best option. He promises a cut of the profits to anyone willing to bring him ten decent specimens. Crank Fizzlebub has identified an eager market for the Singing Crystals unique to Stranglethorn Vale. Unfortunately for his business ambitions, the aggressive presence of the Venture Company makes it hard for him to gather raw crystal in the field. To circumvent his rivals, Fizzlebub turns to an alternative method: basilisks consume the crystals, incorporating the mineral into their hardened hides, which allows usable shards to be retrieved from them instead. While any basilisk in the jungle might yield acceptable crystal fragments, Fizzlebub says the gentler ones are found along the shores south of Zul'Kunda, up north. Gathering ten shards allows him to move forward with his buyers, after which his business concerns shift toward the operations of the Venture Company itself.

quest:610.text: "Pretty Boy" Duncan. After tracking down Catelyn the Blade on behalf of her father, an adventurer learns that her weapon is no longer in her hands. She demands that her lost dagger be retrieved from a pirate named Pretty Boy Duncan before she cooperates further. Following the trail from Ansirem's Key leads directly to Catelyn the Blade, who ran away from a quiet life of scholarship and dusty tomes alongside mages. She cannot hand over her dagger at her father's request, since she no longer has it. If anyone hopes to secure her blade, they will first have to deal with the Bloodsail Buccaneer who took it. Catelyn suffered an uncharacteristic defeat at the hands of Pretty Boy Duncan, who struck her unconscious and made off with her signature weapon. As a fighter who relies on her personal knife, she insists on recovering that exact weapon from the buccaneer before anything else can move forward.

quest:6132.text: Get Me Out of Here!. Melizza Brimbuzzle traveled into the Valley of Spears hoping to do business with the Maraudines, but they would not talk, and she fears they mean to eat her. She asks you to get her out of there; her brother Hornizz will pay you handsomely. Melizza walked into the Valley of Spears to speak with the Maraudines, thinking she could strike a deal. They would not talk, and she suspects they would rather eat her. She says she overheard centaurs only minutes ago discussing wood for their cookpot, and she wants out quickly. Hornizz Brimbuzzle waits at the family camp, east of here and beside the kodo graveyard. Melizza promises that her brother will pay you well for bringing her out of the valley.

quest:6134.text: Ghost-o-plasm Round Up. Hornizz Brimbuzzle thinks there is money in the ghosts of the Valley of Bones. He figures the Magram centaurs would pay plenty for ghost energy, and he gives you a crate of ghost magnets to draw the spirits out. Hornizz points you southeast, to the Valley of Bones, where Magram ghosts walk. It sounds frightening, he admits, but surely it is scarier still for the Magram. He is sure that ghost energy captured there would be worth plenty to those centaurs. He hands you a crate of ghost magnets. Set down between the two huge skeletons in the valley, known as the Dead Goliaths, a magnet lures the ghosts toward it. From them you take ghost-o-plasm, which is what Hornizz plans to sell to the Magram. He wants eight ghost-o-plasms brought back to him, along with the crate.

quest:6141.text: Brother Anton. Brother Crowley speaks of Brother Anton, a fellow warrior who learned of undead in distant Kalimdor and booked passage at once to destroy them. Anton is looking for people with bravery and resolve, and waits in Nijel's Point in Desolace. Brother Crowley says rumors of an undead infestation in Desolace, a land in far-off Kalimdor, reached Anton, who immediately booked passage to seek and destroy the menace. Anton wants help from those with bravery and resolve. If your heart is true, Crowley tells you to speak with Anton in Nijel's Point, the Alliance town in Desolace.

quest:6142.text: Clam Bait. Mai'Lahii at Shadowprey Village has fished all his life and says the best bait is soft-shelled clam meat, which no fish can resist. He wants ten pieces, to be found around a wrecked ship up the coast to the north. Mai'Lahii has fished all his life, and he swears by soft-shelled clam meat as bait, since the fish cannot resist it. To the north, off the coast, lies a wrecked ship, and soft-shelled clams are scattered throughout that area. He asks for ten pieces of the meat.

quest:6143.text: Other Fish to Fry. Drulzegar Skraghook, a fisherman at Shadowprey Village in Desolace, lost the entire crew to the naga while fishing near Ranazjar Isle. Guilt weighs on Drulzegar, who asks you to go after the Slitherblade. Drulzegar Skraghook and the crew fished by Ranazjar Isle, which lies north of a wreck on the coast, and had done so many times. One morning the naga attacked and killed everyone except Drulzegar. Since then revenge is all Drulzegar thinks about, and the guilt is too much to bear. Drulzegar wants seven Slitherblade Myrmidons, seven Slitherblade Naga and five Slitherblade Sorceresses slain. A bad knee keeps Drulzegar from going along. The naga, Drulzegar says, usually lurk far down among the coral reefs beneath the waves, and the effort will be rewarded.

quest:616.text: The Haunted Isle. Krazek keeps his ears open for unusual rumors throughout Booty Bay on behalf of Baron Revilgaz. A tale shared by tavern sailors speaks of a haunted island off the coast, inhabited by water elementals and the ghost of a raving goblin. Delivering this rumor to Revilgaz piques the baron's interest in an ancient troll legend. In the bustling port of Booty Bay, Krazek gathers word of anything unusual happening throughout Stranglethorn Vale at the request of Baron Revilgaz. While Krazek normally pays little heed to spectral gossip, stories told by sailors drinking in the local tavern caught his attention. They speak of an offshore isle occupied by water elementals and haunted by a raving goblin ghost, so he asks you to relay the story to the baron. Upon hearing Krazek's report of the haunted isle, Baron Revilgaz recalls an old troll legend he once read about in a book. The presence of water elementals and the goblin apparition leads the baron to suspect that an ancient relic, the Stone of the Tides, might finally be within his grasp to add to his personal collection of artifacts.

quest:6161.text: Claim Rackmore's Treasure!. Rackmore's log tells of a ship bound for Feathermoon Stronghold that was set upon by creatures of the sea. To keep his treasure from his enemies, Rackmore hid the chest on Ranazjar Isle, and the silver key and golden key that open it are lost. The log says Rackmore's ship was on its way to Feathermoon Stronghold when seafaring creatures attacked it. Hoping to keep his treasure from his enemies, he hid the chest on Ranazjar Isle. Two keys open it, one silver and one gold, and both were lost. Someone who finds the keys and the chest will find a treasure.

quest:627.text: Favor for Krazek. While repairing a crock pot brought down to Booty Bay, the goblin Krazek demands a personal favor in return. He wants rare lesser bloodstone ore retrieved from a distant cave in the northern hills before he will hand back the repaired cookware. After accepting the broken cookware in Booty Bay, Krazek pauses his tinkering to ask for a trade. Rather than repairing the pot for free, he directs you far northward into the Arathi Highlands. Within a cave in Drywhisker Gorge lies lesser bloodstone ore, a low-grade yet prized mineral sought after by those who understand its properties. Krazek promises to work on fixing the pot while you make the long journey north. He expects four loads of the bloodstone brought back to the port, offering payment in exchange for the favor if you return with enough samples. He also makes it clear that if you lack the knowledge to extract the ore yourself, you will need to rely on someone who does.

quest:6282.text: Harpies Threaten. In the Charred Vale, Bloodfury harpies threaten the routes west of Sun Rock Retreat. Maggran Earthbinder sends Horde warriors to cull their growing ranks and protect travel through Stonetalon. Tauren at Sun Rock Retreat protect Stonetalon and its peaceful travelers. Maggran Earthbinder, the retreat’s elder leader, has watched the harpy numbers rise. The Bloodfury coven has spread through the scorched Charred Vale, harrying beasts and choking off routes. If their flocks keep growing, Sun Rock Retreat could be isolated. The Charred Vale lies west of Sun Rock Retreat, a wasteland of ash, scorched earth, and smoldering trees left by catastrophic fires. Bloodfury harpies nest high in the charred remains of ancient woods and have made the vale their stronghold. Maggran sends Horde warriors into the hostile caldera to cull dozens of harpies: Bloodfury ambushers, slayers, and roguefeathers. Thinning the flock weakens the coven’s immediate grip on the vale and clears the way to confront its matriarchal lineage.

quest:6283.text: Bloodfury Bloodline. In the Charred Vale, Maggran Earthbinder seeks to end the harpies’ hold. He sends you to kill their leader, Bloodfury Ripper, and bring back proof. Harpies at the edge of the Charred Vale keep threatening Sun Rock Retreat. Maggran Earthbinder believes their attacks will only end when their matriarch, Bloodfury Ripper, is dead. The flock treats her like a queen, and her leadership gives them the unity and boldness they show along the craggy western ridge. Bloodfury Ripper’s remains are the proof Maggran asks you to bring back. With the brood queen gone, the harpies lose their order and become easier to keep at bay, easing the threat to Sun Rock Retreat. Her death also lifts Maggran’s burden of anger and constant watchfulness, leaving him free to seek the harmony and balance the tauren value.

quest:6284.text: Arachnophobia. A Horde bounty sends you west of Windshear Crag after Besseleth, the ancient spider haunting southern Stonetalon Mountains. Claim her fang for Maggran Earthbinder at Sun Rock Retreat, and the mountain roads may grow safer for travelers after dark. A weathered wanted poster warns travelers on the main road south of Windshear Crag of dangers to the west. Sishir Canyon and Webwinder Path are overrun by spiders. At the heart of the threat is Besseleth, an unusually large orange spider who commands her brood. After sunset, she ambushes anyone who strays from the path. Maggran Earthbinder, a tauren at Sun Rock Retreat, has posted the bounty on Besseleth. He nearly died in an earlier encounter, when her massive two-foot fang struck him. Maggran fought her off and limped to safety, but the wound still reminds him of the danger in the canyon shadows. He hopes an adventurer will bring him Besseleth's Fang and secure the passes, so trade and travel to Sun Rock Retreat can continue without fear.

quest:629.text: The Vile Reef. Kin'weelay at Grom'gol Base Camp seeks a piece of an ancient stone tablet resting deep beneath the Savage Coast. The sunken city, known as the Vile Reef, is infested with aggressive murlocs and holds the legendary history of Gri'lek, which the Darkspear tribe wishes to preserve in Orgrimmar. Northwest of Grom'gol Base Camp, an ancient troll city slipped beneath the waters along the Savage Coast when a violent earthquake shattered the land long ago. Now referred to as the Vile Reef, its flooded ruins crawl with hostile murlocs that assault anyone venturing near. Resting on the sea floor among the ruins is a massive stone tablet carved with the story of Gri'lek, a legendary troll hero whose memory remains sacred to the Darkspear. Because the full monument is far too massive to carry away from the depths, Kin'weelay asks you to break off a shard from the stone. He intends to carry this fragment back to Orgrimmar, enshrining it in a sacred place so the Darkspear will never forget the strength and honor of Gri'lek.

quest:63.text: Call of Water. Across the sea, Call of Water carries Barrens shamans to Silverpine Forest. There, an initiate faces the blight on an ancient coastal shrine to earn communion with water spirits. After gathering drops of pure water with help from the hermit Brine, you return to Islen Waterseer on the Barrens coast. She sends you across the sea with the purified essence to Silverpine Forest's haunted shore, just west of the Forsaken refuge called the Sepulcher.

quest:6301.text: Cycle of Rebirth. At Sun Rock Retreat, Tammra Windfield seeks Gaea seeds to help heal Stonetalon. She asks the Horde to gather the rare seeds from Mirkfallon Lake, hoping to bless them and restore the mountain’s damaged soil. Stonetalon’s peaks bear wounds from commercial exploitation and regional conflict. Logging and clashes between rival factions have left forests scorched, cut down, or reduced to ash. For the tauren stationed at Sun Rock Retreat, the rapid destruction of the natural world is a grievous wound. Shamans like Tammra Windfield seek the Earthmother’s restorative cycle as they work to mend the land. Tammra seeks rare Gaea seeds around Mirkfallon Lake, north of Sun Rock Retreat. The lake’s banks nurture sturdy seed pods along the water’s edge. These seeds have a resilience unique to Stonetalon, though danger surrounds the region. Once they are gathered, Tammra channels ancestral shamanistic blessings into each kernel, awakening its power to speed its growth.

quest:631.text: The Thandol Span. After a blast shatters the northern crossing, Rhag Garmason asks travelers to search for a missing dwarf scout. The Dark Iron clan has attacked Dun Modr, cutting off communication and stranding its defenders without reinforcements. Ol' Rustlocke may hold a clue to the sabotage. A blast has torn through the bridge between Wetlands and the Arathi Highlands. Bronzebeard soldiers at the border were caught in the devastation when Dark Iron dwarves attacked Dun Modr. Their ranks are thinned, and their strongholds are under siege. The survivors, led by Longbraid the Grim, hold their ground against the attackers. Longbraid sent veteran scout Ebenezer Rustlocke to inspect the eastern span and see whether a crossing or a northern route remained usable. Days have passed without a report. Dun Modr is under siege, and Rhag Garmason and the garrison have too few soldiers to search the enemy-held rubble for him.

quest:633.text: The Thandol Span. On the Thandol Span, a murder exposes a threat to Ironforge's northern road. Ebenezer Rustlocke has been killed, and Rhag Garmason finds that Kam Deepfury has hidden explosives to cut that route. A recovered document reveals what happened beneath the Thandol Span. Ebenezer Rustlocke was murdered in its substructure, and the papers expose a further act of sabotage. Kam Deepfury, the Dark Iron agitator who first destroyed part of the bridge, has not stopped. His network planted a second cache of heavy munitions just across the northern border in the Arathi Highlands, ready to finish the destruction.

quest:634.text: Plea To The Alliance. At the shattered Thandol Span, Plea To The Alliance carries a desperate call for aid from Dun Modr's dwarven survivors. Dark Iron infiltrators slaughtered the garrison, and the dwarves appeal to the human forces at Refuge Pointe, though the Alliance is stretched thin. Dun Modr lies devastated, and Dark Iron dwarves have sabotaged the Thandol Span. The survivors hold a precarious foothold at the Wetlands' northern rim. Ironforge's main reserves have yet to arrive, so Rhag Garmason and Longbraid the Grim look north to the Arathi Highlands. They learn that Alliance forces have made camp at Refuge Pointe. Garmason sends an emissary across the shattered bridge to ask Captain Nials for urgent military aid. At Refuge Pointe, Captain Nials offers sympathy to Longbraid's soldiers, but cannot spare a single fighter. Stromgarde has fallen into ruin, overrun by Syndicate rogues, Boulderfist ogres, and Witherbark trolls. Its surviving defenders are committed to reclaiming their ancestral capital. Bound by honor and pressed by their own desperate struggle, Nials sends word that the dwarves at the Span must stand alone.

quest:635.text: Crystal in the Mountains. The Pendant of Myzrael pulses in your hand and a pleading reaches you, as if someone desperately needs help. A vision shows a gleaming crystal rising out of the ground in the northern mountains of Arathi, and you feel drawn to that place. The pendant pulses as you hold it. From it comes a sense of pleading, as if someone is trying to reach you and badly needs your help. Then a vision opens before you: the mountains in the north of Arathi, and a gleaming crystal thrusting up out of the ground. You feel drawn to that place.

quest:637.text: Sully Balloo's Letter. At the Thandol Span, Sully Balloo's Letter carries a dwarf's last words to his wife in Ironforge. Found beneath the bridge, it tells where he died. Beneath the stone pilings of the Thandol Span, the land bridge between the Wetlands and the Arathi Highlands, a drowned skeleton still clutches an envelope. Its water-damaged pages begin, “My dear Sara,” and preserve the tenderness of Sully Balloo's careful writing. Alliance forces and their enemies have fought fiercely for the Thandol Span. Dark Iron saboteurs and warbands contesting the borderlands have threatened the crossing. Sully Balloo was among the dwarven soldiers sent north to defend it. His family in the mountains knew nothing of his fate until a diver brought his farewell letter up from beneath the waves.

quest:638.text: Trollbane. Vol'jin has ordered the Darkspear trolls to recover the ancient sword Trol'kalar from the ruined human kingdom of Stromgarde. With King Thoras Trollbane fallen, the blade is meant to serve the Horde in future conflicts against the trolls of Zul'Gurub. Following the death of King Thoras Trollbane and the collapse of Stromgarde into ruin, Chieftain Vol'jin has ordered that every effort be made to spirit Trol'kalar away. This storied blade has long rested in human hands, but the Darkspear tribe hopes to claim it for the battles looming against the jungle trolls dwelling within Zul'Gurub. To carry out Vol'jin's directive, a seasoned hunter named Zengu was sent to the Horde outpost of Hammerfall, situated in the northeastern reaches of the Arathi Highlands. Nimboya directs travelers from Stranglethorn Vale to seek out Zengu and assist in securing the legendary weapon.

quest:6381.text: New Life. Tammra Windfield sends travelers west from Sun Rock Retreat to plant Gaea seeds in the Charred Vale. She hopes the scorched land can begin to heal. Tammra Windfield sends you into the Charred Vale, where soot, fire elementals, and harpies haunt the ruined ground. She trusts in the Earth Mother's resilience and asks you to find Gaea Dirt Mounds, where fertile soil survived the fire. Gaea seeds can take root despite the lingering elemental corruption. Their roots form an ecological anchor against decay and invite plants back into the valley. Tammra hopes that, as life reclaims the basin, the fire spirits will settle, the harpies will lose their desolate roost, and the Venture Company's logging will eventually be driven out.

quest:6382.text: The Ashenvale Hunt. In Ashenvale, Horde hunters face a new test beneath the ancient trees. Jorn Skyseer at Camp Taurajo sends proven hunters north to Splintertree Post, where Senani Thunderheart awaits. Horde hunters who have proven themselves in the Barrens are sent toward Ashenvale. Jorn Skyseer sees when a traveler has outgrown the local game and points the way north. For the young Horde, these old forests offer resources and mark a political and spiritual frontier they must learn to understand and claim. The road north passes the Mor'shan Rampart before reaching Splintertree Post, a fortified Horde camp deep among the trees. The tauren huntress Senani Thunderheart welcomes experienced hunters seeking harder tests of survival. The Horde depends on skilled trackers to face Ashenvale's native predators and the watchful defenders of the forest.

quest:6383.text: The Ashenvale Hunt. In Ashenvale, Horde hunters face the ancient forest's three great predators. Senani Thunderheart oversees the trial at Splintertree Post, where hunters track Ursangous, Shadumbra, and Sharptalon to prove their skill. Senani Thunderheart gives the Horde's presence in Ashenvale a different kind of test. While Orcs gather lumber, she sends hunters into the shadowed forest to face its strongest predators. The hunt calls for more than strength: hunters must meet the wilderness with cunning and respect, and learn what they can endure. Three solitary beasts test those who take up the hunt. Ursangous, an immense elder bear, roams near the Talondeep Path. Shadumbra, a cunning nightsaber, stalks the eastern borders near Raynewood Retreat and the Laughing Sisters. South of Splintertree Post, Sharptalon, a fierce hippogryph, wheels above the forest canopy.

quest:639.text: Sigil of Strom. Zengu in Hammerfall wants the sigils that guard Trol'kalar, the sword of Lord Ignaeus Trollbane. The first, the Sigil of Strom, was taken by the Syndicate, and a Syndicate agent in Stromgarde is likely to hold it. In ancient times the trolls fought the Arathorian Empire, and their ablest foe was Lord Ignaeus of Strom, called Trollbane. He went into battle wielding Trol'kalar, a name that means troll slayer in the trolls' old tongue. Now Trollbane's sons are weakened and their stronghold lies in ruins. Several sigils protect the sword, and the survivors of Stromgarde each took a share of them. Zengu says they must all be retrieved. The Syndicate seized the first, and Zengu reckons one of their agents in Stromgarde has it. Bring it back to him at Hammerfall.

quest:6393.text: Elemental War. Elemental War is a task undertaken for Tsunaman, an envoy of the water elementals residing at Sun Rock Retreat in Stonetalon Mountains. Guided by the will of Neptulon the Tidehunter, adventurers are sent into the scorched depths of the Charred Vale to extinguish blazing fire elementals and collect their smoldering Incendrite cores. It provides a rare glimpse into the ancient, perpetual rivalry that divides the elemental planes. In the rugged reaches of Stonetalon Mountains, an envoy named Tsunaman has arrived at Sun Rock Retreat on behalf of the Tribunal of the Tides. Acting under the supreme will of Neptulon the Tidehunter, the lord of water elementals, Tsunaman seeks to carry out an ancient vendetta against their fiery kin. Rather than a dispute over mortal borders, this conflict represents the unending clash of Azeroth's primal forces. The primary battleground for this struggle is the Charred Vale, a scarred wasteland smoldering in southern Stonetalon Mountains. Fire elementals thrive amidst the ashes, threatening the surrounding regions. Adventurers are enlisted to descend into the vale, snuff out these flame-wreathed entities, and gather Incendrites—blazing remnants left behind upon an elemental's defeat—to prove their destruction to the Tribunal.

quest:6394.text: Thazz'ril's Pick. Foreman Thazz'ril accidentally left his favorite enchanted mining pick deep inside the northern cavern during a mineral survey. Now overrun by dangerous beasts, the cave known as the Burning Blade Coven holds the glowing tool awaiting recovery. Foreman Thazz'ril, the supervisor overseeing work details in the Valley of Trials, previously ventured into the northern cavern to prospect for mineral veins. While surveying the rocky interior, he accidentally left behind his prized mining pick. By the time he realized his mistake and returned to fetch it, vicious beasts and hostile inhabitants had overtaken the cavern, forcing the foreman to seek assistance from capable recruits to recover his lost tool. To make his prized pick easier to use in dim subterranean depths, Thazz'ril enchanted it with a spell that causes it to glow in the dark. This magical illumination allows adventurers to easily spot the implement resting inside a waterfall chamber within the Burning Blade Coven, though retrieving it requires facing whatever dangerous creatures prowl the cavern shadows. Once returned, Thazz'ril hopes to put the pick back to work uncovering new mining opportunities across the valley.

quest:642.text: The Princess Trapped. The Princess Trapped begins when adventurers uncover an iridescent crystal shard in the Arathi Highlands and hear the plea of Myzrael, a self-styled princess of the earth imprisoned deep underground. Claiming she was trapped by hostile giants, she begs travelers to confront their kobold allies in Drywhisker Gorge and restore power to her crystalline communication network. Scattered across the rolling plains of the Arathi Highlands, strange crystal shards hum with distant power. Approaching them reveals a desperate voice echoing from deep subterranean caverns: Myzrael, a self-proclaimed princess of the earth. She claims that ancient giants cast her down and bound her far beneath the soil, cutting her off from the sunlit lands above. The crystals embedded in the earth represent her sole means of contacting the surface, carrying her pleas for salvation to any adventurer willing to listen. To maintain her tenuous contact and begin breaking through her subterranean isolation, Myzrael directs travelers eastward toward Drywhisker Gorge. The gorge is infested with Drywhisker kobolds, creatures she identifies as allies of her giant captors. These kobolds carry resonant Motes of Myzrael and guard a prominent cluster of iridescent shards. By wresting these motes from the kobolds and applying their energy to the formation, rescuers can empower the crystal cluster and deepen their communication with the trapped princess.

quest:647.text: MacKreel's Moonshine. Foggy MacKreel sleeps through his watch on the broken Thandol Span after drinking too much of his own moonshine. Now he needs an Alliance traveler to hurry a fresh batch to Brewmeister Bilger in Southshore and settle his debt. Foggy MacKreel keeps watch on the shattered Thandol Span, where the hours are wet, cold, and dull. To bear the damp chill, he drinks his homemade moonshine, a brew so fierce he likens its aftereffects to siege engines pounding across his skull. One drink too many leaves him passed out through his shift. Longbraid the Grim commands the dwarves defending the Span, and Foggy cannot afford another lapse in discipline. Foggy also owes Brewmeister Bilger in Southshore a longstanding debt. He promised a batch of his personal brew to settle the account, but his hangover and watch duties leave him minutes from missing the deadline. With gryphons and swift feet, you race across the Arathi Highlands to Southshore with the jug, before Bilger decides Foggy has skipped out on his tab again.

quest:6481.text: Earthen Arise. In Boulderslide Ravine, Mor'rogal finds Goggeroc asleep inside a Resonite cask. The tauren shaman fears what the ancient Earthen could do to Kalimdor, and sends a champion to break the cask and kill Goggeroc before its strength returns. Scouts searching Boulderslide Ravine for vermin found a strange relic among the kobolds: a Resonite cask filled with unearthly force. Mor'rogal, a tauren shaman in the Stonetalon Mountains, recognized it as both prison and sanctuary for Goggeroc, a dormant Earthen. These ancient beings of stone can outmatch mortal warriors, and Goggeroc's freedom could threaten the whole region.

quest:6503.text: Ashenvale Outrunners. Night elf scouts have slipped out from Silverwing Outpost into Ashenvale. Kuray'bin calls for a strike against the Ashenvale Outrunners before they can report on Horde encampments and defenses. Night elf scouts from Silverwing Outpost are moving through the woods east of their base and south of nearby Horde holdings. In Ashenvale's contested forest, they watch the paths and ridges, mapping fortifications and tracking troop movements. Kuray'bin has learned that these scouts, known as Ashenvale Outrunners, have slipped into the wilderness to gather intelligence. The Horde strikes at enemy scouts before they can return to Silverwing Outpost. Hunting down the outrunners denies its commanders knowledge of Horde troop strength and outpost defenses. Without their forward eyes, the night elves are left disoriented and less willing to risk aggressive moves through the contested woods.

quest:6504.text: The Lost Pages. A gust has scattered The Lost Pages across Ashenvale. Gurda Ragescar is stranded near Splintertree Post, unable to run the shredder she is taking from Ratchet to the Warsong Lumber Camp without its manual. The Warsong Clan uses steam-powered shredders bought from Ratchet to clear lumber across Ashenvale. Their delicate workings are not easy for an orc warrior to master. As Gurda Ragescar carried a newly bought shredder north, a sudden gust tore the instruction booklet from her hands. Twelve parchment leaves scattered across the forest floor. The wind carried the manual pages across Ashenvale, and wandering creatures, cultists, and forest denizens have taken them. The shredder cannot run without all three chapters. Gurda is stranded on the road to Splintertree Post, unable to report for logging duty.

quest:6546.text: Warsong Outrider Update. A Warsong scout keeps watch along eastern Ashenvale’s perilous paths. Warsong Outrider Update carries intelligence about nearby Alliance forces, entrenched satyr, and naga moving through neighboring Azshara. A lone Warsong Outrider watches the contested eastern edge of Ashenvale. Horde supply lines face constant harassment here, so the outriders scout enemy movements before raiding parties can strike Mor'shan Rampart or Splintertree Post. Meeting one on patrol means the forest is under watch, and the report he carries may help decide whether a Horde fortification holds or falls to ambush. A Warsong Outrider’s report describes danger across Kalimdor’s central forests. Night elves and the wider Alliance remain a threat, while cunning, demonic satyr haunt eastern Ashenvale. Scouts have also found a massive naga presence spreading through the ruined coastal lands of neighboring Azshara. The Horde faces hostile powers from almost every direction.

quest:6547.text: Warsong Scout Update. Orders from Kadrak reach Warsong Scout Update as scouts watch the contested woods. The Horde depends on their reports to guard its positions in Ashenvale against night elf attacks. Kadrak depends on scattered Warsong scouts to watch the Ashenvale border. The forest gives night elf sentinels cover, and the scouts face the risk of being cut off. Couriers carry written updates between them so isolated outposts can report what they see and remain connected to Horde command. Warsong scouts watch for night elf raids meant to reclaim the forest. Every stretch of Ashenvale the clan has cleared or occupied has cost lives. Kadrak's orders keep the forward scouts in touch with the Horde and give them a way to report that their defenses are holding against elven resistance.

quest:655.text: Hammerfall. Hammerfall recounts the tragic fall of Warchief Orgrim Doomhammer during the liberation of an Alliance internment camp in the Arathi Highlands. Through the grief-stricken memories of Gor'mul, travelers learn how the camp was freed and why the stronghold bears its solemn name. Hammerfall was once a grim Alliance internment camp where captive orcs were kept behind wood and steel after the Second War. That changed when young Thrall and Warchief Orgrim Doomhammer launched an assault to shatter the enclosures and free their kin. Though the raid succeeded in freeing many captives and bringing down the camp's defenses, it ended in tragedy when Doomhammer was struck from behind by a mounted lance, dying on the very soil where the Horde settlement now stands. Not every captive found freedom on that fateful day. In the chaos of battle and the tremors of the earth, an orc named Gor'mul watched the legendary Warchief fall and lost all will to fight. Left behind as his brethren fled, Gor'mul spent years wandering the highlands in directionless grief. Even now that the Horde has reclaimed the site as a fortified base, the memory of that cowardly strike continues to haunt those who survived it.

quest:65601.text: Love Hurts. Gan'rul sends you along Orgrimmar's main drag to find Magar. His longing for Krilge may reveal the object Gan'rul needs to lure an incubus into the world. East of the Cleft of Shadow, Magar longs for Krilge to return. He asks you to search for something precious. Bring that object to Gan'rul, who needs a token of love and devotion to summon an incubus.

quest:6561.text: Blackfathom Villainy. Inside Blackfathom Deeps, Blackfathom Villainy reaches a wounded scout who cannot finish his mission alone. Argent Dawn scout Thaelrid asks passing Horde champions to end Twilight Lord Kelris's blood sacrifices to Aku'mai in the sunken ruins. Argent Dawn scout Thaelrid lies wounded in the underground temple along the Ashenvale coast. His reconnaissance uncovered horrors beyond naga incursions, but his strength is spent and he cannot complete the mission alone. He calls on passing Horde champions to strike at the cult's leaders in the sunken halls. Twilight Lord Kelris leads the Twilight's Hammer cultists within the ruined Temple of the Moon. With the local naga, he performs dark rites over the defiled Moon Well. Captives are fed alive to Aku'mai, a ravenous hydra and beast of the Old Gods, as Kelris seeks cosmic power and primordial chaos.

quest:65610.text: Wish You Were Here. A mooncloth maker in Ashenvale asks you to find Krilge, who vanished while guarding civilians. His comrades call him a deserter, but the maker believes he held his post. A mooncloth maker met Krilge while making mooncloth in Ashenvale. Krilge was stationed there to protect civilians, then disappeared. They often met at Fallen Sky Lake, until aggressive bog beasts overran it. The maker still hopes to learn what became of him. You are asked to search Fallen Sky Lake and report your findings to Gan'rul Bloodeye in Orgrimmar. Krilge's comrades have stopped looking for him. Perhaps the lake still holds a sign of what became of him.

quest:6562.text: Trouble in the Deeps. Tsunaman sends Horde travelers from Stonetalon Mountains to aid Je'neu Sancrea on Ashenvale's remote coast. The troll scholar waits at Zoram'gar Outpost, where danger gathers along the shore. Tsunaman hears troubling reports from the north and calls on Horde travelers to reach Je'neu Sancrea. The troll scholar is at Zoram'gar Outpost, on Ashenvale's far western shore, the Zoram Strand. Je'neu faces mounting danger and needs help from beyond the outpost. The road to Ashenvale's western shore is dangerous for Horde travelers. You can pass through Windshear Crag, disturbed by goblins, or travel north from the Barrens. Either way, you enter forest watched by night elf sentinels. Far beneath Ashenvale's dense canopy, Zoram'gar Outpost holds on along the storm-washed Zoram Strand, facing the shadowed waters.

quest:6563.text: The Essence of Aku'Mai. Je'neu Sancrea has found the naga harvesting sapphires in Blackfathom Deeps. At Zoram'gar Outpost, the shaman asks Horde adventurers to recover them before their power is misused. Je'neu Sancrea watches over the Kaldorei ruins from the Zoram Strand. Naga now mine sapphire clusters in the submerged chambers of Blackfathom Deeps, where the gems grow along damp cavern walls. Sancrea senses the serpentine invaders mean to harness their power and seeks to stop the harvest before they can use it. The Sapphires of Aku'mai carry elemental water energy and hold clinging water spirits. Adept sorcerers could use them to fuel dangerous arcane rituals or strengthen Aku'mai, the shadowy hydra whose presence fills the subterranean temple. Recovering the clusters keeps this potent reagent from the naga and helps guard the coastline against unchecked elemental magic.

quest:6564.text: Allegiance to the Old Gods. Horde scouts find a waterlogged message inside Blackfathom Deeps. You carry the naga's note to Je'neu Sancrea at Zoram'gar Outpost, where its words reveal a ritual plot deep within the flooded ruins. Horde scouts find a damp, crumpled note while battling the naga in Blackfathom Deeps. Its frantic handwriting gives orders to the naga priestesses: gather elemental water crystals. The crystals are not for random pillaging. They will fuel the summonings of naga aquamancers, who are marshaling elemental forces for a darker purpose.

quest:6565.text: Allegiance to the Old Gods. At Zoram'gar, the Horde moves against the Twilight's Hammer cult in Blackfathom Deeps. Je'neu Sancrea sends champions after Lorgus Jett to disrupt the cultists who seek to awaken ancient forces of destruction beneath Ashenvale's coast. Zoram'gar Outpost watches Blackfathom Deeps from the Ashenvale shore. Naga, corrupted beasts, and Twilight's Hammer fanatics overrun the submerged temple complex. Je'neu Sancrea, an Earthen Ring seer stationed on the coast, sees that the cultists serve the Old Gods rather than the land's natural balance and spirits. These monstrous beings of chaos were defeated in ancient times, yet their malign touch still lingers in Azeroth's forgotten places. Je'neu sends Horde champions into the underground ruins to hunt Lorgus Jett, a key leader among the cultists established in Blackfathom Deeps. Lorgus works deep in the stone passages between the chambers of Ghamoo-ra, the giant turtle, and Baron Aquanis, the water elemental. Je'neu is too frail to enter the damp darkness himself. Lorgus's defeat is vital to severing the dark rituals he sought to orchestrate beneath Ashenvale's waves.

quest:657.text: Hints of a New Plague?. Kinelory needs your protection while she seeks Jorell’s remaining research at Go'Shek Farm. Quae has learned from the folder that Apothecary Jorell is conducting deadly experiments there, but she is too hurt to help after clashing with orcs. The folder reveals Jorell’s deadly experiments at Go'Shek Farm. Quae does not know how they affect Hillsbrad, but Phin would not want them to continue. Some of Jorell’s research has already reached Tarren Mill. Quae clashed with some orcs while you were away and cannot help Kinelory. Kinelory plans to go to the farm and steal the research Jorell has not yet sent to Tarren Mill. She will need your protection.

quest:6571.text: Warsong Supplies. At Splintertree Post, Locke Okarr needs supplies to keep the Warsong Lumber Camp running. Some await in town, some in Booty Bay, and others lie in enemy hands across Ashenvale. Locke Okarr works to keep the Warsong Lumber Camp supplied from Splintertree Post. The Warsong Clan needs a steady flow of heavy tools to harvest Ashenvale's ancient timber. Raids by furbolgs and satyrs have scattered or seized local supplies, leaving the camp short of vital gear. You gather equipment from across Kalimdor and beyond. Pixel, the goblin courier at Splintertree Post, has circular saw blades, while Wharfmaster Lozgil in Booty Bay holds a crate of heavy axes. Foulweald and Thistlefur furbolgs have taken logging ropes, and satyrs at Night Run, Satyrnaar, and Xavian have stolen barrels of Warsong machinery oil for their profane rites.

quest:658.text: Hints of a New Plague?. At Go'Shek Farm, Quae and Kin have watched for days. Kin saw a courier leave a small house to the south, and they suspect she carries notes to Tarren Mill. Quae asks if you are a skilled tracker and wants the documents. Quae expected Phin Odelic to send you, since he worries too much. Quae and Kin have watched the farm for days. Kin recently saw a courier leave a small house to the south. Kin talks often, but Quae trusts Kin's senses in dangerous places. Quae asks if you are a skilled tracker. The courier may carry notes bound for Tarren Mill, and the documents could shed light on what is happening in Hillsbrad. You are to find the Forsaken Courier and bring her Sealed Folder to Quae near Go'Shek Farm. While you search, Kin spots an apothecary leaving that same house. Quae suspects the apothecary is up to no good, but needs proof before anyone acts rashly.

quest:6581.text: Warsong Saw Blades. At Splintertree Post, the Warsong loggers wait on blades from Ratchet. Pixel, their courier, will trade the shipment for a weapon to protect herself on Ashenvale's dangerous roads. The blades are needed to keep the Horde's lumber camps working. Pixel has brought heavy saw blades from Ratchet to Splintertree Post, but she will not hand them over for free. In Ashenvale's wilds, she values safety more than coin. She asks for a Deadly Blunderbuss in trade, so she can protect herself on her dangerous travels through hostile territory. The Horde needs timber from Ashenvale to ease shortages across Durotar and the Barrens. Axes dull quickly against the ancient groves, so the Warsong loggers need goblin-forged blades. Pixel's shipment supplies the lumber camps, where the Horde cuts timber for outposts and war machines despite fierce resistance from the night elves.

quest:659.text: Hints of a New Plague?. In Hillsbrad, Phin Odelic's companions search for signs of trouble. Quae and Kinelory have been missing for days since heading to Go'Shek Farm in the Arathi Highlands. Phin Odelic's cousin in Hillsbrad had to put down his dog, Stanley. The beast had mystically grown huge and savagely attacked anyone who came near. Phin believes the undead are involved in these odd happenings, and his band searches for signs to prove it. Quae and Kinelory, Phin Odelic's companions, headed to Go'Shek Farm in the Arathi Highlands. They have not checked in for days, and Phin fears for them. He wants you to find them near the farm.

quest:66.text: The Legend of Stalvan. In Darkshire, The Legend of Stalvan begins with Madame Eva's vision of death for her granddaughter, Alyssa. Her cards and trance leave one name: Stalvan. She sends travelers to the Darkshire Town Hall to search the records. Madame Eva reads cards and portents for troubled locals in Darkshire. After a terrible disturbance jolts her awake, she draws the Death card for her young granddaughter, Alyssa. Eva enters a deep trance, seeking what the omen means, but finds only one clue: the name Stalvan. Fearing for her family and the town, she asks you to follow that name before tragedy strikes. Madame Eva sends you across the square to the Darkshire Town Hall to search its records for Stalvan. There you can speak with Clerk Daltry, who keeps the town's ledgers and public archives. He can help determine whether Stalvan once lived in Darkshire, passed through as a traveler, or is a name buried in Duskwood's past.

quest:660.text: Hints of a New Plague?. Kinelory is ready to return to Quae, and asks you to go with her to the farm. She fears the undead may harm Hillsbrad while they wait, and she needs you to see her safely back. Kinelory is ready to act after the earlier steps of the investigation. She asks you to go with her down to the farm, then see her safely back to Quae. Anyone who cares about the people of Hillsbrad is urged to protect her.

quest:661.text: Hints of a New Plague?. In Arathi, Quae and Kinelory stay while you carry news to Southshore. Quae has the items from the farm, and Kinelory has returned safely. Quae is pleased with how you cared for Kinelory. She says Kinelory is in better shape than after a night at the tavern. The items from the farm should help Phin Odelic understand what is happening in Arathi. Since the farm was attacked, Quae and Kinelory plan to stay there a little longer in case anyone retaliates. They ask you to return to Southshore and speak with Phin.

quest:6621.text: King of the Foulweald. Karang Amakkar orders a Horde strike against the Foulweald furbolgs southeast of Astranaar. Horde champions plant a war banner on the tribe’s sacred totem mound, drawing out Chief Murgut and killing him. Karang Amakkar at Zoram'gar Outpost sees the corrupted Foulweald as a danger to the Horde. The tribe is smaller than the northern Thistlefur, but its members are fierce. Rather than wait for them to ambush Horde patrols, Karang orders a show of force meant to break their will. Greenpaw Village lies northeast of Mystral Lake. Karang prepares a tribal war banner to plant in the center of the Foulweald totem mound, insulting the tribe’s ancestral spirits and pride. Furbolg defenders rush to tear it down, and Chief Murgut emerges to defend his honor in open combat. Taking Murgut’s personal totem breaks the tribe’s leadership and establishes Horde supremacy in the area.

quest:6627.text: Test of Lore. The Test of Lore is a trial of intellect and historical memory set by the hermit Braug Dimspirit in the Stonetalon Mountains. After retrieving the ancient tome Legacy of the Aspects, travelers must demonstrate their understanding of ancient history by answering Braug's inquiry. Those who fail to heed the text find themselves abruptly banished across Kalimdor. Part of a broader series of trials originating with Dorn Plainstalker at the Weathered Nook, the Test of Lore shifts focus away from martial survival or blind trust toward understanding the world's ancient past. Braug Dimspirit, residing in the crags of the Stonetalon Mountains, requires seekers to recover ancient texts and genuinely absorb the knowledge held within their pages. The lesson centers upon the creation and division of the Dragon Aspects, specifically the fateful pact made long before the Great Sundering. Braug tests the seeker's recall regarding the Earth Warder, Neltharion, whose descent into madness and betrayal reshaped the surface of Azeroth. Those who do not respect history are not allowed to proceed along the path of wisdom.

quest:6628.text: Test of Lore. This trial marks the intellectual examination in a broader series of spiritual tests originating in Thousand Needles. After scouring the world for historical texts, initiates present themselves to Parqual Fintallas in the Undercity to prove they understand the darker histories that shape Azeroth. While many trials among the Horde test martial strength or raw endurance, the Test of Lore demands scholarly dedication. Originating from Dorn Plainstalker's spiritual regimen at the Weathered Nook, the journey carries candidates far from the wind-carved canyons of Thousand Needles into the shadowed halls of the Undercity. Parqual Fintallas serves as the examiner, holding seekers to an exacting standard of historical literacy.

quest:663.text: Land Ho!. At Faldir's Cove, the lookout Lolo greets you with news that Captain O'Breen's stop here will last far longer than planned. Two ships of the formation, the Spirit of Silverpine and the Maiden's Folly, are lost, and Lolo suggests you speak with the captain. Lolo, ever on the lookout, spots you arriving at Faldir's Cove. Captain O'Breen had promised the crew only a few hours here, time enough to collect the treasure and head back to Booty Bay. Lolo doubts it will be so quick. Two ships of the formation, the Spirit of Silverpine and the Maiden's Folly, now rest on the bottom of the sea. Anyone who means to stay is told to talk to the captain.

quest:6661.text: Deeprun Rat Roundup. Deeprun Rat Roundup is an Alliance task in the Deeprun Tram where players assist Monty with pest control. Using a charming musical flute, players round up living Deeprun rats to supply Monty's brother with fresh meat for rat kabobs. Down in the subterranean tube of the Deeprun Tram, a colorful character named Monty struggles to keep the underground transit line clear of pests. Speaking in salty sea slang and treating the tramway like a ship's deck, Monty enlists passing travelers to help round up the scurrying vermin infesting the station.

quest:6662.text: Me Brother, Nipsy. Me Brother, Nipsy is an Alliance delivery quest that takes travelers across the Deeprun Tram between Ironforge and Stormwind. A gnome named Monty tasks commuters with transporting a crate of live rats to his brother Nipsy, who runs a rat kabob stall at the opposite terminal. Beneath the quirky errand lies a touching look at Monty's fractured mind following the tragedy of Gnomeregan. Me Brother, Nipsy is a brief courier errand that introduces commuters to the wonders—and hazards—of the Deeprun Tram. Stationed on the Ironforge side of the tramway, an odd gnome named Monty tasks travelers with ferrying a carton of fresh critters through the subterranean transit corridor to his brother Nipsy at the Stormwind depot. The delivery highlights the bizarre everyday commerce taking place beneath the mountains connecting the dwarven and human capitals. While labeled as a Carton of Mystery Meat, the parcel is actually packed with live, squirming Deeprun rats. Nipsy operates a rat kabob enterprise at the Stormwind terminal and requires his stock delivered before it goes bad. When the crate arrives intact and twitching, Nipsy is relieved to keep his culinary operation stocked for hungry travelers passing through the transit hub.

quest:67.text: The Legend of Stalvan. In Darkshire, Clerk Daltry searches the town records for Stalvan Mistmantle. The oldest entry points west to the abandoned schoolhouse in Moonbrook, Westfall, where the search for Stalvan’s past begins. After your inquiries in Darkshire, Clerk Daltry searches the town registry for Stalvan Mistmantle. The ledger has not been updated in years, and it gives Stalvan’s last known home as the schoolhouse in Moonbrook, far to the west. Daltry treats the old address as routine record keeping. He asks you to look into it and bring back any records that might bring Darkshire’s dusty archives up to date. The trail leads from Duskwood into Westfall, where Defias Brotherhood outlaws hold Moonbrook. The town was once a thriving farming settlement. Near its center stands the abandoned schoolhouse, quiet amid the bandit occupation. Inside, an old footlocker holds the first clear clues to Stalvan’s former life as an educator. A restless sorrow also lingers around the chest.

quest:671.text: Foul Magics. Foul Magics is a Horde quest originating in Hammerfall within the Arathi Highlands. Tor'gan senses a disturbing demonic presence to the west and discovers traces of dark summoning rituals at Northfold Manor. He asks adventurers to venture into the manor and retrieve bloodstone amulets used in these summonings so he can study their dark magic. Tor'gan, an orc stationed at the Horde outpost of Hammerfall, began noticing an unsettling disturbance drifting through the Arathi Highlands. For an orc, demonic energies are not merely an abstract threat; they evoke a visceral, biological reaction rooted in the history of the blood curse. As Tor'gan tracked the source of his agitation westward toward Northfold Manor, the ambient corruption caused his blood to boil and stoked an involuntary rage within him. Recognizing the telltale aftermath of demonic summoning, he retreated before the dark influence overwhelmed his senses, seeking outside help instead of returning himself. At Northfold Manor, Tor'gan discovered physical evidence of dark rituals: an amulet carved from bloodstone lying on the ground. These magical charms are actively employed to facilitate and stabilize demonic summoning rituals. The specific amulet Tor'gan managed to recover was already depleted of its magical reserves, making thorough magical analysis impossible. In order to investigate the full extent of the summoning and determine what entities were brought forth, he charges Horde travelers with heading into Northfold Manor to retrieve ten intact bloodstone amulets from the practitioners residing there.

quest:672.text: Raising Spirits. Raising Spirits is a Horde quest in the Arathi Highlands where Tor'gan seeks to lift the spirits of a despondent orc named Gor'mul. When tales of Orgrimmar and Warchief Thrall fail, Tor'gan turns to newly rediscovered shamanic traditions to craft a revitalizing amulet from highland raptor eyes. At the remote outpost of Hammerfall in the Arathi Highlands, the orcs face enemies from without and quiet battles within. One of their own, Gor'mul, has fallen into a deep, unshakable melancholy. His companions attempted to rally him with proud tales of Kalimdor, the mighty fortress city of Orgrimmar, and the visionary leadership of young Warchief Thrall. Yet none of these grand victories or distant wonders could pierce Gor'mul's gloom or give him reason to hope. Recognizing that mere words are powerless against Gor'mul's despondency, Tor'gan turns to the Horde's revived spiritual heritage. By gathering the eyes of fierce highland raptors roaming Arathi, Tor'gan crafts an amulet blessed with the predators' spirits. Rather than relying on brute force or fel power, this ritual invokes the restorative strength of newly embraced shamanistic traditions, hoping the beast's vital flame can awaken a brother's dormant will to live.

quest:674.text: Raising Spirits. Raising Spirits is a Horde quest aimed at rekindling the fighting will of Gor'mul, a broken warrior consumed by despair. An emissary delivers a Raptor Talon Amulet in hopes of awakening the fierce spirit he once possessed. However, Gor'mul remains bitter, questioning whether any simple trinket could ever mend his sorrow or restore glory to the Horde. Raising Spirits involves delivering a Raptor Talon Amulet to an orc named Gor'mul. His allies hope that the wild strength and ferocity of raptors, channeled through the talisman, will reawaken the warrior's flame that once burned fiercely within his veins.

quest:675.text: Raising Spirits. Raising Spirits is a Horde quest that addresses the lingering emotional trauma of an old orc veteran. Through the guidance of Tor'gan, a shaman attempts to reach the embittered Gor'mul using ancestral magic to restore his lost pride and will to live. In the wake of past wars, many orcish veterans struggle with the burdens of survival and perceived dishonor. Gor'mul is one such warrior, languishing in bitter despondency because he was denied what he considers an honorable death alongside his fallen Warchief. Tor'gan, an empathetic shaman, seeks to alleviate Gor'mul's suffering by reminding him of his people's spiritual strength. Believing that ancestral energies can heal emotional wounds, Tor'gan prepares an enchanted amulet intended to rekindle the old fighter's pride.

quest:676.text: The Hammer May Fall. Tallow sends fighters from Tarren Mill across the mountains to relieve Hammerfall in the Arathi Highlands. Before reporting to Drum Fel, you prove your battle readiness against Boulderfist ogres near the ruins of Stromgarde. In Tarren Mill, Tallow has little patience for untested fighters wandering the Foothills. While recruits stand idle, allies are under attack far away. He sends capable fighters east through Thoradin's Wall into the Arathi Highlands, where Hammerfall is besieged from several sides. Tallow wants them to prove their worth against a strong foe before he sends them to the outpost. Tallow demands a display of strength at the ogre mound northeast of the ruins of Stromgarde. Boulderfist ogres and their enforcers hold much of Arathi, threatening travelers on the highland trails. Fighting them thins the hostile forces flanking the road and proves you can stand against the danger before reaching Hammerfall.

quest:677.text: Call to Arms. Call to Arms is a Horde military initiative directed by Drum Fel from the outpost of Hammerfall in the Arathi Highlands. Threatened by an alliance between the local Witherbark forest trolls and Boulderfist ogres, the Horde launches a preemptive campaign against the Witherbark to secure their foothold in the region. From the fortified sanctuary of Hammerfall, Drum Fel organizes a preemptive military strike against the hostile native powers of the Arathi Highlands. Surrounded by old human ruins and aggressive local factions, the Horde settlement faces an imminent threat from a cooperative pact formed between the indigenous Witherbark forest trolls and the brute Boulderfist ogres. Rather than allowing their enemies to dictate the terms of survival, Drum Fel calls on champions to take the offensive.
