The initial offensive focuses south of Hammerfall, targeting the heart of Witherbark territory. The Witherbark have turned their backs on any diplomacy, choosing instead to conspire with the Boulderfist ogres to purge the Horde from the highlands. By culling their specialized axe throwers, headhunters, and witch doctors, Hammerfall seeks to shatter their martial leadership and demonstrate that the Horde is here to stay.

quest:678.text: Call to Arms. Call to Arms is a Horde martial trial issued by Drum Fel at the Hammerfall outpost in the Arathi Highlands. Having proven their basic combat readiness, adventurers are ordered southwest toward the dwarven bridge to engage the dangerous Boulderfist ogres. Eliminating both front-line brutes and spellcasting magi tests the warrior's resolve while protecting the Horde's vulnerable foothold in Arathi. At the isolated Horde redoubt of Hammerfall, survival demands unwavering martial strength. Drum Fel, recognizing the growing capabilities of travelers aiding the outpost, refuses to let anyone rest on easy victories. Rather than facing minor skirmishers, warriors must prove their mettle against what Fel considers a genuine threat: the hulking Boulderfist ogres. These brutes have consistently harassed the Horde expedition and tested the resolve of Hammerfall’s defenders. Fel offers simple terms for the task—warriors are expected to return successful in flesh or honorably in spirit, with praise promised for sheer tenacity in battle. The Boulderfist clan has established an entrenched lair southwest of Hammerfall, extending their territory toward the grand dwarven bridge connecting Arathi to the Wetlands. Unlike undisciplined beasts, the ogres command both crushing physical power and lethal mystical arts, fielding durable brutes alongside cunning magi. Their aggressive presence poses a direct challenge to the Horde's supply lines and regional dominance. By ordering the destruction of ten Boulderfist brutes and four magi, Drum Fel seeks to blunt their strength, ensuring the Boulderfists understand that the warriors of Hammerfall will neither yield ground nor tolerate rivals in Arathi.

quest:68.text: The Legend of Stalvan. In Moonbrook, The Legend of Stalvan leads back to Darkshire's records. A dusty, unsent letter from an old footlocker proves Stalvan Mistmantle stayed there before his trail went cold. You find a dusty, unsent letter in an old footlocker while tracing Stalvan Mistmantle's past. Moonbrook was once an agricultural settlement, but now lies in ruin, crowded with outlaws and restless specters. Few remember Stalvan's brief stay, yet the letter places him in the hamlet. You carry the letter across the border to Darkshire, where Clerk Daltry needs it for the town records. He finds it strange that the letter was never mailed, but the evidence confirms Stalvan's connection to Moonbrook. The records can now point toward where Stalvan fled next.

quest:681.text: Northfold Manor. Captain Nials, at Refuge Pointe, asks for help against the Syndicate holding Northfold Manor. Their hold on the land between the defenders of Stromgarde and Southshore makes it hard for supplies to arrive. Stromgarde has been carved up between the ogres, the Syndicate and the Alliance, and every faction fights the others to a bloody stalemate. The Alliance's forces dwindle while their enemies grow. The defenders need help from Southshore, but supplies are slow to arrive. The Syndicate holds the ground between the defenders and Southshore. Captain Nials wants you to go to their base at Northfold Manor and cut down their highwaymen and mercenaries, in the hope that the pressure on the supply trains eases and more get through.

quest:683.text: Sara Balloo's Plea. In Ironforge, Sara Balloo grieves for Sully and asks you to carry her plea to King Magni Bronzebeard. Sara has received Sully’s final letter, recovered from the waters of the Thandol Span. She wants the king to remember his sacrifice, so she writes him a plea. Grief keeps her from appearing before the throne herself. She entrusts the sealed letter to you, a champion of the Alliance, to carry to King Magni Bronzebeard.

quest:684.text: WANTED: Marez Cowl. At Stromgarde, Marez Cowl advises Syndicate leaders and traffics with demons. Her influence threatens Alliance forces in the Arathi Highlands. At Refuge Pointe, Alliance commanders offer a bounty on a high-ranking Syndicate leader. Marez Cowl advises the Syndicate and directs its work in Stromgarde’s ruins as a field operative. The bounty aims to break the group’s local command. Marez Cowl is a warlock among the Syndicate’s brigands and dispossessed nobles. She deals openly with demonic powers to enforce her will and defend Syndicate territory. To reach her lair in Stromgarde, you must face armed criminals and the demons she commands.

quest:685.text: WANTED: Otto and Falconcrest. A bounty posted by the Stromgarde Militia marks Lord Falconcrest, leader of the local Syndicate forces, and his deadly bodyguard Otto for death. Eliminating them strikes a crucial blow against the criminal organization's foothold in the Arathi Highlands. Proof of their demise must be delivered to Captain Nials at Refuge Pointe. The Stromgarde Militia has issued an official bounty targeting two key figures in the Arathi Highlands: Lord Falconcrest and his ferocious bodyguard, Otto. Stationed out of Refuge Pointe, the beleaguered defenders of Stromgarde seek to break the Syndicate's hold over their ancestral lands. Hunters must bring the heads of both targets to Captain Nials to claim the reward. Lord Falconcrest serves as the mastermind behind the Syndicate's coordinated push into the Arathi Highlands. His death represents a vital strategic victory for the Alliance, promising to severely disrupt the criminal network's operations in the region. Beside him stands Otto, a brutally effective bodyguard whose blades have already cut down dozens of Stromgarde's remaining militia soldiers.

quest:686.text: A King's Tribute. King Magni Bronzebeard answers Sara Balloo with a lasting tribute to her fallen husband, Sully. He sends you across Ironforge with a royal commission for Grand Mason Marblesten. Sara Balloo's plea weighs on King Magni Bronzebeard. War's harsh needs can be hard for common folk to understand, yet every soldier beneath the Alliance banner weighs on his conscience. He cannot undo a death on the front lines. He can see that Sully Balloo's sacrifice is remembered. King Magni chooses a stone memorial for Sully, not empty words. He entrusts you with his royal commission and sends you across Ironforge to Grand Mason Marblesten. The master stonemason receives the king's personal charge and prepares to carve the fallen defender's memory into stone.

quest:689.text: A King's Tribute. King Magni Bronzebeard has ordered a memorial for Sully Balloo, who died defending the Thandol Span. Grand Mason Marblesten sends you north to Hillsbrad for stone worthy of the fallen soldier. Grand Mason Marblesten carries King Magni Bronzebeard’s commission to honor Sully Balloo. Sully died in the disaster at the Thandol Span. Dark Iron saboteurs have attacked the span, a vital artery between the dwarven lands and the northern kingdoms. Marblesten will shape a sculpture to withstand time and war, so the Great Forge remembers the dwarven sacrifice. For Sully Balloo’s likeness, Marblesten requires Alterac Granite. Its dense, resilient stone and clean texture make it prized by masons. The finest deposits lie around Darrow Hill in Hillsbrad’s contested foothills. The journey into the troubled north is dangerous, but Marblesten seeks stone worthy of the heroism it will honor.

quest:69.text: The Legend of Stalvan. A scratched entry in Darkshire points the search for Stalvan Mistmantle toward Goldshire. Clerk Daltry finds another destination beneath Stalvan Mistmantle's earlier entry in Darkshire's town registry. The hurried note is partly scratched out, as if someone meant to hide the route or changed their mind. It points northwest, toward the Lion's Pride Inn in Elwynn Forest. You leave Duskwood's shadowed groves for Goldshire's sunny roads, but Stalvan's trail reaches here too. The Lion's Pride Inn stands at Elwynn Forest's crossroads, where travelers, merchants, and soldiers gather. Innkeeper Farley runs the busy taproom and may know of an educated wanderer looking for a room.

quest:690.text: Malin's Request. In Stormwind, Archmage Malin asks for help recovering relics from fallen Stromgarde. He sends seasoned Alliance adventurers north to Refuge Pointe in the Arathi Highlands, where an expedition seeks the magical relics left behind when Stromgarde fell. Archmage Malin serves in Stormwind's Wizard's Sanctum and acts for his former mentor, Archmage Trelane. When Stromgarde fell into chaos, Trelane made a desperate stand at the Tower of Arathor. As hostile forces took the city, he had to abandon his post and leave powerful enchanted possessions behind. Malin fears those relics may fall into hostile hands. He sends capable mercenaries north to strengthen his agents in the field and reclaim Trelane's lost belongings. Refuge Pointe lies on the road to Trelane's relics, in the central Arathi Highlands. The outpost is a hard-pressed refuge for Stromgarde loyalists, and Malin's chief contact there is the dwarf Skuerto. Syndicate outlaws, Witherbark trolls, and Boulderfist ogres press the outpost from every side. When you arrive, Skuerto and the garrison are stretched too thin to welcome you warmly without immediate help.

quest:691.text: Worth Its Weight in Gold. At Refuge Pointe, Apprentice Kryten is after Witherbark tusks, medicine pouches and a shadow hunter's knife, all reagents for Archmage Malin, who sent him and Skuerto to gather them. He asks you to seek them among the Witherbark trolls in the southeast of Arathi. Archmage Malin sent Kryten and Skuerto to Arathi to collect reagents, and Kryten had no idea how to gather them until you arrived. He needs ten Witherbark tusks, four medicine pouches and one shadow hunter knife. The Witherbark trolls make their home in the southeast of Arathi. By Kryten's research, any Witherbark troll should have tusks, and the witch doctors carry the medicine pouches. The knife belongs to the mightiest shadow hunters, handed to them after they finish their rites of passage. Only battle will show which of them has one.

quest:6921.text: Amongst the Ruins. At Zoram'gar Outpost, Je'neu Sancrea sends Horde adventurers into Blackfathom Deeps for a fathom core. The Earthen Ring hopes the relic will reveal what the Twilight's Hammer is doing with the elements. The Twilight's Hammer has taken hold of Blackfathom Deeps, the ancient night elven temple once sacred to Elune. Its cultists command the submerged passages. At Zoram'gar Outpost on Ashenvale's shore, Darkspear shaman Je'neu Sancrea watches the corruption spread. He fears the cult means to bend the local elements against the land and its defenders. Je'neu Sancrea sends Horde champions to retrieve a fathom core from the fathom stone beneath the waters of the Moonshrine Ruins. Shamans who can decipher the core will find a detailed record of elemental currents and disturbances. The Earthen Ring hopes the relic will expose the Twilight's Hammer's work and help keep the region safe from elemental disaster.

quest:6922.text: Baron Aquanis. Beneath Ashenvale, Baron Aquanis leaves a strange globe filled with tainted fluid. Je'neu Sancrea of the Earthen Ring believes it may show what corrupted the elemental, and suspects the Twilight's Hammer cultists in the submerged ruins. Blackfathom Deeps holds Baron Aquanis, a water spirit twisted by foul sorcery. When the elemental is destroyed, a Strange Water Globe remains behind. The impervious orb holds putrid fluid that seems to have sustained and warped Aquanis's natural essence. Physical force cannot harm it, and its energies unsettle those attuned to the balance of the elements.

quest:693.text: Wand over Fist. Skuerto at Refuge Pointe has worked out where the first of Trelane's items ended up. Kor'gresh has Trelane's Wand of Invocation in Boulderfist Hall, and Skuerto wants it brought back. After your work for Apprentice Kryten, Skuerto has found where Trelane's first item went. Kor'gresh holds it in Boulderfist Hall, and has been throwing blasts of ice at his own kin to keep them in line. Skuerto reckons the ogre must be close to figuring out all of the wand's powers. Boulderfist Hall lies south of Refuge Pointe and then east of Thandol Span.

quest:694.text: Trelane's Defenses. With the wand in hand, Skuerto turns to the ogres that surround the Tower of Arathor. To bring the tower's defenses to life, he needs an azure agate from the Boulderfist shaman, to be taken to Apprentice Kryten at Refuge Pointe. Ogres surround the Tower of Arathor in Stromgarde. Skuerto says the tower's defenses must be activated if you are to stand a chance against them and still reach the items alive. Certain gems from the tower have caught the fancy of the Boulderfist shaman, who carried them off, though Skuerto says they will not keep them for long. Bring one azure agate to Apprentice Kryten at Refuge Pointe, who knows the spell to enchant it so that it works as a key.

quest:695.text: An Apprentice's Enchantment. Apprentice Kryten has enchanted the agate you brought him from the Boulderfist shaman. Touched to a pedestal at the foot of the tower, it will wake the tower's defenses. Before you leave, he sends you to Skuerto for the rest. Kryten hands you the enchanted gem. He explains that touching it to a pedestal at the foot of the tower will wake the tower's defenses, and that you should use it when you are ready to go in after the rest of Trelane's items. He will await your return at the camp. First, speak to Skuerto, who will fill in whatever else you need to know.

quest:696.text: Attack on the Tower. With the tower's defenses awake, Skuerto at Refuge Pointe sends you into the ogre-held tower for Trelane's phylactery, orb and ember agate. They should lie in chests inside, and Skuerto says Malin will be more than pleased if you bring them back. After Kryten's enchantment, Skuerto tells you what to look for: Trelane's phylactery, orb and ember agate. The three should be sitting in chests inside the tower, and you should have no trouble opening them yourself, though the ogres call for care. The tower's defenses will not deal with them on their own, and if the ogres find you stealing from them, they will put the hurt on you.

quest:697.text: Malin's Request. Skuerto gives you a sealed letter for Archmage Malin, who is found in Stormwind's Mage Quarter. It tells Malin that Kryten and Skuerto will be home soon, and Skuerto is certain Malin will repay you well for helping them in Arathi. After the work in Arathi, Skuerto hands you a letter to take back to Stormwind. Its message for Archmage Malin in the Mage Quarter is that Kryten and Skuerto will be home soon. Skuerto has no doubt that Malin will repay you well for helping them, and sends you off with a wish for a safe journey.

quest:6981.text: The Glowing Shard. The Glowing Shard is a mysterious emerald-hued gem plucked from the dark depths of the Wailing Caverns. Swirling with smoky essence beneath its polished surface, this disturbing relic drives adventurers to seek answers in Ratchet and beyond. Drawn from deep within the Wailing Caverns, the glowing shard immediately unnerves those who hold it. Brilliant green and seemingly solid, it holds churning, mist-like shadows beneath its crystalline face. The crystal exerts a subtle pull, demanding attention while exuding a deeply unsettling aura that hints at the corrupted nature of the slumbering druids and their nightmare-infested sanctuary.

quest:70.text: The Legend of Stalvan. In Goldshire, the search for Stalvan Mistmantle turns to an old letter left at the inn. Its trail leads from Elwynn Forest to Stormwind's Canal District. At the Lion's Pride Inn, Innkeeper Farley remembers a stormy night from years ago. A traveling courier came in from the pouring rain to find shelter, then rushed downstairs around midnight in a panic. He wore only his sleepwear as he fled into the dark storm. No one saw him again. The courier left his satchel and personal chest in the upstairs room when he fled. Among the forgotten cargo was an unsent letter bearing the name Stalvan, addressed to someone in Stormwind City's Canal District. The chest sat untouched at the foot of the bed until Farley allowed it to be opened.

quest:700.text: A King's Tribute. Magni Bronzebeard gives Sully Balloo a memorial in Ironforge. Granite from Lordaeron keeps the fallen dwarf in his people's memory. King Magni Bronzebeard commissioned a monument for Sully Balloo, a dwarf who died serving his people. Grand Mason Marblesten carved it from fine granite brought from Lordaeron's war-torn lands. The monument stands in Ironforge, honoring soldiers whose sacrifices help preserve the dwarven kingdom. When told the monument is complete, Magni considers stone and mortality. Carved rock can never equal a brave dwarf's life, he knows, yet he hopes the memorial endures. Then generations walking Azeroth may remember the heroes who bled to secure their tomorrow.

quest:701.text: Guile of the Raptor. Guile of the Raptor is a quest in which Tor'gan seeks to awaken the dormant warrior spirit within Gor'mul. By harvesting the hearts of Highland Fleshstalkers, Tor'gan plans to fashion an enchanted item imbued with the cunning and predatory power of the raptor. Tor'gan works to restore a listless compatriot named Gor'mul, whose warrior spirit has fallen dormant. Rather than relying on simple persuasion, Tor'gan turns to primal magic to shock Gor'mul back into action. By crafting a charm imbued with the essence of wild predators, he hopes to reintroduce Gor'mul to martial resolve and demonstrate the strength of their new power. To channel the predatory instincts of the wild, Tor'gan requires the hearts of Highland Fleshstalkers. In shamanic and primal traditions, the heart of a cunning hunter carries its ferocity and guile. Tor'gan weaves both a physical token and a spell from these trophies, aiming to infuse Gor'mul directly with the predator's cunning so he can rediscover his true calling.

quest:702.text: Guile of the Raptor. After the earlier Guile of the Raptor, Tor'gan hands you an orb and sends you to Gor'mul at Hammerfall. Its energy carries the essence of the raptor, meant to stir Gor'mul's spirit and give him new purpose. Tor'gan gives you an orb whose energy is meant to fill Gor'mul with the raptor's essence. He hopes it will rouse the warrior's spirit and set him on a fresh course in life. Once Gor'mul is himself again, Tor'gan means to explain the current state of the Horde to him and gain a great warrior's help in the unceasing battles. Gor'mul greets your return with sourness, saying he wants nothing more than more of Tor'gan's pity and mocking you with talk of brightly colored string.

quest:7162.text: Proving Grounds. In Alterac, recruits face a trial before joining the Stormpike Guard. Lieutenant Haggerdin sends them into Icewing Caverns to recover a planted battle standard. Success earns an official Stormpike Insignia and begins their rise through the expedition’s ranks. The Stormpike Guard fights the Frostwolf Clan in Alterac Valley. Lieutenant Haggerdin directs Alliance forces from their encampment in the Alterac Mountains. He tests new recruits before sending them to the battlefield, demanding proof of skill and nerve in Icewing Caverns, southwest of Dun Baldar. A Stormpike banner waits deep in the icy tunnels of Icewing Caverns. Frost harpies nest in the frozen recesses and attack unwary trespassers. Bringing back the banner intact shows a recruit can cross dangerous ground, face the predators, and keep discipline under pressure. Returning from the caverns with the standard earns a soldier the Stormpike initiate’s insignia and a place in the expeditionary force. Haggerdin promises that the insignia can be improved as a soldier earns greater honor on the battlefield, with honors such as the Eye of Command as a distant aim.

quest:72.text: The Legend of Stalvan. In Stormwind, you search the Flintridge belongings for clues to Stalvan Mistmantle. Sealed crates by the canals hold the household’s remaining possessions, while restless spirits tied to the massacre guard what remains. You trace Stalvan’s path from Duskwood to Stormwind. Beside the city canals, Caretaker Folsom watches over what remains of the Flintridge household. His father served the estate before him and had to mop up blood after a massacre that claimed the household. The name Stalvan is somehow tied to that slaughter. The Flintridge trust funds are gone, and royal tax collectors press the estate. Its surviving heirlooms and packed belongings are sealed inside shipping crates along the canal embankment, awaiting auction. You search the boxes for Stalvan’s trail before the family’s remaining goods are scattered to collectors across the kingdom.

quest:729.text: The Absent Minded Prospector. In southern Darkshore, hostile stone golems overrun a dig site, and Archaeologist Hollee seeks help in Auberdine. She fears for Prospector Remtravel, her senior colleague, whose research often blinds him to mortal danger. Archaeologist Hollee crossed the sea with the Explorers' League, sent by Master Greywhisker to apprentice under Prospector Remtravel. His discoveries had made him renowned in Ironforge's academic circles. The League sent him to study ancient ruins along Darkshore's untamed coast. As the pair excavated what seemed to be the remains of a great civilization, violent stone golems burst from the earth and overran the site. Hollee fled in panic through the night to Auberdine, the night elf port, to seek help. Remtravel barely noticed the danger. Absorbed in the relics he had uncovered, the elderly prospector stayed among the rubble while lumbering constructs surrounded his camp. South of Auberdine, anyone who reaches him finds him grumbling about missing stone brushes and misplaced fossils.

quest:731.text: The Absent Minded Prospector. At the southern ruins of Darkshore, Prospector Remtravel presses on with his dig, hoping to find a prize for the Explorers' League. Hostile troggs and his forgetfulness make the search perilous, and word of his safety must reach his assistant in Auberdine. Far south in Darkshore, Remtravel's Dig lies among ancient ruins. Dwarven excavators searching there uncovered troggs, who drove out the workers and besieged the camp. Remtravel will not leave for Auberdine empty-handed. He wanders into danger to recover a fossil, hoping to justify the expedition's costs to the Explorers' League.

quest:7321.text: Soothing Turtle Bisque. In Tarren Mill, Christoph Jeffcoat is trying to prove the Forsaken can cook with care. He needs snapjaw meat from Hillsbrad's waterways and the shores of Lordamere Lake for his turtle bisque. Many believe the Forsaken have left the comforts of life behind, including fine cooking. Christoph Jeffcoat in Tarren Mill rejects that belief. He boasts that his rich turtle bisque could tempt souls back from beyond the grave. Through careful cooking, he means to show that undead hands can still make a warming dish in a land marked by plague and war. Jeffcoat once gathered ingredients himself from Hillsbrad's waterways and Lordamere Lake's eastern shores in neighboring Alterac. Duties in Tarren Mill and nearby Alliance forces keep him from hunting. He depends on passing Horde cooks to hunt snapjaws, bring back their meat, and keep the recipe alive.

quest:736.text: The Star, the Hand and the Heart. The Star, the Hand and the Heart is an Undercity quest wherein Keeper Bel'dugur tests an aspiring leader seeking to establish a new chapter of their order. To earn the essential Yagyin's Digest, the petitioner must track down three items of power whose names Bel'dugur dares not speak aloud. Within the shadowed corridors of the Undercity, ambitious practitioners seeking to lead their own circle turn to Keeper Bel'dugur. To establish a new flock and open a chapter of their order, an aspiring leader requires Yagyin's Digest, an authoritative text of ritual lore guarded by the keeper. Bel'dugur stands ready to support his fellow brother, but demands proof of worthiness before yielding such authority. Keeper Bel'dugur will not part with Yagyin's Digest lightly. He requires three distinct items of power to fulfill his side of the exchange. These relics carry such perilous or sacred significance that their names cannot even be spoken aloud; Bel'dugur instead pens them onto a private note. Only a practitioner capable of tracking down and retrieving all three unspoken artifacts proves worthy of founding their own chapter.

quest:74.text: The Legend of Stalvan. Beside Stormwind City's canals, the Flintridge crate yields a clue to Stalvan Mistmantle's past. The torn journal page leads to Marshal Haggard in Elwynn Forest. A torn page from Stalvan Mistmantle's journal lies beneath a ceramic vase in a sealed crate. The crate holds musty Flintridge heirlooms, old hunting trophies, and family portraits. Stalvan's own hand offers a glimpse of the reclusive scholar before tragedy struck.

quest:741.text: The Absent Minded Prospector. Hollee sends Remtravel's fossil from Darkshore to Darnassus. She stays behind to watch the wandering prospector, and Chief Archaeologist Greywhisker takes a keen interest in the find. Prospector Remtravel has unearthed a curious fossil along Darkshore's coast. He cares more about digging deeper than following protocol. Archaeologist Hollee stays behind to watch over him among the shore's dangerous beasts and hostile cultists. She asks you, an Alliance traveler, to carry the specimen to Darnassus, where the dwarven guild keeps a scholarly delegation. Dwarves from Ironforge have crossed the Great Sea under the Explorers' League banner, searching Kalimdor's soil for ancient relics and lost history. In Darnassus, Chief Archaeologist Greywhisker marvels at Remtravel's knack for finding ancient treasures. Night elves see their forests as living sanctuaries, while the League sees ancient lands as ground to study and decipher.

quest:742.text: The Ashenvale Hunt. In Thunder Bluff, the Ashenvale Hunt calls young Horde champions north to serve at the forest outposts. Heralds direct them to report to Senani Thunderheart at Splintertree Post for a proving hunt. Bluff Runner Windstrider carries an open invitation through Thunder Bluff for proven adventurers. The Horde has established footholds in the ancient forest north of the Barrens, and its outposts need young warriors. Those who answer will face a harsher land and test their survival skills beyond Mulgore. Ashenvale offers the Horde rich resources and severe peril. Splintertree Post stands along the main road, while a remote outpost lies on the western coast at Zoram Strand. At Splintertree Post, Senani Thunderheart, a veteran outdoorswoman, organizes a great hunt to tame the wilderness and win glory for the Horde.

quest:744.text: Preparation for Ceremony. You are preparing to appear before Chief Cairne Bloodhoof, and your sibling is making the headdress for the occasion. The tauren tradition calls for leather bands and vibrant feathers gathered from harpies beyond Thunder Bluff. Among the tauren, standing before Chief Cairne Bloodhoof brings pride and reverence. Your family honors the occasion by preparing proper attire. The traditional headdress is made from treated leather and symbolic plumage, with each part chosen to show dignity and respect before the leader of the united tribes. A ceremonial headdress needs a leather band and feathers for its crown. While the leather straps are tanned, long, pristine feathers must be gathered. Harpies roost in the craggy hills north and northwest of Thunder Bluff, so you must venture into their hostile nests to find feathers of the needed size and color.

quest:75.text: The Legend of Stalvan. In Elwynn, your search for Stalvan Mistmantle reaches Marshal Haggard's home. The aging veteran's eyesight has failed, and an upstairs chest holds papers left behind when he moved in. Marshal Haggard lives on Elwynn Forest's southeastern edge, near Duskwood and Redridge. An old chest upstairs holds parchments he found when he moved into his secluded home. His failing eyesight kept him from reading them, and they remain untouched until you ask about Stalvan.

quest:750.text: The Hunt Continues. The Hunt Continues is an early rite of passage assigned by Grull Hawkwind in Camp Narache. It tasks aspiring hunters with gathering mountain cougar pelts from the southern hills to clothe the tribe's children and mend their tents. In Camp Narache, young hunters are taught that taking a beast is never an idle pursuit or a search for trophies. Grull Hawkwind charges fledgling adventurers with venturing into the southern hills of Red Cloud Mesa to track down mountain cougars. Rather than proving martial prowess alone, the task emphasizes responsibility to the community, showing that true hunters must provide essential provisions for their people. Life on the mesa demands durable materials to withstand the open elements. Grull explains that the cougar hides are urgently needed to sew clothing for the tribe's children and to mend worn hide tents throughout Camp Narache. Proving oneself capable of securing these prized pelts earns the gratitude of the elders, and Grull promises to bring word of the hunter's selfless contributions directly to his father, Chief Hawkwind.

quest:755.text: Rites of the Earthmother. Rites of the Earthmother marks the beginning of an initiate's spiritual journey on Red Cloud Mesa. Directed by Chief Hawkwind, travelers seek out Seer Graytongue in the southern hills of Camp Narache. Undertaking these venerable ceremonies is considered a vital trial of passage for tauren coming of age. Upon the Red Cloud Mesa, Chief Hawkwind directs young tauren seeking to prove themselves to Seer Graytongue. Residing in the quiet hills directly south of Camp Narache, Graytongue oversees the spiritual beginnings of the youth. This simple journey marks the formal threshold between everyday camp life and the serious commitments demanded by tribal custom. The Earthmother is central to the creation beliefs and everyday existence of the tauren. Her rites serve as sacred trials of maturity, resilience, and spiritual depth. As Seer Graytongue cautions all who arrive at his sanctuary, embarking upon the Rites of the Earthmother is no light endeavor, requiring total dedication to the traditions of the mesa.

quest:7792.text: A Donation of Wool. In Darnassus, wool cloth is gathered to support the city's stores. Your sixty pieces earn recognition for your generosity. Darnassus needs sixty pieces of wool cloth from you. Others across the realm are expected to provide the rest of its stores. Your donation earns full recognition for your generosity.

quest:78.text: The Legend of Stalvan. Marshal Haggard sends you back to Darkshire with a page he cannot read. Tavernkeep Smitts may know the hand that wrote it. Marshal Haggard cannot read the faded writing on the torn journal page you recovered from his chest in Elwynn Forest. His eyesight is failing. The retired commander remembers serving with the Stormwind Guard and spending evenings at the Scarlet Raven Tavern in Darkshire. The trail leads back across the river, so he sends you to Tavernkeep Smitts. Years behind the bar have made Smitts a keeper of local history and rumors.

quest:7802.text: A Donation of Wool. At Ironforge, wool donations help support its stores. Sixty pieces bring full recognition for your generosity. Ironforge asks you for sixty pieces of wool cloth. Its stores need only that much from you. Others are expected to give enough to support the drive.

quest:7807.text:
A Donation of Wool. Across the realm, A Donation of Wool calls for aid to the Gnomeregan Exiles. Driven from Gnomeregan, they need wool cloth to sustain their displaced people. Sixty pieces earn formal recognition among the gnomes. Gnomeregan's fall to trogg invaders and radioactive contamination drove its surviving gnomes from their high-tech city. They now live as refugees, hosted chiefly by their dwarven cousins in Ironforge.

Outside their ancestral halls, the Gnomeregan Exiles face severe strain in supplying their people. Regular drives for cloth and other basics help keep them clothed, supplied, and organized. The drive asks each volunteer for exactly sixty pieces of wool cloth. By gathering modest contributions from across the realm, the exiles can collect the textiles they need for bedding, bandages, and clothing without overburdening any one supplier. Those who aid their recovery receive formal recognition among their people.

quest:78124.text: Nar'thalas Almanac. Scholars seek the Nar'thalas Almanac to preserve ancient magical study. Its recovery brings forgotten lore into a library where researchers can study it. A rare work of arcane study, the Nar'thalas Almanac comes from the ancient traditions of pre-Sundering night elven scholarship. For caretakers of great archives, securing the volume rescues centuries-old lore from obscurity and adds an important piece of history to their shelves. Those who uncover neglected works help bridge forgotten antiquity and modern scholarship. Across Azeroth, archivists and researchers seek lost treatises, field notes, and chronicles. Bringing the Nar'thalas Almanac to a dedicated library lets its keepers safeguard, catalog, and study it, rather than leave it to rot in ruins or fall into careless hands. Each recovered volume offers fresh insight into the arcane arts of past eras.

quest:78127.text: The Dalaran Digest. The librarian asks you to bring magical works for the collection. Each book adds knowledge to the library. The librarian welcomes magical works that may benefit the library. You bring a book to join the collection, helping its knowledge grow.

quest:78142.text: Bewitchments and Glamours. In Ironforge, the library is seeking magical works for its shelves. You can help its keepers widen their knowledge by bringing in books that may benefit the collection. Bring magical works to the library in Ironforge, where each addition can broaden what its keepers know.

quest:78143.text: Secrets of the Dreamers. A library's scholars seek writings tied to the Dreamers and other magical lore. Travelers bring forgotten works from across the realm, where they can be studied and kept in the archives. Scholars across the realm depend on travelers to recover rare magical texts and historical treatises. These works lie in ancient ruins or private hoards, far from the archives. So adventurers carry them safely to those who study Azeroth's arcane mysteries and preserve its lore. When travelers bring in treatises, archivists add them to the library's permanent collection. Researchers seek obscure writings on the Emerald Dream and arcane theory. Their work continues, and they welcome further magical texts found in the field.

quest:78146.text: Goaz Scrolls. The librarian asks you to bring Goaz Scrolls for the collection. Your contribution adds to the library’s knowledge. The librarian thanks you for contributing Goaz Scrolls. More magical works could help the library too, and the librarian welcomes them.

quest:7820.text: A Donation of Wool. Thunder Bluff seeks wool cloth, and you can earn its full recognition by giving sixty pieces. Other donors are expected to bring enough supplies to support the drive. Thunder Bluff is gathering wool cloth. Give sixty pieces to earn full recognition for your generosity. Other donors in the realm are expected to bring enough to support the drive.

quest:7826.text: A Donation of Wool. In Orgrimmar, A Donation of Wool asks for help gathering cloth. The city has wool in its stores and expects more donors to bring in enough for the drive. Orgrimmar asks you to give sixty pieces of wool cloth. In return, the city promises recognition. Its stores already hold some wool, and other donors are expected to help support the drive.

quest:7833.text: A Donation of Wool. A Darkspear troll gathers wool donations, and your sixty pieces of Wool Cloth join a larger collection. The Darkspear trolls are gathering Wool Cloth to replenish their stores. The collector can take your sixty pieces now, while help from others is expected to complete the collection.

quest:789.text: Sting of the Scorpid. Sting of the Scorpid is an early trial assigned by Gornek to Horde recruits at the Den in the Valley of Trials. Novices are challenged to hunt venomous scorpid workers northwest of camp and return ten tails to prove their combat readiness. The task serves as a vital lesson in surviving battlefield hazards and respecting even the smallest adversaries. In the sun-baked canyon of the Valley of Trials, Gornek tests novice Horde recruits by sending them against the local wildlife. The venomous scorpids roaming the arid dirt northwest of the Den have humbled seasoned warriors and clumsy initiates alike. To prove their battlefield competence, young champions must venture into the rocks, slay scorpid workers, and return with ten of their severed tails as proof of prowess. While deadly, the venomous predators also supply the very salvation of injured initiates. The Den maintains stockpiles of antivenom brewed directly from extracted scorpid venom to treat fallen novices. Beyond surviving the venom, Gornek emphasizes a core tactical truth: in the chaos of battle, arrogance is fatal, and even the smallest foe wields enough lethal venom to bring down a mighty warrior.

quest:79.text: The Legend of Stalvan. In Darkshire, The Legend of Stalvan now rests on proof in muddy journal pages. Tavernkeep Smitts gives them to you and sends you to Commander Althea Ebonlocke. Tavernkeep Smitts and Marshal Haggard once investigated the slaughter of a visiting noble family in Duskwood. Haggard was then a leader of the Stormwind Guard. They found torn, muddy journal pages at the scene, but had no handwriting samples or other papers to confirm who wrote them. The notes could not formally implicate the recluse rumored to live in the wilderness. Now, evidence gathered across Elwynn, Westfall, and Duskwood links the handwriting to Stalvan Mistmantle. The rumors have become proof of murder.

quest:79007.text: ... and that note you found. At a recent campsite, cooling embers and scattered supplies are all that remain. A scorched parchment bears a riddle about finding a twin land, the only clue left behind. A recent campfire is dying beside scattered provisions and a blistered piece of paper. Whoever stayed here left recently, and the parchment narrowly escaped the flames. The supplies remain exposed, as though the traveler departed in haste or was interrupted. The surviving scrap bears one instruction: “Not all that burns is lost. Find the twin land, find the place.” No signature, coordinates, or further context survived the fire. The riddle is the only trail left for whoever finds it.

quest:79008.text: ... and that note you found. A scorched note lies beside a dying campfire in Westfall. Its brief message points to a place called the twin land. Travelers crossing Westfall’s abandoned fields and wind-scoured plains find camps left by vagrants, outlaws, or desperate wanderers. This small camp was left in haste or secrecy. Its provisions lie abandoned, embers still glow, and a scorched slip of parchment rests among the scattered debris. The blistered note bears two short sentences: “Not all that burns is lost. Find the twin land, find the place.” Its words point away from Westfall but give no clear direction. What place shares a name, geography, or fate with this land?

quest:79091.text: Archmage Antonidas: The Unabridged Autobiography. In Ironforge, you seek Archmage Antonidas: The Unabridged Autobiography. The rare volume holds the late Kirin Tor leader's own account and offers insight into Dalaran's history and high arcane scholarship. Archmage Antonidas led the Kirin Tor for decades and ruled Dalaran. One of Azeroth's most brilliant minds, he rose through the ranks of the Violet Citadel and mastered the arcane. His unabridged autobiography records his leadership during the Second and Third Wars. For scholars and practitioners of magic, it offers a firsthand view of Dalaran's inner workings and the arcane arts. Before reaching its new home, the rare manuscript rested in Ironforge's grand library. In the Hall of Explorers, dwarven archivists kept it beside ancient titan relics and dwarven histories. Their vast collections hold texts gathered from ruins and foreign kingdoms across Azeroth. Yet arcane scholars elsewhere seek such works for their own collections, sure the busy archivists will never notice one missing volume.

quest:79092.text:
Archmage Theocritus' Research Journal. At the Tower of Azora, Archmage Theocritus keeps a journal of his investigations. Now you carry its magical insights to the scholars of the Ironforge Library, where they can join the dwarven archive. Archmage Theocritus is an esteemed spellcaster known throughout the Alliance. He is stationed at the Tower of Azora in eastern Elwynn Forest, where he has studied alone for years. His investigations range from curious artifacts and ley line anomalies to nearby magical threats.

He records his findings in detailed journals. This volume offers a rare chance to study the personal observations of a senior Kirin Tor archmage. The Explorers' League and the caretakers of the Ironforge Library maintain one of the continent's greatest archives. You bring Archmage Theocritus' Research Journal to them, helping preserve and catalog its arcane insights beside the historic volumes of Khaz Modan. The librarians welcome further magical discoveries that can broaden their shared wisdom.

quest:79093.text: Rumi of Gnomeregan: The Collected Works. A compiled work by Rumi of Gnomeregan is sought for a library’s collection. Its pages preserve gnomish writings and knowledge that might otherwise be lost. Gnomish writings were scattered, buried, or left in danger when troggs overran Gnomeregan. Now scholars and archivists seek surviving manuscripts, treatises, and compiled works. They hope to keep the wisdom and ingenuity of gnomish thinkers alive. When travelers find collected works in the field and bring them to the archives, curators add them to their growing collections. Each recovered manuscript widens what scholars can study. Archivists welcome more magical and historical texts, keeping them within reach of scholars, mages, and historians who guard Azeroth’s learning.

quest:79095.text: The Apothecary's Metaphysical Primer. Curators seek The Apothecary's Metaphysical Primer to enrich their archives. Its delivery helps preserve rare alchemical and arcane theory for researchers and spellcasters. Curators welcome The Apothecary's Metaphysical Primer for its study of esoteric and magical principles. Owen Thadd adds the text directly to his working collection of magical references. Owen Thadd's collection in Undercity preserves specialized treatises. By bringing him rare primers on arcane and alchemical theory, you help keep metaphysical insights safe in the archives and accessible to researchers instead of leaving them lost in the wilderness.

quest:79096.text: Ataeric: On Arcane Curiosities. Ataeric seeks rare magical writings to enlarge a library's collection. Scholars hope these works will deepen their study of the arcane and keep its lore safe. Across Azeroth, scholars rely on travelers to recover rare tomes and treatises from dangerous ground. Ataeric seeks magical writings to broaden an institution's study of the arcane. Each volume can help scholars piece together practices that might otherwise be scattered or lost. The curator adds each curiosity to the archive. The library remains eager for further magical writings found across the world, so its collection can grow with ongoing scholarship.

quest:79097.text: Baxtan: On Destructive Magics. At the library, Baxtan: On Destructive Magics joins the works scholars gather to understand dangerous arcane power. Scholars seek to preserve what is known of arcane lore. When you find a text on destructive magic, its place is in careful academic keeping. There, its power and peril can be understood instead of lost. The library holds works on history, science, and the arcane. Its scholar welcomes travelers who recover forgotten treatises from dangerous corners of the world. Each volume adds to the library's knowledge.

quest:79192.text: Stepping Stones. A weathered note in the Barrens points travelers toward Stepping Stones, a mountain refuge near Desolace. It says two couriers made deliveries for the New Plague, and calls what happened to them simple apothecary accidents. A torn message hangs from a wooden plank at a backcountry camp in the Barrens. Mercenaries, cutthroats, and drifters pass through such camps for brief shelter, far from the eyes of the Crossroads or Ratchet. Among the wilds' ordinary signs, the note offers a reason to look beyond the camp and toward the mountains.

quest:79236.text: Cherry for Your Thoughts?. In Booty Bay, a mercenary named Tokal is seeking a drink in exchange for the truth behind recent attacks on human and dwarven outposts. While rumors point the finger at the Horde, Tokal insists her group was operating under a private mercenary contract. In the bustling port of Booty Bay, an individual named Tokal is keeping a low profile while watching out for law enforcement. A series of aggressive raids recently devastated human and dwarven camps, fueling rumors that the Horde had orchestrated the attacks. When approached by travelers who clearly do not work for the inquiring marshal, Tokal is quick to push back against the widespread narrative, offering a different version of events in exchange for a drink.

quest:79974.text: Wet Job. On a mountainside, Wet Job sends you to recover an emergency reserve stash. Someone prepared it for a hasty escape and hid it near a high cliffside perch. In dangerous country, a reserve can make a quick escape possible. You search the rugged heights for a stash someone left there in case plans went wrong. Its supplies are waiting to be recovered. The directions lead to a high mountain perch, described as carved from the waterfalls of time. There, at the eagle's nest, a weathered messenger bag lies partly buried in the earth. Inside, provisions and parchment have endured beneath the soil, protected by dwarven craft.

quest:79975.text: Eagle's Fist. At a misty overlook, Eagle's Fist keeps a lonely watch over a weathered barricade. A letter speaks of loyalty to the Old Kingdoms and the Eagle and Fist, though its writer has left in haste. A folded letter lies inside a toolbox at a high overlook. From here, its writer says, one can call the shots or launch a parachute glider across the land. Misty spray dampens this lonely post, but the view reaches across historic lands. The letter's writer pledges lasting loyalty to the Eagle and Fist. To serve that cause well, the writer says, one must keep a measured distance. The nearby barricade has fallen into disrepair, like the Old Kingdoms it once shielded from danger. Still, the watcher vows never to abandon the post.

quest:79976.text: This Must Be The Place. At This Must Be The Place, a camper has vanished moments before anyone could catch up. A torn note says the writer has taken their work underground to keep it from the wrong hands. Someone broke camp at this secluded spot only moments ago. An inadequately secured sleeping bag unrolls underfoot, while heavy canvas lies bundled over assorted gear. A small scrap of paper holds a hurried parting message, but whoever camped here has vanished before anyone could catch up.

quest:79980.text: Scramble. A scavenger's note sends travelers down a steep cliff in search of Scramble's hidden supplies. One hundred paces north, they find provisions and a dirty parchment. A note points the way to a hidden supply cache. Its writer offers a few informal words of encouragement, then gives precise directions: go one hundred paces due north down the treacherous cliffside. Provisions wait there to keep a traveler going.

quest:80.text: The Legend of Stalvan. In Darkshire, the search for Stalvan Mistmantle brings a bloodstained journal page before the Night Watch. Commander Althea Ebonlocke sends you to Clerk Daltry to compare its writing with the town records. The Night Watch has gathered journal pages from across Duskwood and the surrounding human territories. Together, they appear to condemn Stalvan Mistmantle, the elusive tutor. Commander Althea Ebonlocke has suspected him for some time, but she needs certainty before passing judgment. The bloodstained page alone cannot prove who wrote it. The writing must be matched to Stalvan’s own hand.

quest:815.text: Break a Few Eggs. Break a Few Eggs is an errand assisting a harried cook who must keep up with endless meal preparations. Securing fresh, fragile ingredients without breaking them keeps the kitchen running and the cooking on schedule. Feeding a crowd is an exhausting, never-ending endeavor. Between breakfast, lunch, and dinner, there is scarcely any time to step away from the stove, let alone leave the kitchen to scrounge for raw provisions. In Break a Few Eggs, a hard-pressed cook turns to passing adventurers to secure fresh eggs before the next meal service falls behind. Transporting eggs requires a gentle touch that brute force cannot replace. The cook may offer sharp words and little praise, but intact ingredients speak for themselves. Once the eggs are delivered safe and unbroken, the cook wastes no time sending the gatherer off and returning straight to work over the fire.

quest:822.text: Chen's Empty Keg. In Ratchet, Brewmaster Drohn turns to another recipe shared by Chen Stormstout. Trogg ale calls for rare organs and glands from beasts of the Barrens. After helping Brewmaster Drohn recreate Chen Stormstout's first draught, you learn the wandering pandaren shared more than one brewing secret. Drohn has the formula for trogg ale, a strange brew made not from grain, but from potent parts of the wild beasts of central Kalimdor. To make trogg ale, Drohn needs lightning glands from stormhides, a thunderhawk saliva gland from greater thunderhawks, and a hearty liver from the plains' roaming kodos. Once distilled, these ingredients make a fiercely stimulating drink for life in the wilderness.

quest:824.text: Je'neu of the Earthen Ring. At Zoram'gar Outpost, Je'neu of the Earthen Ring studies a spreading corruption. Horde travelers bring him a corrupted water globe recovered from Ashenvale's elementals. As a shaman devoted to elemental harmony, he seeks to understand the blight along the Zoram Strand and within Blackfathom Deeps, in hope of halting the poison in the region's waters. Mastok Wrilehiss sends you to Je'neu Sancrea with a corrupted water globe recovered from Ashenvale's elementals. Strange elementals have surfaced across the region, animated by unnatural power that scouts cannot explain. Among their remains, the intact globe pulses with corrupted magic. Mastok knows soldiers and scouts lack the spiritual insight to understand it, so he directs Horde travelers to someone versed in ancient legends and elemental lore. Je'neu Sancrea serves the Earthen Ring, an order of shamans devoted to balance among Azeroth's primal forces. Horde forces guard the Zoram Strand frontier while he studies the spiritual wound in Blackfathom Deeps' nearby temple ruins. To Je'neu, an elemental drawing strength from a tainted vessel is no isolated threat. It is an alarming omen: unseen, ancient powers are perverting the natural order.

quest:8249.text: Junkboxes Needed. Fahrad keeps Ravenholdt supplied with locked boxes for rogue training. His demand never ends, and he trades specialized throwing knives to anyone who brings authentic heavy junkboxes. Ravenholdt Manor is a hidden redoubt in the mountains above Hillsbrad Foothills. Training never ceases there. Master thief Fahrad oversees the guild's operatives and prizes practical skill at picking locks. Zan supplies practice contraptions for new recruits, but Fahrad finds them too crude for experienced thieves who must open stubborn mechanisms in the field. Fahrad contracts for heavy junkboxes stolen from dangerous targets across Azeroth, and he accepts deliveries in batches. Only skilled thieves can lift the boxes from their marks in the wild, but anyone may bring them to the manor. Even boxes picked clean of major valuables earn Fahrad's favor and a supply of the manor's finely balanced throwing knives, so long as a token coin remains inside to motivate the initiates.

quest:8312.text: Hallow's End Treats for Spoops!. For Hallow's End Treats for Spoops!, an ailing child asks travelers to gather holiday sweets. Innkeepers in the cities and Kali Remik in Sen'jin Village share treats, and Spoops offers magical candy in return. Spoops is too ill to join Hallow's End outdoors. While others celebrate, Spoops asks travelers to gather holiday treats. In return, Spoops offers candy that changes whoever eats it into strange shapes. Travelers can find holiday treats in settlements across the realm. Innkeepers in major cities ask visitors to perform tricks before sharing their sweets. Kali Remik also gives out treats in Sen'jin Village on the coast of Durotar.

quest:837.text: Encroachment. Encroachment is a Horde quest directed by Gar'Thok at Razor Hill in central Durotar. It charges champions with striking deep into the western bramble dens to eliminate the entrenched Razormane quilboar threatening the borders of the young orc nation. When Thrall led the orcs to Kalimdor and founded Durotar, they found much of the harsh, arid land already inhabited by the Razormane quilboar. These aggressive, boar-like creatures proved a constant thorn in the side of the new settlement. Through sustained military efforts, the Horde drove back the bulk of their numbers, yet fortified pockets of Razormane continue to cling stubbornly to their thorned redoubts west of Razor Hill. Gar'Thok, an officer stationed at Razor Hill, oversees the effort to purge the lingering Razormane threat once and for all. He tasks seasoned defenders with striking directly into the western bramble camps to eliminate their scouts, warriors, and dustrunners. For Gar'Thok and the Horde leadership, allowing the quilboar any foothold near Razor Hill invites disaster, and striking them here is seen as the first step toward securing Kalimdor. Eliminating the quilboar defenders clears the path for Horde forces to torch the bramble dens, preventing the Razormane from reclaiming the western foothills. By burning these structures to the ground, the Horde removes an enduring menace and secures the western perimeter of Durotar, safeguarding vital supply roads between Razor Hill and the wider realm.

quest:8373.text: The Power of Pine. During Hallow’s End, Sergeant Hartman asks you to clear Forsaken stink bombs from Southshore. A pine-scented cleaner helps keep the village clean. During Hallow’s End, the Forsaken foul Southshore with stink bombs. The bombs mar the celebration of liberation. Sergeant Hartman asks you to remove any that have landed in the village with a Stink Bomb Cleaner.

quest:843.text: Gann's Reclamation. In the southern Barrens, Gann Stonespire seeks travelers to strike back at Bael Modan. The wandering tauren exile was driven from his clan’s ancestral home and hunting grounds, and asks you to slay the dig’s workers and bring him its leader’s journal. Gann Stonespire walks alone along the southern road, seeking bloody restitution for his fallen kin. His clan’s ancestral birthplace and hunting grounds lay among the red bluffs south of the Barrens. Dwarves from Ironforge came to build Bael Modan, and drove the tauren out or killed them to make room for quarries and trenches. Gann says peaceful protests and diplomacy failed. Now he seeks vengeance for the clan that was displaced and slain. At Bael Modan, dwarven excavators tear into the hills with steam engines and explosives. Prospector Khazgorm leads the dig deep into the earth. Gann asks you to thin the ranks of Bael'dun excavators and foremen, kill Khazgorm, and take the prospector’s personal excavation notes. He wants the notes to learn what the Alliance expedition seeks in the sacred soil.

quest:846.text: Revenge of Gann. In the southern Barrens, Gann Stonespire prepares to strike back at the Bael Modan dwarves. After Prospector Khazgorm's death, he sends Horde allies into the fortress for volatile munitions to fuel his attack. Gann Stonespire knows Prospector Khazgorm's death only slowed the Bael Modan dig site. Dwarven work will resume, and another foreman will soon oversee the machines tearing through Gann's ancestral land. He refuses to watch the earth suffer more excavation. Instead, Gann plans to turn the invaders' demolitions gear against them and rupture their stronghold from within. Bael Modan's fortress holds an excavation base and a garrison of soldiers, riflemen, and officers protecting dwarven interests in the Barrens. Gann has learned that its defenders carry nitroglycerin, wood pulp, and sodium nitrate, materials used in industrial demolition. He sends Horde allies past the perimeter to take these volatile supplies from the dwarves. With enough gathered, he can assemble a powerful satchel charge.

quest:847.text: Guile of the Raptor. After Tor'gan's orb gave Gor'mul the raptor's essence, the power he felt has him wondering about the shamans' magic. He sends you to tell Tor'gan he has been convinced, for the time being, and will listen. Gor'mul wonders aloud whether the power coursing through him is the shamans' power that Tor'gan tried to show him. He finds it interesting. He asks you to tell Tor'gan that he has been convinced, for the time being, and will hear what Tor'gan has to say.

quest:849.text: Revenge of Gann. At Bael Modan, Gann Stonespire turns the dwarves’ own plans against their flying machine. The Horde agent seeks revenge for the fallen Stonespire tribe. At Bael Modan, the dwarven excavation sits atop the ancestral grounds of the displaced Stonespire tauren. The Prospectors rely on a gyrocopter for their reach and military strength. It is stationed on a watchtower above the dig, where it surveys the surrounding Barrens and protects the dwarves’ supply lines. For Gann, the machine also marks the Alliance’s intrusion into kalimdorian soil.

quest:857.text: The Tear of the Moons. At Bael Modan, a relic called the Tear of the Moons has left Feegly the Exiled mad and obsessed. General Twinbraid has locked it away as a curse, but Feegly still demands its return. The dwarves found the Tear of the Moons while cutting into the southern Kalimdor hills for Bael Modan. It was their first major discovery, and its strange influence fell at once on Feegly, one of the expedition's workers. Feegly claimed the Tear granted him immense power and turned violently on his comrades to protect it. General Twinbraid saw the relic's corrupting hold, called it cursed, took it from Feegly, and secured it in the keep. Banished from the excavation camp, Feegly took refuge among the cliffs. Bitter and obsessed, he begs passing travelers to steal the Tear back.

quest:862.text: Dig Rat Stew. Grub waits east of the Crossroads, hungry for a pot of dig rat stew. He sends travelers to Bael Modan in the southern Barrens to bring back dig rats for his recipe. Across the dry Barrens, hunters bring down zhevras, plainstriders, and raptors. Grub, an orc camping east of the Crossroads, craves something different: dig rats. He says he is hungry all day and offers to share his recipe with any traveler willing to catch the burrowing rodents. Bael Modan lies deep in the southern Barrens, where dwarven prospectors dig into the red earth. Their work has disturbed nests of dig rats. The dwarves see the small rodents as an infestation, while Grub sees a feast close to the excavation. Grub says dig rats taste best after rotting for several weeks. For a hungry traveler who wants food now, he accepts fresher meat. His recipe shows how forgiving roadside cooking can be on Kalimdor's frontier.

quest:86576.text: Bloodfury Trinkets. Mor'rogal asks you to bring him sunstones from the Bloodfury harpies in the Charred Vale. He says they are bound to the lights of the skies. The Bloodfury harpies gather shiny things, among them golden-yellow sunstones. Mor'rogal is up on the hills above you and has mentioned using them. He asks you to bring him any Glittering Sunstones you find. Mor'rogal says sunstones reflect the sun's majesty. They can adorn shrines and homes with small motes of light. At night, the moon lends them its silver beauty. To him, they recall a bond with the lights of the skies.

quest:86585.text: Banner of the Fallen. In trogg territory, Mountaineer Ylva’s search for missing comrades ended beneath the trampled standard of Ironforge. Raising it again draws out the trogg that struck her down. Mountaineer Ylva’s trampled Ironforge standard marks where the Alliance scout met her end. She entered trogg territory to find comrades who had vanished on patrol, carrying the city’s banner as a sign of defiance. A powerful trogg struck with enough force to shatter her defenses. The standard was left in the dirt.

quest:86614.text: Silver of the Waves. A lost silver hair clip waits among fishing debris, and its owner is caught up in daily chores. Its return brings relief and restores a keepsake thought lost to the water. Among discarded fishing debris, you find an ornate silver hair clip marked with the initials K.D. Rusted hooks and broken wire spools lie nearby. Moisture has tarnished the clip, but its fine work still shows beneath the corrosion. The clip belongs to a hardworking local, busy with daily chores. You return the keepsake, which its owner had thought lost to the water for good. A little polishing will restore its shine, and the grateful owner welcomes its return.

quest:86667.text: Snowbound. In Loch Modan, Grenhild studies the local elementals while Norric Lochthane asks for snow from South Gate Pass. His request carries a deeper hope: the aging shaman longs to see his former student again. Grenhild is studying Loch Modan's local elementals when a minor elemental arrives with a message from Norric Lochthane, her former mentor. He urgently needs fresh, unmelted snow for his shamanic workings. Grenhild asks a traveler to fetch it so she can stay with her studies. The snow comes from South Gate Pass, where cold drafts preserve the drifts year-round, and must be sealed in a specially crafted ceramic jar to keep the valley heat at bay. Norric Lochthane lives in a quiet cottage on the Loch's northwest coast, away from the settlements. When the jar arrives, he is pleased to have the cold reagent for his mystical research. Yet he laments that Grenhild did not come herself. His request was for more than a magical ingredient: the aging shaman hoped to reconnect with his former student, now following her own path.

quest:86776.text: Ingredients for the Forge. In Thelsamar, Morhan Coppertongue needs bronze bars to fill his dwindling workshop stores. Far from Ironforge's steady trade, the settlement depends on travelers to bring the metals its forge needs. Thelsamar keeps a quieter pace than Ironforge's Great Forge. Far from the capital, supplies can be hard to come by. Morhan Coppertongue, the local blacksmith, makes the hardware, pots, and tools the township needs. Yet bronze and other raw metals often run short. Without regular shipments from the city, passing travelers and prospectors help keep the local anvils at work. Bronze bars let Morhan resume making goods for daily use. But the forge still faces shortages, and Loch Modan has no reliable merchant route bringing coal to town.

quest:868.text: Egg Hunt. Across the Barrens, Korran seeks silithid eggs for study. The Horde scholar at the Crossroads has heard of intelligent insect creatures in the south and wants intact eggs brought to Orgrimmar. Korran watches the Barrens from the Crossroads and reports to Orgrimmar. While the Horde faces tribal conflicts and Alliance incursions, he studies strange changes in the land. Intelligent, hive-minded insect creatures have begun burrowing into the southern Barrens. Korran needs samples to learn where the silithid come from and what drives them. With an excavation claw, you go to the Field of Giants and take intact eggs from the dirt mounds. Disturbing a mound draws the nearby brood to defend it, showing the swarm's uncanny coordination.

quest:8682.text: Skyseer the Elder. Skyseer the Elder is an honored ancestral spirit residing atop Freewind Post during the Lunar Festival. Travelers seek out his presence high above Thousand Needles to pay their respects to the ancestors and receive his ancient blessing. Perched upon the lofty wooden bluffs of Freewind Post, Elder Skyseer appears bathed in a radiant pillar of celestial light. Positioned near the bridges leading toward the massive mechanical lifts, his ghostly presence offers a quiet sanctuary amid the windswept mesas of Thousand Needles. Elder Skyseer receives visiting adventurers who come to honor the past during the celebration of the Lunar Festival. Beyond acknowledging their homage, the venerable elder can guide travelers toward his kin scattered across Kalimdor, including Elder Morningdew and Elder Runetotem.

quest:8724.text: Morningdew the Elder. Morningdew the Elder is an honored ancestral spirit visited during the Lunar Festival in Thousand Needles. Illuminated by a radiant beam of starlight, she offers ancient wisdom and directs pilgrims toward other elders scattered across Kalimdor. During the Lunar Festival, the spirits of ancient ancestors manifest across Azeroth to share their blessings with travelers. Elder Morningdew appears bathed in a shaft of lunar light, standing out starkly against the dusty red stone and noisy industrial hubbub of Thousand Needles. She reminds mortal travelers to look beyond earthly concerns to the starry expanse above. When approached, Morningdew encourages seekers to look toward the countless stars for answers to earthly mysteries. Beyond her contemplative greetings, she serves as a guide for festival pilgrims, sharing knowledge of the locations of other venerated spirits walking the lands, including Elder High Mountain, Elder Grimtotem, Elder Mistwalker, Elder Moonwarden, and Elder Windtotem.

quest:87288.text: Soft Saber Pelts. Soft Saber Pelts represents a trade agreement aimed at keeping wilderness roads secure from predatory cats. Hunters bring in the thick furs of local sabers so they can be crafted into warm, protective blankets and shawls. Traversing the untamed paths of Azeroth requires constant vigilance against prowling predators. Large sabers frequently roam near well-traveled thoroughfares, presenting a persistent hazard to couriers, merchants, and lone adventurers. While local inhabitants admire the grace and majesty of these great cats, allowing their numbers to swell unchecked along trade routes invites deadly ambushes. Gathering hunters to keep the local roads safe serves as a necessary measure for communal survival. Hunting such impressive beasts is not done merely for sport or eradication. In frontier encampments, every resource is valued, and the dense, velvety coats of wild sabers are prized for their warmth and durability. Once brought in by capable hunters, the pelts are tailored into fine shawls and heavy blankets capable of fending off harsh weather, ensuring that nothing taken from the wild goes to waste.

quest:873.text: Isha Awak. Along the Merchant Coast, Mahren Skyseer calls you to a hunt in the Great Sea. You are to slay Isha Awak, the Deep Doom, and bring back its heart for a rite of spirit and respect. South of Ratchet, Isha Awak prowls beneath the waves. Known as the Deep Doom, this immense sea creature commands the coastal waters with great strength. Human forces camped along the shore fear those waters after losing many scouts and soldiers to the predator's hunger. Mahren Skyseer reveres the leviathan, unlike the humans who fear it. To the tauren mystic, Isha Awak is no curse or mere pest, but a worthy foe whose might tests a hunter's resolve. Slaying the beast is an act of spiritual communion. Its heart holds the beast's essence, and claiming it lets the hunter carry that untamed spirit forward.

quest:874.text: Mahren Skyseer. At Camp Taurajo, hunters who have mastered the plains are sent east to Mahren Skyseer. Jorn Skyseer sends them to his sister to learn coastal tracking along the Barrens shore. Jorn Skyseer tests hunters at Camp Taurajo against the dangerous beasts of the southern Barrens. Once they have proved themselves on the red plains, he points them beyond dry earth and open savanna. A tracker must learn to follow prey through swamps, over sheer crags, and beside the crashing waves of the Great Sea. Mahren Skyseer keeps a camp far east along the coast. While Jorn studies thunderhawks and plains stalkers, his sister follows creatures that live in the salt spray. Reaching her means crossing dangerous ground. Kul Tiras marines and Theramore expedition forces hold fortified outposts and watchtowers across the coastal lowlands.

quest:87491.text: Spark of Freedom. The fire elemental has spent its strength in a blazing display. The Dark Irons held its attention, and the rest of the group is relieved it never turned on them. The fire elemental's display leaves the onlooker amazed, then relieved when the creature runs out of strength. The Dark Irons had drawn its attention. Had it turned on the rest of the group, they too could have been in danger.

quest:876.text: Serena Bloodfeather. Across the northern Barrens, harpy raids threaten the Crossroads supply lines. Serena Bloodfeather leads the Witchwing flock, driven by a blood feud with the Horde after Rexxar slew her sister. Ending her campaign could break the harpies’ coordination. Witchwing harpies strike the trails northwest of the Crossroads under Serena Bloodfeather’s command. Their attacks are driven by more than hunger: Serena seeks vengeance against the Horde. During Durotar’s founding, the beastmaster Rexxar slew her sister, the notorious matriarch Bloodfeather. Serena has rallied her flock to attack supply trains, scouts, and merchants traveling the arid trails.

quest:878.text: Tribes at War. Mangletooth bargains for help against the Bristleback from his cage in Camp Taurajo. The captive Razormane quilboar offers intelligence about quilboar incursions in exchange for the deaths of rival spiritual leaders. Mangletooth, a Razormane quilboar, is held in Camp Taurajo by the tauren. The Barrens has long been contested by two powerful quilboar tribes, the Razormane and the Bristleback. The Horde struggles to secure its settlements and supply lines against sudden ambushes. Mangletooth offers insight into who is tormenting Thork's outpost, but he asks a Horde champion to kill the Bristleback's most revered casters. Mangletooth sends you north to strike at the Bristleback's spiritual heart: its Water Seekers, Thornweavers, and Geomancers. Both tribes revere the earth and draw power from ancient magic tied to their demigod progenitor, Agamaggan. Killing the casters weakens Bristleback rituals, leaves the tribe vulnerable to Razormane rivals, and eases pressure on nearby trails.

quest:879.text: Betrayal from Within. At Camp Taurajo, Betrayal from Within begins with Mangletooth's offer of bloody vengeance. Imprisoned in a cage, the quilboar says his kin left him for dead. He offers Horde travelers knowledge of the three Razormane warlords who emerged from Razorfen Kraul to organize assaults across the Barrens. At Camp Taurajo, Mangletooth has lost all loyalty to his Razormane kin. They left him behind in defeat, and he faces execution in his cage. Now he wants vengeance against the leaders who abandoned him. He offers Horde travelers knowledge of the true architects behind the ruthless raids across the plains. Razormane attacks keep troubling the Horde, and Thork at the Crossroads struggles to curb them. Mangletooth names three commanders from deep within Razorfen Kraul: Lok Orcbane, a formidable warrior, and his companions Nak, a tracker, and Kuz, a spellcaster. They direct Razormane raiders from encampments far to the south. Mangletooth demands their severed skulls as proof that his betrayers have fallen before his own end arrives.

quest:883.text: Lakota'mani. At Camp Taurajo, hunters bring Lakota'mani's hoof to Jorn Skyseer after the hunt. The offering honors the mighty kodo's spirit and marks the hunter as an equal to its strength. Among the Barrens herds, Lakota'mani is a kodo of great size and endurance. In Taur-ahe, the tauren tongue, his name means “Earthshaker,” and his steps rumble across the plains. Tauren hunters track and defeat such a beast not for slaughter, but to meet the raw vigor of Kalimdor's wildlife in a sacred hunt. When you bring Lakota'mani's hoof to Jorn Skyseer at Camp Taurajo, the hunt reaches its close. Jorn sees a new power and stride in hunters who return from the encounter. Presenting the trophy earns his blessing, honoring Lakota'mani's courage and primal spirit as companions on your path.

quest:884.text: Owatanka. Across the southern Barrens, Owatanka roams as a swift thunder lizard known to the tauren as Bluebolt. Slaying the beast yields a crackling tailspike, carried to Jorn Skyseer at Camp Taurajo in honor of the elders’ tradition of learning from Kalimdor’s primordial beasts. Owatanka prowls the southern Barrens, where tauren hunters speak of him with reverence. Unlike his massive, plodding kin, he moves with blinding speed. The tauren call him Bluebolt, for the storm changed him. Tauren lore says lightning struck Owatanka long ago. The thunder lizard survived, and the strike filled him with unending energy and fury. Even after his death, his tailspike crackles with stray sparks when handled, a remnant of the storm’s power. Taking Owatanka's Tailspike to Jorn Skyseer at Camp Taurajo marks a hunter’s prowess and spirit. Jorn recognizes the encounter in the eyes of any hunter who has outmatched the beast’s speed. Presenting the trophy honors Bluebolt’s enduring swiftness.

quest:885.text: Washte Pawne. Across the southern Barrens, Washte Pawne's quill leaves a sting that hunters carry to Jorn Skyseer at Camp Taurajo. Its pain makes the hunt a trial of regret for the tauren. Thunderhawks are elusive creatures of the Barrens, and wandering nomadic tribes treat them with reverence. Washte Pawne means “Spirit Biter” in Taurahe and holds a special place among them. Its death is no ordinary hunt: shamans whisper that striking down a thunderhawk can bring omens of triumph or misfortune. After Washte Pawne falls, its feather burns with a pain that lingers on the skin. Jorn Skyseer at Camp Taurajo explains that the ache is not poison, but regret. Taking a magnificent life bears a burden. The hunter must face that sorrow and turn it into lasting wisdom.

quest:8852.text: Ten Signets for War Supplies. Warlord Gorchuk trades Horde Commendation Signets for war supplies in Orgrimmar. Champions give up formal recognition for equipment that can help keep soldiers supplied at the front. Warlord Gorchuk oversees the Horde's supplies in the Valley of Spirits. As the Horde gathers its legions, weapons, rations, and armor must reach the front. Champions who have proved their dedication can trade commendation signets for useful equipment drawn from the army's reserves. Horde Commendation Signets usually prove a soldier's service and bring prestige with the leadership. Trading them for gear gives up that formal recognition for the chance to survive the fighting. Gorchuk knows that a satchel of supplies or a sturdy weapon can mean the difference between life and death when armies clash.

quest:88756.text: Bring Back a Bang. A construction site has lost blasting powder to Dark Iron dwarves camped east on Direforge Hill. Their marked barrels could bring danger to the surrounding lands. Dark Iron dwarves camp east on Direforge Hill. They raided a nearby construction site and carried its vital blasting powder back to their tents. Blasting powder in malicious Dark Iron hands threatens the surrounding lands. The stolen barrels bear red markings that set them apart from common supplies. Recover them before the dwarves put the powder to destructive use.

quest:889.text: Spirit of the Wind. At Camp Taurajo, Mangletooth offers travelers a burst of speed drawn from Agamaggan's blood shards. The captive quilboar's ritual helps them cross the Barrens swiftly. Crossing the Barrens quickly can help you avoid its beasts and centaur warbands. At Camp Taurajo, the captive quilboar Mangletooth draws on red crystalline blood shards scattered across the region. Give him ten, and he channels their lingering power into a burst of swiftness called the Spirit of the Wind. Quilboar honor Agamaggan, the Great Boar whose blood was spilled across central Kalimdor during the ancient War of the Ancients. Mangletooth knows the rites that channel that spilled blood, even in captivity. The ritual stirs wild vigor, lending a runner speed to match the zhevra herds. Though quilboar are bitter enemies of the Horde, Mangletooth shares Agamaggan's boons with travelers who bring him fresh shards.

quest:89.text: The Everstill Bridge. In Lakeshire, The Everstill Bridge still waits for repairs. Iron meant for the work went into weapons during the last orc invasion, and Redridge gnolls ambushed the replacement caravan from Stormwind. You find Lakeshire's stone bridge across Lake Everstill unfinished. It links the western roads toward Elwynn Forest with the far bank and the northern passes. Recent orc incursions brought the town close to ruin. To survive, Lakeshire melted its structural iron into munitions, blades, and plate armor to repel the Blackrock invaders. The bridge was left incomplete and vulnerable. Foreman Oslow asked the House of Nobles and Stormwind for fresh materials to finish the repairs. A caravan carrying iron set out, but Redridge gnolls ambushed it on the road. They took iron pikes and rivets to their camps in the northern hills. You can help recover the stolen supplies; without them, the bridge work remains stalled as gnolls and orcs tighten their hold on the mountains.

quest:891.text: The Guns of Northwatch. Captain Thalo'thas Brightsun in Ratchet wants the guns at Northwatch Hold silenced. Alliance gunners there have been blasting merchant vessels, so he sends you down the Merchant Coast to strike the artillery officers and bring back badges from fallen infantry. Northwatch Hold guards the southern Barrens coast for the humans of Theramore. Its soldiers watch Horde activity in Kalimdor, but fear has made them see every unfamiliar sail as a threat. The guns on the ramparts fire without warning at passing ships, endangering Ratchet's merchant traffic and its privateering vessels. Captain Brightsun wants the attacks on his ships answered. Captain Fairmount commands Northwatch, with Whessan and Smythe directing its guns. Defeating them and taking Theramore medals from the garrison throws the artillery into disarray and gives Ratchet's ships room to travel along the Merchant Coast.

quest:893.text: Weapons of Choice. At Camp Taurajo, Tatternack Steelforge investigates reports of sturdy Razormane weapons.
