He sends travelers past the Field of Giants to recover them, so the Horde can judge the threat. The Razormane are making unusually durable weapons in the southern Barrens. Most quilboar are dismissed as crude fighters with tools of wood, bone, and stone, so the reports have caught the Horde’s attention. Tatternack Steelforge, an orc smith at Camp Taurajo, is investigating under orders from Warchief Thrall. He doubts the quilboar know proper metalwork and wants proof of whether they have learned new techniques or found better supplies. Tatternack needs weapons from different parts of the Razormane arsenal to study their craft. South of the Field of Giants, scouts face Razormane war camps and seize weapons from their fighters. Razormane Stalkers carry backstabber daggers, Razormane Seers wield charred wands, and frenzied shock troops bear heavy war shields. Each item offers a glimpse of the martial and mystic arts behind the Razormane push against Horde territory.

quest:897.text: The Harvester. A severed head found in the southern Barrens brings The Harvester’s strange presence to Camp Taurajo. Jorn Skyseer examines the remains, and the creature’s intrusion raises concerns for the land’s spiritual and ecological balance. In the southern Barrens, you find the severed head of a silithid called the Harvester. Lions, raptors, and kodos roam these grasslands, but this chitinous insectoid is unlike the native wildlife. Its presence suggests an alien ecology has reached the open plains of Kalimdor.

quest:898.text: Free From the Hold. Gilthares Firebough is held at Northwatch Hold after Alliance forces sink his ship off the Barrens coast. The elf deckhand wants to reach his captain in Ratchet. Gilthares Firebough is held in the dungeons at Northwatch Hold. Theramore uses the fortress as its military foothold on the Barrens coast, where its garrison watches for threats. Gilthares had been aboard a ship carrying moonshine along the trade route between Ratchet and Booty Bay when Alliance forces bombarded it and sent it beneath the sea. He alone survived the wreck. The soldiers took him to Northwatch and accused him of being an enemy agent conspiring against the Alliance. Gilthares says he is only a deckhand who was carrying illicit liquor. With help from Horde forces, he fights his way out of Northwatch Hold and flees north along the shore toward Ratchet. Captain Thalo'thas Brightsun welcomes him back to the crew of the Thalo'dan Privateers.

quest:899.text: Consumed by Hatred. Mankrik turns his grief at the Crossroads into a campaign against the Bristleback quilboar. The orc was separated from his wife in a violent ambush, and now he calls on Horde travelers to kill the creatures and bring back their tusks. Mankrik carries the grief of a quilboar ambush that left him battered and his wife missing. At the Crossroads, he watches the arid horizon, still thirsting for the blood of the Bristlebacks despite the many he has killed himself. He calls on fellow Horde travelers to help him continue the fight. Mankrik demands sixty Bristleback quilboar tusks. Each one is a measure of suffering returned to the creatures that tore his life apart. The trophies cannot heal his grief or end his desire for revenge, but seeing the Bristlebacks bleed brings the wounded warrior a fleeting, bitter satisfaction.

quest:90.text: Seasoned Wolf Kabobs. In Darkshire, Chef Grual prepares his signature dish at the Scarlet Raven Tavern. He asks you to hunt Duskwood wolves for meat while his herbs arrive from Stormwind City. Darkshire sits isolated among Duskwood's creeping horrors. Trade caravans rarely come, farming has collapsed, and undead lurk nearby, yet the town still needs food. Chef Grual cooks at the Scarlet Raven Tavern, turning dangerous forest wolves into hearty skewers. Local timber and soil cannot support delicate crops, so he depends on spices brought from the capital to make the gamey meat palatable. Grual has just received his latest shipment of Stormwind Seasoning Herbs. All he lacks is lean meat from the ferocious wolves stalking Duskwood. The delivery shows how Darkshire remains tied to the wider kingdom: royal military aid has dwindled, while small civic ties and supply lines between city merchants and outer hamlets barely endure.

quest:906.text: Betrayal from Within. In the central Barrens, Betrayal from Within brings the hunt for Lok Orcbane to its end. His fall will weaken the Razormane raids, and you carry his severed head to Thork at the Crossroads. At Camp Taurajo, Mangletooth is a captured Razormane quilboar held in a cage. He names Lok Orcbane as the chieftain directing attacks on Horde caravans. After you slay Lok deep in the southern thorn mazes, Mangletooth gives you the chieftain's skull. He finds it amusing that the orcs will benefit from betrayal within the tribe without knowing a captive quilboar helped them.

quest:91.text: Solomon's Law. In Lakeshire, Solomon's Law puts the Shadowhide gnolls under sentence of death for aiding Morganth, an enemy of Stormwind. Bailiff Conacher issues the decree from the town hall and seeks proof that the sentence has been carried out. Lakeshire governs Redridge with little military help from Stormwind. Magistrate Solomon and the town officials rely on strict frontier authority to keep order. Bailiff Conacher works from the town hall as the magistrate court's arm. When threats reach the township, the court places bounties on offenders and depends on hired mercenaries and traveling defenders to uphold the kingdom's laws. The Shadowhide clan faces execution for aiding Morganth, a rogue spellcaster in the eastern hills. Lakeshire and Stormwind law calls for death when someone directly helps a declared enemy of the realm. The gnolls carry out Morganth's bidding, so the court treats them as treasonous fighters rather than wild scavengers.

quest:91282.text: A Second Home. Newly risen Forsaken are being invited to join an order in Tirisfal Glades. They are directed to Bandarion Keep, a monastery on the bluffs northwest of the Solliden Farmstead near the Whispering Woods. The order offers community, shared faith, and mutual support as they make a place in their new unlife. Newly risen Forsaken in Tirisfal Glades are urged to find fellowship among their peers. Together, they can face unlife through mutual faith and community, and discover their full potential. Travelers are directed to Bandarion Keep, a monastery on the bluffs northwest of the Solliden Farmstead. Beside the Whispering Woods, it offers the new order a refuge to study, practice, and establish roots in Tirisfal.

quest:91285.text: Murlocs at the Gates. Breton Samuels asks you to drive back murlocs troubling the keep. Their attacks make rebuilding harder. Murlocs still trouble the keep after you and the others drove them from their spawning grounds. Their attacks are growing harder to manage, so Breton Samuels asks you to drive back some of them. They lurk in the bluffs along the eastern road and in camps around the lake to the west. Breton Samuels expects the attacks to continue. He hopes pushing back the Vile Fin attackers and seers will slow them down. The keep is already hard to rebuild while murlocs strike at its people.

quest:91294.text: Touring the Grounds. Breton asks you to walk Bandarion Keep after the murloc attacks come under control. Meeting Danitha Morr is your first step toward settling among the residents. Breton asks you to meet Bandarion Keep’s residents and look around the stronghold. Once you have finished, Danitha Morr can help you settle in. The keep is still small, but its people call it home. Danitha Morr introduces herself as the closest thing Bandarion Keep has to a commander. She welcomes those seeking fellowship with people still loyal to the Light. The keep needs help before it can be fully established.

quest:913.text: Cry of the Thunderhawk. In the southern Barrens, Cry of the Thunderhawk brings a hunter to the final trial. Entrusted by Camp Taurajo's elders, you seek a winged serpent in the scrublands and return with its wings to prove mastery of the savanna's fiercest beasts. After hunters prove themselves against prowling plainstriders, prowlers, and agitated thunder lizards, Jorn Skyseer directs them toward their final challenge. The thunderhawk is one of the fiercest aerial predators around Camp Taurajo. Slaying one takes patience, sharp aim, and an awareness of the sky that few landbound predators possess. Bringing back the thunderhawk's wings ends a novice's tutelage under Camp Taurajo's watch. To the tauren, hunting is no mere slaughter. It is a spiritual walk in harmony with the Earthmother and the wild's natural order. Besting this proud creature shows strength, courage, and honor, virtues needed before entering the harsher wilderness beyond the central plains.

quest:91316.text: Making Repairs. At the fortress, a shortage of building materials has made restoration difficult. You are sent to Shadowvale to search for lumber. Shadowvale is a ruined village in the Whispering Forest, southwest of the fortress. Search an old root cellar in one of its buildings for usable materials. The fortress lies far from settled lands, so bringing in supplies is difficult. Its repairs depend on what can be found there.

quest:91317.text: The Tarnished. At Shadowvale in Tirisfal Glades, the Tarnished threaten a fledgling order's place among the Forsaken. Their attacks deepen mistrust and put the order's future at risk. Some risen still bear prejudices from their former lives, and now attack their fellow Forsaken. The Tarnished have gathered at Shadowvale, southwest of here. Their violence must end, and Commander Rudolph Gelhardt’s head must be brought back. The Tarnished’s attacks give those who distrust the order more reason to turn against it. Stopping them may help the order earn a place among the Forsaken. Acceptance could still take years or decades.

quest:914.text: Leaders of the Fang. Leaders of the Fang is a pivotal Horde quest tasked by Nara Wildmane from the heights of Thunder Bluff. It directs adventurers into the Wailing Caverns to strike down the four leaders of the corrupted Druids of the Fang and retrieve their twisted dream gems. Halting these rogue druids is essential to preventing their serpentine nightmare from permanently overtaking the Barrens. The night elf druid Naralex ventured into the subterranean springs of the Wailing Caverns with a selfless ambition: to use the Emerald Dream to restore lush vitality to the arid Barrens. Tragically, when his slumber took root, his dream turned into a waking nightmare. The acolytes who accompanied him lost their devotion to nature's harmony, succumbing to the nightmare's corruption and adopting the mantle of the Druids of the Fang. To reshape the Barrens into their own viperous Eden, the leaders of the splintered sect channel the warped dream energies through specialized foci known as dream gems. Lord Cobrahn, Lady Anacondra, Lord Pythas, and Lord Serpentis each bear one of these gems. As long as these artifacts remain in their grasp, their corrupting influence will seep outward into the soil and waters of Kalimdor.

quest:91723.text: Delicate Instruments. Delicate Instruments is a quest in Elwynn Forest given by Hamish Bergwort at the Tower of Azora. Hamish's sensitive arcane equipment is being disrupted by erratic magical surges radiating from the north. To restore stability, travelers must enter Jasperlode Mine and cull the kobold geomancers responsible for the disturbances. Inside the Tower of Azora, Hamish Bergwort oversees delicate arcane apparatus that requires fine calibration. Unfortunately for the scholar, the surrounding countryside is far from quiet. Repeated surges of uncontrolled energy constantly throw off his measurements, rendering careful magical adjustments impossible until the source of the interference is addressed. Investigation traces the magical pulses directly northward to Jasperlode Mine. The subterranean tunnels have been claimed by kobolds, whose geomancers channel crude earth magic within the stone. While their sorcery lacks scholarly refinement, the sheer frequency of their crude rituals generates elemental ripples potent enough to travel through the earth and unsettle Azora's sensitive instruments.

quest:91724.text: Delicate Instruments. Delicate Instruments is a quest in eastern Elwynn Forest focused on restoring magical stability to the Tower of Azora. Hamish Bergwort's sensitive equipment is being disrupted by erratic spellcasting practiced by nearby Defias rogue wizards. Resolving the disturbance requires putting an end to the amateur sorcery around Stone Cairn Lake. Within the Tower of Azora, Hamish Bergwort attempts to conduct delicate magical experiments, only to be repeatedly interrupted by unexplained ambient disruptions. In an arcane sanctuary where precise measurements are everything, even slight ripples in the local magical weave can ruin hours of careful work. Bergwort suspects the disruptions are not natural, but rather the result of crude spells cast nearby. The source of the magical static traces back to Stone Cairn Lake, where Defias rogue wizards have been practicing unchecked spellcraft. The Defias Brotherhood's reliance on rogue spellcasters introduces unstable, amateur magic into the Elwynn countryside. Dispatching these rogue wizards silences the magical noise, finally allowing Bergwort's sensitive instruments to register clean readings.

quest:91725.text: Stolen Enchanting Supplies. Stolen Enchanting Supplies is an errand undertaken near the Tower of Azora in eastern Elwynn Forest. An apprentice named Blixie Fitzwink lost a shipment of magical reagents during a gnoll ambush, and adventurers must retrieve the stolen goods from camps around Stone Cairn Lake. Recovering the materials spares the apprentice severe chore duty and keeps Master Theocritus's arcane studies supplied. A routine supply run turns perilous when Blixie Fitzwink, an apprentice assisting Master Theocritus, is ambushed by hostile gnolls between the trading post and the Tower of Azora. Fleeing for her life, she drops her cargo, leaving valuable enchanting reagents scattered among the gnoll camps dotting the shores of Stone Cairn Lake. Desperate to avoid weeks of disciplinary cleanup duty following arcane polymorph experiments, she appeals to passing adventurers to recover the missing goods. The Tower of Azora serves as an arcane bastion in eastern Elwynn Forest, where Master Theocritus conducts sensitive magical research. Sourcing delicate reagents requires regular traffic with local trading posts, but the rising boldness of gnoll packs around Stone Cairn Lake makes transport hazardous. Recovering the lost supplies ensures that Theocritus's studies continue uninterrupted while keeping his beleaguered assistant out of trouble.

quest:91732.text: Good Steel. Good Steel is an Alliance quest originating at Eastvale Logging Camp in eastern Elwynn Forest. In the wake of recent conflicts, high-quality metal has become scarce, leaving the camp's woodcutting equipment worn and difficult to replace. Craftsman Hagar Lowe tasks adventurers with delving into Jasperlode Mine to salvage well-crafted pickaxes so their steel can be repurposed. Following the devastating conflicts that have battered the human kingdoms, high-grade steel has become an increasingly scarce luxury in Elwynn Forest. At Eastvale Logging Camp, daily timber harvesting relies heavily on durable axes, saws, and hardware, but the tools currently available have suffered badly from substandard metal and constant wear. Without reliable shipments coming from Stormwind's foundries, camp craftsmen like Hagar Lowe are forced to find inventive solutions to keep the forestry camp functioning. To replace worn equipment, Hagar sets his sights on Jasperlode Mine, an abandoned excavation north of the camp. The miners who worked the rich veins before the mine's fall used finely crafted picks forged from an era when steel was plentiful and expertly tempered. Rather than letting those sturdy implements rust away in the dark, adventurers are dispatched to venture into the infested tunnels, recover the abandoned picks, and bring them back to Eastvale so their superior metal can be melted down and repurposed for the camp's lumberjacks.

quest:91733.text: Downstream. Downstream is a quest in eastern Elwynn Forest tasked by Ormin Pelford at Eastvale Logging Camp. After Ormin's wagon accidentally overturns into the river, adventurers are asked to brave murlocs and wolves downstream to recover waterlogged timber supplies. While transporting a shipment of gear back from a local trading post, laborer Ormin Pelford suffered a mishap when his wagon tipped over along the waterway near Eastvale Logging Camp. The cargo tumbled into the current and was quickly swept downstream before he could secure it. Without these vital woodworking tools, the loggers face delays in their timber operations. Retrieving the waterlogged cargo is complicated by the hazardous local wildlife. Aggressive murlocs claim the muddy shoals downstream, while predatory wolves roam the surrounding woods. Unable to fend off these threats alone, Ormin relies on hardy travelers to braze the riverbanks, salvage the submerged saw, axe, and toolbox, and bring them back safely.

quest:91736.text: Applejack Still. The Applejack Still is a distillation apparatus used to process fermented apples into high-proof liquor. Approaching the device reveals a stinging vapor of concentrated fruit, which the machine condenses and dispenses as a clear spirit. The Applejack Still is a functional distillation device constructed to refine fermented cider into high-proof spirits. Anyone stepping close to the apparatus is immediately greeted by a pungent aroma of concentrated apples sharp enough to sting the nostrils. Its piping and condensing coils efficiently extract and concentrate the essence of the orchard harvest into potent liquor. Once activated and allowed to run its course, the machine condenses the vaporized alcohol into a clear, purified spirit. The finished applejack dispenses neatly into a waiting bottle at the outlet, ready for consumption or storage. Despite the rough-and-ready nature of field distilling, the apparatus reliably produces a clear and potent brew.

quest:91740.text: Croaky's Head. Croaky's Head is the severed bounty from a menacing murloc leader who terrorized the roads of eastern Elwynn Forest. Bringing proof of the creature's death to the Stormwind guard at Ridgepoint Tower offers grim relief to a garrison grieving their fallen comrades. It marks an essential victory for local defenders struggling to secure Elwynn's contested waterways. Murlocs along the rivers and streams of Elwynn Forest have grown increasingly bolder, ambushing unwary travelers and threatening vital trade routes. Among these aquatic raiders, Croaky stood out as a particularly aggressive chieftain, rallying other murlocs and leading attacks dangerously close to local roads. For merchants, farmers, and travelers moving between Elwynn and Redridge, the creature's presence turned peaceful roadways into deadly hazard zones. Striking down this aggressive raider halts a relentless series of ambushes, removing a brazen menace that openly challenged Stormwind's hold over the eastern woodland outskirts. Ridgepoint Tower stands as Stormwind's easternmost sentinel post in Elwynn Forest, guarding the strategic crossing into Redridge Mountains. The guards stationed here, led by Officer Merell Ross, have found themselves stretched thin against the surrounding dangers. The escalating murloc aggression recently claimed the lives of two watchmen on patrol, shaking the outpost and highlighting just how vulnerable the border has become. Presenting Croaky's severed head to Officer Ross delivers tangible proof of retribution, lifting the beleaguered garrison's morale and giving the defenders an opening to finally drive the aquatic raiders back from Elwynn's borders.

quest:91741.text: Nibbled-On Book. The Nibbled-On Book is a volume from Northshire Abbey's library recovered from kobold scavengers in Northshire Valley. Bearing the tooth marks of a confused or ravenous creature, it must be returned to Brother Paxton to preserve the abbey's modest collection. Among the subterranean pests troubling Northshire Valley, kobolds are notorious scavengers known for dragging off anything left unguarded. When an adventurer recovers a chewed tome dropped by a slain kobold, it becomes evident that the creature was not merely hoarding shiny trinkets, but actively trying to gnaw through the cover and parchment. The text clearly originates from the library shelves of nearby Northshire Abbey, bearing marks from the pests' voracious appetites. Inside Northshire Abbey, Brother Paxton diligently tends to a small library intended for the quiet contemplation and instruction of the Brotherhood of Northshire. Unfortunately, the brazen vermin creeping around the valley have developed a troublesome habit of slipping in and snatching volumes straight off the shelves. While Brother Paxton is grateful to recover this particular nibbled volume, he remains anxious about the rest of his scattered collection still missing in the hands of the valley's pests.

quest:91743.text: Rascally Rodents. Rascally Rodents is a quest in Northshire Valley where Brother Paxton tasks adventurers with recovering stolen books from the local kobolds. Though Paxton initially fears the vermin are devouring his library, retrieving the texts reveals an unsettling mystery behind the creatures' motives. Brother Paxton in Northshire Valley is in distress over the local kobold infestation, which has spilled over from the surrounding hills and mines into the sacred grounds. Convinced that the ravenous creatures have begun devouring the texts from his collection, he enlists the aid of young adventurers to hunt down the vermin and salvage whatever volumes remain before the entire library is lost.

quest:91745.text: Mining Consultant. Mining Consultant is a Northshire Valley quest that sends adventurers to confer with Kelsey Fargo, a mining apprentice stationed outside Echo Ridge Mine. Her observations reveal an unusual development: the local kobolds have begun plundering books from Northshire Abbey's library. The kobold infestation at Echo Ridge Mine has taken an unexpected turn. Rather than merely defending subterranean claims and gathering candles, the creatures have caught the attention of local authorities due to strange, coordinated disturbances. Adventurers are directed to seek out Kelsey Fargo, a mining apprentice stationed near the mine's entrance, to ascertain what she has witnessed from her vantage point outside the tunnels.

quest:91746.text: Elmpaw's Head. Elmpaw's Head is a trophy quest rewarding an adventurer for hunting down the formidable beast Elmpaw. The creature's head is traded to an artisan who prepares mounted trophies for wealthy collectors. Elmpaw's Head marks the conclusion of a hunt against the creature known as Elmpaw. Felling such a beast is regarded as an impressive accomplishment by wilderness trackers and collectors alike, who value tangible proof of victory over dangerous wildlife. Upon presenting Elmpaw's severed head, the hunter is rewarded directly by an enterprising handler. Rather than letting the remains go to waste, the recipient prepares and mounts the trophy to sell to affluent patrons looking to adorn their mantles with fierce wild prizes.

quest:91751.text: Rough Wolf Pelts. Rough Wolf Pelts is an introductory skinning quest in Elwynn Forest offered by Helene Peltskinner near Goldshire. With her husband away assisting near Northshire Abbey, Helene relies on capable skinners to harvest raw hides from local wolves to complete her pending leatherworking orders. Just outside Goldshire, Helene Peltskinner works diligently to supply travelers and residents with cured leather and furs. While her husband typically hunts the prowling timber wolves of Elwynn Forest to keep her workshop supplied, duties near Northshire Abbey have taken him away from the workbench. Left with a backlog of customer orders to finish, Helene enlists the aid of passing apprentices willing to turn their skinning knives toward the local wildlife. The dense woodlands of Elwynn Forest teem with timber wolves that stalk the edges of farmlands and roadways. For novice skinners, gathering rough wolf pelts serves as practical field experience in the trade of hide harvesting. Delivering these skins allows Helene to maintain her business and keep trade flowing through Goldshire, while providing wandering hunters a chance to hone their woodcraft.

quest:91752.text: The Big Picture. The Big Picture is a Northshire Valley task concerning a thieving kobold named Shinyfinder Narf, who has been hoarding stolen books deep within the local mine. Adventurers are dispatched by local authorities to recover the illustrated volumes and return them to Marshal McBride at Northshire Abbey. A peculiar incident has disrupted the peace of Northshire Valley: kobolds lurking around the region have been seen scurrying away with books, crying out 'Picture for Narf!' While kobolds are typically infamous for scavenging candles and shiny trinkets, one particular cave-dweller known as Shinyfinder Narf has developed an appetite for illustrated tomes, accumulating a whole sack of them in his subterranean hideout.

quest:91753.text: An Enchanting Lesson. At the Tower of Azora in Elwynn Forest, Kitta Firewind gives An Enchanting Lesson to apprentice enchanters. Kobold geomancers bind simple magic into crude wax effigies, showing why practice matters alongside arcane theory. Kitta Firewind, an enchanter at the Tower of Azora, challenges apprentice enchanters to look beyond polished libraries. She asks them to examine magic where it appears naturally. Even the uneducated kobolds beneath Elwynn Forest channel cantrips into everyday talismans, proof that magical instinct can thrive without formal schooling. Kobold geomancers shape Crude Wax Effigies with simple folk enchantments. Students obtain the effigies and carefully unravel their bound magic through disenchantment, extracting Luminous Residue. By taking these primitive charms apart, they learn how raw magic behaves in the field. Enchantment's fundamental threads are found through observation as well as in grimoires.

quest:91758.text: Follow That Kobold!. Follow That Kobold! is an Alliance quest in Northshire Valley dealing with a bizarre theft from the local mines. A kobold has fled with a sack of Brother Paxton's books, prompting the abbey to recruit the dwarven hunter trainer Tordrin Sternblade to assist in tracking the thief. Just when the workers and clerics of Northshire Abbey believed the vermin problem in the mines was under control, an unusual report arrived from Kelsey: a lone kobold was spotted fleeing the tunnels hauling a heavy sack of books. The stolen volumes belong to Brother Paxton, who urgently requires their return to the abbey's collection. Tracking a nimble subterranean scavenger through the wooded grounds of Northshire requires specialized skill. To find the thief, adventurers are directed behind the abbey to the stables to seek out Tordrin Sternblade, a dwarven Hunter trainer newly arrived from Ironforge who possesses the wilderness knowledge needed to pick up the scent.

quest:91772.text: Shhh! We're Hunting Kobolds. 'Shhh! We're Hunting Kobolds' is a quest that leads adventurers out of Northshire Valley to track wandering kobolds into Elwynn Forest. Using a tracking kit, players discover the trail leads toward the infested Fargodeep Mine and report the findings to Marshal Dughan in Goldshire. As the kobold infestation in Northshire Valley escalates, signs indicate that the vermin are organizing beyond the isolated abbey grounds. Equipped with a tracking kit, scouts are dispatched to follow the trail of the creatures to determine where they are concentrating their efforts. This reconnaissance serves as a crucial bridge between Northshire's local troubles and the broader defense of Elwynn Forest.

quest:91775.text: Book Return. Book Return is an Elwynn Forest quest directing adventurers to recover Brother Paxton's lost reading materials from the infested depths of Fargodeep Mine. Chief among the missing volumes is 'Fun with Elementals,' a beginner's guide that risks granting the mine's kobolds dangerous conjuration abilities if left in their clutches. While investigating the growing kobold menace within Fargodeep Mine, Marshal Dughan tasks adventurers with recovering missing volumes belonging to Brother Paxton of Northshire Abbey. Among the scattered texts lost in the dim subterranean tunnels is a particularly volatile primer titled 'Fun with Elementals.' Paxton fears that the instructions within are so accessible that even the mine's crude kobold squatters could decipher them and conjure an elemental creature in the depths. Fargodeep Mine was once a prosperous gold venture for the kingdom of Stormwind, but recent troubles have allowed vermin to overrun its lower levels. As Elwynn's defenders stretch thin, recovered texts must be stored safely in a protective book bag to survive the damp, treacherous caverns. Retrieving Paxton's lost library ensures that mundane records are preserved and hazardous arcane lessons stay out of primitive hands.

quest:91777.text: Rare Books. Rare Books is an Alliance quest in Northshire Valley focused on recovering two stolen magical primers for Brother Paxton. Kobolds have hauled the missing texts into the Jasperlode Mine, where they appear to be studying elementary magic and summoning rituals. Brother Paxton of Northshire Abbey faces a crisis in his library: several volumes have been carried off by vermin infesting the valley. Only two books remain missing from his catalog: 'Geomancy for Curious Young Wizards' and 'Arcane Explainer: Magical Stuff in Simple Words'. These educational primers were carted away into the depths of the Jasperlode Mine by the occupying kobolds.

quest:91859.text: A Curious Pair. In the Sepulcher, Trevan Rol spots an unusual pair passing through Silverpine Forest. The tauren and high elf travel under the Earthen Ring's banner, a rare sight in Horde territory that draws suspicion. Trevan Rol sees two travelers claiming to represent the Earthen Ring pass along the road by the Sepulcher. The outpost is a grim waystation where strangers, especially those on diplomatic business, draw close scrutiny. A tauren traveling under the shamanic order's banner raises little surprise. His cloaked companion is another matter: the scout recognizes an unmistakable high elf, a sight that strikes the Forsaken as exceedingly strange. A high elf traveling openly beside a member of the Horde's shamanic circles raises questions among the Forsaken sentries. The Earthen Ring concerns itself with the balance of the elements, and high elves are rarely seen in Lordaeron, much less as companions to tauren envoys. To learn where the pair went and what business brought them to the forest, you are directed to Deathguard Baldren at the edge of town.

quest:91899.text: A Sealed Crate. Trade handlers seek lost cargo as bandits disrupt the roads. You can recover sealed crates from the wilderness and outlaw camps to help keep supplies moving. Highway crime has risen of late. Organized bandits and rogue thieves prey on trade routes, ambushing wagons, pack trains, and lone couriers. Their cargo is scattered across wilderness roads or carried off to outlaw camps. These raids threaten the supply lines between settlements. Traders and cargo handlers rely on independent adventurers to recover lost freight and keep supplies moving. Sealed crates rescued from bandits or found abandoned in the brush can be brought to trade handlers. There, the goods help secure supplies, curb illicit trade, and restore safety to regional commerce.

quest:91904.text: A Sealed Crate. A Sealed Crate is a turn-in task involving recovered trade goods that have fallen into the hands of highwaymen or were lost along commercial routes. Adventurers return intercepted cargo to trade handlers to secure regional supply lines and receive payment. Wagon trails and shipping lanes have become treacherous due to a sharp rise in ambushes by bandits and thieves targeting trade caravans. Unsuspecting haulers and couriers frequently lose their shipments when caught unawares, leaving heavy sealed crates abandoned along wild roads and wilderness paths until someone recovers them. Merchants and supply coordinators maintain standing bounties for the safe return of missing merchandise. Adventurers who retrieve displaced crates and haul them back to regional collection points help restore compromised distribution lines, earning direct monetary compensation for safeguarding commerce.

quest:91905.text: A Sealed Crate. Trade recipients seek A Sealed Crate after bandits disrupt the roads. Recovered cargo helps keep local stores supplied and out of outlaw hands. Bandits and thieves have struck established trade routes, leaving merchant cargo scattered. Their ambushes put caravans and supply lines at risk. Across contested lands, lost shipments are a common sight. Recovering the crates helps local trade endure the lawlessness. Merchants and handlers rely on couriers to bring lost goods back to storage depots. Each returned crate adds to local stores and denies outlaws the gains of highway robbery. In return, salvage workers receive fair pay for facing dangerous roads.

quest:91920.text: Wild Eyes. In Silverpine Forest, Wild Eyes brings an ailing Forsaken scout to a desperate choice. Apothecary Renferrel's heart-based draughts have failed, and the scout seeks another way to stave off a second death. In Silverpine Forest, a Forsaken Deathstalker feels their body failing and faces a second death. Apothecary Renferrel's draughts have brought no relief. So the scout risks Renferrel's wrath and seeks another cure along the creature-ridden shores of Lake Lordamere.

quest:91921.text: Return to Quinn (Again). At the Ivar Patch, Quinn Yorick needs a remedy before his affliction claims his mind and body. A courier brings him a mixture brewed from six hearts, restoring his strength for the travels ahead. North of the Sepulcher, Quinn Yorick rests at the Ivar Patch in Silverpine Forest. His affliction threatens both mind and body, so a special alchemical mixture brewed from six hearts is sent to his camp. For the Forsaken and their allies, bringing remedies to wandering kin can hold back rot and madness.

quest:92110.text: My First Real Potion. A child asks you to bring murloc eyes for My First Real Potion. She is eager to mix it herself. The child is glad to see the murloc eyes. While you were away, she gathered more herbs and found empty vials downstairs. Now she asks you to mix the ingredients as she watches. The potion turns sickly orange when the eyes go in.

quest:92401.text:
A Frightened Request. Edward Heartweaver’s wife waits in fear after he vanishes in the Ruins of Lordaeron. Since their son was lost when the capital fell, Edward has gone each week to search the graveyard for his remains. Now his usual journey has lasted several days. When the Scourge destroyed Lordaeron during the Third War, the Heartweavers lost their young son. His body was never found in the ruin. So Edward Heartweaver went each week to the capital’s graveyard, still hoping to find some trace of his child.

Grief and guilt kept Edward from letting go. The graveyard lay within the ruined capital, where the search was perilous. The surface ruins of Lordaeron are overrun by hostile creatures and lurking horrors. They are no place for ordinary citizens. Edward’s frightened wife warned him and begged him to stop going, but he kept to his weekly search.

Then Edward failed to return for several days. His wife turned to capable adventurers and asked them to brave the ruins and learn what had become of him.

quest:92415.text: Remember That I Love You. "Remember That I Love You" begins with a torn, stained parchment discovered among the undead-stalked graves in the Ruins of Lordaeron. The letter tells the tragic tale of a lost child belonging to the Heartweaver family. Seeking answers requires carrying this fragile relic south to the orphanage in Stormwind City. Amid the blighted earth and shambling undead haunting the ruins of Capital City, survivors and scavengers occasionally stumble across reminders of the Third War's devastation. This torn, blood-stained bundle of parchment has barely survived the undead-trodden grounds of the graveyard. Mentioning a missing child of the Heartweaver lineage, it is a testament to lives shattered when Prince Arthas and the Scourge tore through the kingdom. With Lordaeron fallen and the Undercity claiming the catacombs below, the few refugees who escaped south scattered across the kingdoms of the Alliance. In Stormwind City, Orphan Matron Nightingale tends to the children who lost their parents to the wars. Delivering the blood-stained letter to her care represents one of the few hopes that a surviving child of the Heartweaver family might be identified and brought closure.

quest:92421.text: Light's Justice. In the Undercity, Morbin Lightbane sends warriors above to gather what the Forsaken need. Intact limbs from the Scourge in the Ruins of Lordaeron help repair wounded Forsaken and sustain their ranks. Above the Undercity, Scourge remnants still prowl the ruined streets of Lordaeron's former capital. Though the Dark Lady has defeated the dreadlords and founded the Forsaken kingdom, clearing the surface remains costly work. The undead threaten the gateway below and drain the forces sent to reclaim the fallen kingdom. Forsaken bodies do not mend on their own. Rotting tissue and shattered sinew cannot knit again, so Morbin Lightbane sends warriors to gather intact limbs from destroyed Scourge in the ruins above. Those parts can repair wounded Forsaken and help them endure and fight again. Morbin Lightbane honors his late commander, Captain Garek Bandarion, by carrying on this work. Bandarion pledged to heal their people and free Lordaeron from Scourge occupation. To Morbin, destroying their mindless enemies and restoring their kin is justice in the service of the Banshee Queen.

quest:92422.text: The Wrath of Rath'mael. In the Ruins of Lordaeron, a fog hides Scourge movements above the Undercity. Rath'mael, a Scourge necromancer, has shrouded the ruined streets and graveyard. Deathguard Kristof in Brill calls for you to strike him down. Scout reports from Lordamere Overlook tell of a sinister presence in the Ruins of Lordaeron. An unholy fog now covers the ruined streets and nearby graveyard, hiding lingering Scourge forces. Rath'mael cast the shroud. His spells conceal the undead above the heart of Forsaken territory. Deathguard Kristof in Brill sends you to rally your allies and strike Rath'mael down. The Forsaken cannot let this menace take root unchecked. The Scourge may replace him, but his fall will disrupt their coordination, disperse the fog, and give Tirisfal Glades room to breathe.

quest:92456.text: A Green Sample. A Green Sample is an errand offered by Shylamiir in Stormwind City, directing adventurers to infiltrate the secluded magical city of Dalaran. Expecting a pristine specimen of mana-infused vegetation from the central garden, the expedition uncovers unexpected demonic taint among the Kirin Tor's flora. In Stormwind City, the enigmatic Shylamiir seeks an adventurous traveler willing to run a discreet errand into restricted lands. Intrigued by the Kirin Tor's unusual pursuit of botany, Shylamiir desires a living specimen of the mana-infused vegetation cultivated within Dalaran's central garden. Because the secretive sorcerers keep their borders closed to outsiders, obtaining such flora requires someone adept at slipping into places uninvited.

quest:92457.text: Starving Arcane. Archmage Modera asks you to clear rogue elementals from the City of Dalaran. A breach has unsettled the city's enchantments and defenses, and the Kirin Tor needs room to tend its wards. The breach has disturbed factotums and enchantments across Dalaran. Some of those enchantments protect the city's defenses. Fragmented arcane energy has drawn Seeking Remnants, Saturated Remnants, and Mana Echoes. They gather to fill themselves with its free-flowing magic. Archmage Modera asks you to thin their numbers while the Kirin Tor tends the wards and other incidents.

quest:92458.text: Heart of Disruption. The Image of Archmage Modera needs help containing an arcane disruption in Dalaran. The Violet Citadel’s wards are under strain, and the Kirin Tor need time to bring the crisis under control. At the top of the Violet Citadel, a thunderous crash sounded from the parlors. The disturbance began there, and rampant arcane power now threatens the wards. The Kirin Tor are occupied inside, so you receive a key and are asked to find a less public way into the city before the disruption worsens. Modera asks you to collect an Arcane Mote. She does not ask what you saw in the citadel. Her concern is containing the mote and ending the disruption. The Kirin Tor must now take up that work while the wards hold.

quest:92466.text: Call of Earth. The Call of Earth is an elemental trial undertaken by spiritual initiates to prove their steadfastness. By retrieving requested materials, the petitioner demonstrates their grit and determination to their instructor. Successfully enduring the task confirms their readiness to proceed to the next stage of their training. The Call of Earth is a foundational trial for aspiring practitioners of the elements. Initiates are tasked with fulfilling specific demands to test their patience, resilience, and connection to the stubborn, enduring nature of the earth. Fulfilling the request demonstrates that an adventurer possesses the inner fortitude required to commune with primeval forces. Upon returning with the requested offerings, the mentor recognizes the petitioner's unquestionable grit and determination. Having proven steadfast in the face of elemental demands, the initiate earns recognition and is deemed prepared to undertake the next step of their spiritual journey.

quest:92467.text: Call of Earth. Call of Earth is a sacred trial in which an elemental initiate drinks an Earth Sapta at the Rise of Spirits to pierce the veil between worlds. Guided by an elemental spirit, the seeker learns the endurance and steadfast resolve of the earth as the foundation for rekindling their lost bond with the winds. To perceive the unseen elemental world, shamans utilize saptas—potent magical brews specifically formulated to align a mortal spirit with a particular elemental realm. When consumed by those possessing sufficient resolve, a sapta opens one's spiritual vision to elemental manifestations that are otherwise hidden from mortal sight. Because of their profound nature, these potions are closely guarded secrets known only to select practitioners. Ritual tradition strictly demands that saptas be consumed solely within sacred sites. For communion with the earth, initiates are directed northeast through a pass to the Rise of Spirits. Drinking the draught upon these consecrated grounds allows the seeker to pierce the veil and behold what the spirits wish to reveal.

quest:92468.text: Call of Earth. Call of Earth is a sacred trial of communion where an initiate obtains a piece of Rough Quartz from an earth spirit. Brought to Windshaper Boros in Thendal Grove, this mineral shard becomes the core of the practitioner's first Earth Totem, grounding their bond with the elemental forces. The quest begins when an earth spirit grants an initiate a shard of Rough Quartz as living proof of their communion. The spirit instructs the bearer to take this token to Windshaper Boros in Thendal Grove, explaining that even the smallest fragment carries enduring strength. The spirits demand patience, resilience, and wisdom before granting their favor and respect. Windshaper Boros uses the Rough Quartz as the core to fashion an Earth Totem. He reminds the initiate that the elemental path is multifaceted: although their ultimate desire may be to hear and sing the songs of the wind, true mastery requires understanding all four elemental forces, starting with the unyielding ground beneath their feet.

quest:92479.text: A Scribbled Letter. A Scribbled Letter is a summons delivered to adventurers at Northshire Abbey following their early clashes with nearby kobolds. Sent under the seal of Tordrin Stemblade, it directs promising recruits to seek out his training and guidance. The letter marks a crucial step in preparing defenders to face the escalating perils threatening the kingdom of Stormwind. Upon returning from skirmishes with the kobold camps infesting the valley, adventurers at Northshire Abbey receive a hasty missive. Marked with the seal of Tordrin Stemblade, the note requests their prompt attention before attending to other business. The letter serves as an urgent summons to connect budding champions with formal mentorship within the abbey's protective grounds. When presented with the letter, Tordrin Stemblade remarks on how times have changed, observing how unfamiliar folk have taken up weapons in defense of the realm. Acknowledging that the surrounding wilderness grows more hazardous by the day, he invites travelers to seek out his counsel day or night as they master their skills and assist the beleaguered people of Stormwind.

quest:92489.text: Power Overwhelming. Power Overwhelming is a quest issued by High Sorcerer Andromath in Stormwind City to assist the secluded Kirin Tor. Players are dispatched to the ruined city of Dalaran to quell a dangerous outbreak of wayward arcane energy manifested as a Mana Elemental. Following the devastating destruction of Dalaran at the hands of the arch-demon Archimonde during the Third War, the Kirin Tor retreated inward. Once welcoming scholars and sorcerers from across the world, the surviving magi have grown secretive, reclusive, and deeply distrustful of outsiders as they work tirelessly behind closed borders to rebuild their ruined city. Recent reconstruction efforts to restore Dalaran to its former glory have met severe complications. Dangerous leaks of volatile arcane energies have surged out of control, coalescing into beings of pure mana. Fearing that Dalaran might fall to internal turmoil or abandon its historic ties to the Alliance, High Sorcerer Andromath dispatched champions from Stormwind to quell the Mana Elemental and remind the Kirin Tor of their enduring allies.

quest:92514.text: Welcome to Shen'dar Village. Welcome to Shen'dar Village introduces travelers to the key figures and local dynamics of Shen'dar Village. Upon arrival, newcomers are directed to consult the local Windshaper elder and the village innkeeper before assisting with pressing threats like regional bandits. Arriving in Shen'dar Village, travelers are encouraged to familiarize themselves with the settlement's key residents before taking on local tasks. Newcomers exhibiting spirit-touched qualities are directed to meet with Elder Illaya Amberwind near the village square, as well as Coriella Calmbreeze at the village inn for lodging and supplies. This greeting ensures visitors understand the settlement's delicate social dynamics before taking up arms. Beneath the quiet exterior of Shen'dar Village lies political friction between the spirit-attuned Windshapers and the High Order. Although ideological disputes between the two factions run hot across the region, residents in Shen'dar keep their disagreements civil. Both groups recognize that petty squabbles must take a backseat to pressing survival matters, not least of which is an encroaching bandit menace threatening the area.

quest:92515.text: The Problem With Prideclaws. The Problem With Prideclaws addresses the encroaching threat of wild prideclaw predators in the Shen'dar Highlands. As local settlements already grapple with bandits and cultists, culling the encroaching beasts protects vulnerable villagers while yielding useful pelts for the community. The hills surrounding the Shen'dar Highlands are fraught with peril, pressed not only by roving bandits and unhinged cultists but also by an encroaching population of prideclaws. These fierce beasts have begun pressing inward toward the village perimeter, growing bolder as their territory expands and creating an imminent hazard for the local inhabitants. To avert disaster before pets or children are snatched by the wandering predators, villagers have organized a culling effort. Taking down the prideclaws serves a dual purpose: it drives the predators back from the settlement borders while providing sturdy pelts that craftsmen can fashion into essential goods for the village.

quest:92516.text: Hippogryph Harassment. Hippogryph Harassment is a local task concerning an aggressive flock of wild hippogryphs nesting southeast of Shen'dar Village. Travelers passing along the nearby road have come under frequent attack from the territorial beasts inhabiting the Shen'dar Highlands. To secure the passage, adventurers are called upon to cull the flock's youths, protectors, and their commanding matriarch. Travelers navigating the roads near Shen'dar Village face a rising danger from the skies. A wild flock of hippogryphs has recently claimed the rugged territory southeast of the settlement, carving out active nesting grounds in the Shen'dar Highlands. While hippogryphs are known across Kalimdor as noble beasts occasionally bonded to elven riders, untamed flocks guard their territory with fierce ferocity. Any wagon or lone traveler traversing the paths below has become a target for aerial ambushes, disrupting vital passage and leaving the village vulnerable to isolation if the creatures are left unchecked. To eliminate the immediate threat, the nesting grounds in the Shen'dar Highlands must be directly confronted. Restoring peace to the high roads requires curbing the flock's rapid expansion by taking down their younger members before they reach maturity, as well as breaking through the vigilant hippogryph protectors guarding the perimeter. The true disruption, however, stems from the flock's matriarch, whose leadership directs the attacks on passersby. Only by striking at the nest and felling the matriarch can the roads be made safe once more for travelers.

quest:92517.text: The Criminal Element. The Criminal Element involves striking against the Highlands Bandits and their leader, "Badwind" Bennic, who operate out of a concealed cave behind a waterfall in the Shen'dar Highlands. With local forces overwhelmed by the recent arrival of a menacing cult, outside help is required to eliminate Bennic and disrupt the outlaw gang. In the Shen'dar Highlands, a den of outlaws known as the Highlands Bandits has entrenched itself inside a hidden cave concealed behind a northern waterfall. Led by the notorious "Badwind" Bennic, the cutthroats were already a persistent nuisance to locals before an enigmatic cult arrived in the highlands, after which their lawlessness escalated into an outright terror. With local defenders stretched thin and unable to spare forces, adventurers are tasked with infiltrating the waterfall redoubt, breaking the gang's ranks, and eliminating Bennic.

quest:92519.text: Ward Restocking. Ward Restocking is a task in the Arathi Highlands where travelers assist Doctor Gregory Victor in Hammerfall. With the outpost's infirmary running short on vital elixirs, couriers are dispatched to retrieve neglected supplies from Apothecary Jorell's lab at Go'Shek Farm. At the Horde settlement of Hammerfall in the Arathi Highlands, Doctor Gregory Victor tends to the wounded and ailing in the outpost's medical ward. Keeping the infirmary functional demands a regular supply of remedies, antidotes, and elixirs, which are usually provided by the Forsaken apothecary stationed nearby. When these deliveries stall, Victor must enlist capable travelers to step in and keep the clinic stocked. Apothecary Jorell conducts his alchemical experiments out of a cramped, poorly-ventilated shack at Go'Shek Farm, south and west of Hammerfall. According to Doctor Victor, Jorell's absence is nothing out of the ordinary; the eccentric Forsaken chemist is notorious for either ignoring his official duties or accidentally succumbing to his own noxious concoctions. Couriers sent to retrieve the packaged tonics are expected to find the medicine waiting, regardless of whether Jorell is present.

quest:92528.text: Among the Faithful. Among the Faithful follows an undercover investigation into the Faithful of Al'Akir stationed at Falaath Village in the Shen'dar Highlands. By blending in as a prospective recruit, an adventurer learns that the cult's supreme leadership is secretly gathering to launch an imminent offensive against local settlements and outposts. Posing as an eager recruit among the Faithful of Al'Akir, an infiltrator enters Falaath Village in the Shen'dar Highlands. The cultists openly celebrate their growing ranks, boasting that their collective devotion lends shape and fury to the storm itself. New arrivals are typically sent directly to Skypriest Aanders for scrutiny, but an unexpected meeting at the local inn disrupts normal protocol.

quest:92529.text: Falaath Village. Falaath Village is a gathering place for penitent shen'dorei seeking to win back the favor of the Windlord, Al'Akir. Marked recruits journey from Shen'dar Village to report to Missionary Jasaan and join their fellow faithful. In Shen'dar Village, Sania Silverstream laments that her people grew prideful, taking the bounty of the air for granted until the spirits of the wind abandoned them into stagnation. To remedy this fall from grace, penitent recruits are marked and sent to Falaath Village, seeking fellowship with fellow shen'dorei who believe that only acts of contrition can restore the wind's favor. Upon reaching the outskirts of Falaath Village bearing the Mark of Akir, initiates are greeted by Missionary Jasaan. Viewing the arrival of fresh acolytes as a sign of blessing from the four winds, Jasaan welcomes all who arrive seeking to bask in the elemental grace of Al'Akir.

quest:92550.text: Havoc in the Highlands. Havoc in the Highlands is a preemptive strike undertaken on behalf of Shen'dar Village to disrupt an impending assault by Al'Aketh zealots. By striking their vanguard at the ruins of Falaath Village and eliminating Commander Cyclas, defenders turn the tables on the cultists before they can overrun the highlands. Facing an imminent invasion from zealous cultists, the leadership of Shen'dar Village decides that a swift preemptive offensive offers the best chance of survival. Rather than awaiting an attack behind fragile defenses, an adventurer is dispatched into the ruins of Falaath Village to catch the hostile Al'Aketh forces off guard before their assault can launch. The staging grounds at Falaath Village crawl with dangerous zealots wielding chaotic elemental power. Striking at the gathering forces requires dispatching Al'Aketh Stormcallers, shattering conjured Living Lightning, and tracking down Commander Cyclas himself to behead the expedition's leadership.

quest:92551.text: Stolen Supplies. Stolen Supplies tasks adventurers with recovering plundered highland goods from the Al'Aketh in Falaath Village. Caravan ambushes have cut off vital shipments of food and windstones between the lowlands and the Shen'dar Highlands, leaving local skyborne communities on the brink of starvation. For months, caravans traveling between the lowlands and the Shen'dar Highlands have faced persistent attacks along their trade routes. These shipments transport vital necessities, including food and windstones, to sustain the highland settlements. Without steady deliveries, local townsfolk have been pushed to the brink of starvation, struggling to squeak by as supplies dwindle across the region. While the Al'Aketh publicly point fingers at common bandits for the caravan ambushes, the missing cargo tells a different story. The stolen packs of Shen'dar supplies consistently make their way into Falaath Village, where the Al'Aketh hoard the caches. Recovering these goods allows local authorities and the constable to redistribute much-needed sustenance directly to the most vulnerable skyborne.

quest:92553.text: Restocking the Larders. Restocking the Larders is a provisioning quest in the Shen'dar Highlands of Zephras. With escalating wilderness threats keeping villagers from foraging, an adventurer is enlisted to gather eggs and strider meat to sustain the settlement. As unrest and rising dangers spread across the Shen'dar Highlands, normal daily life on Zephras has grown increasingly fraught. Everyday villagers can no longer safely venture into the wilderness to forage or hunt, leaving communal food stores severely diminished. To keep the settlement fed, local cooks must turn to traveling adventurers with the strength and skill to brave the wild trails. The task calls for tracking down native wildlife across the highlands to secure strider meat and fresh small eggs. For those who supply the provisions, the cook is eager to share culinary knowledge, teaching recipes and culinary techniques refined around local game, including eggs fried in rich ursera tallow alongside a quiet pipe of dried peacebloom.

quest:92579.text: To Valanaar. "To Valanaar" is an island quest in which adventurers carry an urgent military report from Aonda in Shen'dar to Peacekeeper leader Valennia Stormfist. The message alerts the settlement at the southeastern edge of the island that an aggressive cult is expanding rapidly and that direct conflict can no longer be avoided. Following the defense of Shen'dar and its pylon, the highlander Aonda dispatches a trusted traveler to carry urgent word across the island to Valanaar. Situated at the southeastern edge of the land, Valanaar houses the headquarters of the island's peacekeepers under the command of Valennia Stormfist. The mission carries a vital warning: the peaceful days on the island are ending, and Valennia must prepare her people for an inevitable clash with an aggressive, expanding cult.

quest:92595.text: The Windshapers. "The Windshapers" is a quest in which Illaya Amberwind introduces the player to the Windshapers and their spiritual mission. Tasked with reconnecting with the wind spirits, the order strives to protect Zephras and ensure the survival of the Shen'dorei amidst threats within Skywall. The Windshapers are an order dedicated to communing with the wind spirits and protecting the Shen'dorei. Welcoming those with innate spiritual perception, they seek to bridge the growing rift between their people and the elemental forces that sustain their aerial realm. Illaya Amberwind guides new recruits into understanding the heavy burdens the order carries. Survival in Skywall is far from assured. The Windshapers must navigate treacherous internal turmoil caused by the Al'Aketh while enduring the wider perils of the elemental plane. Re-establishing dialogue with the spirits of the winds is deemed vital if Zephras is to endure and the Shen'dorei are to weather the storm.

quest:92596.text: The High Order. On Zephras, Rathiril Sunlance tells newcomers why the shen'dorei must now stand alone. Their elemental benefactors are gone, so these Highborne descendants of Eldre'Thalas turn to ancient arcane magic to protect their people. The shen'dorei on Zephras are working to reclaim their strength and choose their own path. For a long time, elemental benefactors protected them. Now those patrons are gone, leaving the people exposed to strife within and dangers around them. Rathiril Sunlance seeks those gifted in arcane magic to help preserve their people and build their strength on their own. The shen'dorei carry the legacy of Eldre'Thalas and an innate wellspring of arcane energy. Even those never formally trained in wizardry share that power. The High Order sees it as the destiny of Highborne descendants to wield these ancient gifts. With them, the shen'dorei hope to resist the Al'Aketh within and face the many threats to their home on Zephras.

quest:92640.text: Desperate Times. Valennia Stormfist waits in Valanaar with a plan to strike the cult at its shrine. Lorthuna must be stopped there, but the Windshapers and the High Order must first set aside their deep tensions. The cult cannot be safely faced in the open, so the defenders need a bolder plan. They will strike at the cult's shrine instead of fighting a long battle on unfavorable ground. If they eliminate Lorthuna before she completes her part in the cult's grand scheme, they can cripple the threat at its source. In Valanaar, Valennia Stormfist has spent time planning an assault on the shrine. The attack needs substantial reinforcements and strength united across the factions. Yet the Windshapers and the High Order remain divided by severe political tensions, putting their alliance at risk.

quest:92642.text: Disrupting Logistics. At the Gustberry Lowlands, Al'Aketh cultists are pressing a full-scale assault. Their healers keep the brawlers fighting, and the defenders need help before their lines give way. A fierce assault is bearing down on the defenders above the Gustberry Lowlands. Enemy forces are gathering, and the local lines are near breaking. The commanders expected substantial reinforcements from Valennia, but they must rely on whatever capable hands arrive. Strikes against the enemy's support may be the only way to hold the defense together. Al'Aketh brawlers press forward in ranks, sustained by healers who mend their wounds. In the Gustberry Lowlands, taking out those healers can break the cultists' push. That gives the defenders a chance to rally and drive back the invasion.

quest:92643.text: The Turncoat. A cultist of the Al'Aketh offers to defect and reveal what the cult intends for the island. You are sent to bring him from a secluded highland retreat northwest of Valanaar, where the meeting may be a trap. A cultist within the Al'Aketh ranks claims to know the cult's true intentions for the island. He offers to defect, but demands firm assurances of protection. The cult guards its plans closely, so reaching out may be worth the danger. The defector waits alone in a secluded residence in the highlands northwest of Valanaar. You must reach him with care. The meeting may be an Al'Aketh ambush meant to draw out those who pry into the cult's affairs.

quest:92644.text: Unfortunate News. You find the turncoat dead before they can speak. A damaged blue crystal remains beneath the body, and you carry it to High Elder Talanaanis Shadowsong in Valanaar. You reach the rendezvous and find the defecting cultist already slain. Their body is still warm. Beneath it lies a small, glowing blue crystal, damaged but still humming. You carry it to High Elder Talanaanis Shadowsong in Valanaar.

quest:92645.text:
Breaking the Breaker. In the Gustberry Lowlands, cultists press the defenders hard. Commander Belguilos leads the assault from her hillside villa, and striking her there may be the defenders’ only chance to survive. Cultists assault the Gustberry Lowlands, driving the local defenders to the brink. Repelling them seems nearly impossible while Commander Belguilos directs the attack. All fear her as “the Breaker.”

Her villa is the operation’s base. Slaying her there is perilous, near-suicidal, yet passivity leaves the defenders doomed. Before she commanded the cultists, Belguilos kept order as a peacekeeper. Even then, those around her found something deeply unsettling in her manner. When the cult’s influence spread beyond control, she embraced its extremism. Now she commands the cultists and is a terror.

quest:92646.text: Confront Lorthuna. Elaadrin Evengale and Ayessa Dawnsinger pursue High Priestess Lorthuna through a portal into the Rohashi Spires above Zephras. They call for your aid before she can escape justice or strengthen her power. High Priestess Lorthuna flees through a mystic gateway into the Rohashi Spires above Zephras. An injured ally remains behind at the portal's threshold. Elaadrin Evengale and Ayessa Dawnsinger follow her into the heights and call for your help before she escapes justice or strengthens her power.

quest:92679.text: Blood Tithe. Blood Tithe is a quest initiated by Alvarion Windfield, an ailing Skyborne farmer seeking aid in the settlement of Valanaar. Desperate to protect his livelihood, he recruits adventurers to travel west to his lowland orchard and assist his wife, Aamelia. In the settlement of Valanaar, an injured Skyborne man named Alvarion Windfield desperately searches for capable adventurers. Wracked with visible pain, Alvarion has traveled from his homestead into town to hire fighters who can help save his livelihood. Rather than tasking travelers on the spot, he implores those willing to help to journey westward into the lowlands, where his wife Aamelia maintains their family orchard. The Windfield Orchard lies situated in the lowlands to the west of Valanaar. With Alvarion incapacitated by intense suffering, the burden of holding the farm falls upon Aamelia Windfield. Adventurers taking up Alvarion's offer must make their way into the western valley to discover what threatens the orchard and lend their strength to the embattled family.

quest:92682.text: Make Yourself Useful. Make Yourself Useful is an assignment at Windfield Orchard where adventurers help secure the stormapple crop against undisciplined bandits. An extortionist named Ferauu is due to collect his regular share of the harvest, but hungry outlaws have broken ranks to pilfer the trees ahead of time. Dealing with these rogue thieves earns the respect of the watchful orchard keeper. At Windfield Orchard, farming is complicated by extortion. A bandit leader named Ferauu and his crew have established an arrangement to collect their regular cut of the fruit harvest. However, lack of discipline within the bandit ranks means that petty outlaws cannot always wait for their boss's scheduled visit, sneaking in early to pick over the trees. Rather than enduring undisciplined thieves among the stormapple trees, the orchard caretaker puts ambitious newcomers to work before Ferauu's scheduled arrival. Adventurers are tasked with securing the ripe stormapple yield and dispatching the hungry bandits trespassing among the trees. The keeper notes that Ferauu would likely execute these rogues himself for going behind his back and tampering with the cut.

quest:92684.text: Ornery Ornery Galestriders. Ornery Ornery Galestriders concerns an orchard farmer in the Gustberry Lowlands struggling with a meager seasonal harvest. The local lowlands galestriders—larger and more vicious than their highland kin—have been raiding the orchard for stormapples and threatening the farm's livelihood. Culling the aggressive birds secures the remaining fruit while providing much-needed fresh tenderloins for dinner. In the Gustberry Lowlands, local farmers face tough times following an already meager seasonal harvest. To make matters worse, wild galestriders have invaded the orchards, stripping branches of ripe stormapples and jeopardizing what little fruit remains. Keeping the farm viable means driving off or thinning out the boldest birds before the entire crop is lost. Unlike their smaller and comparatively calmer cousins in the highlands, the galestriders of the lowlands are towering, bad-tempered beasts. Travelers in the lowlands must approach them with extreme care, as a single well-aimed kick from their powerful legs is enough to incapacitate or kill an inattentive fighter. Taking them down yields massive tenderloins that supply hungry locals with rare, substantial meals.

quest:92685.text: The Hills Have Eyes. "The Hills Have Eyes" is a quest in the Gustberry Lowlands where the beleaguered farmer Aamelia takes a stand against highwayman bandits. Adventurers launch a preemptive strike on an encampment in the northern hills to diminish the bandit forces before their leader, Ferauu, launches a raid. In the Gustberry Lowlands, a farmer named Aamelia faces an impending assault from a ring of outlaws led by Ferauu. Rather than waiting passively for doom to arrive at her doorstep, she urges travelers to launch a preemptive strike against a bandit encampment in the hills to the north. By taking out the highwaymen before they muster their attack, she aims to thin their ranks and buy precious time.

quest:92693.text: Standing Our Ground. Standing Our Ground is a decisive quest where an adventurer stands alongside Aamelia Windfield in a desperate confrontation against a menacing bandit leader. Having prepared the defenders for battle, you face what seemed like a lost cause to secure safety from the brigands. Standing Our Ground marks the climax of a desperate struggle against a gang of bandits. Having helped prepare the local defenders for an inevitable clash, you are given one final opportunity to walk away and return safely to Valanaar rather than throw yourself into what appears to be a doomed last stand.

quest:92698.text: What Is My Purpose?. "What Is My Purpose?" is a quest centered on a giant Malfunctioning Cyclone Construct wandering aimlessly through agricultural fields. Repeating broken fragments of speech beneath its armor plating, the ancient machine has forgotten its original duties after decades of neglect following the departure of the wind elementals. Investigating the construct leads adventurers to consult local orchardist Aamelia Windfield to learn about its mysterious past and former caretakers. Deep within the fields stands a towering Cyclone Construct, aimlessly pacing across the land while trapped in a broken operational loop. Those who approach the armored giant can hear muffled, fragmented speech vibrating from beneath its heavy plates, endlessly repeating errors and questioning its own fundamental function. Decades of isolation have left the machine hollow of purpose, its internal directives corrupted or forgotten. While towering and formidable in appearance, the automaton poses no active threat to passersby, existing instead as a melancholic relic of an older era whose voice has been reduced to static queries echoing over the soil. When questioned about the machine, the local resident Aamelia Windfield reveals that the automaton has wandered the surrounding fields for decades, seemingly ever since the wind elementals departed. A local named Alvarion speculated that the machine once hauled bountiful harvests to distant markets or tended livestock centuries ago, long before the land was transformed into an orchard. In bygone ages, a group known as the Windshapers built and maintained these cyclone constructs. Although the orchard workers have occasionally discussed petitioning the Windshapers to repair the machine, the matter has never been urgent, leaving the construct to roam unbothered and largely ignored.

quest:92699.text: The Supreme Magister. In Valanaar, Elaadrin Evengale draws new arrivals toward the High Order. From a lodge in the settlement’s southeast, the order seeks allies as it faces hostile Windshapers and a nearby cult. New arrivals of promise in Valanaar are directed to the High Order. Supreme Magister Elaadrin Evengale leads it from a lodge in the settlement’s far southeast. He watches newcomers closely, seeking the strength, resolve, and arcane aura to face the dangers threatening their home. Peace in Valanaar is fragile. The High Order and the Windshapers are bitter enemies, so newcomers are warned to keep their distance from the Windshapers lest violence break out in the streets. A dangerous cult lurks nearby. With threats outside the town, its leaders cannot afford bloodshed within.

quest:92700.text: The Grand Skyseer. The Grand Skyseer is an introductory journey into the heart of Valanaar, directing travelers to seek an audience with Ayessa Dawnsinger at the Windshaper lodge. As tensions simmer between local factions and a shadowy cult threatens the region, the Windshapers urgently seek individuals gifted with spiritual sight. Upon arriving in the town of Valanaar, travelers are directed toward the central lodge where the Windshapers convene under the leadership of Grand Skyseer Ayessa Dawnsinger. Having caught the attention of Elder Amberwind through notable deeds in Shen'dar Village, new arrivals are welcomed into the fold of those attuned to the spirits. Yet Valanaar remains fraught with external and internal dangers, requiring newcomers to navigate fragile local politics carefully. Peace in Valanaar is fragile. The Windshapers maintain an open hostility with the High Order, and street skirmishes between the factions threaten to destabilize the settlement. With a shadowy cult actively menacing the region, local leaders have mandated that both factions keep their distance, prioritizing survival against common adversaries over bitter territorial feuds. Grand Skyseer Ayessa Dawnsinger observes that the spiritual perception known as skysight is becoming increasingly rare among the people of Zephras. Those who arrive displaying a strong aura and spiritual harmony are treated as essential allies, urgently needed to help the Windshapers steer through the trying times confronting their land.

quest:92701.text: To Valanaar. At Valanaar, Valennia Stormfist must face the cult's growing threat. Aonda sends urgent news from Shen'dar, where the village and its pylon were defended. After Shen'dar and its pylon were defended, Aonda sends a trusted messenger across the island. The message is bound for Valanaar on the island's southeastern edge. There, the commander of the peacekeepers must hear how quickly the cult is advancing. Valennia Stormfist and her peacekeepers have long tried to avoid open conflict with the cult spreading across the island. Yet the events at Shen'dar mark a change. The cult's influence is growing, and Valennia can no longer hold back from a clash. Her dwindling force must ready Valanaar for an assault.

quest:92703.text: Deliver the News. Deliver the News is a quest concluding the plight of the Windfield family orchard in Skywall. After helping Aamelia secure the farm, the adventurer travels to Valanaar to deliver tidings of their safety to an anxious Alvarion Windfield. Deliver the News marks the resolution of an ordeal at the Windfield family orchard. Having stepped in to save the farm from an impending crisis, the adventurer receives heartfelt thanks from Aamelia, who is ready to put the danger behind them. With the orchard secured, the immediate priority shifts to reassuring Alvarion Windfield, who fled to the settlement of Valanaar to plead for assistance. In Valanaar, Alvarion Windfield is overcome with emotion upon learning that his family and home are safe. Having left for the city believing his search for help was a desperate, almost vain hope, the traveler's success evokes for him the legendary heroes remembered from before his people arrived in Skywall. With their home saved, the Windfield family extends an enduring welcome to their savior.

quest:92706.text: WANTED: Bruuz. Bruuz threatens the harbor traffic that keeps Ratchet busy. Gazlowe has posted a bounty for the huge shark prowling the docks and disrupting coastal trade. Ratchet is the primary neutral gateway between Kalimdor and the Eastern Kingdoms, and its trade depends on merchant ships. Lately, a huge shark called Bruuz has been prowling the bay. Dockworkers gave the shark its name after it began attacking small skiffs, sailors, and cargo being unloaded near the docks. Its presence disrupts the port and puts the ships that keep Ratchet supplied at risk. Gazlowe has posted a public bounty to keep ships from avoiding his port for fear of the shark. The notice calls on anglers and promises a hefty reward. To claim it, you need to slay Bruuz and bring back the shark's dorsal fin as proof.

quest:92708.text: A Grand Adventure. A Grand Adventure marks a turning point for the crisis on Zephras Isle within Skywall. Led by Ayessa Dawnsinger and the Windshapers, it outlines a bold plan to seek salvation for their home by journeying down to the mortal realm of Azeroth. Zephras Isle faces an escalating crisis as wind spirits have vanished without explanation. In response, the Windshapers have been investigating these disturbances, uncovering unexpected revelations about their missing kin and the fate of their elemental home. Ayessa Dawnsinger seeks capable adventurers to heed their findings and prepare for an unprecedented undertaking.

quest:92709.text: A Grand Adventure. In Valanaar, Elaadrin Evengale asks you to hear the High Order’s plans. Their search for ancient magic may shape Zephras Isle’s future. Elaadrin speaks of your Highborne lineage and the young people who may help save their home. The High Order seeks the ancient magic of its forebears, and what has been lost over many millennia.

quest:92727.text: The Missing Scholar. Fillion Flamebreeze is missing after setting out to study atmospheric magic on Zephras. The High Order sent the scholar toward the Shen'dar Highlands, and concern grows as the road from Valanaar yields no word of his return. The High Order gathers and preserves knowledge across Zephras. Yet field research on the island has grown perilous. Fillion Flamebreeze set out for the Shen'dar Highlands to study atmospheric arcane phenomena, but never reported back. His peers now fear the dangers along the frontier roads have claimed him.

quest:92741.text: Unwelcome Visitors. In Shadowgale Forest, shrieklings are pressing toward the woods' edge. Iaadaria Bitterwind in Valanaar asks travelers to gather their talons for the High Order. Shadowgale Forest is a dangerous woodland that ordinary adventurers are forbidden to enter. Now its shrieklings have multiplied in numbers never seen before. They are pressing toward the forest's edge and extending their hunting grounds beyond the canopy. If they keep spreading, settled lands and travel routes will face a growing danger. In Valanaar, Iaadaria Bitterwind of the High Order sees both danger and opportunity in the shrieklings' growing numbers. The Order usually leaves pest control and trapping to others. Yet shriekling talons have rare alchemical properties, making an exception worthwhile. Travelers are asked to enter Shadowgale Forest and bring back eight talons. The High Order can then help protect the region and study the reagents.

quest:92834.text: Avenged Tenfold. Elaadrin turns from diplomacy to retribution after the Al'Aketh cult answers his appeal with violence. The High Order scholar had sent his dear friend Belathaan Brightwish to seek peace at the Shrine of Akir, north of Valanaar. The Al'Aketh cult's violence brought armed posturing from factions like the Peacekeepers and Windshapers. Elaadrin spoke for the High Order and saw such displays as a foolish escalation. His order prizes pragmatism and avoids conflict, so he still believed reasoned dialogue could work. He sent his close friend, Belathaan Brightwish, to the Shrine of Akir to negotiate peace. The High Order puts logic before sentiment and holds that avoiding bloodshed is usually the prudent path. Yet Elaadrin shows how cold logic cuts both ways when foes mistake restraint for helplessness. Crackling arcane energy gathers around him. The High Order favors peace, but those who butcher its emissaries face overwhelming retribution.
