Despite her eye for craft and trade, Kristy Grant is no warrior and possesses no combat experience to face the ferocious predators of the canyon herself. The Pesterhide hyenas are vicious pack scavengers that roam the dusty expanses beneath the towering mesas, making the harvesting of pristine pelts dangerous for any lone traveler. To secure five unblemished hides without risking her own neck, Kristy enlists the aid of seasoned adventurers passing through the needles. The task requires venturing out into the wilderness, overcoming the territorial beasts, and carefully collecting the hides needed for her family's crafting ventures back home.

quest:98189.text: Return the Statuette. A statuette's delivery to Menethil Harbor was interrupted by tragedy. You are asked to bring it to Captain Stoutfist at Menethil Keep. The statuette was meant for Menethil Harbor, where Captain Stoutfist at Menethil Keep was expected to sign for it. Now you are asked to finish the delivery.

quest:98190.text: A Friend of the Family. Menethil Harbor fears its relics will fall to local enemies. The harbor authorities send the Menethil Statuette to Highlord Bolvar Fordragon in Stormwind Keep for safekeeping. Menethil Harbor links the northern Eastern Kingdoms to the south. The port honors the late King Terenas Menethil II of Lordaeron, but treacherous marshes and enemies surround it. With threats mounting, harbor leaders fear the exposed outpost cannot protect relics from the fallen northern kingdom. Dragonmaw orcs still infest the Wetlands. The clan has a dark past and a taste for ruthless advantage. Harbor defenders fear the orcs would pillage the Menethil Statuette for conquest, then defile it or turn it to their own ends. The courier carries the relic straight to Stormwind Keep, bypassing the usual military and bureaucratic channels. There it goes to Highlord Bolvar Fordragon, regent to the young King Anduin Wrynn. The capital's leaders are trusted to safeguard a piece of Lordaeron's heritage.

quest:98191.text: A Friend of the Family. Highlord Bolvar Fordragon sends a rare likeness of King Terenas to the Cathedral of Light. Lord Grayson Shadowbreaker will keep the Menethil Statuette safe. King Terenas Menethil II helped shape the Grand Alliance during the Second War. He lived with deep personal devotion, yet held great standing among humanity's kingdoms. Humble by nature, he disliked monuments made in his honor. Few likenesses were commissioned, and fewer survived Lordaeron's ruin and the Scourge's devastation. Highlord Bolvar Fordragon sees more than fine carving in the surviving Menethil Statuette. The Holy Light has begun to gather within it, lending the figure a quiet spiritual presence. Bolvar decides Stormwind Keep is no place for so sacred a piece. He sends it across the city to the Cathedral of Light, into the care of Lord Grayson Shadowbreaker, who trains paladins.

quest:98197.text: Spoils of War. As the Dragonmaw move, Valstag Ironjaw seeks timber and iron from Menethil Harbor. He needs them to strengthen the town’s defenses. Menethil Harbor once served the Old Horde as a staging ground for an invasion of Hillsbrad. The fleet built there drew on resources stolen from Khaz Modan. Some supplies remain in the harbor, and Valstag asks you to bring him the timber and iron for the town’s defenses.

quest:98208.text: Bloom of the Heavens. Sylessa Duskwhisper searches the waters south of Menethil Harbor for Bloom of the Heavens. The sacred flower Nord'el was lost when the night elf vessel Flying Osprey wrecked alongside ships of the Kul Tiran Third Fleet. Murlocs now occupy the wreck, where Nord'el lies among the ruins. Sylessa Duskwhisper has come from Auberdine to Menethil Harbor to recover Nord'el. The flower was gathered beneath a full moon atop Mount Hyjal, and holds deep meaning for the night elves. Those who now live in Teldrassil treasure relics from their ancestral mountain as reminders of their heritage. Many moons ago, the night elf vessel Flying Osprey wrecked on the rocky coast south of Menethil Harbor while sailing with the Kul Tiran Third Fleet. Its ruined hull rests in the shallows. Fierce murloc raiders have made the wreck their home and defend it from anyone seeking the night elf cargo.

quest:98209.text: Bloom of the Heavens. Across the Great Sea, Nord'el is bound for Auberdine after its recovery in the Wetlands. For night elves still grieving the loss of their immortality, the flower carries the grace of Elune. In the Wetlands, Sylessa recovers Nord'el, the legendary flower, despite an attack by local murlocs. Worn out by her escape, she entrusts the plant to you for its voyage across the Great Sea to Auberdine. From Menethil Harbor, a boat sails directly to Darkshore, linking the Eastern Kingdoms with northern Kalimdor. When Nord'el reaches Auberdine, Elder Thundris Windweaver is astonished. He believed the sacred bloom had vanished forever. Night elves still bear the cost of surrendering their immortality after the Battle of Mount Hyjal, and Nord'el's survival feels like a blessing from Elune. Thundris prepares to send the delicate plant to Darnassus, where it can be cultivated and preserved for future generations.

quest:98245.text: Razormaw Needling. In the Wetlands, Howin Kindfeather seeks Razormaw teeth for dragon whelp armor. He plans to make awls that can stitch the scales together against dragonfire. Howin Kindfeather means to strike back at the foes who have plagued the Wetlands: the Dark Iron dwarves, the Dragonmaw orcs, and the drakes they brought into battle. He is making armor from dragon whelp scales to guard against dragonfire. Their hides are too tough for ordinary tools to sew. Howin needs sharp, sturdy tools to pierce the whelp hide. He looks to the Razormaw raptors that stalk Raptor Ridge in the northeast and Saltspray Glen in the northwest. Their needle-sharp incisors make strong awls. These can pierce dragon scales without shattering under pressure.

quest:98246.text: Trying Times. Before Howin Kindfeather can fly through the Wetlands, Bassbeak needs a meal. He seeks a dozen intact eggs from the fierce Razormaw raptors. Howin Kindfeather tends Bassbeak in the Wetlands. The dwarf will not fly with his gryphon until her hunger is eased. A hungry gryphon can be stubborn and unpredictable. She may lash out, so a proper meal must come before any flight through the marshes. Howin seeks food for Bassbeak among the Razormaw raptors. Their nests lie at Raptor Ridge to the northeast and Saltspray Glen to the northwest. Razormaw eggs have yolks as large as a gnome's head. Howin wants those substantial meals to satisfy Bassbeak before she faces the dangers of the Wetlands.

quest:98248.text: Shipping Label. A torn manifest points couriers toward Durotar Supply and Logistics in the Barrens. The company depends on travelers to recover lost crates and return paperwork to its post west of the Crossroads, keeping supplies and trade moving across central Kalimdor. A torn manifest is fixed to a freshly restocked cargo crate. Its recipient's name has worn away, but the heading names Durotar Supply and Logistics, a freight company in Horde territory. Beside the writing, a rough map points couriers toward the company's staging grounds in the central plains. The notice welcomes travelers bringing stray containers, damaged goods, or proof of salvage to the trade outpost west of the Crossroads. Durotar Supply and Logistics depends on independent haulers to recover scattered freight across the Barrens. Those who help keep regional supplies moving receive compensation.

quest:98283.text: Carnage. In the Wetlands, Rethiel the Greenwarden asks you to draw Carnage from its lair. The Razormaw alpha's plague-driven frenzy has thrown the marshes out of balance. The Razormaw raptors once kept wild growth in check across the Wetlands. Now a bloodthirsty alpha named Carnage rules the pack. It slaughters without restraint and terrorizes its own kind. The marshes are in turmoil. Rethiel the Greenwarden watches over the Green Belt and believes corruption has taken hold of Carnage. Diseased Rotclaw bears came down from Loch Modan. You gather their malignant entrails and place the foul meat in Carnage's cave below Raptor Ridge. The frenzied alpha attacks, and its suffering can end.

quest:98286.text: Camping 101: Enchanting. At Shen'dar Village, skilled enchanters can learn to make an Enchanted Lute for the campfire. Nasalanna Windsinger teaches them how it entertains and bolsters companions. On the open road, sharpened blades and rations are not enough. Travelers need rest and good spirits to endure long expeditions. Enchanters bring magical comforts to camps across Azeroth, helping weary travelers recover their strength and spirits before they return to perilous trails. Aspiring enchanters seeking to learn campsite magic travel to Shen'dar Village. There, Nasalanna Windsinger teaches capable spell-weavers to make an Enchanted Lute. First, they must prove their dedication and skill in enchanting. Then Nasalanna shares how to fashion an instrument whose melodies restore spirits beneath the stars.

quest:98291.text: Death to the Dragonmaw. At Dragonmaw Retreat, Howin Kindfeather asks you to thin the Dragonmaw ranks. He hopes to reach Grim Batol and reclaim it for the Wildhammers, or learn more about it. Dragonmaw orcs have gathered along the retreat, where red dragons routed them before. Howin needs their numbers reduced before he can approach Grim Batol. He points you east along the road to find them.

quest:98293.text: Forced Disarmament. Forced Disarmament is an Alliance quest in the Wetlands tasking adventurers with seizing weapon caches from the Dragonmaw clan at Dragonmaw Retreat. By collecting thirty bundles of armaments, players prevent the hostile orcs from equipping additional soldiers for future raids. The confiscated gear is delivered to Captain Stoutfist at Menethil Keep to safeguard the region's vital harbor. In the marshlands of the Wetlands, the hostile Dragonmaw clan has begun gathering an alarming stockpile of weapons within the Dragonmaw Retreat. Left unchecked, these supplies would allow the renegade orcs to equip fresh waves of warriors and launch devastating raids against neighboring settlements. Disarming their encampments strikes directly at their logistical capability, blunting any planned offensive before their warbands can fully mobilize and take the field. Menethil Harbor serves as the primary gateway connecting Khaz Modan and Stormwind to the sea, making any nearby military build-up a severe peril. Captain Stoutfist coordinates defensive measures from Menethil Keep, keeping vigilant watch over the hostile clans and beasts encroaching upon the town. Recovering thirty sets of Dragonmaw armaments deprives the orcs of essential munitions while providing the dwarven garrison with vital intelligence regarding the enemy's readiness.

quest:98297.text: Stopping the Cycle. At the Dragonmaw Gates, warlocks are trying to enslave a red dragonspawn. Howin Kindfeather returns from a test flight with troubling news, and the Wildhammer will not let it happen again. Howin Kindfeather asks you to face the subdued dragonspawn at the Dragonmaw Gates. First, kill the warlocks holding it down. That should free it. Then put the dragonspawn out of its misery. Howin expects you to bring friends, for the Wildhammer will not let the Dragonmaw stand in their way.

quest:98298.text: Arugal's Folly. At the Sepulcher, Dalar Dawnweaver seeks the truth behind the worgen near the Greymane Wall. He hopes their remains will prove that Archmage Arugal bound the beasts but did not bring their curse into being. At the Sepulcher in Silverpine Forest, Forsaken mage Dalar Dawnweaver means to strip away the mystery around his rival, Archmage Arugal. Enchanted shackles show that Arugal lacked the power to summon or create the worgen packs terrorizing the region. His magic could only hold the beasts for a time. How the affliction began remains unknown. Dalar sends you south to the Greymane Wall for proof. Feral worgen attack and infect nearby human populations in the wilderness around its imposing fortifications. You can bring Dalar physical evidence by killing the beasts and gathering pieces of their bodies. He needs those samples to study the affliction's nature.

quest:98299.text: Stop the Spread. Stop the Spread is a Silverpine Forest quest concerning the containment of the worgen curse linked to Archmage Arugal. While researchers seek a way to halt the affliction, preemptive measures are ordered against living human refugees at the Greymane Wall to prevent them from turning into Arugal's servants. In Silverpine Forest, the scourge of the worgen spreads at the hands of the renegade Archmage Arugal. While the exact methods and mechanics behind the spread of this feral condition remain largely unknown, the danger it presents to the territory is undeniable. Researchers are actively working to understand the nature of the magic, but their immediate focus is preventing Arugal from amassing an unstoppable host of savage followers.

quest:98310.text: Gleaning Our Future. Prospector Whelgar sees a way to learn more from the Goaz Stone. Four larger golems bear names that match its missing pieces. You've found missing pieces of the Goaz Stone. Prospector Whelgar points to four larger golems named Ados, Modr, Golm, and Neru. He asks you to use the stone near each one, then bring their hearts back. He hopes they will reveal more of its markings.

quest:98313.text: For Further Study. Historian Karnik awaits a package in Ironforge, tied to something epic. What has been seen so far makes further study worthwhile. You are carrying the Whelgar Relic Package to Historian Karnik in the Hall of Explorers. He is usually in the library, reading at the back.

quest:98319.text: Secure the Mountain. You face a growing danger in Dun Morogh: wendigos have overrun the Grizzled Den, and Whitebeard's report is missing. Cornelius entered the cavern while his partner waited outside. Wendigos are multiplying across the cold mountain slopes and crowding into the Grizzled Den to the north. Dwarven scouts already contend with Frostmane trolls. Now savage beasts make the crags perilous for patrols and couriers. Cornelius charged into the Grizzled Den to secure Whitebeard's vital report. His partner waits outside, seeking help to find the scout and thin the ferocious wendigos in the cave.

quest:98321.text: Flintfire's Shipment. Tognus Flintfire in Kharanos is facing a severe supply shortage after savage wendigos overran his primary source of ore at the Grizzled Den. With the miners forced to abandon their crates during the evacuation, adventurers are tasked with recovering the lost shipments to keep the local forges running. In the snowy settlement of Kharanos, Tognus Flintfire faces a critical supply crisis at his forge. The region's most productive and dependable source of ore has suddenly fallen silent after savage wendigos invaded the dig site. Caught off guard by the ferocious predators, the local miners were forced to abandon their posts on a moment's notice, fleeing for their lives and leaving behind freshly packed crates of valuable ore scattered across the cavern floor. The overrun mine, known as the Grizzled Den, lies to the west of Kharanos. Although Tognus is thankful that every miner managed to escape the ferocious beasts in one piece, the work stoppage threatens to halt local blacksmithing entirely. Rather than waiting for an armed expedition to clear the cave, Tognus seeks daring adventurers to slip into the wendigo lair, gather the stranded crates, and bring the vital ore back to the forge.

quest:98322.text: Secure the Mountain. Secure the Mountain is an Alliance quest originating in Kharanos, Dun Morogh. A local official compiling intelligence for Ironforge sends adventurers west of town to check on Mountaineer Gretchen after scouts investigating aggressive wendigos fail to report back. Tasked with compiling local military intelligence for the high seat of Ironforge, an official in Kharanos finds his routine correspondence interrupted. A mountaineer team sent to assess nearby wendigo activity has failed to return with updates. Rather than spelunking through icy caverns himself, the bureaucrat enlists capable travelers to venture just west of town and determine the scouts' status.

quest:98323.text: Secure the Mountain. Secure the Mountain is a scouting report delivered on behalf of Mountaineer Gretchen to Senir Whitebeard in Kharanos. After an expedition into a nearby cave proves catastrophic, Gretchen determines the cavern is a lost cause and refuses to send any more scouts into the overrun death trap. The mission highlights the ongoing struggle of Ironforge's mountaineers to keep Dun Morogh safe amidst rising threats. Stationed out in the freezing peaks of Dun Morogh, Mountaineer Gretchen stands watch with orders to ensure the high passes remain safe. However, a recent foray into a nearby cavern reveals that the wilderness is far from pacified. Having assessed the situation, Gretchen concludes that the cave has become a complete death trap, overrun by hostile mongrels. Rather than risk further lives, she remains at her post on the slopes, determined to hold the line while dispatching an emissary to deliver her written assessment. In the bustling settlement of Kharanos, Senir Whitebeard tracks the numerous dangers encroaching on the dwarven heartland. Upon receiving Gretchen's grim assessment, Whitebeard shows little surprise at the news that the cavern is completely overrun. Resigned to the grim reality facing Dun Morogh, he quietly folds Gretchen's letter into his growing stack of field reports. The intelligence serves as another sobering piece of documentation in Ironforge's broader effort to catalog and manage the volatile frontier.

quest:98326.text: Frosthowl. Frosthowl is a quest in Dun Morogh tasking adventurers with recovering a stolen sack of fish from a thieving wendigo. The beast ambushed a local dwarven fisher and fled into the depths of the Grizzled Den. Ice fishing across the freezing waters of Dun Morogh is grueling, bitter labor. A dwarven fisher and her husband, Paxton, spent days out on the frozen lake braving biting winds just to harvest a single sack of fish. Their hard work was abruptly undone when Frosthowl, a menacing and thunderous wendigo, ambushed the camp and made off with their entire haul into the snowy wilderness. Frosthowl is not just an ordinary scavenger; the beast is notorious for its booming roars that rattle the ice and scare off the lake's sparse fish. After snatching the fisher's supply sack, the drooling creature retreated deep into the dark tunnels of the Grizzled Den to the southeast, leaving the stranded fishers desperate for someone to confront the monster and retrieve their stolen goods.

quest:98341.text: The Great Windborne Cat Spirit. In Moonglade, the Avatar of Saeyleenan guides young shen'dorei druids through a spiritual trial. The spirit comes from Zephras and helps them embody the windborne feline form of their homeland. South of Moonglade's twin bridges, a spirit from distant Zephras has appeared in the sacred sanctuary. Calling itself the Avatar of Saeyleenan, this windborne cat spirit has crossed into Azeroth to guide young shen'dorei druids ready to unlock their feline form. Druids seek wisdom in the feline form, but those from Zephras follow a different tradition from Azeroth's native peoples. The shen'dorei embody the windborne predator of their homeland instead of an Azerothian wildcat. So Saeyleenan oversees their trial in Moonglade, to teach them the spirit's nature.

quest:98362.text: To Thunder Bluff. After communion in Moonglade, a young tauren druid makes a triumphant return to Thunder Bluff. Having earned the Great Cat Spirit's favor, the initiate goes to Turak Runetotem on the Elder Rise to master feline shapeshifting. You return to Mulgore after meeting Dendrite Starblaze and the Great Cat Spirit in Moonglade's sacred groves. The communion joins ancient night elven teachings with the tauren's earthen heritage, marking a pivotal milestone in a druid's training. Turak Runetotem awaits you atop the Elder Rise in Thunder Bluff. Dendrite guided your communion with the Great Cat Spirit; Turak now teaches the physical change. With the spirit's blessing acknowledged, the elder trainer shares the knowledge to take the cat's swift, predatory shape.

quest:98372.text: An Unfortunate End. In Duskwood, a Night Watchman lies dead in the gloom. A beast mauled him, and the unlit brand in his hand may help you see what the darkness hides. A Night Watch patrolman lies dead on Duskwood's dark soil. Deep gashes and cuts mark his body. A great beast caught him before he could escape. An unlit torch remains in the fallen guard's rigid hand. Take it, and its light can reveal what hides in Duskwood's gloom and along other dark paths.

quest:98387.text: Blackrock Blockade. Marshal Marris is pressing the Blackrock Blockade east of Lake Everstill. Lakeshire's guard aims to starve out the Blackrock orcs and take their weapons. Blackrock raiders in Redridge are pushing Alliance forces to their limits. Cut off from regular supply trains, their forward parties live off the hills. Marshal Marris knows even fierce orcs cannot keep fighting without food and steel. South of Stonewatch Keep, Blackrock camps lead the clan's advance. Lakeshire's defenders strike those camps to seize supplies and stolen weapons, weakening the orcs' fighting strength and morale.

quest:98391.text: The Sisterhood of Elune. The Sisterhood of Elune is an introductory quest directing adventurers to Darnassus to meet Sister Aquinne. Serving as the primary spiritual authority among the night elves, the Sisterhood requires swift outside aid to confront brewing challenges in their lands. "The Sisterhood of Elune" is a summons directing adventurers to seek out Sister Aquinne in the night elf capital of Darnassus. As representatives of Elune's faithful, the priestesses often dispatch calls for reliable champions to assist with urgent matters affecting their people and sacred lands. Upon arriving in Darnassus and locating Sister Aquinne, she expresses profound relief at your prompt arrival. Her welcome marks the start of direct service to the Sisterhood, signaling that the priestesses face mounting demands requiring trustworthy hands from outside their cloistered ranks.

quest:98392.text: Darkness in the Glade. Sentinel Arynia Cloudsbreak investigates tainted harpy belts in the Oracle Glade. Their amulets may show what is spreading through Teldrassil. Sentinel Arynia Cloudsbreak finds something wrong among the harpies of the Oracle Glade. Their leather belts carry an unnatural taint woven through the fibers. She suspects demonic corruption, not ordinary aggression. Before she warns Darnassus, she needs proof.

quest:98393.text: The Great Cat Spirit. In Nighthaven, druids gather at Dendrite Starblaze's call to learn the cat's ways. They have mastered the bear and now turn to another aspect of the wild under Father Cenarius's blessing. Druids who have mastered the enduring bear are summoned to Moonglade again. Elder Dendrite Starblaze calls them to Nighthaven, where they can deepen their communion with nature. Their spiritual gifts carry them across the distance to this haven of Cenarion wisdom. When you reach Nighthaven, Dendrite Starblaze invokes Father Cenarius and greets you with a faint aura of power. He says it is time to embrace the cat's perspective: swift, agile, and predatory. As before, Dendrite opens the path to understanding, while the work of embodying and spreading the feline spirit rests with you.

quest:98397.text: To Darnassus. In Darnassus, your trial with the Great Cat Spirit brings you back to the Cenarion Enclave. After proving yourself to Dendrite Starblaze in Moonglade, you return to Mathrengyl Bearwalker to learn cat form. You return to Teldrassil after communing with the Great Cat Spirit under Dendrite Starblaze's guidance in Moonglade. Starblaze sees that you have proved yourself a worthy student and sends you to your primary instructor, Mathrengyl Bearwalker. He waits beneath the boughs of the Cenarion Enclave in Darnassus. In Darnassus, Mathrengyl Bearwalker recognizes the wisdom you have gained from the Great Cat Spirit. Every generation of druids faces a trial shaped by this ancient spirit, playful yet deadly. Your bond is established and your spirit prepared; Mathrengyl teaches you the final rites for taking the cat's form.

quest:98398.text: The Oracle Tree. A fallen piece of bark draws travelers to the Oracle Tree, where an ancient voice reaches the mind. Its message calls those who have finished their first duties toward greater work. The Oracle Tree watches its surroundings and guides travelers who have proved their mettle. When it needs an agent in the world, it deliberately sheds a piece of bark nearby. Those who notice are called to step forward, for their first duties are finished and greater responsibilities await. The Oracle Tree reaches the mind through its fallen bark rather than speaking aloud. Examine the piece, and its calm presence washes over you. Its thoughts and desires come like a soft breeze through a canopy of leaves.

quest:98403.text: Twisted Hatred. Twisted Hatred is a quest in Teldrassil uncovering the puppeteer behind Lord Melenas's actions. Adventurers journey into the Cleft northwest of Dolanaar to confront Xethorr the Wicked and eradicate his corrupted spiders before his vile schemes can spread across the boughs. The discovery that Lord Melenas did not operate in isolation reveals a darker undercurrent running through Teldrassil's wilderness. Behind Melenas stood Xethorr the Wicked, an entrenched satyr pulling strings from the shadows of the forest to undermine the tranquil boughs of the World Tree.

quest:98404.text:
The Great Windborne Cat Spirit. At the Avatar of Saeyleenan, young druids face a trial of cunning and stealth. They enter the nearby Stormrage Barrow Den to recover three relics while avoiding enraged spirits. Passing the rite earns them the blessing to wield cat form. A seeker must show the nature of a predator before drawing upon the Great Windborne Cat Spirit. The cat calls for cunning and patience, then fierce action when cornered. The spirit tests those who seek its power, asking them to think, move, and strike like wild feline hunters. Only then may an initiate earn the right to take the cat's shape. The trial leads into the Stormrage Barrow Den, just east of the spirit's avatar. Three sacred tokens lie in its halls: the Relic of the Fang, the Relic of the Claw, and the Relic of the Silent Shadow.

Enraged spirits have overrun the den and attack intruders on sight. A seeker cannot rely on brute force alone, but must tread carefully through the darkness to reach the relics. The Avatar of Saeyleenan is the physical manifestation through which the Great Windborne Cat Spirit speaks to young initiates. Untutored seekers lack a seasoned predator's stealth, so a statue at the barrow den's entrance grants them temporary concealment.

Those who slip past the frenzied spirits and return all three relics show they have learned the predator's ways. The Avatar recognizes their worthiness and grants the blessing to wield cat form.

quest:98423.text: The Treaty of Understanding. The Treaty of Understanding is an ancient dwarven tablet detailing the historic peace agreement between the Bronzebeard and Wildhammer clans following the War of the Three Hammers. Recovered from subterranean depths and brought before King Magni Bronzebeard, the artifact preserves a pivotal moment in dwarven history while highlighting the bitter rift that left the Dark Iron clan excluded from the peace. Recovered from deep within an ancient vault, the Treaty of Understanding is a historic stone tablet documenting the formal cessation of hostilities between dwarven clans. Dating to the turbulent aftermath of the War of the Three Hammers, it represents the moment peace was forged between the Bronzebeard and Wildhammer clans after the Bronzebeards secured control of Ironforge mountain. When presented with the recovered tablet, King Magni Bronzebeard recognizes it as the work of his ancestor, Madoran Bronzebeard, the first Bronzebeard king of Ironforge. While the document bears the signatures of both the Bronzebeard and Wildhammer leaders, it conspicuously lacks the mark of the Dark Iron clan, serving as a lasting testament to the enduring rift between the Dark Irons and their mountain kin.

quest:98424.text: Fizsprockets Notizen. In the Venture Co. mine, Morin Cloudstalker seeks the notebook pages still missing. They hold important information about the company's schemes in the region. Morin Cloudstalker waits at Bloodhoof Village for the pages still missing from Fizsprocket’s notebook. You have found folded pages in Fizsprocket’s pocket, and the remaining notes lie in the Venture Co. mine. Their information can guide what comes next.

quest:98427.text: Schluss damit!. Morin Cloudstalker calls for Schluss damit! before the shredder fells another tree. He asks you to gather allies, return to the mine in the northeast, and stop it from cutting more trees. Morin has heard of the shredder described on a page. Such machines can bring down a forest far faster than axes and muscle. Groves that sheltered the children of the Earth Mother for ages can vanish in days. He asks you to gather allies, return to the mine in the northeast, and make sure the machine fells no more trees. Bring the Mechanoroderschlüssel to Morin at Bloodhoof Village.

quest:98430.text: Die Langläufer. At Bleachmane Rock, Perith Stormhoof is trapped after a peace effort with the gnolls turned violent. Cairne Bloodhoof sent the scout, and his safe return matters to the Tauren people. Cairne Bloodhoof sent Perith Stormhoof to meet the gnolls settled here. Perith is one of Cairne’s Long Runners, so he cannot speak of the full mission. The attempt at peace turned violent, and he fears the gnolls will eat him if he stays through the night. You are asked to help him escape Bleachmane Rock and report his safety to Cairne in Thunder Bluff.

quest:98435.text: Thunderhorns Bericht. Mull sends you to carry Thunderhorn’s report to Archdruid Hamuul Runetotem in Thunder Bluff. The elders need to hear what your help has accomplished. You bring Thunderhorn’s report to Hamuul on the Elder Rise in eastern Thunder Bluff. The report concerns Mulgore’s springs, which sustain the tauren and the animals they rely on for food, clothing, and companionship.

quest:98459.text: A Lack of Virtue. A Lack of Virtue is a delivery quest involving an enduring petty grudge between two card-playing sailors, Tom Half-fish and Bart Tidewater. Travelers carry a packaged gift across the sea to Menethil Harbor, stepping right into the middle of a mutual cheating accusation over how the Maiden's Virtue was won. A Lack of Virtue centers on an acrimonious rivalry between two salty seafaring gamblers: Tom Half-fish and Bart Tidewater. Tom recruits passing travelers to deliver a packaged parcel across the water to Bart in Menethil Harbor, using the delivery as a petty spiteful jab against his former companion. Along the way, Tom warns that Bart is no true sea dog at all, but rather a former actor who cheated his way through card games to purchase his command.

quest:98461.text: Unrequited Love. Unrequited Love is an Alliance delivery quest originating in Auberdine on the shores of Darkshore. Hollee asks travelers taking the vessel to Menethil Harbor to deliver a personal note to Tarrel Rockweaver, an excavation classmate for whom she still holds quiet affection. In the port town of Auberdine along the misty coast of Darkshore, Hollee watches travelers boarding ships for the Eastern Kingdoms. She seeks aid from passersby to reach an old classmate, Tarrel Rockweaver, with whom she shared years studying the craft of excavation before graduation separated them across continents. While Hollee fondly recalls Tarrel's sharp mind and skill with excavation, her composure falters at the mention of his wife, Merrin. Despite the distance and his marriage, Hollee entrusts an adventurer with a personal letter, asking them to seek out Tarrel near Menethil Harbor to ensure he is safe.

quest:98463.text: Talk of the Town. A friendly barkeep points travelers eager for a livelier gathering toward the port of Booty Bay in Stranglethorn Vale. Those looking for wilder company are directed to seek out Nixxrax Fillamug at the Salty Sailor Tavern. Word passes quickly between drink-servers and their patrons, and news travels far beyond the local counter. A friendly bartender passes along a tip about where the genuine commotion is brewing, pointing anyone searching for wilder spectacles toward the port of Booty Bay. The destination is the Salty Sailor Tavern, a lively establishment maintained by goblins amidst the bustle of Stranglethorn Vale. There, Nixxrax Fillamug keeps cups topped up for anyone who walks in.

quest:98512.text: Al'Aketh Assassins. A scout asks you to end the Al'Aketh Assassins' deadly threat. Your survival and aid will be recorded for Valanaar. Scouts in the field call the Al'Aketh assassins stone-cold killers. They move together with ruthless purpose, putting nearby scouts and travelers in grave danger. You face a perilous fight before they can strike their targets. After the Al'Aketh force is defeated, the scout is relieved to find you alive. Your timely aid will go into an official report for Valanaar.

quest:98545.text: Leonid's Letter. Leonid's Letter is a delivery quest directing travelers into the depths of Undercity. Wary of entering the Forsaken capital himself due to a strained past with Lady Sylvanas Windrunner, Leonid hires an impartial courier to deliver a message to Glix Xizzix, an old goblin acquaintance stationed in the Trade Quarter. Leonid needs a courier to transport a sealed letter to an acquaintance in Undercity. Because of past friction and a fraught relationship with Lady Sylvanas Windrunner, Leonid chooses not to walk the halls of the Forsaken capital himself, entrusting a traveling neutral party to pass past the city's guards without raising alarm. The recipient is Glix Xizzix, an opportunistic goblin doing business in the Trade Quarter of Undercity. Upon receiving the message, Glix reminisces about surviving alongside Leonid under the shadow of the Scourge citadel Naxxramas. Though surprised and annoyed by Leonid's promise of compensation, Glix reluctantly pays out from the assorted lost-and-found items left behind by careless undead clientele.

quest:98574.text: Hallowed Memorandum. The Hallowed Memorandum is a written summons directing fledgling gnome priests in Coldridge Valley to meet with Branstock Khalder inside Anvilmar. It marks the commencement of their spiritual training, framing the Holy Light as a philosophical riddle well-suited to gnomish intellect and curiosity. While assisting allies in Coldridge Valley, promising gnomish novitiates receive the Hallowed Memorandum, an introductory message directing them to seek out Branstock Khalder inside Anvilmar. Serving as a call to spiritual study, the note invites aspiring priests to begin their formal tutelage in Dun Morogh. Upon presenting the memorandum, Branstock Khalder welcomes the novice into the fold. He explains that delving into the Holy Light is not a rigid technical craft, but a profound riddle requiring curiosity, keen intelligence, and harmony between intellect and emotion. Through contemplation and practice, students learn to channel these holy mysteries into restorative mending and divine retribution.

quest:98575.text: Tainted Tablet. In the Valley of Trials, Tainted Tablet calls new practitioners to Nartok inside the Den. He teaches warlocks to command the Nether and shape their own fate, though its powers must be kept guarded. A stone message passes through uneasy camp caretakers to newly arrived practitioners in the Valley of Trials. Nartok, a warlock trainer who makes his home inside the Den, calls them to him. He invites you to leave ordinary tribal duties and study deeper, forbidden magic. Nartok speaks plainly about the troubled history between orcs and the Nether. He says the strong should command these volatile powers instead of rejecting them from shame or fear. Where ordinary chieftains falter, he believes those who cunningly master Nether entities can rise to prominence. Yet fearful minds strike at what they cannot understand, so these powers must be guarded closely.

quest:98581.text: Archaic Rune. The Archaic Rune is an introductory quest given to fledgling dwarf Shamans in Dun Morogh. Imbued with elemental power from ancient Wildhammer inscriptions, this sacred tablet introduces young initiates to their elemental heritage. Delivering the stone to Teo Hammerstorm in Anvilmar marks the formal beginning of their training in the ways of earth, air, fire, and water. Fledgling adventurers in Coldridge Valley discover the Archaic Rune after assisting local allies near Anvilmar. Bearing distinctive script carved in the style of the Wildhammer clan, the stone is visibly and palpably charged with ancient elemental power. The rune serves not merely as a relic of stonecraft, but as an elemental test: only those who possess a nascent attunement to the primordial spirits can comprehend the markings etched upon its weathered surface. For those capable of reading the script, it provides clear guidance to seek out proper instruction within the nearby dwarven outpost. Inside the great hall of Anvilmar, the Wildhammer shaman Teo Hammerstorm receives the inscribed stone. For generations, the spiritual arts of the elements remained largely preserved by the Wildhammer clan among their windswept peaks. Now, those traditions have begun to take root among the Bronzebeard dwarves of Ironforge and Dun Morogh. Hammerstorm serves as a vital bridge between the two dwarven cultures, welcoming young initiates who show a calling to commune with the elements and offering formal instruction in the disciplines of earth, air, fire, and water.

quest:986.text: A Lost Master. In Auberdine, Terenthis prepares to help find Volcor, a night elf lost in Darkshore. He can weave a camouflage cloak to protect the searcher, but needs pelts from the coast's fiercest moonstalkers. Terenthis in Auberdine fears for Volcor and his companion, Grimclaw, as danger closes around the coast of Darkshore. The southern wilds hold aggressive predators and corrupted wildlife. Rather than send an unprotected scout into that danger, Terenthis plans a cloak woven with wild illusions. Ordinary hides cannot confound Darkshore's beasts. Terenthis needs fine pelts from mature moonstalker sires or matriarchs. These great cats roam the woodlands south of Auberdine, near the Wildbend River and toward the forested border of Ashenvale. Moonstalker fur and nature enchantments let the finished cloak's wearer pass through hostile territory while searching for Volcor. Terenthis warns that the illusion is delicate. Strenuous activity or combat breaks the enchantment and leaves the searcher exposed.

quest:98738.text: Blessings of the Great Windborne Cat Spirit. After meeting the Great Cat Spirit of Zephras, an initiate returns to Dendrite with a newly awakened aura. The blessing brings the wild cat's stealth, speed, and ferocity, and Dendrite prepares the initiate for further instruction. An initiate returns to Dendrite after seeking the Great Cat Spirit of Zephras and earning its favor. The communion has awakened the wild cat's cunning, predatory stealth, and ferocity within them. Dendrite reads the initiate's newly awakened aura with subtle gestures. Sensing feline instincts woven into their spirit, he sees that the initiate is ready to focus their mind and call upon the true aspect of the cat.

quest:98815.text: Highland Hides. Highland Hides is an expedition contract commissioned by James Halloran, a tanner based in Menethil Harbor. Seeking superior materials from the misty mountain marshes of the Highlands, Halloran trades crafted leather goods for the tough skins of predatory Thicket Raptors. James Halloran, a skilled tanner working out of the port town of Menethil Harbor, constantly keeps an eye out for exotic crafting materials. When word arrives of an expedition exploring forgotten ruins in the Highlands, Halloran pays less mind to ancient history and more to the formidable beasts prowling the mountain marshland. Recognizing the commercial and craft value of the wildlife, he contracts bold adventurers to venture into the mist-shrouded peaks and bring back choice pelts. Among the fauna lurking within the Highlands, Thicket Raptors are notorious predators suited to the rugged marsh terrain. Their tough, textured skins are prized by craftsmen for specialized leatherworking. Halloran tasks travelers with tracking down these creatures and returning with four intact hides, which he uses to produce fine detailing and decorative trim for his workshop's creations.

quest:98824.text: Prehistoric Prism. In the Wetlands, Prospector Whelgar finds a relic marked by the keepers. He sends you with it to Ironforge, where the Explorers' League can study the titans' legacy. Prospector Whelgar finds a remarkable artifact while surveying the Wetlands. Intricate keeper inscriptions cover its many facets, and Whelgar authenticates the titan-like markings. He urges you to carry the relic to Ironforge, where scholars can study it. Whelgar hopes the discovery will enter the official catalogue, with both your recovery and his authentication properly credited. High Explorer Magellas receives the relic for the Explorers' League in Ironforge's Hall of Explorers. Its maker marks confirm its authenticity. Magellas says the light passing through its polished facets recalls wonders he saw on his first excavation in Uldaman. Your donation preserves the artifact for study and adds to the League's records of the titans' legacy.

quest:98895.text: Darkspear Islands Clash. Darkspear Islands Clash is an Alliance military call to arms urging champions to defend vital ground against fierce Darkspear Raiders. Without immediate support on the front lines, the Alliance risks losing the contested archipelago entirely. The struggle for control of the Darkspear Islands has erupted into open war between the Alliance and aggressive warbands of Darkspear Raiders. Alliance commanders warning that without urgent reinforcements, their foothold in the archipelago will be overwhelmed, have sounded a call to arms for capable champions to stem the hostile tide. Alliance leadership relies on proven combatants willing to step directly onto the front lines. To ensure discipline and recognize genuine heroism, commanders require warriors to bring back Darkspear Islands Marks of Honor as tangible proof of their combat service, honoring those who turn the tide of battle.

quest:98896.text: Darkspear Islands Clash. Darkspear Islands Clash calls upon fighters to rally their companions and defeat the hostile Darkspear Raiders contesting the archipelago. The ongoing battle demands coordinated action to stem enemy incursions across the contested island chain. The Darkspear Islands Clash represents an active military push within the contested Darkspear Islands. Forces deployed to the theater are urged to stand fast against waves of Darkspear Raiders who continue to wage skirmishes across the beaches and interior grounds. Rather than an isolated incident, the clash forms part of a sustained campaign to secure foothold territory in the archipelago. Commanders on the front line emphasize the necessity of organization and numbers to overcome the resilient raiders. Survival and victory depend upon rallying nearby allies into a cohesive force capable of withstanding counterattacks, routing fortified raiding bands, and breaking their grip over the disputed island strongholds.

quest:99046.text: The Lost Runner. The Lost Runner is a task to locate Sentinel Eralya Leafshadow, an initiate courier overdue from the Oracle Tree. It matters because communications between the sacred tree and the elders in Darnassus are vital to the night elf leadership. The Council of the Forest maintains a contingent of Sentinels stationed at the revered Oracle Tree within Teldrassil. The tree conveys sacred messages to the night elf elders, relying on dedicated runners to carry these dispatches back to Darnassus along the winding forest roads. Ensuring these missives arrive safely is essential for the guidance and governance of the kaldorei. Communication from the Oracle Tree varies in timing, but an unusually long silence raises alarm when a courier fails to appear. The latest duty fell to Sentinel Eralya Leafshadow, an initiate still undergoing her training. Fearful that misfortune has met her on the trail, her superiors direct travelers to search the westward road toward the Oracle Glade to determine her fate.

quest:99047.text: Not Dead Yet. 'Not Dead Yet' is an urgent plea from Eralya, a mortally wounded night elf discovered after a disastrous mission toward the Oracle Tree. Overwhelmed by vicious harpies, she begs travelers to deliver word of her patrol's fate to Byancie in Dolanaar. It highlights the deadly threats encroaching upon the woodland paths of Teldrassil. A desperate plea in the wilderness of Teldrassil, 'Not Dead Yet' centers on Eralya, a wounded night elf messenger found bleeding and clinging to life. Sent on a crucial mission toward the sacred Oracle Tree alongside her sisters, the patrol was violently ambushed and cut down by encroaching harpies. With no help coming and her own strength fading rapidly, Eralya entrusts passing travelers with carrying urgent news back to safety. Through ragged breaths and coughing up blood, Eralya begs the player to carry her report to Byancie in the nearby village of Dolanaar. The harpies that infest the great boughs of Teldrassil have grown increasingly bold and aggressive, posing a deadly threat to lone messengers and sentinels trying to navigate the forest paths. Delivering Eralya's plea ensures that the settlement of Dolanaar learns of the ambush at the Oracle Tree before more lives are lost.

quest:99048.text: A Missing Hand. A Missing Hand is a quest in Durotar concerning the sudden disappearance of Heglan Shadeeye, a Shattered Hand scout tasked with keeping watch on Tiragarde Keep. When her regular intelligence dispatches abruptly cease, an investigator is sent to find her post and uncover what silenced her. A Missing Hand begins with growing concern over Heglan Shadeeye, a scout belonging to the Shattered Hand. Stationed in Durotar to monitor the hostile human garrison occupying Tiragarde Keep from afar, her steady stream of intelligence reports suddenly vanished without explanation. Her superiors doubt the human soldiers managed to detect and capture her, raising fears that an unexpected and more dangerous hazard intervened. Adventurers are dispatched north of the keep to locate her post and determine whether the disruption is merely a delay in communication or something far grimmer.

quest:99049.text: Threat from Below. Threat from Below is a Horde quest centered on investigating a violent ambush along the eastern shores of Durotar. After scout Heglan Shadeeye is ambushed at her post in a fierce skirmish, adventurers must inspect the devastated area for clues regarding the attackers. Uncovering physical evidence reveals an encroaching threat that directly endangers Razor Hill's defensive lines. A violent skirmish along the Durotar coast leaves behind shattered earth and immediate cause for alarm among the Horde's defenders. Heglan Shadeeye, a Shattered Hand scout keeping watch from her post, was ambushed by an unseen adversary. The skirmish site clearly demonstrates that Heglan fought back fiercely and injured her attackers. With hostile forces moving unchecked along the eastern shoreline, Horde adventurers are called upon to survey the devastated campsite, comb the surrounding ground for clues, and determine what manner of enemy struck the scout.

quest:99050.text: The Great Tree Provides. Byancie works in Dolanaar to save Eralya from a dangerous affliction. Dewy lasher fronds from Teldrassil's lakes and a few simple supplies can make a salve to keep the illness at bay. Byancie tends to the night elves of Dolanaar. When she learns that Eralya has fallen ill in the wilds of Teldrassil, she begins preparing an urgent treatment. Without a salve to slow the affliction, Eralya may not survive the journey back to Dolanaar for proper care. Byancie seeks a remedy in Teldrassil's living bounty. Dewy lasher fronds grow near Lake Al'Ameth to the south and Wellspring Lake to the northwest. Blended with clean spring water in a glass vial, the leaves make medicine that can hold the affliction at bay.

quest:99051.text: Threat from Below. Threat from Below is a defensive mission to purge aggressive naga scouts who are setting up camp nearby. By striking the scout forces and taking their spinefins, adventurers aim to drive the serpentine invaders back north and safeguard the area. Threat from Below addresses a mounting border disturbance caused by encroaching naga scouts. The serpentine raiders have begun setting up advance camps nearby, prompting local defenders to strike before the intruders can secure a permanent foothold. Adventurers are dispatched to cull the scout forces and return with naga spinefins as proof that the encampment has been crushed. This is not the first time the serpentfolk have troubled the area, and local command makes it clear that their presence will not be tolerated. Following the strike against their scout camps, the goal is to drive any surviving naga back to the north, leaving vigilant Horde grunts posted to guard against stragglers or sudden ambushes.

quest:99052.text: Threat from Below. Threat from Below is a Horde bounty tasking adventurers with hunting down a dangerous sea giant prowling Durotar's north coast. Overcoming such an enormous coastal titan protects the nearby shores and earns the respect of the warriors of Durotar. Along the northern coastline of Durotar, the waters of the Great Sea wash against jagged sands and rocky shores. While typically frequented by simple scavengers and crabs, the northern coast harbors a far deadlier menace: a hulking sea giant roaming the shallows, threatening anyone attempting to travel or secure the waters bordering the Horde's arid new homeland. Sea giants are towering brutes capable of shattering longboats and crushing warriors beneath massive fists. Slaying one is no ordinary feat for young adventurers, and bringing down this behemoth of the waves earns deep respect among the orcs, celebrated with the traditional war cry of 'blood and thunder' echoing across the dry red bluffs.

quest:99053.text: Escaping Ban'ethil. Escaping Ban'ethil is a rescue mission within the subterranean barrow den on Teldrassil. Sentinel Lynessa Duskblossom, captured by aggressive Gnarlpine furbolg while delivering a message to slumbering druids, must be escorted safely back to the surface and reported safe to Dolanaar. Sentinel Lynessa Duskblossom was dispatched on an urgent errand by the Oracle Tree to convey a message to the druids resting within Ban'ethil Barrow Den. What was meant to be a routine courier duty turned disastrous when she discovered the subterranean chambers thoroughly overrun by aggressive Gnarlpine furbolg. Cut off and ambushed before she could retreat, she was taken prisoner in the dark tunnels, fearing a grim demise at the hands of the tribe until an adventurer intervened to fight her to the surface. For the kaldorei Sentinels, the subterranean gloom of a barrow den is an unnatural and abhorrent place to be trapped, far removed from the soothing starlight of Elune and the open air of Teldrassil. Following her rescue from the depths, Lynessa makes her escape back toward civilization while word of her survival is carried to Dolanaar. There, Sentinel Kyra Starsong receives the news of her friend's survival with profound relief, rewarding those who aided her comrade in defending the kaldorei people.

quest:99073.text: Easing Suffering. Near the Oracle Tree, Sentinel Eralya Leafshadow lies stricken by a spreading rot. You carry Lashwater Salve to ease her pain and calm her failing breath. Sentinel Eralya Leafshadow lies on the road to the Oracle Tree, stricken by a rot spreading fast. To ease her agony, you bring her freshly made Lashwater Salve before the affliction takes firmer hold.

quest:99079.text: Longwalker Malah. Longwalker Malah is a missing tauren scout dispatched to survey the eastern borderlands of Mulgore on behalf of Bloodhoof Village. As an elite Longwalker answering directly to the High Chieftain, her sudden failure to return after three days prompts an urgent search to ensure both her survival and the safety of the valley. The Longwalkers serve as the eyes and ears of the shu'halo, renowned across the plains for their tireless stride and survival prowess. Pledged directly to High Chieftain Cairne Bloodhoof, these elite scouts are tasked with traversing vast territories to gather intelligence and deliver vital messages. Though their ultimate loyalty lies with the High Chieftain alone, young Baine Bloodhoof occasionally calls upon their aid to safeguard the settlement of Bloodhoof Village and its surrounding pastures. Dispatched to monitor Mulgore's eastern borders, Longwalker Malah Longwind ventured out on a routine three-day reconnaissance run. When she failed to return to Bloodhoof Village on schedule, concern spread among the village leadership. Given the vital intelligence Longwalkers carry and the ever-present dangers lurking along Mulgore's frontier cliffs, scouts and willing travelers are called upon to seek out her trail and confirm her safety. Malah can be recognized by the traditional markings of her order: a ceremonial headband and a feathered staff.

quest:99080.text: Vertreibt sie. Baine Bloodhoof asks you to clear the Galak centaurs from the village’s path. Their defeat could give the children a measure of safety. Baine asks you to kill six Galak centaurs and four Galak scouts. Then bring him Herak the Plunderer’s head. The village’s safety is at stake.

quest:99081.text: Schwieriges Unterfangen. Langläuferin Malah’s report carries word of a new centaur camp in Mulgore. Kriegerheld Wildrunner needs to know what happened to her, who killed her, and why the camp points to a small raiding party entering the land. You bring Langläuferin Malah’s report to Kriegerheld Wildrunner in Bloodhoof Village. He needs to know what happened to Malah and who killed her. Her report brings troubling news, and Baine must hear it at once.

quest:99082.text: The High Chieftain. Cairne Bloodhoof’s son sends you to Thunder Bluff to seek his father’s audience. Your defense of your people has earned recognition. Cairne Bloodhoof and the young Warchief Thrall led the effort to reclaim these plains from the centaurs. As High Chieftain, Cairne can recognize your part in defending your people.

quest:99101.text: Our Ancient Enemy. Malah's report has reached Baine Bloodhoof, and his answer is grim. The matter will not go unanswered.

quest:99108.text: Sparring Match. Sparring Match is an introductory trial overseen by the martial instructor Tang Stonehoof. Designed to test newcomers regardless of their class or background, the trial challenges adventurers to defeat three arena novices or fellow duelists to prove their mettle in direct combat. Overseen by the veteran instructor Tang Stonehoof, the sparring match invites adventurers of all backgrounds into the ring to test their mettle. Though Tang specifically acknowledges those who walk paths outside the warrior tradition, he maintains that martial discipline and direct battle offer universal wisdom to any traveler in a dangerous world. Within Tang Stonehoof's arena, distinctions of lineage and preferred weaponry fall away. Whether wielding sword, bow, or spellcraft, challengers are tasked with proving their combat readiness by defeating three willing opponents—either the training Novice Warriors or fellow adventurers in duels. Overcoming these bouts earns Tang's respect and bandages to dress the wounds of honest combat.

quest:99123.text: Lost in the Shadows. 'Lost in the Shadows' is a quest involving the rescue of Pal'juh, an impetuous hunter who ventured into danger alone. Her rescue highlights the delicate balance between raw aggression and patient stalking required of wilderness trackers. 'Lost in the Shadows' involves locating and rescuing Pal'juh, a talented but hotheaded hunter who ventured out alone into hostile territory. Unwilling to wait for support, she found herself in over her head, requiring outside assistance to ensure her safe return. Upon Pal'juh's rescue, her overseers note that while her potential as a scout and tracker is undeniable, she charges headlong like a raptor rather than stalking with the patience of a tiger. Surviving the ordeal serves as a stark reminder of the wilderness's unforgiving nature.

quest:99127.text: A Net Disaster. A Net Disaster is an Elwynn Forest quest centered on an unusual disruption at Crystal Lake. With hook-and-line fishing yielding nothing and even minnows disappearing from the shallows, adventurers are dispatched to check overnight traps. The ruined traps reveal that hostile neighboring intruders are actively wrecking local fishing gear. At Crystal Lake in Elwynn Forest, local fishermen face an alarming drought in their daily catch. Empty hooks are common enough, but when not even minnows appear in the shallows, everyday angling turns into a serious mystery. To salvage what they can, overnight traps are set in hopes of pulling in basic stock.

quest:99128.text: Slimy Menace. Slimy Menace addresses a growing murloc infestation along the shores of Crystal Lake in Elwynn Forest. These aggressive creatures threaten to deplete the lake's fish supply and endanger nearby locals, requiring swift action to keep their numbers in check. Along the eastern shore of Crystal Lake, an aggressive enclave of murlocs has established a foothold. These savage, semi-aquatic creatures possess sharp teeth and fierce tempers, turning a once-peaceful body of water into a dangerous feeding ground. Local residents rely heavily on the lake for their daily livelihoods, but the murloc presence now threatens anyone daring to fish or approach the water's edge. Beyond the physical danger they present to travelers, the murlocs threaten to devour every fish in the lake if allowed to multiply unchecked. Thinning their numbers provides a much-needed respite for the local waters, though their eerie, echoing warbles remain a grim reminder of their tenacity. Even when scattered, murlocs replenish their ranks swiftly, ensuring that vigilant watch over the shoreline remains an ongoing necessity.

quest:99129.text: A Man About a Murloc. A Man About a Murloc is an errand undertaken on behalf of a fisherman named Jason who is troubled by local murlocs raiding his fish. Jason sends adventurers to consult Remy "Two Times", a local eccentric harboring a deep grudge and schemes of his own against the creatures. A local fisherman named Jason has grown fed up with murlocs raiding his catches. Knowing that Remy "Two Times" harbors a mutual hatred for the amphibians, Jason directs travelers to confer with Remy to see if he has devised any practical ways to drive them away from the waters. Upon being approached, Remy vents his frustration that the local guards refuse to heed his persistent warnings about the murloc threat. Rather than waiting on official help, Remy prepares his own retaliatory measures against the creatures, enlisting able travelers to assist in his plans.

quest:99130.text: An Enticing Offer. 'An Enticing Offer' is a local initiative aimed at repelling encroaching murlocs using bait concocted from toxic duskweed. By harvesting the noxious weed directly from nearby farmland, the plan simultaneously assists local growers and establishes a deterrent against shoreline pests. Dealing with pervasive murloc infestations often calls for inventive pest control rather than endless frontline skirmishes. 'An Enticing Offer' proposes a clever solution to address two local nuisances in a single stroke: crafting a specialized bait laced with duskweed to deter murlocs from encroaching onto settled lands, while clearing encroaching weeds from neighboring crop fields in the process. The core ingredient of the concoction is duskweed, a persistent wild weed that plagues nearby agricultural plots. In substantial quantities, the petals of duskweed contain potent toxins harmful to most beasts. By gathering the weed directly from troubled farmers, the fields are purged of an aggressive pest plant, while its toxic harvest provides the necessary base to train murloc packs to steer clear. While the resulting concoction is relatively simple to prepare, duskweed's indiscriminate toxicity makes handling it somewhat hazardous. Domestic animals and pets must be strictly kept away from the finished mixture, and the quest giver offers a parting caution to ensure that local acquaintances, namely someone named Jason, do not mistake the pungent bait for a meal.

quest:99131.text: Baited for Success. Baited for Success involves assisting local fisherman Jason Mathers in dealing with a disruptive murloc infestation. By coordinating with Remy to prepare a targeted poisoned bait, Mathers hopes to clear the waterways and safely resume selling his catch. Jason Mathers depends on open waters for his fishing trade, but an infestation of aggressive murlocs has disrupted his work. Unable to sell his fish safely, he seeks a solution to rid the area of the creatures. Remy steps in to craft a specialized poisoned bait designed to thin out the local murlocs so ordinary fishing can resume.

quest:99143.text: Bottles and Baubles. Bottles and Baubles is a quest built around the quirky logic that because murlocs look like fish, they must think like them. Adventurers are sent to rummage through a nearby murloc camp for glittering junk and discarded trinkets that an eager angler can fashion into fishing bait. Bottles and Baubles begins with a rather unusual theory of aquatic biology: that because murlocs are fish-like beings, their minds must function just like the fish swimming in the deep. Driven by this logic, an eccentric angler posits that whatever curious oddities catch a murloc's wandering eye will surely entice a hungry fish on a hook. Scavengers are tasked with venturing into a nearby murloc camp to rummage through their hoard piles and gather shiny discarded junk to test the hypothesis. Murlocs along coastal waterways and riverbanks are notorious scavengers, hoarding bright stones, shells, bits of polished glass, and metal scraps in messy mounds around their huts. Sifting through these muddy collections yields all manner of glittering refuse that an opportunistic fisherman can fashion into crude lures and flashers. Once retrieved and handed over, the odd assortment proves satisfactory enough to earn the adventurer a set of starter fishing supplies.

quest:99144.text: Seeking Refuge. Seeking Refuge is a Tirisfal Glades quest involving the rescue of Bareth Dawnstone, an emissary from Bandarion Keep held captive at Crusader's Outpost. His struggle highlights the emergence of an unconventional order devoted to the Holy Light despite severe prejudice from local zealots. Safely returning news of his escape to Brill secures vital ties for this fledgling sanctuary. Seeking Refuge recounts the perilous journey of Bareth Dawnstone, a messenger dispatched from the secluded monastery of Bandarion Keep. While en route to confer with Shari Stilwell in Brill, Bareth was intercepted and captured by zealous warriors at Crusader's Outpost. Despite the hatred directed at his undead state, Bareth remains steadfast in his devotion to the Light, yearning only to escape his tormentors and ensure his message reaches its destination. Bareth's captivity highlights the bitter ideological divide haunting Tirisfal Glades. The zealots at Crusader's Outpost channel the Holy Light through vengeful fury and dogmatic righteousness, viewing Bareth's existence as an affront. In stark contrast, Dawnstone meditates on the Light as a source of protection and inner purity, lamenting how his captors' cruelty distorts the sacred teachings he cherishes. Following his escape, Bareth's safety is confirmed with Shari Stilwell in Brill. Stilwell reveals that their monastic order is still establishing its roots in the bluffs northwest of Solliden Farmstead. Losing a practitioner as promising as Dawnstone would have dealt a tragic blow to their young fellowship, which opens its doors to any traveler seeking authentic spiritual guidance.

quest:99152.text: As Above, So Below. At Bandarion Keep, Hilda the Breaker sends you to investigate the hidden Scourge beneath Shadowvale. Bones still humming with reanimation magic may reveal how the undead gathered beneath the town unseen. Hilda the Breaker prepares defenders at Bandarion Keep for the dangers around them. To the southwest, Shadowvale faces regular unrest from the Tarnished, a hostile faction. Yet beneath the town, the Scourge gathers strength in hidden cellars. If left unchecked, it may erupt in a sudden assault on the keep.

quest:99153.text: The One That Got Away. Near Naxxramas's remnants, Ephram Barbaro seeks the cultist who escaped with a dangerous crystal fragment. The fugitive fled beneath Shadowvale, and its power may raise or strengthen the dead. After the clash with cultists near the Naxxramas battle remnants, word spreads among the ranks. Ephram Barbaro hears that one cultist slipped past the perimeter with an active piece of a Scourge focusing crystal. He seeks capable adventurers to find the fugitive. The escaped cultist fled into passages beneath Shadowvale. The fragment still holds necromantic power, and may raise the dead or strengthen hostile forces underground. Ephram Barbaro sends you to track it down and secure it before that power brings greater harm.

quest:99158.text: Dawn in the Mountains. Dawn in the Mountains is a quest to deliver a shipment of holy candles to Father Gavin at Misty Pine Refuge. A gentle priest of the Argent Dawn, Gavin maintains this mountain shelter to heal and comfort weary travelers rather than wage war with weapons. While many within the Argent Dawn take up arms to purge unholy horrors from Azeroth, some choose the gentler calling of the Light. Father Gavin, a priest dwelling in the rugged mountain wilderness, has turned away from the blade to focus wholly on healing the afflicted and tending to the weary. Taking an abandoned structure, he restored it into Misty Pine Refuge, a safe stop for travelers facing the perils of the high passes. Maintaining an isolated refuge in the mountains requires constant upkeep and practical devotion. To sustain his spiritual ministry and keep the lamps and altars burning, Father Gavin relies on the charity of distant allies. A delivery of consecrated candles ensures that the sanctuary remains a beacon of light, warmth, and hope amidst the unforgiving wilderness.

quest:99159.text: Finding Warmth. Finding Warmth is a humble errand centered on keeping a welcoming hearth fueled with firewood. With the host occupied by other responsibilities, travelers are asked to gather logs so that any soul seeking warmth can find comfort. Completing the task keeps the fire burning and opens the way to further chores. Finding Warmth is a simple chore undertaken to sustain a welcoming fire. The questgiver keeps an open hearth ready to warm any wandering soul, but mounting obligations have left them unable to gather fuel on their own. By stepping in to collect firewood, travelers ensure the hearth remains alight for anyone seeking shelter and comfort. Not all timber retrieved from the surroundings is ready for immediate burning. Upon delivery, pieces too damp or wet to catch fire are set aside to dry properly, while seasoned wood feeds the flames right away. Pleased with the timely assistance, the host quickly turns to other pressing matters that still demand attention.

quest:99160.text: Rime's Wrath. Rime's Wrath is a quest focused on quelling a hazardous outbreak of minor ice elementals. Because methods to peacefully soothe the aggressive frost spirits were unknown, eliminating them became necessary to keep the area safe. Rime's Wrath involves dealing with a localized surge of minor ice elementals. These spirits of biting frost and cold have become an active danger in the area, necessitating swift intervention before their chill spreads further or harms passersby. Rather than a coordinated assault, the response is a containment measure against wild, hostile elemental manifestations. While the preferred outcome was to soothe the agitated frost spirits, the knowledge required to placate them was out of reach. With no practical means of pacification available and the spirits growing increasingly perilous, the only remaining choice was to destroy them to protect the surrounding territory.

quest:99161.text: Rime's Wrath. Following a rockslide, an unusually large elemental named Avala emerged and began triggering erratic weather swings and secondary landslides. An observer tasks adventurers with hunting down the elemental and claiming its core to secure the area. Defeating the creature restores stability to the mountain slopes and safeguards travelers from deadly winter perils. The disturbances began when a sudden rockslide destabilized the mountain pass, opening the way for elemental activity. Among the creatures that surfaced, one particular elemental stood out, towering over its kin in sheer size and raw power. Given the informal moniker "Avala" by the watchful questgiver, this potent entity is not merely an imposing presence—it directly fuels localized atmospheric turmoil and destabilizes the surrounding cliffs. Its presence poses an immediate peril to anyone attempting to navigate the area, as unstable earth and sudden winter chills make ordinary travel lethal. Recognizing the escalating danger of Avala's influence over the terrain, a call was put forth to eliminate the beast before further collapses claimed lives. Slaying the creature requires facing both its elemental ferocity and the harsh conditions it generates, culminating in the recovery of its core as definitive proof of its demise. With Avala vanquished and its animating heart secured, the violent weather shifts subside, restoring a measure of safety to the surrounding mountain passes and safeguarding future travelers from needless catastrophe.

quest:99162.text: Treacherous Cold. Treacherous Cold is a recovery effort in the treacherous high peaks of Dun Morogh following devastating snow and ice slides. Adventurers are tasked with retrieving the inscribed rifles of fallen Ironforge mountaineers to ensure their identities are confirmed and their families receive closure. The rugged, snowy crags of Dun Morogh pose a constant danger to travelers and soldiers alike. Even the hardened mountaineers of Ironforge can find themselves overwhelmed by sudden avalanches and sheets of falling ice, with novice recruits paying with their lives when winter strikes without warning. When mountain slides bury patrols, searching the hazardous terrain becomes a grim race against time. Heightened elemental activity across the region makes thorough rescue expeditions perilous, forcing scouts to enlist brave wanderers to search the drifts for fallen mountaineers and recover their inscribed rifles before the snow conceals them forever. Every Ironforge mountaineer engraves their name into the stock of their rifle, serving as a lasting mark of identification in the harshest conditions. By securing these firearms from the drifts, searchers ensure the fallen can be identified and their honored service recognized by their families back in Ironforge.

quest:99191.text: A Donation of Wool. The High Order is taking wool cloth from those who seek its full recognition. Sixty pieces meet its current need. The High Order is accepting wool cloth, and sixty pieces meet its current needs. The giver can take your donation now. In return, the order grants you full recognition.

quest:99196.text: A Donation of Wool. The Windshapers are taking wool cloth donations, and sixty pieces will earn their full recognition. The Windshapers accept wool cloth from you. When you are ready to give, their representative can take sixty pieces.

quest:99260.text: Fillion's Mission. Fillion lies wounded after his survey at the Overlook Standing Stones. The readings meant to guide skycutters between Skywall and Azeroth are presumed lost. Fillion went to the Overlook Standing Stones to measure elemental currents. Those readings are needed to calculate safe courses for skycutter vessels between Skywall and Azeroth. After an ordeal that required his rescue, he is too wounded to finish the work. The vital data is presumed lost, so he sends his rescuer to report to the Supreme Magister.

quest:993.text: A Lost Master. In Darkshore, you follow Grimclaw’s trail to find the missing scout Volcor. You carry the Enchanted Moonstalker Cloak Terenthis made from fine moonstalker pelts. Terenthis in Auberdine has woven the Enchanted Moonstalker Cloak, and the search for Volcor begins. Grimclaw, the missing night elf scout’s loyal bear, waits on the road south of the settlement for help sent by Terenthis. Give Grimclaw a familiar greeting, and he leads you off the road toward the cave where Volcor is hiding.

quest:994.text: Escape Through Force. In Darkshore, Volcor fights through the wild to reach safety. He reunites with Grimclaw by the road, and you carry word of his escape to Terenthis in Auberdine. Volcor is stranded in Darkshore's perilous wilderness, with danger closing around him. He chooses to fight through the hostile creatures rather than slip away unseen. His skill in battle clears a path straight to the main road and safety.

quest:99411.text: Kyle's Gone Missing!. Kyle's Gone Missing! is a local quest in Bloodhoof Village where Ahab Wheathoof asks passing adventurers to find his wayward dog, Kyle the Frenzied. Feeding the hungry pup a cut of tender strider meat soothes his temper and ensures his safe return home. In Bloodhoof Village, elder Ahab Wheathoof worries over his wayward pet, Kyle the Frenzied. While the title might sound alarming to outsiders, Kyle is Ahab's prized puppy who has slipped away onto the grassy plains of Mulgore. Ahab asks travelers passing through the settlement to track down his unruly companion and offer him a hearty meal to calm his wild spirits. Pacifying Kyle requires a cut of tender strider meat, sourced from the swift plainstriders that roam Mulgore. Presenting the treat satisfies the hungry pup, soothing his frenzied mood and nudging him safely back toward Bloodhoof Village and his grateful owner.

quest:995.text: Escape Through Stealth. In Darkshore, Volcor needs help escaping a furbolg den. Guide the trapped night elf scout past hostile beasts, then report to Terenthis in Auberdine. Volcor, a night elf scout sent to investigate Darkshore's mounting threats, is trapped inside a furbolg cave. Cut off from the main roads and outnumbered, he needs an ally to help him escape before the furbolgs discover him. Volcor chooses a careful path through the cave instead of charging the corrupted denizens. Once outside, he runs ahead on foot and asks you to meet him in Auberdine, where he can travel faster alone. Back in Auberdine, you bring news of Volcor's rescue to Terenthis, a night elf leader working to protect the troubled coast. Volcor's safe return shows that discipline and teamwork can resist the darkness spreading through Darkshore and the wilderness beyond.
